normative_rules.name: ee_impl_flex
normative_rules.text:
The implementation of a RISC-V
execution environment can be pure hardware, pure software, or a
combination of hardware and software. For example, opcode traps and
software emulation can be used to implement functionality not provided
in hardware.

normative_rules.name: base_integer_variants
normative_rules.text:
There are two primary base
integer variants, RV32I and RV64I, described in
<<rv32>> and <<rv64>>, which provide 32-bit
or 64-bit address spaces respectively.

normative_rules.name: xlen_definition
normative_rules.text:
We use the term XLEN to refer to
the width of an integer register in bits (either 32 or 64).

normative_rules.name: twos_complement_signed_integers
normative_rules.text:
The base integer instruction sets use a two's-complement
representation for signed integer values.

normative_rules.name: exception_def
normative_rules.text:
We use the term exception to refer to an unusual condition occurring
at run time associated with an instruction in the current RISC-V hart.

normative_rules.name: interrupt_def
normative_rules.text:
We use the term interrupt to refer to an external asynchronous event
that may cause a RISC-V hart to experience an unexpected transfer of
control.

normative_rules.name: trap_def
normative_rules.text:
We use the term trap to refer to the transfer of control to a
trap handler caused by either an exception or an interrupt.

normative_rules.name: rv32i_xreg_sz
normative_rules.text: For RV32I, the 32 x registers are each 32 bits wide, i.e., XLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: x0eq0
normative_rules.text: Register x0 is hardwired with all bits equal to 0.

normative_rules.name: rv32i_rv64i_other_xregs
normative_rules.text:
General purpose registers x1&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;x31 hold values that various
instructions interpret as a collection of Boolean values, or as two's
complement signed binary integers or unsigned binary integers.

normative_rules.name: pcreg_op
normative_rules.text: There is one additional unprivileged register: the program counter pc holds the address of the current instruction.

normative_rules.name: taken_cti_misaligned_exc
normative_rules.text:
An instruction-address-misaligned exception is generated on a taken branch
or unconditional jump if the target address is not IALIGN-bit aligned.
This exception is reported on the branch or jump instruction, not on the target instruction.

normative_rules.name: cond_br_no_ia_misaligned_exc_not_taken
normative_rules.text:
No instruction-address-misaligned exception is generated
for a conditional branch that is not taken.

normative_rules.name: addi_op
normative_rules.text: insn:addi[] adds the sign-extended 12-bit immediate to register rs1.

normative_rules.name: addi_overflow
normative_rules.text: Arithmetic overflow is ignored and the result is simply the low XLEN bits of the result.

normative_rules.name: slti_sltiu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:slti[] (set less than immediate) places the value 1 in register rd if
register rs1 is less than the sign-extended immediate when both are
treated as signed numbers, else 0 is written to rd. insn:sltiu[] is similar
but compares the values as unsigned numbers (i.e., the immediate is
first sign-extended to XLEN bits then treated as an unsigned number).

normative_rules.name: andi_ori_xori_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:andi[], insn:ori[], insn:xori[] are logical operations that perform bitwise AND, OR, and
XOR on register rs1 and the sign-extended 12-bit immediate and place
the result in rd.

normative_rules.name: slli_op
normative_rules.text: insn:slli[] is a logical left shift (zeros are shifted into the lower bits);

normative_rules.name: srli_op
normative_rules.text: insn:srli[] is a logical right shift (zeros are shifted into the upper bits);

normative_rules.name: srai_op
normative_rules.text: insn:srai[] is an arithmetic right shift (the original sign bit is copied into the vacated upper bits).

normative_rules.name: lui_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:lui[] places the 32-bit U-immediate value into the
destination register rd, filling in the lowest 12 bits with zeros.

normative_rules.name: auipc_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:auipc[] forms a 32-bit offset from
the U-immediate, filling in the lowest 12 bits with zeros, adds this
offset to the address of the insn:auipc[] instruction, then places the result
in register rd.

normative_rules.name: R-type_operands
normative_rules.text:
All operations read
the rs1 and rs2 registers as source operands and write the result into register rd.

normative_rules.name: add_op
normative_rules.text: insn:add[] performs the addition of rs1 and rs2.

normative_rules.name: sub_op
normative_rules.text: insn:sub[] performs the subtraction of rs2 from rs1.

normative_rules.name: add_sub_overflow
normative_rules.text: Overflows are ignored and the low XLEN bits of results are written to the destination rd.

normative_rules.name: slt_sltu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:slt[] and insn:sltu[] perform signed and unsigned compares respectively, writing 1 to rd if
rs1 < rs2, 0 otherwise.

normative_rules.name: and_or_xor_op
normative_rules.text: insn:and[], insn:or[], and insn:xor[] perform bitwise logical operations.

normative_rules.name: sll_srl_sra_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:sll[], insn:srl[], and insn:sra[] perform logical left, logical right, and arithmetic
right shifts on the value in register rs1 by the shift amount held in
the lower 5 bits of register rs2.

normative_rules.name: nop_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:nop[] instruction does not change any architecturally visible state,
except for advancing the pc and incrementing any applicable
performance counters.

normative_rules.name: nop_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:nop[] is encoded as insn:addi[x0,x0,0].

normative_rules.name: no_cti_delay_slots
normative_rules.text:
Control transfer instructions in RV32I
do not have architecturally visible delay slots.

normative_rules.name: ia_fault_exc_on_target
normative_rules.text:
If an instruction access-fault or instruction page-fault exception
occurs on the target of a jump or taken branch, the exception is
reported on the target instruction, not on the jump or branch instruction.

normative_rules.name: jal_target
normative_rules.text:
The offset is sign-extended and added to the address of the jump instruction to
form the jump target address.

normative_rules.name: jal_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:jal[] stores the address of the instruction
following the jump (pc+4) into register rd.

normative_rules.name: jalr_target
normative_rules.text:
The target address is obtained by adding the
sign-extended 12-bit I-immediate to the register rs1, then setting the
least-significant bit of the result to zero.

normative_rules.name: jalr_op
normative_rules.text:
The address of the
instruction following the jump (pc+4) is written to register rd.

normative_rules.name: jump_misaligned_exception
normative_rules.text: The insn:jal[] and insn:jalr[] instructions will generate an instruction-address-misaligned exception if the target address is not aligned to a four-byte boundary.

normative_rules.name: br_target
normative_rules.text:
The 12-bit B-immediate encodes signed offsets in multiples-of-two bytes. The offset
is sign-extended and added to the address of the branch instruction to give the target address.

normative_rules.name: beq_bne_op
normative_rules.text: insn:beq[] and insn:bne[] take the branch if registers rs1 and rs2 are equal or unequal respectively.

normative_rules.name: blt_bltu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:blt[] and insn:bltu[] take the branch if rs1 is less than rs2, using signed and
unsigned comparison respectively.

normative_rules.name: bge_bgeu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:bge[] and insn:bgeu[] take the branch if rs1 is greater than or equal to rs2,
using signed and unsigned comparison respectively.

normative_rules.name: branch_misaligned_taken_exception
normative_rules.text:
The conditional branch instructions will generate an
instruction-address-misaligned exception if the target address is not
aligned to a four-byte boundary and the branch condition evaluates to
true.

normative_rules.name: branch_misaligned_untaken_exception
normative_rules.text:
If the branch condition evaluates to false, the
instruction-address-misaligned exception will not be raised.

normative_rules.name: load_exc_x0
normative_rules.text:
Loads with a destination of
x0 must still raise any exceptions and cause any other side effects
even though the load value is discarded.

normative_rules.name: endianness
normative_rules.text: The EEI will define whether the memory system is little-endian or big-endian.

normative_rules.name: ldst_endian_byte_invariant
normative_rules.text: In RISC-V, endianness is byte-address invariant.

normative_rules.name: ldst_ea
normative_rules.text:
The effective address is obtained by adding register rs1 to the
sign-extended 12-bit offset.

normative_rules.name: load_op
normative_rules.text: Loads copy a value from memory to register rd.

normative_rules.name: store_op
normative_rules.text: Stores copy the value in register rs2 to memory.

normative_rules.name: lw_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:lw[] instruction loads a 32-bit value from memory into rd.

normative_rules.name: lh_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:lh[] loads a 16-bit value from memory, then sign-extends to 32-bits before storing
in rd.

normative_rules.name: lhu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:lhu[] loads a 16-bit value from memory but then zero extends to
32-bits before storing in rd.

normative_rules.name: lb_lbu_op
normative_rules.text: insn:lb[] and insn:lbu[] are defined analogously for 8-bit values.

normative_rules.name: sw_sh_sb_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sw[], insn:sh[], and insn:sb[] instructions store 32-bit, 16-bit, and
8-bit values from the low bits of register rs2 to memory.

normative_rules.name: ldst_no_exc_aligned
normative_rules.text:
loads and stores whose effective addresses are
naturally aligned shall not raise an address-misaligned exception.

normative_rules.name: misaligned_ldst_eei_dependent_behavior
normative_rules.text:
Loads and stores whose effective address is not naturally aligned to the
referenced datatype (i.e., the effective address is not divisible by the
size of the access in bytes) have behavior dependent on the EEI.

normative_rules.name: misaligned_ldst_hw_support
normative_rules.text:
misaligned loads and stores can be handled in hardware, or
via an invisible trap into the execution environment implementation, or possibly a
combination of hardware and invisible trap depending on address.

normative_rules.name: misaligned_ldst_exc_type
normative_rules.text:
loads and stores that are not naturally aligned
may either complete execution successfully or raise an exception. The exception raised can be either an
address-misaligned exception or an access-fault exception.
For a memory access that would otherwise be able
to complete except for the misalignment, an access-fault exception can
be raised instead of an address-misaligned exception if the misaligned
access should not be emulated, e.g., if accesses to the memory region
have side effects.

normative_rules.name: misaligned_ldst_contained_or_fatal_trap
normative_rules.text:
When an EEI does not guarantee misaligned loads and
stores are handled invisibly, the EEI must define if exceptions caused
by address misalignment result in a contained trap (allowing software
running inside the execution environment to handle the trap) or a fatal
trap (terminating execution).

normative_rules.name: ldst_atomicity_for_aligned
normative_rules.text:
naturally aligned
loads and stores are guaranteed to execute atomically

normative_rules.name: fence_op
normative_rules.text:
A insn:fence[] (with fm=0000) orders all memory operations in its predecessor set
before all memory operations in its successor set.

normative_rules.name: fence-tso_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fence.tso[] orders
all load operations in its predecessor set before all memory operations
in its successor set, and all store operations in its predecessor set
before all store operations in its successor set. This leaves non-AMO
store operations in the insn:fence.tso[]'s predecessor set unordered with
non-AMO loads in its successor set.

normative_rules.name: fence_unused_flds_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The unused fields in the
insn:fence[] instructions, rs1 and rd, are reserved
for finer-grain fences in future extensions. For forward compatibility,
base implementations shall ignore these fields

normative_rules.name: ecall_service_request_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:ecall[] instruction is used to make a service request to the execution environment.

normative_rules.name: ebreak_debug_env_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:ebreak[] instruction is used to return control to a debugging environment.

normative_rules.name: hints_op
normative_rules.text:
HINTs do not change any architecturally
visible state, except for advancing the pc and any applicable
performance counters. Implementations are always allowed to ignore the
encoded hints.

normative_rules.name: hints_enc
normative_rules.text:
Most RV32I HINTs are encoded as integer computational instructions with
rd=x0. The other RV32I HINTs are encoded as insn:fence[] instructions with
a null predecessor or successor set and with fm=0.

normative_rules.name: rv64i_xreg_sz
normative_rules.text:
RV64I widens the integer registers and supported user address space to
64 bits, i.e., XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: rv64_w_sex
normative_rules.text:
These
insn:*w[] instructions ignore the upper 32 bits of their inputs and always produce
32-bit signed values, sign-extending them to 64 bits, i.e. bits XLEN-1
through 31 are equal.

normative_rules.name: addiw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:addiw[] is an RV64I instruction that adds the sign-extended 12-bit
immediate to register rs1 and produces the proper sign extension of a
32-bit result in rd.

normative_rules.name: addiw_overflow
normative_rules.text:
Overflows are ignored and the result is the low
32 bits of the result sign-extended to 64 bits.

normative_rules.name: slliw_srliw_sraiw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:slliw[], insn:srliw[], and insn:sraiw[] are RV64I-only instructions that are analogously
defined but operate on 32-bit values and sign-extend their 32-bit
results to 64 bits.

normative_rules.name: slliw_srliw_sraiw_imm5_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:slliw[], insn:srliw[], and insn:sraiw[] encodings with
imm[5]≠0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: lui_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
insn:lui[] places the
32-bit U-immediate into register rd, filling in the lowest 12 bits
with zeros. The 32-bit result is sign-extended to 64 bits.

normative_rules.name: auipc_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
insn:auipc[] forms a 32-bit offset from the U-immediate, filling in the lowest
12 bits with zeros, sign-extends the result to 64 bits, adds it to the
address of the insn:auipc[] instruction, then places the result in register rd.

normative_rules.name: addw_subw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:addw[] and insn:subw[] are RV64I-only instructions that are defined analogously
to insn:add[] and insn:sub[] but operate on 32-bit values and produce signed 32-bit results.

normative_rules.name: addw_subw_overflow
normative_rules.text:
Overflows are ignored, and the low 32-bits of the result is
sign-extended to 64-bits and written to the destination register.

normative_rules.name: sll_srl_sra_shamt_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
In RV64I, only the low 6 bits of rs2 are considered
for the shift amount.

normative_rules.name: sllw_srlw_sraw_op
normative_rules.text: insn:sllw[], insn:srlw[], and insn:sraw[] are RV64I-only instructions that are analogously defined but operate on 32-bit values and sign-extend their 32-bit results to 64 bits. The shift amount is given by rs2[4:0].

normative_rules.name: ld_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ld[] instruction loads a 64-bit value from memory into register rd
for RV64I.

normative_rules.name: lw_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
The insn:lw[] instruction loads a 32-bit value from memory and sign-extends
this to 64 bits before storing it in register rd for RV64I.

normative_rules.name: lwu_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:lwu[] instruction, on the other hand, zero-extends the 32-bit value from
memory for RV64I.

normative_rules.name: lh_lhu_lb_lbu_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
insn:lh[] and insn:lhu[] are defined analogously for 16-bit values,
as are insn:lb[] and insn:lbu[] for 8-bit values.

normative_rules.name: sd_sw_sh_sb_op_rv64i
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sd[], insn:sw[], insn:sh[], and insn:sb[] instructions
store 64-bit, 32-bit, 16-bit, and 8-bit values from the low bits of
register rs2 to memory respectively.

normative_rules.name: diff_rv32e_rv32i
normative_rules.text: RV32E and RV64E use the same instruction-set encoding as RV32I and RV64I respectively, except that only registers x0‍–‍x15 are provided. All encodings specifying the other registers x16‍–‍x31 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_single_hart_op
normative_rules.text:
Under RVWMO, code running on a single hart appears to execute in order
from the perspective of other memory instructions in the same hart, but
memory instructions from another hart may observe the memory
instructions from the first hart being executed in a different order.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_single_copy_atomic
normative_rules.text:
All memory operations are single-copy atomic:
they can never be observed in a partially complete state.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_aligned_memop
normative_rules.text:
Each aligned memory instruction that accesses XLEN or
fewer bits gives rise to exactly one memory operation, unless specified otherwise.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_aligned_amo_memop
normative_rules.text:
An aligned AMO gives rise to a single memory operation that
is both a load operation and a store operation simultaneously.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_misaligned_ldst_memops
normative_rules.text:
A misaligned load or store instruction may be decomposed
into a set of component memory operations of any granularity.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_fp_gt_xlen_memops
normative_rules.text:
A floating-point load or store of more than XLEN bits may
also be decomposed into a set of component memory operations of any granularity.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_order_multi_memops
normative_rules.text:
The memory operations generated by such instructions
are not ordered with respect to each other in program order, but they are ordered normally with
respect to the memory operations generated by preceding and subsequent
instructions in program order.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_misaligned_in_atomic_pma
normative_rules.text:
memory accesses affected by the
misaligned atomicity granule PMA that lie within a misaligned atomicity granule
are not decomposed.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_lead_in
normative_rules.text: The complete definition of preserved program order is as follows (and note that AMOs are simultaneously both loads and stores): memory operation a precedes memory operation b in preserved program order (and hence also in the global memory order) if a precedes b in program order, a and b both access regular main memory (rather than I/O regions), and any of the following hold:

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_overlap1
normative_rules.text: b is a store, and a and b access overlapping memory addresses

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_overlap2
normative_rules.text:
a and b are loads, x is a byte read by both a and
b, there is no store to x between a and b in program order, and a and b return values for x
written by different memory operations

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_overlap3
normative_rules.text:
a is generated by an AMO or insn:sc[] instruction, b is a load, and
b returns a value written by a

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_sync1
normative_rules.text: There is a insn:fence[] instruction that orders a before b

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_sync2
normative_rules.text: a has an acquire annotation

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_sync3
normative_rules.text: b has a release annotation

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_sync4
normative_rules.text: a and b both have RCsc annotations

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_sync5
normative_rules.text: a is paired with b

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_dep1
normative_rules.text: b has a syntactic address dependency on a

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_dep2
normative_rules.text: b has a syntactic data dependency on a

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_dep3
normative_rules.text: b is a store, and b has a syntactic control dependency on a

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_pipe1
normative_rules.text:
b is a load, and there exists some store m between a and b
in program order such that m has an address or data dependency on a,
and b returns a value written by m

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ppo_pipe2
normative_rules.text:
b is a store, and there exists some instruction m between a
and b in program order such that m has an address dependency on a

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_obeyed
normative_rules.text: An execution of a RISC-V program obeys the RVWMO memory consistency model only if there exists a global memory order conforming to preserved program order and satisfying the load value axiom, the atomicity axiom, and the progress axiom.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ld_val_axiom_lead_in
normative_rules.text: Each byte of each load i returns the value written to that byte by the store that is the latest in global memory order among the following stores:

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_ld_val_axiom_list
normative_rules.text:
Stores that write that byte and that precede i in the global memory order
Stores that write that byte and that precede i in program order

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_atomicity_axiom
normative_rules.text: If r and w are paired load and store operations generated by aligned insn:lr[] and insn:sc[] instructions in a hart h, s is a store to byte x, and r returns a value written by s, then s must precede w in the global memory order, and there can be no store from a hart other than h to byte x following s and preceding w in the global memory order.

normative_rules.name: rvwmo_progress_axiom
normative_rules.text: No memory operation may be preceded in the global memory order by an infinite sequence of other memory operations.

normative_rules.name: rvtso_adj_rvwmo
normative_rules.text: RVTSO makes the following adjustments to RVWMO:

normative_rules.name: Ztso_ld
normative_rules.text: All load operations behave as if they have an acquire-RCpc annotation

normative_rules.name: Ztso_sd
normative_rules.text: All store operations behave as if they have a release-RCpc annotation.

normative_rules.name: Ztso_amo
normative_rules.text:
All AMOs behave as if they have both acquire-RCsc and release-RCsc
annotations.

normative_rules.name: Ztso_vect_mem
normative_rules.text:
Additionally, if the ext:ztso[] extension is implemented, then vector memory
instructions in the ext:v[] extension and ext:zve*[] family of extensions follow RVTSO at
the instruction level.

normative_rules.name: fence-i_op
normative_rules.text: A insn:fence.i[] instruction orders all explicit memory accesses and instruction fetches that precede the insn:fence.i[] in program order before all instruction fetches that follow the insn:fence.i[] in program order.

normative_rules.name: fence-i_rsv
normative_rules.text: The unused fields in the insn:fence.i[] instruction, funct12, rs1, and rd, are reserved for finer-grain fences in future extensions. For forward compatibility, base implementations shall ignore these fields, and standard software shall zero these fields.

normative_rules.name: csrrw_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:csrrw[] (Atomic Read/Write CSR) instruction atomically swaps values in the CSRs and integer registers. insn:csrrw[] reads the old value of the CSR, zero-extends the value to XLEN bits, then writes it to integer register rd. The initial value in rs1 is written to the CSR. If rd=x0, then the instruction shall not read the CSR and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.

normative_rules.name: csrrs_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:csrrs[] (Atomic Read and Set Bits in CSR) instruction reads the value of the CSR, zero-extends the value to XLEN bits, and writes it to integer register rd. The initial value in integer register rs1 is treated as a bit mask that specifies bit positions to be set in the CSR. Any bit that is high in rs1 will cause the corresponding bit to be set in the CSR, if that CSR bit is writable.

normative_rules.name: csrrc_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:csrrc[] (Atomic Read and Clear Bits in CSR) instruction reads the value of the CSR, zero-extends the value to XLEN bits, and writes it to integer register rd. The initial value in integer register rs1 is treated as a bit mask that specifies bit positions to be cleared in the CSR. Any bit that is high in rs1 will cause the corresponding bit to be cleared in the CSR, if that CSR bit is writable.

normative_rules.name: csrrs_csrrc_rs1_x0
normative_rules.text: For both insn:csrrs[] and insn:csrrc[], if rs1=x0, then the instruction will not write to the CSR at all, and so shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs. Both insn:csrrs[] and insn:csrrc[] always read the addressed CSR and cause any read side effects regardless of rs1 and rd fields. Note that if rs1 specifies a register other than x0, and that register holds a zero value, the instruction will not action any attendant per-field side effects, but will action any side effects caused by writing to the entire CSR.

normative_rules.name: csrrw_rs1_x0
normative_rules.text: A insn:csrrw[] with rs1=x0 will attempt to write zero to the destination CSR.

normative_rules.name: csrrsi_csrrci_uimm_zero
normative_rules.text:
For insn:csrrsi[] and insn:csrrci[], if the uimm[4:0] field is zero, then these
instructions will not write to the CSR, and shall not cause any of the
side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise
illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs.

normative_rules.name: csrrwi_rd_x0
normative_rules.text:
For
insn:csrrwi[], if rd=x0, then the instruction shall not read the CSR and
shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read.

normative_rules.name: csrrwi_csrrsi_csrrci_ops
normative_rules.text: The insn:csrrwi[], insn:csrrsi[], and insn:csrrci[] variants are similar to insn:csrrw[], insn:csrrs[], and insn:csrrc[] respectively, except they update the CSR using an XLEN-bit value obtained by zero-extending a 5-bit unsigned immediate (uimm[4:0]) field encoded in the rs1 field instead of a value from an integer register. For insn:csrrsi[] and insn:csrrci[], if the uimm[4:0] field is zero, then these instructions will not write to the CSR, and shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, nor raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only CSRs. For insn:csrrwi[], if rd=x0, then the instruction shall not read the CSR and shall not cause any of the side effects that might occur on a CSR read. Both insn:csrrsi[] and insn:csrrci[] will always read the CSR and cause any read side effects regardless of rd and rs1 fields.

normative_rules.name: csr_side_effects
normative_rules.text: summarizes the behavior of the CSR instructions with respect to whether they read and/or write the CSR.

normative_rules.name: csr_rs1_uimm_side_effect
normative_rules.text:
insn:csrrs[], insn:csrrsi[], insn:csrrc[], and insn:csrrci[]
only action side effects for fields for which the rs1 or uimm argument
has at least one bit set corresponding to that field.

normative_rules.name: csr_access_order
normative_rules.text:
In particular,
unless specified otherwise, a CSR access is performed after the
execution of any prior instructions in program order whose behavior
modifies or is modified by the CSR state and before the execution of any
subsequent instructions in program order whose behavior modifies or is
modified by the CSR state.

normative_rules.name: csrr_order
normative_rules.text:
an explicit CSR read returns the
CSR state before the execution of the instruction

normative_rules.name: csrw_order
normative_rules.text:
an explicit CSR
write suppresses and overrides any implicit writes or modifications to
the same CSR by the same instruction.

normative_rules.name: csr_side_effects_synchronous
normative_rules.text:
Likewise, any side effects from an explicit CSR access are normally
observed to occur synchronously in program order. Unless specified
otherwise, the full consequences of any such side effects are observable
by the very next instruction, and no consequences may be observed
out-of-order by preceding instructions.

normative_rules.name: csr_weakly_ordered
normative_rules.text:
For the RVWMO memory consistency model (<<memorymodel>>), CSR accesses are weakly
ordered by default, so other harts or devices may observe CSR accesses
in an order different from program order.

normative_rules.name: csr_memory_access_ordering
normative_rules.text:
In addition, CSR accesses are
not ordered with respect to explicit memory accesses, unless a CSR
access modifies the execution behavior of the instruction that performs
the explicit memory access or unless a CSR access and an explicit memory
access are ordered by either the syntactic dependencies defined by the
memory model or the ordering requirements defined in
<<sec:memory-ordering-pmas>>.

normative_rules.name: csr_fence_ordering
normative_rules.text:
For the purposes of the insn:fence[] instruction, CSR read
accesses are classified as device input (I), and CSR write accesses are
classified as device output (O).

normative_rules.name: csr_strongly_ordered
normative_rules.text:
The hardware platform may define that accesses to certain CSRs are
strongly ordered, as defined in <<sec:memory-ordering-pmas>>.
Accesses to strongly ordered CSRs have
stronger ordering constraints with respect to accesses to both weakly
ordered CSRs and accesses to memory-mapped I/O regions.

normative_rules.name: Zihpm_op_sz_mode_acc_count
normative_rules.text:
RISC-V ISAs provide a set of up to thirty-two 64-bit performance
counters and timers

normative_rules.name: Zihpm_op_sz_mode_acc_priv
normative_rules.text:
accessible via unprivileged XLEN-bit
read-only CSR registers 0xC00–0xC1F

normative_rules.name: Zihpm_op_sz_mode_acc_xlen32
normative_rules.text:
when XLEN=32, the upper 32 bits
are accessed via CSR registers 0xC80–0xC9F

normative_rules.name: Zihpm_op_sz_mode_acc_partition
normative_rules.text:
These counters are
divided between the ext:zicntr[] and extlink:zihpm[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdcycle_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:rdcycle[] pseudoinstruction reads the low
XLEN bits of the csr:cycle[] CSR which holds a count of the number of clock
cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running from an
arbitrary start time in the past.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdcycleh_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:rdcycleh[] is only present when XLEN=32 and reads bits 63-32
of the same cycle counter.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdtime_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:rdtime[] pseudoinstruction reads the low XLEN bits of the csr:time[] CSR,
which counts wall-clock real time that has passed from an arbitrary
start time in the past.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdtimeh_op
normative_rules.text:
RDTIMEH is only present when XLEN=32 and reads
bits 63-32 of the same real-time counter.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_time_hart_sync
normative_rules.text:
The real-time clocks of all harts must be synchronized to within one
tick of the real-time clock.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdinstret_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:rdinstret[] pseudoinstruction reads the low XLEN bits of the
csr:instret[] CSR, which counts the number of instructions retired by this
hart from some arbitrary start point in the past.

normative_rules.name: Zicntr_rdinstreth_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:rdinstreth[] is only
present when XLEN=32 and reads bits 63-32 of the same instruction
counter.

normative_rules.name: hpmcounter_op_sz_mode
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zihpm[] extension comprises up to 29 additional unprivileged 64-bit
hardware performance counters, csr:hpmcounter3[]-csr:hpmcounter31[].

normative_rules.name: hpm_counter_op_sz_mode_xlen32
normative_rules.text:
When
XLEN=32, the upper 32 bits of these performance counters are accessible
via additional CSRs csr:hpmcounter3h[]-csr:hpmcounter31h[].

normative_rules.name: hpm_counter_op_sz_mode_dependency
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zihpm[] extension
depends on the ext:zicsr[] extension.

normative_rules.name: hpm_platform_specific_impl
normative_rules.text:
The implemented number and width of these additional counters, and the
set of events they count, are platform-specific.

normative_rules.name: hpm_unimplemented_counter_access
normative_rules.text:
Accessing an
unimplemented counter may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may
return a constant value.

normative_rules.name: hpm_misconfigured_event_behavior
normative_rules.text:
If the configuration used to select the events
counted by a counter is misconfigured, the counter may return a constant
value.

normative_rules.name: mul_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:mul[] performs an XLEN-bit×XLEN-bit multiplication of
rs1 by rs2 and places the lower XLEN bits in the destination
register.

normative_rules.name: mulh_mulhu_mulhsu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:mulh[], insn:mulhu[], and insn:mulhsu[] perform the same multiplication but
return the upper XLEN bits of the full 2×XLEN-bit
product, for signed×signed,
unsigned×unsigned, and rs1×unsigned rs2 multiplication.

normative_rules.name: mulw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:mulw[] is an RV64 instruction that multiplies the lower 32 bits of the
source registers, placing the sign extension of the lower 32 bits of the
result into the destination register.

normative_rules.name: div_divu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:div[] and insn:divu[] perform an XLEN bits by XLEN bits signed and unsigned
integer division of rs1 by rs2, rounding towards zero.

normative_rules.name: rem_remu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:rem[] and insn:remu[]
provide the remainder of the corresponding division operation.

normative_rules.name: rem_result_sign
normative_rules.text:
For insn:rem[],
the sign of a nonzero result equals the sign of the dividend.

normative_rules.name: divw_divuw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:divw[] and insn:divuw[] are RV64 instructions that divide the lower 32 bits of
rs1 by the lower 32 bits of rs2, treating them as signed and
unsigned integers, placing the 32-bit quotient in rd,
sign-extended to 64 bits.

normative_rules.name: remw_remuw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:remw[] and insn:remuw[] are RV64 instructions that
provide the corresponding signed and unsigned remainder
operations.

normative_rules.name: remw_remuw_result_sign
normative_rules.text:
Both insn:remw[] and insn:remuw[] always sign-extend the 32-bit result
to 64 bits, including on a divide by zero.

normative_rules.name: div_by_zero
normative_rules.text:
The quotient of division by zero has all bits
set

normative_rules.name: rem_by_zero
normative_rules.text: the remainder of division by zero equals the dividend.

normative_rules.name: signed_div_overflow
normative_rules.text:
Signed division overflow occurs only when the most-negative integer is divided
by −1. The quotient of a signed division with overflow is
equal to the dividend, and the remainder is zero.

normative_rules.name: Zmmul_enc_same
normative_rules.text:
The encodings and semantics are identical to those of the
corresponding instructions in ext:m[].

normative_rules.name: M_implies_Zmmul
normative_rules.text: ext:m[] implies ext:zmmul[].

normative_rules.name: Zmmul_insns
normative_rules.text: The ext:zmmul[] extension implements the multiplication subset of the ext:m[] extension. It adds the following instructions defined in extm: insn:mul[], insn:mulh[], insn:mulhu[], insn:mulhsu[], and (for RV64 only) insn:mulw[]. The encodings and semantics are identical to those of the corresponding instructions in ext:m[]. ext:m[] implies ext:zmmul[].

normative_rules.name: czero-eqz_op
normative_rules.text: If rs2 contains the value zero, this instruction writes the value zero to rd.  Otherwise, this instruction copies the contents of rs1 to rd.

normative_rules.name: czero-eqz_inst_ctime
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, if the Zkt extension is implemented, this instruction’s timing is independent of the data values in rs1 and rs2.

normative_rules.name: czero-nez_op
normative_rules.text: If rs2 contains a nonzero value, this instruction writes the value zero to rd.  Otherwise, this instruction copies the contents of rs1 to rd.

normative_rules.name: czero-nez_Zkt_timing
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, if the Zkt extension is implemented, this instruction’s timing is independent of the data values in rs1 and rs2.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_reg_pairs
normative_rules.text: Operands containing src for store instructions and dest for load instructions are held in aligned x-register pairs, i.e., register numbers must be even.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_bits_to_pair
normative_rules.text:
Regardless of endianness, the lower-numbered register holds the
low-order bits, and the higher-numbered register holds the high-order bits

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_align8_no_exc
normative_rules.text:
As the access size is 64-bit, accesses are only considered naturally aligned for effective addresses that are a multiple of 8.
In this case, these instructions are guaranteed to not raise an address-misaligned exception.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_align8_atomic
normative_rules.text: Even if naturally aligned, the memory access might not be performed atomically.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_align4_atomic
normative_rules.text: If the effective address is a multiple of 4, then each word access is required to be performed atomically.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_ld_resume_trap
normative_rules.text:
To ensure resumable trap handling is possible for the load instructions, the base register must
have its original value if a trap is taken.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_ld_x0
normative_rules.text:
LD instructions with destination x0 are processed as any other load,
but the result is discarded entirely and x1 is not written.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_sd_x0
normative_rules.text: If using x0 as src of insn:sd[], the entire 64-bit operand is zero — i.e., register x1 is not accessed.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_rvwmo_exc_misaligned
normative_rules.text:
For the purposes of RVWMO and exception handling, insn:ld[] and insn:sd[] instructions are
considered to be misaligned loads and stores

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_align4_two_4byte
normative_rules.text:
an insn:ld[] or insn:sd[] instruction whose effective address is a multiple of 4 gives rise
to two 4-byte memory operations.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_ld_op
normative_rules.text: Loads a 64-bit value into registers rd and rd+1. The effective address is obtained by adding register rs1 to the sign-extended 12-bit offset.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_sd_op
normative_rules.text: Stores a 64-bit value from registers rs2 and rs2+1. The effective address is obtained by adding register rs1 to the sign-extended 12-bit offset.

normative_rules.name: Ziccif_if_atomicity
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ziccif[] extension is implemented, main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs must support instruction fetch, and any instruction fetches of naturally aligned power-of-2 sizes of at most min(ILEN,XLEN) bits are atomic.

normative_rules.name: Ziccif_fetch_mechanism
normative_rules.text: An implementation with the ext:ziccif[] extension fetches instructions in a manner equivalent to the following state machine.

normative_rules.name: Ziccif_pma_application
normative_rules.text: Memory protection and executability PMAs are applied only to bytes that are not discarded by this algorithm.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_dep_Ziccif
normative_rules.text: The ext:ziccid[] extension depends on the extlink:ziccif[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_model_scope
normative_rules.text:
This model only applies to instruction fetches to memory regions with the
cacheability and coherence PMAs; instruction fetches to other memory regions
proceed as though the ext:ziccid[] extension were not implemented.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_fetch_order
normative_rules.text:
Harts have two ordered operational stages: instruction fetch and execution.
Each hart has an instruction buffer of bounded capacity.
Instructions are fetched from memory in program order, then inserted into the
instruction buffer in program order.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_fetch_global_order
normative_rules.text:
An instruction fetch is a memory read operation that appears in the global
memory order, in program order with respect to other instruction fetches
from the same hart.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_fetch_value
normative_rules.text:
For each instruction byte fetched from memory, memory
supplies the value written by the most recent store that precedes the read in
global memory order.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_fetch_before_access
normative_rules.text:
Instruction fetches appear in the global memory order before any explicit memory
accesses to which they give rise.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_dequeue_order
normative_rules.text:
After some amount of time, instructions are dequeued in program order from the
instruction buffer and executed.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_exec_order
normative_rules.text:
Instructions are executed in program order, but instructions' explicit memory
accesses may be reordered in any manner consistent with RVWMO.

normative_rules.name: Ziccid_fence-i_op
normative_rules.text:
All of the hart’s older explicit memory accesses become globally visible.
The instruction buffer is flushed.

normative_rules.name: Ziccrse_rsrv_eventual
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ziccrse[] extension is implemented, then main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs must support the RsrvEventual PMA.

normative_rules.name: Ziccamoa_amo_pma
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ziccamoa[] extension is implemented, then main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs must provide AMOArithmetic-level PMA support as defined in .

normative_rules.name: Ziccamoc_casq_pma
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ziccamoc[] extension is implemented, then main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs must provide AMOCASQ-level PMA support as defined in .

normative_rules.name: Zicclsm_misaligned_support
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zicclsm[] extension is implemented, then misaligned loads and stores to main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs must be supported.

normative_rules.name: Zic64b_cache_block_size
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zic64b[] extension is implemented, then cache blocks must be 64 bytes in size, naturally aligned in the address space.

normative_rules.name: Zimop_mop-r_op
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zimop[] extension defines 32 MOP instructions named MOP.R.n, where
n is an integer between 0 and 31, inclusive.
Unless redefined by another extension, these instructions simply write 0 to
x[rd].

normative_rules.name: Zimop_mop-rr_op
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zimop[] extension additionally defines 8 MOP instructions named
MOP.RR.n, where n is an integer between 0 and 7, inclusive.
Unless redefined by another extension, these instructions simply
write 0 to x[rd].

normative_rules.name: cfi_call_term
normative_rules.text: The term call is used to refer to a insn:jal[], insn:jalr[] or insn:c.jal[] instruction with a link register as destination, i.e., rd≠x0. Conventionally, the link register is x1 or x5. A call using insn:jal[] or insn:c.jal[] is termed a direct call. A insn:c.jalr[] expands to insn:jalr[x1,0(rs1)] and thus it is a call. A call using insn:jalr[] or insn:c.jalr[] is termed an indirect call.

normative_rules.name: cfi_return_term
normative_rules.text: The term return is used to refer to a insn:jalr[] instruction with rd=x0 and with rs1=x1 or rs1=x5. A insn:c.jr[] instruction expands to insn:jalr[x0,0(rs1)] and is a return if rs1=x1 or rs1=x5.

normative_rules.name: cfi_indirect_jump_term
normative_rules.text: The term indirect jump is used to refer to a insn:jalr[] instruction with rd=x0 and where the rs1 is not x1 or x5 (i.e., not a return). A insn:c.jr[] instruction where rs1 is not x1 or x5 (i.e., not a return) is an indirect jump.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_enc
normative_rules.text:
The insn:lpad[] instruction (See <<LP_INST>>) is
encoded using the insn:auipc[] major opcode with rd=x0.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_expected
normative_rules.text: The ext:zicfilp[] extension, when enabled, determines if an indirect call or an indirect jump must land on a landing pad, as specified in . If is_lp_expected is 1, then the hart updates the csr::[elp] to LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_indirect_branch_lpad
normative_rules.text: An indirect branch using insn:jalr[], insn:c.jalr[], or insn:c.jr[] with rs1 as x7 is termed a software-guarded branch. Such branches do not need to land on a insn:lpad[] instruction and thus do not set csr::[elp] to LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_label
normative_rules.text:
To support labeled landing pads, the
indirect call/jump sites establish an expected landing pad label (e.g., using
the insn:lui[] instruction) in the bits 31:12 of the x7 register.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_imm_enc
normative_rules.text:
The insn:lpad[] instruction is encoded with a
20-bit immediate value called the landing-pad-label (LPL) that is matched to
the expected landing pad label. When LPL is encoded as zero, the
insn:lpad[] instruction does not perform the label check and in programs
built with this single label mode of operation the indirect call/jump sites do
not need to establish an expected landing pad label value in x7.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_elp_lpad_expected
normative_rules.text: When csr::[elp] is set to LP_EXPECTED, if the next instruction in the instruction stream is not 4-byte aligned, or is not insn:lpad[], or if the landing pad label encoded in insn:lpad[] is not zero and does not match the expected landing pad label in bits 31:12 of the x7 register, then a software-check exception (cause=18) with xtval set to landing pad fault (code=2) is raised else the csr::[elp] is updated to NO_LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_enabled_instr_allowed
normative_rules.text:
When ext:zicfilp[] is enabled, insn:lpad[] is the only instruction allowed to execute when
the csr::[elp] state is LP_EXPECTED. If ext:zicfilp[] is not enabled then the instruction
is a no-op.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_enabled_exception
normative_rules.text:
If ext:zicfilp[] is enabled, the insn:lpad[] instruction causes a
software-check exception with xtval set to landing pad fault (code=2)

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_alignment_exception
normative_rules.text: The pc is not 4-byte aligned and csr::[elp] is LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_label_exception
normative_rules.text: The csr::[elp] is LP_EXPECTED and the LPL is not zero and the LPL does not match the expected landing pad label in bits 31:12 of the x7 register.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_lpad_no_sw_exception
normative_rules.text: If a software-check exception is not caused then the csr::[elp] is updated to NO_LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_enc
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zicfiss[] instructions, except insn:ssamoswap.w[] and insn:ssamoswap.d[], are encoded using a subset of
May-Be-Operation instructions defined by the ext:zimop[] and ext:zcmop[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_sspush_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:sspush[x1] and insn:sspush[x5] - encoded using insn:mop.rr.7[]

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_c-sspush_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:c.sspush[x1] - encoded using insn:c.mop.1[]

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_sspopchk_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:sspopchk[x1] and insn:sspopchk[x5] - encoded using insn:mop.r.28[]

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_c-sspopchk_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:c.sspopchk[x5] - encoded using insn:c.mop.5[]

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_ssrdp_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:ssrdp[] - encoded using insn:mop.r.28[]

normative_rules.name: ssp_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:ssp[] CSR is an unprivileged read-write (URW) CSR that reads and writes
XLEN low order bits of the shadow stack pointer.

normative_rules.name: ssp_addr
normative_rules.text:
The CSR address is
0x011.

normative_rules.name: ssp_sz
normative_rules.text:
There is no high CSR defined as the csr:ssp[] is always as wide as the XLEN
of the current privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: ssp_field_1_0
normative_rules.text:
The bits 1:0 of csr:ssp[] are read-only zero. If the
UXLEN or SXLEN may never be 32, then the bit 2 is also read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: ss_push
normative_rules.text: A shadow stack push operation is defined as decrement of the csr:ssp[] by XLEN/8 followed by a store of the value in the link register to memory at the new top of the shadow stack.

normative_rules.name: sspush_c-sspush_instr
normative_rules.text: The insn:sspush[] instruction and its compressed form insn:c.sspush[] can be used to push a link register on the shadow stack. The insn:sspush[] and insn:c.sspush[] instructions perform a store identically to the existing store instructions, with the difference that the base is implicitly csr:ssp[] and the width is implicitly XLEN.

normative_rules.name: sspush_c-sspush_decrement
normative_rules.text: The csr:ssp[] is decremented by insn:sspush[] and insn:c.sspush[] only if the store to the shadow stack completes successfully.

normative_rules.name: ss_pop
normative_rules.text: A shadow stack pop operation is defined as an XLEN wide read from the current top of the shadow stack followed by an increment of the csr:ssp[] by XLEN/8.

normative_rules.name: sspopchk_shadow_return_pop
normative_rules.text: The insn:sspopchk[] instruction, and its compressed form insn:c.sspopchk[], can be used to pop the shadow return address value from the shadow stack and check that the value matches the contents of the link register, and if not cause a software-check exception with xtval set to shadow stack fault (code=3).

normative_rules.name: sspopchk_load_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:sspopchk[] and insn:c.sspopchk[] instructions perform a load identically to the existing load instructions, with the difference that the base is implicitly csr:ssp[] and the width is implicitly XLEN.

normative_rules.name: sspop_exception
normative_rules.text: If the value loaded from the address in csr:ssp[] does not match the value in rs1, a software-check exception (cause=18) is raised with xtval set to shadow stack fault (code=3). The software-check exception caused by insn:sspopchk[] or insn:c.sspopchk[] is lower in priority than a load/store/AMO access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: sspop_increment
normative_rules.text: The csr:ssp[] is incremented by insn:sspopchk[] and insn:c.sspopchk[] only if the load from the shadow stack completes successfully and no software-check exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: ssrdp_read
normative_rules.text: The insn:ssrdp[] instruction is provided to move the contents of csr:ssp[] to a destination register.

normative_rules.name: rv32_ssamoswap-w_op
normative_rules.text: For RV32, insn:ssamoswap.w[] atomically loads a 32-bit data value from address of a shadow stack location in rs1, puts the loaded value into register rd, and stores the 32-bit value held in rs2 to the original address in rs1. insn:ssamoswap.d[] (RV64 only) is similar to insn:ssamoswap.w[] but operates on 64-bit data values.

normative_rules.name: rv64_ssamoswap-w_op
normative_rules.text: For RV64, insn:ssamoswap.w[] atomically loads a 32-bit data value from address of a shadow stack location in rs1, sign-extends the loaded value and puts it in rd, and stores the lower 32 bits of the value held in rs2 to the original address in rs1.

normative_rules.name: ssamoswap_address
normative_rules.text: Just as for AMOs in the ext:a[] extension, insn:ssamoswap.w[] or insn:ssamoswap.d[] requires that the address held in rs1 be naturally aligned to the size of the operand (i.e., 8-byte aligned for doublewords, and 4-byte aligned for words). The same exception options apply if the address is not naturally aligned.

normative_rules.name: ntl_target_definition
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl[] instructions do not change architectural state, nor do they alter the
architecturally visible effects of the target instruction.

normative_rules.name: ntl-p1_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl.p1[] instruction indicates that the target instruction does not
exhibit temporal locality within the capacity of the innermost level of
private cache in the memory hierarchy.

normative_rules.name: ntl-p1_enc
normative_rules.text:
insn:ntl.p1[] is encoded as
insn:add[x0,x0,x2].

normative_rules.name: ntl-pall_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl.pall[] instruction indicates that the target instruction does not
exhibit temporal locality within the capacity of any level of private
cache in the memory hierarchy.

normative_rules.name: ntl-pall_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:ntl.pall[] is encoded as insn:add[x0,x0,x3].

normative_rules.name: ntl-s1_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl.s1[] instruction indicates that the target instruction does not
exhibit temporal locality within the capacity of the innermost level of
shared cache in the memory hierarchy.

normative_rules.name: ntl-s1_enc
normative_rules.text:
insn:ntl.s1[] is encoded as
insn:add[x0,x0,x4].

normative_rules.name: ntl-all_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl.all[] instruction indicates that the target instruction does not
exhibit temporal locality within the capacity of any level of cache in
the memory hierarchy.

normative_rules.name: ntl-all_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:ntl.all[] is encoded as insn:add[x0,x0,x5].

normative_rules.name: ntl_compressed_variants
normative_rules.text:
If the ext:c[] or ext:zca[] extension is provided, compressed variants of these HINTs are
also provided: insn:c.ntl.p1[] is encoded as insn:c.add[x0,x2]; insn:c.ntl.pall[] is
encoded as insn:c.add[x0,x3]; insn:c.ntl.s1[] is encoded as insn:c.add[x0,x4]; and
insn:c.ntl.all[] is encoded as insn:c.add[x0,x5].

normative_rules.name: ntl_range
normative_rules.text:
The insn:ntl[] instructions affect all memory-access instructions except the
cache-management instructions in the ext:zicbom[] extension.

normative_rules.name: ntl_Zicbop_prefetch_outer
normative_rules.text:
When an insn:ntl[] instruction is applied to a
prefetch hint in the ext:zicbop[] extension, it indicates that a cache line
should be prefetched into a cache that is outer from the level specified by
the insn:ntl[].

normative_rules.name: ntl_trap_behavior
normative_rules.text:
In the event that a trap is taken on the target instruction,
implementations are discouraged from applying the insn:ntl[] to the first
instruction in the trap handler. Instead, implementations are
recommended to ignore the HINT in this case.

normative_rules.name: pause_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:pause[] instruction is a HINT that indicates the current hart's rate
of instruction retirement should be temporarily reduced or paused. The
duration of its effect must be bounded and may be zero.

normative_rules.name: pause_enc_fence
normative_rules.text:
insn:pause[] is encoded as a insn:fence[] instruction with pred=W, succ=0, fm=0,
rd=x0, and rs1=x0.

normative_rules.name: cache_block_size
normative_rules.text:
The capacity and organization of a cache and
the size of a cache block are both implementation-specific, and

normative_rules.name: cache_block_discovery
normative_rules.text:
the execution
environment provides software a means to discover information about the caches
and cache blocks in a system.

normative_rules.name: cache_block_size_uniform
normative_rules.text:
In the initial set of CMO extensions, the size of
a cache block shall be uniform throughout the system.

normative_rules.name: ppo_overlap_1
normative_rules.text:
if a precedes b in program order,
then a will precede b in the global memory order if:

normative_rules.name: ppo_overlap_2
normative_rules.text:
a is an invalidate, clean, or flush, b is a load, and a and b access
overlapping memory addresses

normative_rules.name: invalidate_load_val_no_preceding_cmo
normative_rules.text:
If no clean or flush operations on x precede i in the global memory order,
either the initial value of x or the value of any store to x that precedes
i

normative_rules.name: invalidate_load_val_no_store_before_cmo
normative_rules.text:
If no store to x precedes a clean or flush operation on x in the global
memory order and if the clean or flush operation on x precedes i in the
global memory order, either the initial value of x or the value of any store
to x that precedes i

normative_rules.name: invalidate_load_val_store_before_cmo
normative_rules.text:
If a store to x precedes a clean or flush operation on x in the global
memory order and if the clean or flush operation on x precedes i in the
global memory order, either the value of the latest store to x that precedes
the latest clean or flush operation on x or the value of any store to x
that both precedes i and succeeds the latest clean or flush operation on x
that precedes i

normative_rules.name: invalidate_load_val_noncoherent_store
normative_rules.text:
The value of any store to x by a non-coherent agent regardless of the above
conditions

normative_rules.name: pmp_same
normative_rules.text:
The PMP access control bits shall be the same for all physical addresses in
the cache block, and if write permission is granted by the PMP access control
bits, read permission shall also be granted

normative_rules.name: pma_same
normative_rules.text:
The PMAs shall be the same for all physical addresses in the cache block,
and if write permission is granted by the supported access type PMAs, read
permission shall also be granted

normative_rules.name: cbo_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If the above constraints are not met, the behavior of a CBO instruction is
UNSPECIFIED.

normative_rules.name: cbm_access
normative_rules.text:
A cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the specified cache
block whenever a load instruction or store instruction is permitted to access
the corresponding physical addresses.

normative_rules.name: cbm_unperm_fault
normative_rules.text:
If
access to the cache block is not permitted, a cache-block management instruction
raises a store page-fault or store guest-page-fault exception if address
translation does not permit any access or raises a store access-fault exception
otherwise.

normative_rules.name: cbm_unperm_translate
normative_rules.text:
During address translation, the instruction also checks the accessed
bit and may either raise an exception or set the bit as required.

normative_rules.name: cbz_access
normative_rules.text:
A cache-block zero instruction is permitted to access the specified cache block
whenever a store instruction is permitted to access the corresponding physical
addresses and when the PMAs indicate that cache-block zero instructions are a
supported access type.

normative_rules.name: cbz_unperm_fault
normative_rules.text:
If access to the cache block is not permitted, a
cache-block zero instruction raises a store page-fault or store guest-page-fault
exception if address translation does not permit write access or raises a store
access-fault exception otherwise.

normative_rules.name: cbz_unperm_translate
normative_rules.text:
During address translation, the instruction
also checks the accessed and dirty bits and may either raise an exception or set
the bits as required.

normative_rules.name: cbp_access
normative_rules.text:
A cache-block prefetch instruction is permitted to access the specified cache
block whenever a load instruction, store instruction, or instruction fetch is
permitted to access the corresponding physical addresses.

normative_rules.name: cbp_unperm_noexcep
normative_rules.text:
If access to the cache
block is not permitted, a cache-block prefetch instruction does not raise any
exceptions and shall not access any caches or memory.

normative_rules.name: cbp_unperm_translate
normative_rules.text:
During address
translation, the instruction does not check the accessed and dirty bits and
neither raises an exception nor sets the bits.

normative_rules.name: fault_excep_csr
normative_rules.text:
When a page-fault, guest-page-fault, or access-fault exception is taken, the
relevant *tval CSR is written with the faulting effective address (i.e. the
value of rs1).

normative_rules.name: no_addr_misaligned_excep
normative_rules.text: CMO instructions do not generate address-misaligned exceptions.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval
normative_rules.text: A insn:cbo.inval[] instruction executes or raises either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the csr:envcfg[cbie] fields:

normative_rules.name: cbo-clean_cbo-flush
normative_rules.text: A insn:cbo.clean[] or insn:cbo.flush[] instruction executes or raises an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the csr:envcfg[cbcfe] bits:

normative_rules.name: cbo-zero_basedon_xenvcfg_cbze
normative_rules.text: Finally, a insn:cbo.zero[] instruction executes or raises an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception based on the state of the csr:envcfg[cbze] bits:

normative_rules.name: cbxe_unaffected
normative_rules.text: The csr::[cbie]/csr::[cbcfe]/csr::[cbze] fields in each csr:envcfg[] register do not affect the read and write behavior of the same fields in the other csr:envcfg[] registers.

normative_rules.name: cbo-zero_specified_block
normative_rules.text:
These instructions operate on the cache block, or the memory locations
corresponding to the cache block, whose effective address is specified in rs1.

normative_rules.name: prefetch_operating_block
normative_rules.text:
These instructions operate on the cache block whose effective address is the sum
of the base address specified in rs1 and the sign-extended offset encoded in
imm[11:0], where imm[4:0] shall equal 0b00000.

normative_rules.name: cbo-clean_op
normative_rules.text:
A insn:cbo.clean[] instruction performs a clean operation on the cache block whose
effective address is the base address specified in rs1.

normative_rules.name: cbo-flush_op
normative_rules.text:
A insn:cbo.flush[] instruction performs a flush operation on the cache block
that contains the address specified in rs1.

normative_rules.name: cbo-flush_unaligned
normative_rules.text:
It is not required that rs1 is
aligned to the size of a cache block.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_op
normative_rules.text:
A insn:cbo.inval[] instruction performs an invalidate operation on the cache block
that contains the address specified in rs1.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_unaligned
normative_rules.text:
It is not required that rs1 is
aligned to the size of a cache block.

normative_rules.name: cbo-zero_op
normative_rules.text:
A insn:cbo.zero[] instruction performs stores of zeros to the full set of bytes
corresponding to the cache block that contains the address specified in rs1.

normative_rules.name: cbo-zero_unaligned
normative_rules.text: It is not required that rs1 is aligned to the size of a cache block.

normative_rules.name: prefetch-i_op
normative_rules.text: A insn:prefetch.i[] instruction indicates to hardware that the cache block whose effective address is the sum of the base address specified in rs1 and the sign-extended offset encoded in imm[11:0], where imm[4:0] equals 0b00000, is likely to be accessed by an instruction fetch in the near future.

normative_rules.name: prefetch-r_op
normative_rules.text: A insn:prefetch.r[] instruction indicates to hardware that the cache block whose effective address is the sum of the base address specified in rs1 and the sign-extended offset encoded in imm[11:0], where imm[4:0] equals 0b00000, is likely to be accessed by a data read (i.e. load) in the near future.

normative_rules.name: prefetch-w_op
normative_rules.text: A insn:prefetch.w[] instruction indicates to hardware that the cache block whose effective address is the sum of the base address specified in rs1 and the sign-extended offset encoded in imm[11:0], where imm[4:0] equals 0b00000, is likely to be accessed by a data write (i.e. store) in the near future.

normative_rules.name: A_aq_rl_bits
normative_rules.text:
each atomic
instruction has two bits, aq and rl, used to specify additional
memory ordering constraints as viewed by other RISC-V harts.

normative_rules.name: A_domain_specific_ordering
normative_rules.text:
The bits
order accesses to one of the two address domains, memory or I/O,
depending on which address domain the atomic instruction is accessing.
No ordering constraint is implied to accesses to the other domain, and a
insn:fence[] instruction should be used to order across both domains.

normative_rules.name: A_no_aq_rl
normative_rules.text:
If both bits are clear, no additional ordering constraints
are imposed on the atomic memory operation.

normative_rules.name: A_acquire_semantics
normative_rules.text:
If only the aq bit is set, the atomic
memory operation is treated as an acquire access, i.e., no following
memory operations on this RISC-V hart can be observed to take place
before the acquire memory operation.

normative_rules.name: A_release_semantics
normative_rules.text:
If only the rl bit is set, the
atomic memory operation is treated as a release access, i.e., the
release memory operation cannot be observed to take place before any
earlier memory operations on this RISC-V hart.

normative_rules.name: A_seq_cst_semantics
normative_rules.text:
If both the aq and rl
bits are set, the atomic memory operation is sequentially consistent
and cannot be observed to happen before any earlier memory operations or
after any later memory operations in the same RISC-V hart and to the
same address domain.

normative_rules.name: A_comprises
normative_rules.text:
The ext:a[] extension comprises the extlink:zalrsc[] and extlink:zaamo[] extensions,
which are defined in the following sections.

normative_rules.name: lr-w_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:lr.w[] loads a word from the address in rs1, places the
sign-extended value in rd, and registers a reservation set: a set of
bytes that subsumes the bytes in the addressed word.

normative_rules.name: sc-w_success
normative_rules.text:
insn:sc.w[] conditionally
writes a word in rs2 to the address in rs1: the insn:sc.w[] succeeds only
if the reservation is still valid and the reservation set contains the
bytes being written. If the insn:sc.w[] succeeds, the instruction writes the
word in rs2 to memory, and it writes zero to rd.

normative_rules.name: sc-w_failure
normative_rules.text:
If the insn:sc.w[] fails,
the instruction does not write to memory, and it writes a nonzero value
to rd.

normative_rules.name: sc_retire_permission
normative_rules.text: No insn:sc.w[] instruction shall retire unless it passes memory permission checks,

normative_rules.name: sc_failed_side_effects
normative_rules.text:
but it is UNSPECIFIED whether any side effects of implicit address translation
and protection memory accesses (such as setting a page-table entry D bit)
occur on a failed insn:sc.w[].

normative_rules.name: sc_failed_as_store
normative_rules.text:
For the purposes of memory protection, a failed insn:sc.w[] may be
treated like a store.

normative_rules.name: sc_reservation_invalidate
normative_rules.text:
Regardless of success or failure, executing an
insn:sc.w[] instruction invalidates any reservation held by this hart.

normative_rules.name: lr_sc_rv64
normative_rules.text:
insn:lr.d[] and
insn:sc.d[] act analogously on doublewords and are only available on RV64. For
RV64, insn:lr.w[] and insn:sc.w[] sign-extend the value placed in rd.

normative_rules.name: sc_failure_code
normative_rules.text:
The failure code with value 1 encodes an unspecified failure. Other
failure codes are reserved at this time. Portable software should only
assume the failure code will be non-zero.

normative_rules.name: lr_sc_alignment
normative_rules.text:
For insn:lr[] and insn:sc[], the ext:zalrsc[] extension requires that the address held in rs1
be naturally aligned to the size of the operand (i.e., eight-byte
aligned for doublewords and four-byte aligned for words). If the
address is not naturally aligned, an address-misaligned exception or an
access-fault exception will be generated. The access-fault exception can
be generated for a memory access that would otherwise be able to
complete except for the misalignment, if the misaligned access should
not be emulated.

normative_rules.name: lr_reservation_set_size
normative_rules.text:
An implementation can register an arbitrarily large reservation set on
each insn:lr[], provided the reservation set includes all bytes of the
addressed data word or doubleword.

normative_rules.name: sc_pairs_latest_lr
normative_rules.text:
An insn:sc[] can only pair with the most
recent insn:lr[] in program order.

normative_rules.name: sc_success_conditions
normative_rules.text:
An insn:sc[] may succeed only if no store from
another hart to the reservation set can be observed to have occurred
between the insn:lr[] and the insn:sc[], and if there is no other insn:sc[] between the
insn:lr[] and itself in program order.

normative_rules.name: sc_device_write_failure
normative_rules.text:
An insn:sc[] may succeed only if no write from a
device other than a hart to the bytes accessed by the insn:lr[] instruction can
be observed to have occurred between the insn:lr[] and insn:sc[].

normative_rules.name: sc_addr_not_in_reservation_fail
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sc[] must fail if the address is not within the reservation set of the
most recent insn:lr[] in program order.

normative_rules.name: sc_other_hart_store_fail
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sc[] must fail if a store to the
reservation set from another hart can be observed to occur between the
insn:lr[] and insn:sc[].

normative_rules.name: sc_other_device_write_fail
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sc[] must fail if a write from some other device to the
bytes accessed by the insn:lr[] can be observed to occur between the insn:lr[] and insn:sc[].

normative_rules.name: sc_intervening_sc_fail
normative_rules.text:
An insn:sc[] must fail
if there is another insn:sc[] (to any address) between the insn:lr[] and the insn:sc[] in
program order.

normative_rules.name: lr_sc_atomicity_axiom
normative_rules.text:
The precise statement of the atomicity requirements for
successful insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequences is defined by the Atomicity Axiom in
<<rvwmo>>.

normative_rules.name: sc_not_observable_before_lr
normative_rules.text:
An insn:sc[] instruction can never be observed by another RISC-V hart before
the insn:lr[] instruction that established the reservation.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_loop_size
normative_rules.text:
The loop comprises only an insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequence and code to retry the
sequence in the case of failure, and must comprise at most 16
instructions placed sequentially in memory.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_instruction_set
normative_rules.text:
An insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequence begins with an insn:lr[] instruction and ends with an
insn:sc[] instruction. The dynamic code executed between the insn:lr[] and
insn:sc[] instructions can only contain instructions from the
ext:i[] or ext:e[] base instruction set, excluding loads, stores, backward jumps, taken backward
branches, insn:jalr[], insn:fence[], and insn:system[] instructions.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_compressed_allowed
normative_rules.text:
Compressed forms of the aforementioned ext:i[] or ext:e[] instructions in the
ext:c[] (hence ext:zca[]) and ext:zcb[] extensions are also permitted.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_retry_code
normative_rules.text:
The code to retry a failing insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequence can contain backwards jumps
and/or branches to repeat the insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequence, but otherwise has the same
constraint as the code between the insn:lr[] and insn:sc[].

normative_rules.name: lrsc_eventuality_region
normative_rules.text:
The insn:lr[] and insn:sc[] addresses must lie within a memory region with the
insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] eventuality property. The execution environment is responsible
for communicating which regions have this property.

normative_rules.name: lrsc_same_address_and_size
normative_rules.text:
The insn:sc[] must be to the same effective address and of the same data size
as the latest insn:lr[] executed by the same hart.

normative_rules.name: unconstrained_lrsc_no_progress
normative_rules.text:
insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequences that do not lie within constrained insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] loops are
unconstrained. Unconstrained insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] sequences might succeed on some
attempts on some implementations, but might never succeed on other
implementations.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_forward_progress_intro
normative_rules.text:
If a hart H enters a constrained insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] loop, the execution environment
must guarantee that one of the following events eventually occurs

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_forward_progress_sc
normative_rules.text:
H or some other hart executes a successful insn:sc[] to the reservation set
of the insn:lr[] instruction in H's constrained insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] loops.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_forward_progress_store_amo
normative_rules.text:
Some other hart executes an unconditional store or AMO instruction to
the reservation set of the insn:lr[] instruction in H's constrained
insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] loop, or some other device in the system writes to that reservation set.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_forward_progress_branch
normative_rules.text: H executes a branch or jump that exits the constrained insn:lr[]/insn:sc[] loop.

normative_rules.name: constrained_lrsc_forward_progress_trap
normative_rules.text: H traps.

normative_rules.name: Za128rs_res_set_req
normative_rules.text: The ext:za128rs[] extension requires that the reservation sets used by the instructions in the ext:zalrsc[] extension be contiguous, naturally aligned, and at most 128 bytes in size.

normative_rules.name: Za64rs_res_set_req
normative_rules.text: The ext:za64rs[] extension requires that the reservation sets used by the instructions in the ext:zalrsc[] extension be contiguous, naturally aligned, and at most 64 bytes in size.

normative_rules.name: Za64rs_implies_Za128rs
normative_rules.text: The ext:za64rs[] extension implies the ext:za128rs[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_wrs-nto_stall_exec
normative_rules.text:
The insn:wrs.nto[] and insn:wrs.sto[] instructions cause the hart to temporarily stall
execution in a low-power state as long as the reservation set is valid and no
locally enabled interrupts at any privilege level are pending,
regardless of the global interrupt enable at each privilege level.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_wrs-sto_stall_duration
normative_rules.text:
For insn:wrs.sto[] the stall
duration is bounded by an implementation defined short timeout.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_all_priv_modes
normative_rules.text:
These
instructions are available in all privilege modes.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_stall_terminate
normative_rules.text:
While stalled, an implementation is permitted to occasionally terminate the
stall and complete execution for any reason.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_exec_resume_rules
normative_rules.text:
insn:wrs.nto[] and insn:wrs.sto[] instructions follow the rules of the insn:wfi[] instruction
for resuming execution on a locally enabled pending interrupt.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_priv_illegal_instr_excp
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[tw] (timeout wait) bit in csr:mstatus[] is set and insn:wrs.nto[] is executed
in any privilege mode other than M-mode, and it does not complete within an
implementation-specific bounded time limit, the insn:wrs.nto[] instruction will cause
an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Zawrs_virtual_instr_excp
normative_rules.text:
When executing in VS- or VU-mode, if the csr::[vtw] bit is set in csr:hstatus[], the
csr::[tw] bit in csr:mstatus[] is clear, and the insn:wrs.nto[] does not complete within an
implementation-specific bounded time limit, the insn:wrs.nto[] instruction will cause
a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: amo_op
normative_rules.text:
These AMO instructions atomically load a data
value from the address in rs1, place the value into register rd,
apply a binary operator to the loaded value and the original value in
rs2, then store the result back to the original address in rs1.

normative_rules.name: amo_operand_size
normative_rules.text:
AMOs
can either operate on doublewords (RV64 only) or words in memory. For
RV64, 32-bit AMOs always sign-extend the value placed in rd, and
ignore the upper 32 bits of the original value of rs2.

normative_rules.name: amo_alignment
normative_rules.text:
For AMOs, the ext:zaamo[] extension requires that the address held in rs1 be
naturally aligned to the size of the operand (i.e., eight-byte aligned
for doublewords and four-byte aligned for words).

normative_rules.name: misaligned_atomicity_granule_size
normative_rules.text:
The misaligned atomicity granule PMA, defined in <<sec:misaligned-atomicity-granule>>,
optionally relaxes this alignment requirement.
If present, the misaligned atomicity granule PMA specifies the size
of a misaligned atomicity granule, a power-of-two number of bytes.
The misaligned atomicity granule PMA applies only to
AMOs defined in the ext:zaamo[], ext:zabha[], and ext:zacas[] extensions;
loads and stores
defined in the base ISAs; loads and stores of no more than XLEN bits
defined in the ext:f[], ext:d[], and ext:q[] extensions; the load-acquire and
store-release instructions defined in the ext:zalasr[] extension; and compressed
encodings of the foregoing loads and stores.
For an instruction in that set, if all accessed bytes lie within the same
misaligned atomicity granule, the instruction will not raise an exception for
reasons of address alignment, and the instruction will give rise to only one
memory operation for the purposes of RVWMO--i.e., it will execute atomically.

normative_rules.name: amo_ops_supported
normative_rules.text:
The operations supported are swap, integer add, bitwise AND, bitwise OR,
bitwise XOR, and signed and unsigned integer maximum and minimum.

normative_rules.name: amo_release_consistency
normative_rules.text:
If the aq bit is set, then no
later memory operations in this RISC-V hart can be observed to take
place before the AMO. Conversely, if the rl bit is set, then other
RISC-V harts will not observe the AMO before memory accesses preceding
the AMO in this RISC-V hart. Setting both the aq and the rl bit on
an AMO makes the sequence sequentially consistent, meaning that it
cannot be reordered with earlier or later memory operations from the
same hart.

normative_rules.name: Zalasr_signext_rd
normative_rules.text: The ext:zalasr[] instructions always sign-extend the value placed in rd

normative_rules.name: Zalasr_ignore_rs2_upper
normative_rules.text: ignore the upper bits of the value of rs2.
