normative_rules.name: Zalasr_natural_align
normative_rules.text: The instructions in the ext:zalasr[] extension require that the address held in rs1 be naturally aligned to the size in bytes (2^width^) of the operand.

normative_rules.name: Zalasr_misaligned_exception
normative_rules.text: If the address is not naturally aligned, an address-misaligned exception or an access-fault exception will be generated.

normative_rules.name: Zalasr_misaligned_pma_relax
normative_rules.text: The misaligned atomicity granule PMA, defined in <<sec:misaligned-atomicity-granule>>, optionally relaxes this alignment requirement.

normative_rules.name: Zalasr_misaligned_single_op
normative_rules.text: If all accessed bytes lie within the same misaligned atomicity granule, the instruction will not raise an exception for reasons of address alignment, and the instruction will give rise to only one memory operation for the purposes of RVWMO--i.e., it will execute atomically.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_atomic_load_enc
normative_rules.text: Encoding

normative_rules.name: ldaq_atomic_load_op
normative_rules.text: This instruction loads 2^width^ bytes of memory from rs1 atomically and writes the result into rd.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_signext_rule
normative_rules.text: If the size (2^width+3^) is less than XLEN, it is sign-extended to fill the destination register.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_aq_required
normative_rules.text: This load must have the ordering annotation aq

normative_rules.name: ldaq_rl_optional
normative_rules.text: may have ordering annotation rl encoded in the instruction.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_rcsc_semantics
normative_rules.text: The instruction always has an acquire-RCsc annotation, and if the bit rl is set the instruction has a release-RCsc annotation.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_no_aq_reserved
normative_rules.text: The versions without the aq bit set are RESERVED.

normative_rules.name: ldaq_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:ld.{aq,aqrl}[] is RV64-only.

normative_rules.name: sdrl_atomic_store_enc
normative_rules.text: Encoding

normative_rules.name: sdrl_atomic_store_op
normative_rules.text: This instruction stores 2^width^ bytes from rs2 to memory at the address in rs1 atomically.

normative_rules.name: sdrl_rl_required
normative_rules.text: This store must have ordering annotation rl

normative_rules.name: sdrl_aq_optional
normative_rules.text: may have ordering annotation aq encoded in the instruction.

normative_rules.name: sdrl_rcsc_semantics
normative_rules.text: The instruction always has a release-RCsc annotation, and if the bit aq is set the instruction has an acquire-RCsc annotation.

normative_rules.name: sdrl_no_rl_reserved
normative_rules.text: The versions without the rl bit set are RESERVED.

normative_rules.name: sdrl_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:sd.{rl,aqrl}[] is RV64-only.

normative_rules.name: Zabha_rd_sign_extension
normative_rules.text:
Byte and halfword AMOs always sign-extend the value placed in rd, and ignore
the 0 bits of the original value in rs2.

normative_rules.name: Zabha_amocas-bh_ignore_bits
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:amocas.b/h[] instructions similarly ignore the 1
bits of the original value in rd.

normative_rules.name: Zabha_rs1_align_addr
normative_rules.text:
Similar to the AMOs specified in the ext:zaamo[] extension, the ext:zabha[] extension mandates
that the address contained in the rs1 register must be naturally aligned to
the size of the operand.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv32_amocas-w_op
normative_rules.text:
For RV32, insn:amocas.w[] atomically loads a 32-bit data value from address in rs1,
compares the loaded value to the 32-bit value held in rd, and if the comparison
is bitwise equal, then stores the 32-bit value held in rs2 to the original
address in rs1. The value loaded from memory is placed into register rd.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv32_amocas-d_op
normative_rules.text:
For RV32, insn:amocas.d[] atomically loads 64-bits of a data value from address in
rs1, compares the loaded value to a 64-bit value held in a register pair
consisting of rd and rd+1, and if the comparison is bitwise equal, then
stores the 64-bit value held in the register pair rs2 and rs2+1 to the
original address in rs1. The value loaded from memory is placed into the
register pair rd and rd+1.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv32_amocas-d_frst_pair_entry_reg_even
normative_rules.text:
The instruction requires the first register in
the pair to be even numbered; encodings with odd numbered registers specified
in rs2 and rd are reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv32_amocas-d_rs2_frst_reg_x0
normative_rules.text:
When the first register of a source register
pair is x0, then both halves of the pair read as zero.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv32_amocas-d_rd_frst_reg_x0
normative_rules.text:
When the first
register of a destination register pair is x0, then the entire register
result is discarded and neither destination register is written.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-w_op
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, insn:amocas.w[] atomically loads a 32-bit data value from address in
rs1, compares the loaded value to the lower 32 bits of the value held in rd,
and if the comparison is bitwise equal, then stores the lower 32 bits of the
value held in rs2 to the original address in rs1. The 32-bit value loaded
from memory is sign-extended and is placed into register rd.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-d_op
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, insn:amocas.d[] atomically loads 64-bits of a data value from address in
rs1, compares the loaded value to a 64-bit value held in rd, and if the
comparison is bitwise equal, then stores the 64-bit value held in rs2 to the
original address in rs1. The value loaded from memory is placed into register
rd.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-q_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:amocas.q[] (RV64 only) atomically loads 128-bits of a data value from address in
rs1, compares the loaded value to a 128-bit value held in a register pair
consisting of rd and rd+1, and if the comparison is bitwise equal, then
stores the 128-bit value held in the register pair rs2 and rs2+1 to the
original address in rs1. The value loaded from memory is placed into the
register pair rd and rd+1.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-q_frst_pair_entry_reg_even
normative_rules.text:
The instruction requires the first register in
the pair to be even numbered; encodings with odd numbered registers specified in
rs2 and rd are reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-q_rs2_frst_reg_x0
normative_rules.text:
When the first register of a source register pair
is x0, then both halves of the pair read as zero.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_rv64_amocas-q_rd_frst_reg_x0
normative_rules.text:
When the first register of a
destination register pair is x0, then the entire register result is discarded
and neither destination register is written.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_amocas_rs1_addr_alignment
normative_rules.text:
insn:amocas.w/d/q[] requires that the address
held in rs1 be naturally aligned to the size of the operand (i.e., 16-byte
aligned for quadwords, eight-byte aligned for doublewords, and four-byte
aligned for words).

normative_rules.name: Zacas_amocas_mem_op_success_aq_rl
normative_rules.text:
The memory operation performed by an
insn:amocas.w/d/q[], when successful, has acquire semantics if aq bit is 1 and has
release semantics if rl bit is 1.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_amocas_mem_op_fail_aq_rl
normative_rules.text:
The memory operation performed by an
insn:amocas.w/d/q[], when not successful, has acquire semantics if aq bit is 1 but
does not have release semantics, regardless of rl.

normative_rules.name: Zacas_amocas_w_permission
normative_rules.text: An insn:amocas.w/d/q[] instruction always requires write permissions.

normative_rules.name: Zama16b_mag
Zama16b_atomic_ops
normative_rules.text:
Misaligned loads, stores and AMOs to those regions that do not cross a naturally
aligned 16-byte boundary are atomic.

normative_rules.name: flen_def
normative_rules.text:
FLEN can be 32, 64, or 128 depending on which of the ext:f[], ext:d[], and
ext:q[] extensions are supported.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_Zdinx_incompatible_F_D
normative_rules.text:
These extensions,
intended for lower-cost systems, are incompatible with the ext:f[] and ext:d[]
extensions.

normative_rules.name: F_ieee_compliance
normative_rules.text:
computational instructions
compliant with the IEEE 754-2008 arithmetic standard's binary32 format and
operations.

normative_rules.name: F_depends_Zicsr
normative_rules.text:
The ext:f[] extension depends on the
ext:zicsr[] extension.

normative_rules.name: flen
normative_rules.text:
The ext:f[] extension adds 32 floating-point registers,
f0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;f31, each 32 bits wide, i.e., FLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: fcsr_op_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: The floating-point CSR, csr:fcsr[], is a 32-bit read/write register that selects the dynamic rounding mode for floating-point arithmetic operations and holds the accrued exception flags, as shown in .

normative_rules.name: frm_op_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The csr:frm[] CSR contains the Rounding Mode field
(csr:fcsr[] bits 7&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;5), zero-extended.

normative_rules.name: fflags_op_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The csr:fflags[] CSR contains the Accrued Exception
Flags field (csr:fcsr[] bits 4&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;0), zero-extended.

normative_rules.name: fcsr_rsv
normative_rules.text: Bits 31‍–‍8 of the csr:fcsr[] are reserved for other standard extensions. If these extensions are not present, implementations shall ignore writes to these bits and supply a zero value when read. Standard software should preserve the contents of these bits.

normative_rules.name: roundingmode_dynamic
normative_rules.text:
Floating-point operations use either a static rounding mode encoded in
the instruction, or a dynamic rounding mode held in frm. Rounding
modes are encoded as shown in <<norm:dyn_round_enc>>. A value of 111 in the
instruction's rm field selects the dynamic rounding mode held in
frm

normative_rules.name: roundingmode_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The behavior of floating-point instructions that depend on
rounding mode when executed with a reserved rounding mode is reserved, including both static reserved rounding modes (101&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;110) and dynamic reserved rounding modes (101&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;111).

normative_rules.name: roundingmode_unaffected_rm_decode
normative_rules.text:
Some instructions, including widening conversions, have the rm field but are nevertheless mathematically unaffected by the rounding mode; software should set their rm field to
RNE (000) but implementations must treat the rm field as usual (in
particular, with regard to decoding legal vs. reserved encodings).

normative_rules.name: dyn_round_enc
normative_rules.text:
Rounding Mode|Mnemonic|Meaning
===
000|RNE|Round to Nearest, ties to Even¶001|RTZ|Round towards Zero¶010|RDN|Round Down (towards −∞)¶011|RUP|Round Up (towards +∞)¶100|RMM|Round to Nearest, ties to Max Magnitude¶101||Reserved for future use.¶110||Reserved for future use.¶111|DYN|In instruction’s rm field, selects dynamic rounding mode; In Rounding Mode register, reserved.
===

normative_rules.name: fcsr_fflags_op
canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: Except when otherwise stated, if the result of a floating-point operation is NaN, it is the canonical NaN.

normative_rules.name: F_canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: For single-precision floating-point, the canonical NaN has a positive sign and all significand bits clear except the MSB, the quiet bit. In other words, for single-precision floating-point, the canonical NaN corresponds to the pattern 0x7fc00000.

normative_rules.name: ieee_std_subnormal
normative_rules.text: Operations on subnormal numbers are handled in accordance with IEEE 754-2008.

normative_rules.name: ieee_std_tininess
normative_rules.text: In the parlance of IEEE 754-2008, tininess is detected after rounding.

normative_rules.name: fsw_flw_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point loads and stores use the same base+offset addressing mode as the integer base ISAs, with a base address in register rs1 and a 12-bit signed byte offset. The insn:flw[] instruction loads a single-precision floating-point value from memory into floating-point register rd. insn:fsw[] stores a single-precision value from floating-point register rs2 to memory.

normative_rules.name: fsw_flw_atomic_align
normative_rules.text: insn:flw[] and insn:fsw[] are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned.

normative_rules.name: fsw_flw_bits_maintained
normative_rules.text: insn:flw[] and insn:fsw[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: fp_misaligned
normative_rules.text: As described in , the execution environment defines whether misaligned floating-point loads and stores are handled invisibly or raise a contained or fatal trap.

normative_rules.name: fadd-s_fmul-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fadd.s[] and insn:fmul.s[] perform single-precision floating-point addition and multiplication respectively, between rs1 and rs2

normative_rules.name: fsub-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fsub.s[] performs the single-precision floating-point subtraction of rs2 from rs1

normative_rules.name: fdiv-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fdiv.s[] performs the single-precision floating-point division of rs1 by rs2

normative_rules.name: fsqrt-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fsqrt.s[] computes the square root of rs1

normative_rules.name: fp_rd
normative_rules.text: In each case, the result is written to rd.

normative_rules.name: F_fmt_single
normative_rules.text: The 2-bit floating-point format field fmt is encoded as shown in . It is set to S (00) for all instructions in the ext:f[] extension.

normative_rules.name: F_rm_field
normative_rules.text: All floating-point operations that perform rounding can select the rounding mode using the rm field with the encoding shown in .

normative_rules.name: fmin-s_fmax-s_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point minimum-number and maximum-number instructions insn:fmin.s[] and insn:fmax.s[] write, respectively, the smaller or larger of rs1 and rs2 to rd

normative_rules.name: fmin-s_fmax-s_zero_compare
normative_rules.text: For the purposes of these instructions only, the value −0.0 is considered to be less than the value +0.0

normative_rules.name: fmin-s_fmax-s_both_nan_input
normative_rules.text: If both inputs are NaNs, the result is the canonical NaN

normative_rules.name: fmin-s_fmax-s_one_nan_input
normative_rules.text: If only one operand is a NaN, the result is the non-NaN operand

normative_rules.name: fmin-s_fmax-s_signaling_nan_nv
normative_rules.text: Signaling NaN inputs set the invalid operation exception flag, even when the result is not NaN

normative_rules.name: fma_rs3
normative_rules.text: Floating-point fused multiply-add (FMA) instructions require a new standard instruction format. R4-type instructions specify three source registers (rs1, rs2, and rs3) and a destination register (rd). This format is only used by the floating-point fused multiply-add instructions.

normative_rules.name: fmadd-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fmadd.s[] multiplies the values in rs1 and rs2, adds the value in rs3, and writes the final result to rd. insn:fmadd.s[] computes (rs1×rs2)+rs3.

normative_rules.name: fmsub-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fmsub.s[] multiplies the values in rs1 and rs2, subtracts the value in rs3, and writes the final result to rd. insn:fmsub.s[] computes (rs1×rs2)−rs3.

normative_rules.name: fnmsub-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fnmsub.s[] multiplies the values in rs1 and rs2, negates the product, adds the value in rs3, and writes the final result to rd. insn:fnmsub.s[] computes −(rs1×rs2)+rs3.

normative_rules.name: fnmadd-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fnmadd.s[] multiplies the values in rs1 and rs2, negates the product, subtracts the value in rs3, and writes the final result to rd. insn:fnmadd.s[] computes −(rs1×rs2)−rs3.

normative_rules.name: fma_nv_flag
normative_rules.text: The fused multiply-add instructions must set the invalid operation exception flag when the multiplicands are ∞ and zero, even when the addend is a quiet NaN.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-l-s_fcvt-w-s_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.w.s[] or
insn:fcvt.l.s[] converts a floating-point number in floating-point register
rs1 to a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer, respectively, in integer
register rd

normative_rules.name: fcvt-s-w_fcvt-s-l_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.s.w[] or insn:fcvt.s.l[] converts a 32-bit or 64-bit signed
integer, respectively, in integer register rs1 into a floating-point
number in floating-point register rd

normative_rules.name: fcvt-wu-s_fcvt-lu-s_fcvt-s-wu_fcvt-s-lu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.wu.s[], insn:fcvt.lu.s[], insn:fcvt.s.wu[],
and insn:fcvt.s.lu[] variants convert to or from unsigned integer values. For
XLEN>32, insn:fcvt.w.s[] and insn:fcvt.wu.s[] sign-extend the 32-bit result to the destination register width

normative_rules.name: fcvt_long_float_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.l.s[], insn:fcvt.lu.s[], insn:fcvt.s.l[], and insn:fcvt.s.lu[] are RV64-only instructions

normative_rules.name: fcvt_unrepresentable_nv
normative_rules.text:
If the rounded result is not representable in the
destination format, it is clipped to the nearest value and the invalid
flag is set

normative_rules.name: fcvt_int_float_valid_input
normative_rules.text:
<<int_conv>> gives the range of valid inputs
for insn:fcvt.w.s[], insn:fcvt.wu.s[], insn:fcvt.l.s[], and insn:fcvt.lu.s[] and
the behavior of these instructions for invalid inputs

normative_rules.name: fcvt_round
normative_rules.text:
All floating-point to integer and integer to floating-point conversion
instructions round according to the rm field.

normative_rules.name: fcvt_nx
normative_rules.text: All floating-point conversion instructions set the Inexact exception flag if the rounded result differs from the operand value and the Invalid exception flag is not set.

normative_rules.name: fsgnj-s_fsgnjn-s_fsgnjx-s_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fsgnj.s[], insn:fsgnjn.s[], and
insn:fsgnjx.s[] are floating-point to floating-point sign-injection instructions
that produce a result that takes all bits except the
sign bit from rs1. For insn:fsgnj[], the result's sign bit is rs2's sign
bit; for insn:fsgnjn[], the result's sign bit is the opposite of rs2's sign
bit; and for insn:fsgnjx[], the sign bit is the XOR of the sign bits of rs1
and rs2. Sign-injection instructions do not set floating-point
exception flags, nor do they canonicalize NaNs

normative_rules.name: fmv-x-w_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fmv.x.w[] moves
the single-precision value in floating-point register rs1 represented
in the IEEE 754-2008 encoding to the lower 32 bits of integer register
rd. The bits are not modified in the transfer, and in particular, the
payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved. For RV64, the higher 32
bits of the destination register are filled with copies of the
floating-point number's sign bit

normative_rules.name: fmv-w-x_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fmv.w.x[] moves the single-precision value encoded in the IEEE 754-2008 encoding from the lower 32 bits of integer register rs1 to the floating-point register rd. The bits are not modified in the transfer, and in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: feq-s_flt-s_fle-s_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point compare instructions (insn:feq.s[], insn:flt.s[], insn:fle.s[]) perform the specified comparison between floating-point registers (rs1 = rs2, rs1 < rs2, rs1 ≤ rs2) writing 1 to the integer register rd if the condition holds, and 0 otherwise.

normative_rules.name: flt-s_fle-s_signaling
normative_rules.text:
insn:flt.s[] and insn:fle.s[] perform what IEEE 754-2008
refers to as signaling comparisons: that is, they set the invalid
operation exception flag if either input is NaN

normative_rules.name: feq-s_quiet
normative_rules.text:
insn:feq.s[] performs a quiet comparison: it only sets
the invalid operation exception flag if either input is a signaling NaN

normative_rules.name: feq-s_flt-s_fle-s_nan_input
normative_rules.text:
For all three instructions, the
result is 0 if either operand is NaN

normative_rules.name: fclass-s_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:fclass.s[] instruction examines the value in floating-point register rs1 and writes to integer register rd a 10-bit mask that indicates the class of the floating-point number. The format of the mask is described in . The corresponding bit in rd will be set if the property is true and clear otherwise. All other bits in rd are cleared. Note that exactly one bit in rd will be set. insn:fclass.s[] does not set the floating-point exception flags.

normative_rules.name: D_canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: For double-precision floating-point, the canonical NaN corresponds to the pattern 0x7ff8000000000000.

normative_rules.name: D_flen_64
normative_rules.text:
The ext:d[] extension widens the 32 floating-point registers,
f0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;f31, to 64 bits, i.e., FLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: fp_nan_boxing
normative_rules.text: When multiple floating-point precisions are supported, then valid values of narrower n-bit types, n<FLEN, are represented in the lower n bits of an FLEN-bit NaN value, in a process termed NaN-boxing. The upper bits of a valid NaN-boxed value must be all 1s. Valid NaN-boxed n-bit values therefore appear as negative quiet NaNs (qNaNs) when viewed as any wider m-bit value, n < m ≤ FLEN. Any operation that writes a narrower result to an f register must write all 1s to the uppermost FLEN-n bits to yield a legal NaN-boxed value.

normative_rules.name: fp_transfer_instrs_narrow_transfer_in
normative_rules.text:
A narrower n-bit
transfer, n<FLEN, into the f registers will create a valid NaN-boxed
value

normative_rules.name: fp_transfer_instrs_narrow_transfer_out
normative_rules.text:
A narrower
n-bit transfer out of the floating-point registers will
transfer the lower n bits of the register ignoring the
upper FLEN-n bits

normative_rules.name: fp_nontransfer_instrs_improper_nan_boxed_input
normative_rules.text: Apart from transfer operations described in the previous paragraph, all other floating-point operations on narrower n-bit operations, n<FLEN, check if the input operands are correctly NaN-boxed, i.e., all upper FLEN-n bits are 1. If so, the n least-significant bits of the input are used as the input value, otherwise the input value is treated as an n-bit canonical NaN.

normative_rules.name: fld_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:fld[] instruction loads a double-precision floating-point value from
memory into floating-point register rd

normative_rules.name: fsd_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fsd[] stores a double-precision
value from the floating-point registers to memory

normative_rules.name: fld_fsd_atomic_align
normative_rules.text: insn:fld[] and insn:fsd[] are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned and XLEN≥64.

normative_rules.name: fld_fsd_bits_maintained
normative_rules.text: insn:fld[] and insn:fsd[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: D_computational_instrs
normative_rules.text: The double-precision floating-point computational instructions are defined analogously to their single-precision counterparts, but operate on double-precision operands and produce double-precision results.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-w-d_fcvt-l-d_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.w.d[] or
insn:fcvt.l.d[] converts a double-precision floating-point number in
floating-point register rs1 to a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer,
respectively, in integer register rd

normative_rules.name: fcvt-d-w_fcvt-d-l_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.d.w[] or insn:fcvt.d.l[] converts a
32-bit or 64-bit signed integer, respectively, in integer register rs1
into a double-precision floating-point number in floating-point register
rd

normative_rules.name: fcvt-wu-d_fcvt-lu-d_fcvt-d-wu_fcvt-d-lu_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.wu.d[], insn:fcvt.lu.d[], insn:fcvt.d.wu[], and insn:fcvt.d.lu[] variants convert to
or from unsigned integer values

normative_rules.name: fcvt-w-d_fcvt-wu-d_sign_ext
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, insn:fcvt.w.d[] and insn:fcvt.wu.d[] sign-extend the
32-bit result

normative_rules.name: fcvt_long_double_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.l.d[], fcvt.lu.d[], fcvt.d.l[], and fcvt.d.lu[] are RV64-only instructions.

normative_rules.name: fcvt_int_double_valid_input
normative_rules.text:
The range of valid inputs for insn:fcvt.w.d[], insn:fcvt.wu.d[], insn:fcvt.l.d[], and insn:fcvt.lu.d[] and the behavior of these instructions for invalid
inputs are the same as for insn:fcvt.w.s[], insn:fcvt.wu.s[], insn:fcvt.l.s[], and insn:fcvt.lu.s[]

normative_rules.name: fcvt-s-d_fcvt-d-s_op
normative_rules.text:
The double-precision to single-precision and single-precision to
double-precision conversion instructions, insn:fcvt.s.d[] and insn:fcvt.d.s[], are
encoded in the OP-FP major opcode space and both the source and
destination are floating-point registers. The rs2 field encodes the
datatype of the source, and the fmt field encodes the datatype of the
destination

normative_rules.name: fcvt_float_rounding
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.s.d[] rounds according to the rm field; insn:fcvt.d.s[] will
never round

normative_rules.name: fsgnj-d_fsgnjn-d_fsgnjx-d_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point to floating-point sign-injection instructions, insn:fsgnj.d[], insn:fsgnjn.d[], and insn:fsgnjx.d[], are defined analogously to the single-precision sign-injection instruction.

normative_rules.name: fmv-x-d_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fmv.x.d[] moves the double-precision value in
floating-point register rs1 to a representation in the IEEE 754-2008
encoding in integer register rd

normative_rules.name: fmv-d-x_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fmv.d.x[] moves the
double-precision value encoded in the IEEE 754-2008 encoding from the
integer register rs1 to the floating-point register rd

normative_rules.name: fmv_bits_preserved
normative_rules.text: insn:fmv.x.d[] and insn:fmv.d.x[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: D_compare_instrs
normative_rules.text: The double-precision floating-point compare instructions are defined analogously to their single-precision counterparts, but operate on double-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: fclass-d_op
normative_rules.text: The double-precision floating-point classify instruction, insn:fclass.d[], is defined analogously to its single-precision counterpart, but operates on double-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: Q_flen_128
normative_rules.text:
The floating-point registers are now extended to hold
either a single, double, or quad-precision floating-point value, i.e., FLEN=128.

normative_rules.name: Q_canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: For quad-precision floating-point, the canonical NaN corresponds to the pattern 0x7fff8000000000000000000000000000.

normative_rules.name: fsq_flq_op
normative_rules.text: New 128-bit variants of LOAD-FP and STORE-FP instructions are added, encoded with a new value for the funct3 width field.

normative_rules.name: fsq_flq_atomic_align
normative_rules.text: insn:flq[] and insn:fsq[] are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned and XLEN=128.

normative_rules.name: fsq_flq_bits_maintained
normative_rules.text: insn:flq[] and insn:fsq[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: Q_computational_instrs
normative_rules.text: The quad-precision floating-point computational instructions are defined analogously to their double-precision counterparts, but operate on quad-precision operands and produce quad-precision results.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-w-q_fcvt-l-q_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.w.q[] or insn:fcvt.l.q[] converts a quad-precision floating-point number to a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer, respectively

normative_rules.name: fcvt-q-w_fcvt-q-l_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.q.w[] or insn:fcvt.q.l[] converts a 32-bit or 64-bit signed integer, respectively, into a quad-precision floating-point number

normative_rules.name: fcvt-wu-q_fcvt-lu-q_fcvt-q-wu_fcvt-q-lu_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.wu.q[], insn:fcvt.lu.q[], insn:fcvt.q.wu[], and insn:fcvt.q.lu[] variants convert to or from unsigned integer values

normative_rules.name: fcvt_long_quad_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.l.q[], insn:fcvt.lu.q[], insn:fcvt.q.l[], and insn:fcvt.q.lu[] are RV64-only instructions

normative_rules.name: fcvt_int_quad_valid_input
normative_rules.text: The range of valid inputs for insn:fcvt.w.q[], insn:fcvt.wu.q[], insn:fcvt.l.q[], and insn:fcvt.lu.q[] and the behavior for invalid inputs are the same as for insn:fcvt.w.s[], insn:fcvt.wu.s[], insn:fcvt.l.s[], and insn:fcvt.lu.s[]

normative_rules.name: fcvt-s-q_fcvt-q-s_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.s.q[] or
insn:fcvt.q.s[] converts a quad-precision floating-point number to a
single-precision floating-point number, or vice-versa, respectively

normative_rules.name: fcvt-d-q_fcvt-q-d_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fcvt.d.q[] or insn:fcvt.q.d[] converts a quad-precision floating-point number to
a double-precision floating-point number, or vice-versa, respectively

normative_rules.name: fsgnj-q_fsgnjn-q_fsgnjx-q_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point to floating-point sign-injection instructions, insn:fsgnj.q[], insn:fsgnjn.q[], and insn:fsgnjx.q[], are defined analogously to the double-precision sign-injection instruction.

normative_rules.name: Q_compare_instrs
normative_rules.text: The quad-precision floating-point compare instructions are defined analogously to their double-precision counterparts, but operate on quad-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: fclass-q_op
normative_rules.text: The quad-precision floating-point classify instruction, insn:fclass.q[], is defined analogously to its double-precision counterpart, but operates on quad-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: Zfh_canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: For half-precision floating-point, the canonical NaN corresponds to the pattern 0x7e00.

normative_rules.name: fsh_flh_op
normative_rules.text: New 16-bit variants of LOAD-FP and STORE-FP instructions are added, encoded with a new value for the funct3 width field.

normative_rules.name: fsh_flh_atomic_align
normative_rules.text: insn:flh[] and insn:fsh[] are only guaranteed to execute atomically if the effective address is naturally aligned.

normative_rules.name: fsh_flh_bits_maintained
normative_rules.text: insn:flh[] and insn:fsh[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved. insn:flh[] NaN-boxes the result written to rd, whereas insn:fsh[] ignores all but the lower 16 bits in rs2.

normative_rules.name: Zfh_computational_instrs
normative_rules.text: The half-precision floating-point computational instructions are defined analogously to their single-precision counterparts, but operate on half-precision operands and produce half-precision results.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-w-h_fcvt-l-h_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.w.h[] or insn:fcvt.l.h[] converts a half-precision floating-point number to a signed 32-bit or 64-bit integer, respectively

normative_rules.name: fcvt-h-w_fcvt-h-l_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.h.w[] or insn:fcvt.h.l[] converts a 32-bit or 64-bit signed integer, respectively, into a half-precision floating-point number

normative_rules.name: fcvt-wu-h_fcvt-lu-h_fcvt-h-wu_fcvt-h-lu_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.wu.h[], insn:fcvt.lu.h[], insn:fcvt.h.wu[], and insn:fcvt.h.lu[] variants convert to or from unsigned integer values

normative_rules.name: fcvt_long_half_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.l.h[], insn:fcvt.lu.h[], insn:fcvt.h.l[], and insn:fcvt.h.lu[] are RV64-only instructions.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-s-h_fcvt-h-s_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fcvt.s.h[] or insn:fcvt.h.s[] converts a half-precision floating-point number to a single-precision floating-point number, or vice-versa, respectively

normative_rules.name: fcvt-d-h_fcvt-h-d_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:d[] extension is present, insn:fcvt.d.h[] or insn:fcvt.h.d[] converts a half-precision floating-point number to a double-precision floating-point number, or vice-versa, respectively

normative_rules.name: fcvt-q-h_fcvt-h-q_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:q[] extension is present, insn:fcvt.q.h[] or insn:fcvt.h.q[] converts a half-precision floating-point number to a quad-precision floating-point number, or vice-versa, respectively

normative_rules.name: fsgnj-h_fsgnjn-h_fsgnjx-h_op
normative_rules.text: Floating-point to floating-point sign-injection instructions, insn:fsgnj.h[], insn:fsgnjn.h[], and insn:fsgnjx.h[] are defined analogously to the single-precision sign-injection instruction.

normative_rules.name: fmv-x-h_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:fmv.x.h[] moves
the half-precision value in floating-point register rs1 to a
representation in the IEEE 754-2008 encoding in integer register rd,
filling the upper XLEN-16 bits with copies of the floating-point
number's sign bit

normative_rules.name: fmv-h-x_op
normative_rules.text: insn:fmv.h.x[] moves the half-precision value encoded in the IEEE 754-2008 encoding from the lower 16 bits of integer register rs1 to the floating-point register rd, NaN-boxing the result.

normative_rules.name: fmv_half_bits_preserved
normative_rules.text: insn:fmv.x.h[] and insn:fmv.h.x[] do not modify the bits being transferred; in particular, the payloads of non-canonical NaNs are preserved.

normative_rules.name: Zfh_compare_instrs
normative_rules.text: The half-precision floating-point compare instructions are defined analogously to their single-precision counterparts, but operate on half-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: fclass-h_op
normative_rules.text: The half-precision floating-point classify instruction, insn:fclass.h[], is defined analogously to its single-precision counterpart, but operates on half-precision operands.

normative_rules.name: Zfhmin
normative_rules.text: The ext:zfhmin[] extension includes the following instructions from the ext:zfh[] extension: insn:flh[], insn:fsh[], insn:fmv.x.h[], insn:fmv.h.x[], insn:fcvt.s.h[], and insn:fcvt.h.s[]. If the ext:d[] extension is present, the insn:fcvt.d.h[] and insn:fcvt.h.d[] instructions are also included. If the ext:q[] extension is present, the insn:fcvt.q.h[] and insn:fcvt.h.q[] instructions are additionally included.

normative_rules.name: fli-s_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:fli.s[] instruction loads one of 32 single-precision floating-point constants, encoded in the rs1 field, into floating-point register rd. The correspondence of rs1 field values and single-precision floating-point values is shown in . insn:fli.s[] is encoded like insn:fmv.w.x[], but with rs2=1.

normative_rules.name: fli-d_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:d[] extension is implemented, insn:fli.d[] performs the analogous operation, but loads a double-precision value into floating-point register rd. Note that entry 1 (corresponding to the minimum positive normal value) has a numerically different value for double-precision than for single-precision. insn:fli.d[] is encoded like insn:fli.s[], but with fmt=D.

normative_rules.name: fli-q_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:q[] extension is implemented, insn:fli.q[] performs the analogous operation, but loads a quad-precision value into floating-point register rd. Note that entry 1 (corresponding to the minimum positive normal value) has a numerically different value for quad-precision. insn:fli.q[] is encoded like insn:fli.s[], but with fmt=Q.

normative_rules.name: fli-h_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zfh[] or ext:zvfh[] extension is implemented, insn:fli.h[] performs the analogous operation, but loads a half-precision floating-point value into register rd. Note that entry 1 (corresponding to the minimum positive normal value) has a numerically different value for half-precision. Furthermore, since 216 is not representable in half-precision floating-point, entry 29 in the table instead loads positive infinity—i.e., it is redundant with entry 30. insn:fli.h[] is encoded like insn:fli.s[], but with fmt=H.

normative_rules.name: fmaxm-s_fminm-s_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:fminm.s[] and insn:fmaxm.s[] instructions are defined like the insn:fmin.s[] and insn:fmax.s[] instructions, except that if either input is NaN, the result is the canonical NaN.

normative_rules.name: fmaxm-d_fminm-d_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:d[] extension is implemented, insn:fminm.d[] and insn:fmaxm.d[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on double-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: fmaxm-q_fminm-q_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:q[] extension is implemented, insn:fminm.q[] and insn:fmaxm.q[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on quad-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: fmaxm-h_fminm-h_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zfh[] extension is implemented, insn:fminm.h[] and insn:fmaxm.h[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on half-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: fround-s_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:fround.s[] instruction rounds the single-precision floating-point
number in floating-point register rs1 to an integer, according to the
rounding mode specified in the instruction's rm field. It then writes
that integer, represented as a single-precision floating-point number,
to floating-point register rd

normative_rules.name: fround-s_zero_inf
normative_rules.text:
Zero and infinite inputs are copied to
rd unmodified

normative_rules.name: fround-s_nan_nv
normative_rules.text:
Signaling NaN inputs cause the invalid operation
exception flag to be set; no other exception flags are set

normative_rules.name: froundnx-s_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:froundnx.s[] instruction is defined similarly, but it also sets the inexact exception flag if the input differs from the rounded result and is not NaN. insn:froundnx.s[] is encoded like insn:fcvt.s.d[], but with rs2=5.

normative_rules.name: fround-d_froundnx-d_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:d[] extension is implemented, insn:fround.d[] and insn:froundnx.d[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on double-precision numbers. They are encoded like insn:fcvt.d.s[], but with rs2=4 and 5, respectively,

normative_rules.name: fround-q_froundnx-q_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:q[] extension is implemented, insn:fround.q[] and insn:froundnx.q[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on quad-precision numbers. They are encoded like insn:fcvt.q.s[], but with rs2=4 and 5, respectively,

normative_rules.name: fround-h_froundnx-h_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zfh[] extension is implemented, insn:fround.h[] and insn:froundnx.h[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on half-precision numbers. They are encoded like insn:fcvt.h.s[], but with rs2=4 and 5, respectively,

normative_rules.name: fcvtmod-w-d_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:fcvtmod.w.d[] instruction is defined similarly to the insn:fcvt.w.d[] instruction, with the following differences. insn:fcvtmod.w.d[] always rounds towards zero. Bits 31:0 are taken from the rounded, unbounded two’s complement result, then sign-extended to XLEN bits and written to integer register rd. ±∞ and NaN are converted to zero.

normative_rules.name: fcvtmod-w-d_flags
normative_rules.text: Floating-point exception flags are raised the same as they would be for insn:fcvt.w.d[] with the same input operand.

normative_rules.name: fcvtmod-w-d_enc
normative_rules.text:
It
is encoded like insn:fcvt.w.d[], but with the rs2 field set to 8 and the rm
field set to 1 (RTZ). Other rm values are reserved.

normative_rules.name: fmvh-x-d_op
normative_rules.text: For RV32 only, if the ext:d[] extension is implemented, the insn:fmvh.x.d[] instruction moves bits 63:32 of floating-point register rs1 into integer register rd. It is encoded in the OP-FP major opcode with funct3=0, rs2=1, and funct7=1110001.

normative_rules.name: fmvp-d-x_op
normative_rules.text: For RV32 only, if the ext:d[] extension is implemented, the insn:fmvp.d.x[] instruction moves a double-precision number from a pair of integer registers into a floating-point register. Integer registers rs1 and rs2 supply bits 31:0 and 63:32, respectively; the result is written to floating-point register rd. FMVP.D.X is encoded in the OP-FP major opcode with funct3=0 and funct7=1011001.

normative_rules.name: fmvh-x-q_op
normative_rules.text: For RV64 only, if the ext:q[] extension is implemented, the insn:fmvh.x.q[] instruction moves bits 127:64 of floating-point register rs1 into integer register rd. It is encoded in the OP-FP major opcode with funct3=0, rs2=1, and funct7=1110011.

normative_rules.name: fmvp-q-x_op
normative_rules.text: For RV64 only, if the ext:q[] extension is implemented, the insn:fmvp.q.x[] instruction moves a double-precision number from a pair of integer registers into a floating-point register. Integer registers rs1 and rs2 supply bits 63:0 and 127:64, respectively; the result is written to floating-point register rd. insn:fmvp.q.x[] is encoded in the OP-FP major opcode with funct3=0 and funct7=1011011.

normative_rules.name: fleq-s_fltq-s_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:fleq.s[] and insn:fltq.s[] instructions are defined like the insn:fle.s[] and insn:flt.s[] instructions, except that quiet NaN inputs do not cause the invalid operation exception flag to be set.

normative_rules.name: fleq-d_fltq-d_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:d[] extension is implemented, insn:fleq.d[] and insn:fltq.d[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on double-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: fleq-q_fltq-q_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:q[] extension is implemented, insn:fleq.q[] and insn:fltq.q[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on quad-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: fleq-h_fltq-h_op
normative_rules.text: If the ext:zfh[] extension is implemented, insn:fleq.h[] and insn:fltq.h[] instructions are analogously defined to operate on half-precision numbers.

normative_rules.name: bf16_subnorm
normative_rules.text: BF16 computational instructions defined in this chapter support all IEEE 754-2008 features, including all rounding modes, subnormal inputs and outputs, overflow and underflow, and default exception handling. Tininess is detected after rounding.

normative_rules.name: bf16_canonical_nan
normative_rules.text: For BF16, the canonical NaN corresponds to the pattern 0x7fc0.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-bf16-s_op
normative_rules.text: Narrowing convert FP32 value to a BF16 value. Round according to the RM field.

normative_rules.name: fcvt-s-bf16_op
normative_rules.text: Converts a BF16 value to an FP32 value. The conversion is exact.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_F_instrs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zfinx[] extension adds all of the instructions that the ext:f[] extension adds, except for the transfer instructions insn:flw[], insn:fsw[], insn:fmv.w.x[], insn:fmv.x.w[], insn:c.flw[], insn:c.flwsp[], insn:c.fsw[], and insn:c.fswsp[].

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_x_regs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zfinx[] variants of these ext:f[]-extension instructions have the same semantics, except that whenever such an instruction would have accessed an f register, it instead accesses the x register with the same number.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_narrow_operands
normative_rules.text: Floating-point operands of width w < XLEN bits occupy bits w-1:0 of an x register. Floating-point operations on w-bit operands ignore operand bits XLEN-1: w.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_narrow_result
normative_rules.text: Floating-point operations that produce w < XLEN-bit results fill bits XLEN-1: w with copies of bit w-1 (the sign bit).

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_D_instrs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zdinx[] extension adds all of the instructions that the ext:d[] extension adds, except for the transfer instructions insn:fld[], insn:fsd[], insn:fmv.d.x[], insn:fmv.x.d[], c.fld[], c.fldsp[], c.fsd[], and c.fsdsp[].

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_x_regs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zdinx[] variants of these ext:d[]-extension instructions have the same semantics, except that whenever such an instruction would have accessed an f register, it instead accesses the x register with the same number.

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_x_reg_pair
normative_rules.text: For RV32, double-precision operands in ext:zdinx[] are held in aligned x-register pairs. In other words, register numbers must be even. Use of misaligned (odd-numbered) registers for double-width floating-point operands is reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_endianness
normative_rules.text: Regardless of endianness, the lower-numbered register holds the low-order bits of double-width floating-point operands, and the higher-numbered register holds the high-order bits. For RV32 with ext:zdinx[], bits 31:0 of a double-precision operand might be held in register x14, with bits 63:32 of that operand held in x15, for instance.

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_x0_write
normative_rules.text: When a double-width floating-point result is written to x0, the entire write takes no effect. For RV32 with ext:zdinx[], writing a double-precision result to x0 does not cause x1 to be written.

normative_rules.name: Zdinx_x0_read
normative_rules.text: When x0 is used as a double-width floating-point operand, the entire operand is zero. In other words, x1 is not accessed.

normative_rules.name: Zhinx_Zfh_instrs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zhinx[] extension adds all of the instructions that the ext:zfh[] extension adds, except for the transfer instructions insn:flh[], insn:fsh[], insn:fmv.h.x[], and insn:fmv.x.h[].

normative_rules.name: Zhinx_x_regs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zhinx[] variants of these ext:zfh[]-extension instructions have the same semantics, except that whenever such an instruction would have accessed an f register, it instead accesses the x register with the same number.

normative_rules.name: Zhinxmin_instrs
normative_rules.text: The ext:zhinxmin[] extension includes the following instructions from the ext:zhinx[] extension: insn:fcvt.s.h[] and insn:fcvt.h.s[]. If the ext:zdinx[] extension is present, the insn:fcvt.d.h[] and insn:fcvt.h.d[] instructions are also included.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_mstatus_fs_zero
normative_rules.text: As described in , the csr:mstatus[] field csr::[fs] is hardwired to 0 if the ext:zfinx[] extension is implemented, and csr::[fs] no longer affects the trapping behavior of floating-point instructions or csr:fcsr[] accesses.

normative_rules.name: Zfinx_misa_F_D_Q_zero
normative_rules.text: The csr:misa[] bits csr::[f], csr::[d], and csr::[q] are hardwired to 0 when the ext:zfinx[] extension is implemented.

normative_rules.name: Zca_align16
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zca[] extension allows 16-bit instructions to be freely
intermixed with 32-bit instructions, with the latter now able to start
on any 16-bit boundary, i.e., IALIGN=16.

normative_rules.name: Zca_no_misaligned
normative_rules.text:
With the addition of the ext:zca[]
extension, no instructions can raise instruction-address-misaligned
exceptions.

normative_rules.name: Zca_regs8
normative_rules.text:
CIW,
CL, CS, CA, and CB are limited to just 8 of them.
<<registers>> lists these popular registers, which
correspond to registers x8 to x15.

normative_rules.name: c-lwsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.lwsp[] loads a 32-bit value from memory into register rd. It computes
an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 4,
to the stack pointer, x2. It expands to insn:lw[rd,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-lwsp_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.lwsp[] is
valid only when rd≠x0; the code points with rd=x0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-ldsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.ldsp[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that loads a 64-bit value
from memory into register rd. It computes its effective address by
adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer,
x2. It expands to insn:ld[rd,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-ldsp_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.ldsp[] is valid only when
rd≠x0; the code points with
rd=x0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-swsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.swsp[] stores a 32-bit value in register rs2 to memory. It computes an
effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 4, to
the stack pointer, x2. It expands to insn:sw[rs2,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-sdsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.sdsp[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that stores a 64-bit value in
register rs2 to memory. It computes an effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2. It
expands to insn:sd[rs2,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-lw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.lw[] loads a 32-bit value from memory into register
rd′. It computes an effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 4, to the base address in register
rs1′. It expands to insn:lw[rd′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-ld_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.ld[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that loads a 64-bit value from
memory into register rd′. It computes an effective
address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base
address in register rs1′. It expands to
insn:ld[rd′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-sw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.sw[] stores a 32-bit value in register rs2′ to memory.
It computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset,
scaled by 4, to the base address in register rs1′. It
expands to insn:sw[rs2′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-sd_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.sd[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that stores a 64-bit value in
register rs2′ to memory. It computes an effective
address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base
address in register rs1′. It expands to
insn:sd[rs2′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: Zca_offsets_mul2
normative_rules.text:
As with base RVI instructions, the offsets of all
ext:zca[] control transfer instructions are in multiples of 2 bytes.

normative_rules.name: c-j_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.j[] performs an unconditional control transfer. The offset is
sign-extended and added to the pc to form the jump target address. insn:c.j[] can
therefore target a ±2 KiB range. It expands to
insn:jal[x0,offset].

normative_rules.name: c-jal_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.jal[] is an XLEN=32-only instruction that performs the same operation as
insn:c.j[], but additionally writes the address of the instruction following
the jump (pc+2) to the link register, x1. It expands to
insn:jal[x1,offset].

normative_rules.name: c-jr_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.jr[] (jump register) performs an unconditional control transfer to the
address in register rs1. It expands to insn:jalr[x0,0(rs1)].

normative_rules.name: c-jr_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.jr[] is
valid only when rs1≠x0; the code
point with rs1=x0 is reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-jalr_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.jalr[] (jump and link register) performs the same operation as insn:c.jr[], but
additionally writes the address of the instruction following the jump
(pc+2) to the link register, x1. It expands to
insn:jalr[x1,0(rs1)].

normative_rules.name: c-jalr_ebreak
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.jalr[] is valid only when
rs1≠x0; the code point with
rs1=x0 corresponds to the insn:c.ebreak[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: c-beqz_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.beqz[] performs conditional control transfers. The offset is
sign-extended and added to the pc to form the branch target address.
It can therefore target a ±256 B range. insn:c.beqz[] takes the
branch if the value in register rs1′ is zero. It
expands to insn:beq[rs1′,x0,offset`].

normative_rules.name: c-bnez_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.bnez[] is defined analogously, but it takes the branch if
rs1′ contains a nonzero value. It expands to
insn:bne[rs1′,x0,offset`].

normative_rules.name: c-li_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.li[] loads the sign-extended 6-bit immediate, imm, into register rd.
It expands into insn:addi[rd,x0,imm].

normative_rules.name: c-li_hint
normative_rules.text: The insn:c.li[] code points with rd=x0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-lui_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.lui[] loads the non-zero 6-bit immediate field into bits 17–12 of the
destination register, clears the bottom 12 bits, and sign-extends bit 17
into all higher bits of the destination. It expands into
insn:lui[rd,imm].

normative_rules.name: c-lui_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.lui[] is valid only when
rd≠x2,
and when the immediate is not equal to zero. The code points with
imm=0 are reserved.
The code points with rd=x2 and imm≠0 correspond to the
insn:c.addi16sp[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: c-lui_hint
normative_rules.text: The code points with rd=x0 and imm≠0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-addi_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addi[] adds the non-zero sign-extended 6-bit immediate to the value in
register rd then writes the result to rd. It expands into
insn:addi[rd,rd,imm].

normative_rules.name: c-addi_hint
normative_rules.text: The code points with rd≠0 and imm=0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-addi_nop
normative_rules.text:
The code points with rd=x0 encode the insn:c.nop[] instruction, of
which the code points with imm≠0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-addiw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addiw[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that performs the same
computation but produces a 32-bit result, then sign-extends result to 64
bits. It expands into insn:addiw[rd,rd,imm]. The immediate can be
zero for insn:c.addiw[], where this corresponds to insn:sext.w[rd].

normative_rules.name: c-addiw_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addiw[] is
valid only when rd≠x0; the code points with
rd=x0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-addi16sp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addi16sp[] (add immediate to stack pointer)
shares the opcode with insn:c.lui[], but has a destination field of
x2. insn:c.addi16sp[] adds the non-zero sign-extended 6-bit immediate to the
value in the stack pointer (sp=x2), where the immediate is scaled to
represent multiples of 16 in the range [-512, 496]. insn:c.addi16sp[] is used to
adjust the stack pointer in procedure prologues and epilogues. It
expands into insn:addi[x2,x2,nzimm[9:4]].

normative_rules.name: c-addi16sp_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addi16sp[] is valid only when
nzimm≠0; the code point with nzimm=0 is reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-addi4spn_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addi4spn[] (add immediate to stack pointer, non-destructive)
is a CIW-format instruction that adds a zero-extended
non-zero immediate, scaled by 4, to the stack pointer, x2, and writes
the result to rd′. This instruction is used to generate
pointers to stack-allocated variables, and expands to
insn:addi[rd′,x2,nzuimm[9:2]].

normative_rules.name: c-addi4spn_rsv
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addi4spn[] is valid only when
nzuimm≠0; the code points with nzuimm=0 are
reserved.

normative_rules.name: c-slli_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.slli[] is a CI-format instruction that performs a logical left shift of
the value in register rd then writes the result to rd. The shift
amount is encoded in the shamt field.
It expands into insn:slli[rd,rd,shamt[5:0]].

normative_rules.name: c-slli_hint
normative_rules.text: The insn:c.slli[] code points with shamt=0 or with rd=x0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-slli_shamt5
normative_rules.text:
For XLEN=32, shamt[5] must be zero; the code points with shamt[5]=1
are designated for custom extensions.

normative_rules.name: c-srli_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.srli[] is a CB-format instruction that performs a logical right shift of
the value in register rd′ then writes the result to
rd′. The shift amount is encoded in the shamt field.
It expands into insn:srli[rd′,rd′,shamt].

normative_rules.name: c-srli_hint
normative_rules.text: The insn:c.srli[] code points with shamt=0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-srli_shamt5
normative_rules.text:
For XLEN=32, shamt[5] must be zero; the code points with shamt[5]=1
are designated for custom extensions.

normative_rules.name: c-srai_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.srai[] is defined analogously to insn:c.srli[], but instead performs an
arithmetic right shift. It expands to
insn:srai[rd′,rd′,shamt].

normative_rules.name: c-andi_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.andi[] is a CB-format instruction that computes the bitwise AND of the
value in register rd′ and the sign-extended 6-bit
immediate, then writes the result to rd′. It
expands to insn:andi[rd′,rd′,imm].

normative_rules.name: c-mv_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.mv[] copies the value in register rs2 into register rd. It expands
into insn:add[rd,x0,rs2].

normative_rules.name: c-mv_jr
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.mv[] is valid only when
rs2≠x0; the code points with rs2=x0 correspond to the insn:c.jr[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: c-mv_hint
normative_rules.text: The code points with rs2≠x0 and rd=x0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-add_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.add[] adds the values in registers rd and rs2 and writes the result
to register rd. It expands into insn:add[rd,rd,rs2].

normative_rules.name: c-add_val
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.add[] is only
valid when rs2≠x0; the code points with rs2=x0 correspond to the
insn:c.jalr[] and insn:c.ebreak[] instructions.

normative_rules.name: c-add_hint
normative_rules.text: The code points with rs2≠x0 and rd=x0 are HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-and_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.and[] computes the bitwise AND of the values in registers
rd′ and rs2′, then writes the result
to register rd′. It expands into
insn:and[rd′,rd′,rs2′].

normative_rules.name: c-or_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.or[] computes the bitwise OR of the values in registers
rd′ and rs2′, then writes the result
to register rd′. It expands into
insn:or[rd′,rd′, rs2′].

normative_rules.name: c-xor_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.xor[] computes the bitwise XOR of the values in registers
rd′ and rs2′, then writes the result
to register rd′. It expands into
insn:xor[rd′,rd′,rs2′].

normative_rules.name: c-sub_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.sub[] subtracts the value in register rs2′ from the
value in register rd′, then writes the result to
register rd′. It expands into
insn:sub[rd′,rd′,rs2′].

normative_rules.name: c-addw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.addw[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that adds the values in
registers rd′ and rs2′, then
sign-extends the lower 32 bits of the sum before writing the result to
register rd′. It expands into
insn:addw[rd′,rd′,rs2′].

normative_rules.name: c-subw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.subw[] is an XLEN=64-only instruction that subtracts the value in
register rs2′ from the value in register
rd′, then sign-extends the lower 32 bits of the
difference before writing the result to register rd′.
It expands into insn:subw[rd′,rd′,rs2′].

normative_rules.name: Zca_illegal
normative_rules.text:
A 16-bit instruction with all bits zero is permanently reserved as an
illegal instruction.

normative_rules.name: c-nop_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.nop[] is a CI-format instruction that does not change any user-visible
state, except for advancing the pc and incrementing any applicable
performance counters. insn:c.nop[] expands to insn:nop[].

normative_rules.name: c-nop_hint
normative_rules.text:
The insn:c.nop[] code points
with imm≠0 encode HINTs.

normative_rules.name: c-ebreak_op
normative_rules.text:
Debuggers can use the insn:c.ebreak[] instruction, which expands to insn:ebreak[],
to cause control to be transferred back to the debugging environment.
insn:c.ebreak[] shares the opcode with the insn:c.add[] instruction, but with rd and
rs2 both zero, thus can also use the CR format.

normative_rules.name: Zca_hints
normative_rules.text:
A portion of the ext:zca[] encoding space is reserved for microarchitectural
HINTs. Like the HINTs in the RV32I base ISA (see
<<rv32i-hints>>), these instructions do not
modify any architectural state, except for advancing the pc and any
applicable performance counters. HINTs are executed as no-ops on
implementations that ignore them.

normative_rules.name: c-flwsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.flwsp[] is an RV32FC-only instruction that loads a single-precision
floating-point value from memory into floating-point register rd. It
computes its effective address by adding the zero-extended offset,
scaled by 4, to the stack pointer, x2. It expands to
insn:flw[rd, offset(x2)].
insn:c.flwsp[] uses the <<rvc-form,CI format>>.

normative_rules.name: c-fswsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fswsp[] is an RV32FC-only instruction that stores a single-precision
floating-point value in floating-point register rs2 to memory. It
computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset,
scaled by 4, to the stack pointer, x2. It expands to
insn:fsw[rs2,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: Zc_fp_regs
normative_rules.text:
Compressed register-based floating-point loads and stores use the
CL and CS formats, respectively, with the eight registers mapping to f8 to f15.

normative_rules.name: c-flw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.flw[] is an RV32FC-only instruction that loads a single-precision
floating-point value from memory into floating-point register
rd′. It computes an effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 4, to the base address in register
rs1′. It expands to
insn:flw[rd′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-fsw_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fsw[] is an RV32FC-only instruction that stores a single-precision
floating-point value in floating-point register rs2′ to
memory. It computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended
offset, scaled by 4, to the base address in register
rs1′. It expands to
insn:fsw[rs2′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-fldsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fldsp[] is an RV32DC/RV64DC-only instruction that loads a
double-precision floating-point value from memory into floating-point
register rd. It computes its effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2. It
expands to insn:fld[rd,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-fsdsp_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fsdsp[] is an RV32DC/RV64DC-only instruction that stores a
double-precision floating-point value in floating-point register rs2
to memory. It computes an effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2. It
expands to insn:fsd[rs2,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: c-fld_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fld[] is an RV32DC/RV64DC-only instruction that loads a double-precision
floating-point value from memory into floating-point register
rd′. It computes an effective address by adding the
zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in register
rs1′. It expands to
insn:fld[rd′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: c-fsd_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.fsd[] is an RV32DC/RV64DC-only instruction that stores a
double-precision floating-point value in floating-point register
rs2′ to memory. It computes an effective address by
adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in
register rs1′. It expands to
insn:fsd[rs2′,offset(rs1′)].

normative_rules.name: C_dep_Zca
normative_rules.text: The ext:c[] extension depends upon the extlink:zca[] extension.

normative_rules.name: C_dep_Zcf
normative_rules.text:
If XLEN=32 and the ext:f[] extension is present, the ext:c[] extension additionally
depends upon the extlink:zcf[] extension.

normative_rules.name: C_dep_Zcd
normative_rules.text:
If the ext:d[] extension is present, the ext:c[] extension additionally depends
upon the extlink:zcd[] extension.

normative_rules.name: c-lbu_op
normative_rules.text: loads a byte from the memory address formed by adding rs1' to the zero extended immediate uimm. The resulting byte is zero extended to XLEN bits and is written to rd'.

normative_rules.name: c-lhu_op
normative_rules.text: loads a halfword from the memory address formed by adding rs1' to the zero extended immediate uimm. The resulting halfword is zero extended to XLEN bits and is written to rd'.

normative_rules.name: c-lh_op
normative_rules.text: loads a halfword from the memory address formed by adding rs1' to the zero extended immediate uimm. The resulting halfword is sign extended to XLEN bits and is written to rd'.

normative_rules.name: c-sb_op
normative_rules.text: stores the least significant byte of rs2' to the memory address formed by adding rs1' to the zero extended immediate uimm.

normative_rules.name: c-sh_op
normative_rules.text: stores the least significant halfword of rs2' to the memory address formed by adding rs1' to the zero extended immediate uimm.

normative_rules.name: c-zext-b_op
normative_rules.text:
zero-extends the least-significant byte of the operand to XLEN bits by inserting zeros into all of
the bits more significant than 7.

normative_rules.name: c-sext-b_op
normative_rules.text:
sign-extends the least-significant byte in the operand to XLEN bits by copying the most-significant bit
in the byte (i.e., bit 7) to all of the more-significant bits.

normative_rules.name: c-zext-h_op
normative_rules.text:
zero-extends the least-significant halfword of the operand to XLEN bits by inserting zeros into all of
the bits more significant than 15.

normative_rules.name: c-sext-h_op
normative_rules.text:
sign-extends the least-significant halfword in the operand to XLEN bits by copying the most-significant bit
in the halfword (i.e., bit 15) to all of the more-significant bits.

normative_rules.name: c-zext-w_op
normative_rules.text:
zero-extends the least-significant word of the operand to XLEN bits by inserting zeros into all of
the bits more significant than 31.

normative_rules.name: c-not_op
normative_rules.text: takes the one's complement of rd'/rs1' and writes the result to the same register.

normative_rules.name: c-mul_op
normative_rules.text: multiplies XLEN bits of the source operands from rsd' and rs2' and writes the lowest XLEN bits of the result to rsd'.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_table
normative_rules.text:
Table jump uses a 256-entry XLEN wide table in instruction memory to contain function addresses.
The table must be a minimum of 64-byte aligned.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_endian
normative_rules.text: Table entries follow the current data endianness. This is different from normal instruction fetch which is always little-endian.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_entry_sz
normative_rules.text: The base of the table is in the csr:jvt[] CSR (see <<csrs-jvt>>), each table entry is XLEN bits.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_fetch
normative_rules.text: For a table jump instruction, the table entry that the instruction selects is considered an extension of the instruction itself.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_two_fetches
normative_rules.text:
Hence, the execution of a table jump instruction involves two instruction fetches, the first to read the instruction (insn:cm.jt[]/insn:cm.jalt[])
and the second to read from the jump vector table (JVT).

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_fetch_implicit_exec_perm
normative_rules.text:
Both instruction fetches are implicit reads, and both require
execute permission; read permission is irrelevant.

normative_rules.name: Zcmt_trap
normative_rules.text: If an exception occurs on either instruction fetch, xEPC is set to the PC of the table jump instruction,  xCAUSE is set as expected for the type of fault and xTVAL (if not set to zero) contains the fetch address which caused the fault.

normative_rules.name: jvt_reg
normative_rules.text: The csr:jvt[] register is an XLEN-bit WARL read/write register that holds the jump table configuration, consisting of the jump table base address (BASE) and the jump table mode (MODE).

normative_rules.name: jvt_op
normative_rules.text: If ext:zcmt[] is implemented then csr:jvt[] must also be implemented, but can contain a read-only value.

normative_rules.name: jvt_legal_values
normative_rules.text: If csr:jvt[] is writable, the set of values the register may hold can vary by implementation.

normative_rules.name: jvt_base_align
normative_rules.text: The value in the BASE field must always be aligned on a 64-byte boundary.

normative_rules.name: jvt_base_enc
normative_rules.text: Note that the CSR contains only bits XLEN-1 through 6 of the address base. When computing jump-table accesses, the lower six bits of base are filled with zeroes to obtain an XLEN-bit jump-table base address csr:jvt[base] that is always aligned on a 64-byte boundary.

normative_rules.name: jvt_base_vm
normative_rules.text: csr:jvt[base] is a virtual address, whenever virtual memory is enabled.

normative_rules.name: jvt_mode_acc
normative_rules.text: csr:jvt[mode] is a WARL field, so can only be programmed to modes which are implemented.

normative_rules.name: cm-jt_op
normative_rules.text: insn:cm.jt[] reads an entry from the jump vector table in memory and jumps to the address that was read.

normative_rules.name: cm-jalt_op
normative_rules.text: insn:cm.jalt[] reads an entry from the jump vector table in memory and jumps to the address that was read, linking to ra.

normative_rules.name: Zcmp_reexecute
normative_rules.text: Correct execution requires that sp refers to idempotent memory (also see ), because the core must be able to handle traps detected during the sequence. The entire insn:push[]/insn:pop[] sequence is re-executed after returning from the trap handler, and multiple traps are possible during the sequence.

normative_rules.name: Zcmp_trap
normative_rules.text: If a trap occurs during the sequence then xEPC is updated with the PC of the instruction, xTVAL (if not read-only-zero) updated with the bad address if it was an access fault and xCAUSE updated with the type of trap.

normative_rules.name: Zcmp_push_sp_commit
normative_rules.text: The stack pointer adjustment must only be committed only when it is certain that the entire insn:push[] instruction will commit.

normative_rules.name: Zcmp_bus_fault
normative_rules.text: Stores may also return imprecise faults from the bus. It is platform defined whether the core implementation waits for the bus responses before continuing to the final stage of the sequence, or handles errors responses after completing the insn:push[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: Zcmp_pop_sp_commit
normative_rules.text: The optional insn:li[a0,0], stack pointer adjustment and optional insn:ret[] must only be committed only when it is certain that the entire insn:pop[]/insn:popret[] instruction will commit.

normative_rules.name: cm-push_op
normative_rules.text:
pushes (stores) the registers in reg_list to the memory below the stack pointer,
and then creates the stack frame by decrementing the stack pointer by stack_adj,
including any additional stack space requested by the value of spimm.

normative_rules.name: cm-pop_op
normative_rules.text:
This instruction pops (loads) the registers in reg_list from stack memory,
and then adjusts the stack pointer by stack_adj.

normative_rules.name: cm-popretz_op
normative_rules.text: pops (loads) the registers in reg_list from stack memory, adjusts the stack pointer by stack_adj, moves zero into a0 and then returns to ra.

normative_rules.name: cm-popret_op
normative_rules.text: pops (loads) the registers in reg_list from stack memory, adjusts the stack pointer by stack_adj and then returns to ra.

normative_rules.name: cm-mvsa01_op
normative_rules.text: moves a0 into r1s' and a1 into r2s'.  r1s' and r2s' must be different.

normative_rules.name: cm-mvsa01_sreg
normative_rules.text: The encoding uses sreg number specifiers instead of xreg number specifiers to save encoding space.

normative_rules.name: cm-mva01s_op
normative_rules.text: moves r1s' into a0 and r2s' into a1.

normative_rules.name: cm-mva01s_sreg
normative_rules.text: The encoding uses sreg number specifiers instead of xreg number specifiers to save encoding space.

normative_rules.name: Zce_dep
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zce[] extension depends upon the extlink:zca[], extlink:zcb[],
extlink:zcmp[], and extlink:zcmt[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zce_dep_Zcf
normative_rules.text:
If XLEN=32 and the F extension is present, the ext:zce[] extension
additionally depends upon the extlink:zcf[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_c-ldsp_x0
normative_rules.text: For insn:c.ldsp[], usage of x0 as the destination is reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_c-ldsp_op
normative_rules.text: Loads stack-pointer relative 64-bit value into registers rd' and rd'+1. It computes its effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2. It expands to insn:ld[rd,offset(x2)]. insn:c.ldsp[] is only valid when rd≠x0; the code points with rd=x0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_c-sdsp_op
normative_rules.text: Stores a stack-pointer relative 64-bit value from registers rs2' and rs2'+1. It computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the stack pointer, x2. It expands to insn:sd[rs2,offset(x2)].

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_c-ld_op
normative_rules.text: Loads a 64-bit value into registers rd' and rd'+1. It computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in register rs1'.

normative_rules.name: Zilsd_c-sd_op
normative_rules.text: Stores a 64-bit value from registers rs2' and rs2'+1. It computes an effective address by adding the zero-extended offset, scaled by 8, to the base address in register rs1'. It expands to insn:sd[rs2',offset(rs1')].

normative_rules.name: Zcmop_op
normative_rules.text:
This section defines the ext:zcmop[] extension, which defines eight 16-bit MOP
instructions named insn:c.mop.n[], where N is an odd integer between 1 and
15, inclusive.

normative_rules.name: Zcmop_enc
normative_rules.text:
insn:c.mop.n[] is encoded in the reserved encoding space
corresponding to insn:c.lui[xN,0], as shown in <<norm:c-mop_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: Zcmop_instr_write
normative_rules.text:
Unlike the MOPs defined in the extlink:zimop[] extension, the insn:c.mop.n[] instructions
are defined to not write any register.

normative_rules.name: bitmanip_rv32_rv64
normative_rules.text: The bitmanip extensions are defined for RV32 and RV64.

normative_rules.name: bitmanip_w_suffix_semantics
normative_rules.text: The bitmanip extension follows the convention in RV64 that insn:*w[]-suffixed instructions (without a dot before the insn:w[]) ignore the upper 32 bits of their inputs, operate on the least-significant 32 bits as signed values, and produce a 32-bit signed result that is sign-extended to XLEN.

normative_rules.name: bitmanip_uw_suffix_semantics
normative_rules.text: Bitmanip instructions with the suffix insn:.uw[] have one operand that is an unsigned 32-bit value that is extracted from the least-significant 32 bits of the specified register.  Other than that, these perform full-XLEN operations.

normative_rules.name: bitmanip_bhw_suffix_semantics
normative_rules.text: Bitmanip instructions with the suffixes insn:.b[], insn:.h[], and insn:.w[] only look at the least-significant 8 bits, 16 bits, and 32 bits of the input (respectively) and produce an XLEN-wide result that is sign-extended or zero-extended, based on the specific instruction.

normative_rules.name: Zba_insns_tbl
normative_rules.text:
RV32|RV64|Mnemonic|Instruction
===
|✓|insn:add.uw[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶✓|✓|insn:sh1add[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶|✓|insn:sh1add.uw[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶✓|✓|insn:sh2add[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶|✓|insn:sh2add.uw[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶✓|✓|insn:sh3add[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶|✓|insn:sh3add.uw[rd,rs1,rs2]|¶|✓|insn:slli.uw[rd,rs1,imm]|
===

normative_rules.name: Zbb_sign_zero_extension_function
normative_rules.text: These instructions perform the sign extension or zero extension of the least-significant 8 bits or 16 bits of the source register.

normative_rules.name: Zbb_rotate_semantics
normative_rules.text:
where the shift-logical
instructions shift in zeros, the rotate instructions shift in the bits that were shifted out of the other side of the value.

normative_rules.name: Zbb_orc-b_semantics
normative_rules.text: insn:orc.b[] sets the bits of each byte in the result rd to all zeros if no bit within the respective byte of rs is set, or to all ones if any bit within the respective byte of rs is set.

normative_rules.name: Zbs_single_bit_functionality
normative_rules.text:
The single-bit instructions provide a mechanism to set, clear, invert, or extract
a single bit in a register. The bit is specified by its index.

normative_rules.name: B_extension_composition
normative_rules.text:
The ext:b[] standard extension comprises
instructions provided by the extlink:zba[], extlink:zbb[], and extlink:zbs[]
extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zbc_clmul_clmulh_results
normative_rules.text: insn:clmul[] produces the lower half of the carry-less product and insn:clmulh[] produces the upper half of the 2×XLEN carry-less product.

normative_rules.name: Zbc_clmulr_results
normative_rules.text: insn:clmulr[] produces bits 2×XLEN−2:XLEN-1 of the 2×XLEN carry-less product.

normative_rules.name: Zbkb_insns_tbl
normative_rules.text:
RV32|RV64|Mnemonic|Instruction
===
✓|✓|insn:rol[]|¶|✓|insn:rolw[]|¶✓|✓|insn:ror[]|¶✓|✓|insn:rori[]|¶|✓|insn:roriw[]|¶|✓|insn:rorw[]|¶✓|✓|insn:andn[]|¶✓|✓|insn:orn[]|¶✓|✓|insn:xnor[]|¶✓|✓|insn:pack[]|¶✓|✓|insn:packh[]|¶|✓|insn:packw[]|¶✓|✓|insn:brev8[]|¶✓|✓|insn:rev8[]|¶✓||insn:zip[]|¶✓||insn:unzip[]|
===

normative_rules.name: Zbkc_insns
normative_rules.text:
This extension is a subset of the ext:zbc[] extension, and only
provides insn:clmul[] and insn:clmulh[].

normative_rules.name: Zbkx_lookup_table_model
normative_rules.text:
These instructions implement a lookup table for 4- and 8-bit elements
inside the general purpose registers.

normative_rules.name: Zbkx_indexing_behavior
normative_rules.text:
Each element of the result is formed by using the
corresponding index element from rs2 to select an element from rs1, or zero if the
index element is out of bounds.

normative_rules.name: elen
normative_rules.text:
The maximum size in bits of a vector element that any operation can produce or consume, ELEN ≥ 8, which
must be a power of 2.

normative_rules.name: vlen
normative_rules.text: The number of bits in a single vector register, VLEN ≥ 8, which must be a power of 2, and must be no greater than 2^16^.

normative_rules.name: vreg_count
normative_rules.text: The vector extension adds 32 architectural vector registers, v0-v31 to the base scalar RISC-V ISA.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_sstatus_vs_op
normative_rules.text: A vector context status field, csr::[vs], is added to csr:mstatus[][10:9] and shadowed in csr:sstatus[][10:9].  It is defined analogously to the floating-point context status field, csr::[fs].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_op_off
normative_rules.text: Attempts to execute any vector instruction, or to access the vector CSRs, raise an illegal-instruction exception when csr:mstatus[vs] is set to Off.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_op_initial_clean
