normative_rules.text: When csr:mstatus[vs] is set to Initial or Clean, executing any instruction that changes vector state, including the vector CSRs, will change csr:mstatus[vs] to Dirty. Implementations may also change csr:mstatus[vs] from Initial or Clean to Dirty at any time, even when there is no change in vector state.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_vs_dirty_op
normative_rules.text: If csr:mstatus[vs] is Dirty, csr:mstatus[sd] is 1; otherwise, csr:mstatus[sd] is set in accordance with existing specifications.

normative_rules.name: mutable_misa_v
normative_rules.text: Implementations may have a writable csr:misa[v] field.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_exists
normative_rules.text:
Analogous to the
way in which the floating-point unit is handled, the csr:mstatus[vs]
field may exist even if csr:misa[v] is clear.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_vs_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: When the hypervisor extension is present, a vector context status field, csr::[vs], is added to csr:vsstatus[][10:9]. It is defined analogously to the floating-point context status field, csr::[fs].

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_vs_mstatus_vs_op_off
normative_rules.text: When V=1, both csr:vsstatus[vs] and csr:mstatus[vs] are in effect: attempts to execute any vector instruction, or to access the vector CSRs, raise an illegal-instruction exception when either field is set to Off.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_vs_mstatus_vs_op_active
normative_rules.text:
When V=1 and neither csr:vsstatus[vs] nor csr:mstatus[vs] is set to Off, executing
any instruction that changes vector state, including the vector CSRs, will
change both csr:mstatus[vs] and csr:vsstatus[vs] to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: hw_mstatus_vs_dirty_update
normative_rules.text:
Implementations may also change csr:mstatus[vs] or csr:vsstatus[vs] from Initial or
Clean to Dirty at any time, even when there is no change in vector state.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sd_op_vs
normative_rules.text: If csr:vsstatus[vs] is Dirty, csr:vsstatus[sd] is 1; otherwise, csr:vsstatus[sd] is set in accordance with existing specifications.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_op_vs
normative_rules.text: If csr:mstatus[vs] is Dirty, csr:mstatus[sd] is 1; otherwise, csr:mstatus[sd] is set in accordance with existing specifications.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_vs_exists
normative_rules.text: For implementations with a writable csr:misa[v] field, the csr:vsstatus[vs] field may exist even if csr:misa[v] is clear.

normative_rules.name: vtype_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The read-only XLEN-wide vector type CSR, csr:vtype[] provides the
default type used to interpret the contents of the vector register
file, and can only be updated by insn:vsetvli[], insn:vsetivli[], and insn:vsetvl[] instructions.

normative_rules.name: vtype_fields_sz
normative_rules.text: The csr:vtype[] register has five fields, csr::[vill], csr::[vma], csr::[vta], csr::[vsew], and csr::[vlmul].  Bits csr:vtype[][XLEN-2:8] should be written with zero, and non-zero values in this field are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vtype_vsew_op
normative_rules.text: The value in csr::[vsew] sets the dynamic selected element width (SEW).  By default, a vector register is viewed as being divided into VLEN/SEW elements.

normative_rules.name: vtype_lmul_val
normative_rules.text:
Implementations must support LMUL integer values of
1, 2, 4, and 8.

normative_rules.name: vtype_lmul_fval
normative_rules.text: Implementations must provide fractional LMUL settings that allow the narrowest supported type to occupy a fraction of a vector register corresponding to the ratio of the narrowest supported type’s width to the smaller of VLEN and the largest supported type’s width. In general, the requirement is to support LMUL ≥ SEWMIN/min(ELEN, VLEN), where SEWMIN is the narrowest supported SEW value, ELEN is the widest supported SEW value and VLEN is the number of bits in a vector register. In the standard extensions, SEWMIN=8.  For vector extensions with ELEN=32, fractional LMULs of 1/2 and 1/4 must be supported.  For vector extensions with ELEN=64 and ELEN ≤ VLEN, fractional LMULs of 1/2, 1/4, and 1/8 must be supported. For vector extensions with SEWMIN=8, ELEN=64 and VLEN=32, fractional LMULs of 1/2 and 1/4 must be supported.

normative_rules.name: vtype_sew_val
normative_rules.text: For a given supported fractional LMUL setting, implementations must support SEW settings between SEWMIN and LMUL * min(ELEN, VLEN), inclusive.

normative_rules.name: vtype_lmul_fval_rsv
normative_rules.text: The use of csr:vtype[] encodings with LMUL < SEWMIN/min(ELEN, VLEN) is reserved, but implementations can set csr::[vill] if they do not support these configurations.

normative_rules.name: lmul
normative_rules.text: LMUL is set by the signed csr::[vlmul] field in csr:vtype[] (i.e., LMUL = 2csr::[vlmul]).

normative_rules.name: vlmax
normative_rules.text: The derived value VLMAX = LMUL*VLEN/SEW represents the maximum number of elements that can be operated on with a single vector instruction given the current SEW and LMUL settings as shown in the table below.

normative_rules.name: vreg_offgroup_lmul2_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Instructions specifying an LMUL=2 vector register group
with an odd-numbered vector register are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vreg_offgroup_lmul4_rsv
normative_rules.text:
instructions specifying an LMUL=4 vector register group using vector
register numbers that are not multiples of four are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vreg_offgroup_lmul8_rsv
normative_rules.text:
instructions specifying an LMUL=8 vector register group
using register numbers that are not multiples of eight are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_lmul_indp
normative_rules.text: Mask registers are always contained in a single vector register, regardless of LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vtype_vta_vma_op
normative_rules.text: These two bits modify the behavior of destination tail elements and destination inactive masked-off elements respectively during the execution of vector instructions.  The tail and inactive sets contain element positions that are not receiving new results during a vector operation, as defined in .

normative_rules.name: vtype_vta_vma_val
normative_rules.text: All systems must support all four options:

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_tail_agn
normative_rules.text: Mask destination tail elements are always treated as tail-agnostic, regardless of the setting of csr::[vta].

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_op
normative_rules.text: When a set is marked undisturbed, the corresponding set of destination elements in a vector register group retain the value they previously held.

normative_rules.name: vreg_agnostic_op
normative_rules.text: When a set is marked agnostic, the corresponding set of destination elements in any vector destination operand can either retain the value they previously held, or are overwritten with 1s.  Within a single vector instruction, each destination element can be either left undisturbed or overwritten with 1s, in any combination, and the pattern of undisturbed or overwritten with 1s is not required to be deterministic when the instruction is executed with the same inputs.

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_tail_op
normative_rules.text: In addition, except for mask load instructions, any element in the tail of a mask result can also be written with the value the mask-producing operation would have calculated with csr:vl[]=VLMAX. Furthermore, for mask-logical instructions and insn:vmsbf.m[], insn:vmsif.m[], insn:vmsof.m[] mask-manipulation instructions, any element in the tail of the result can be written with the value the mask-producing operation would have calculated with csr:vl[]=VLEN, SEW=8, and LMUL=8 (i.e., all bits of the mask register can be overwritten).

normative_rules.name: vtype_vill_op
normative_rules.text: If the csr::[vill] bit is set, then any attempt to execute a vector instruction that depends upon csr:vtype[] will raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: vl_acc
normative_rules.text: The XLEN-bit-wide read-only csr:vl[] CSR can only be updated by the insn:vset*[] instructions, and the fault-only-first vector load instruction variants.

normative_rules.name: vl_op
normative_rules.text: The csr:vl[] register holds an unsigned integer specifying the number of elements to be updated with results from a vector instruction, as further detailed in .

normative_rules.name: vlenb_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The XLEN-bit-wide read-only CSR csr:vlenb[] holds the value VLEN/8, i.e., the vector register length in bytes.

normative_rules.name: vstart_acc_sz
normative_rules.text: The XLEN-bit-wide read-write csr:vstart[] CSR specifies the index of the first element to be executed by a vector instruction, as described in .

normative_rules.name: vstart_op
normative_rules.text:
All vector instructions are defined to begin execution with the
element number given in the csr:vstart[] CSR, leaving earlier elements in
the destination vector undisturbed

normative_rules.name: vstart_update
normative_rules.text:
reset the csr:vstart[] CSR to
zero at the end of execution.

normative_rules.name: vstart_unmodified
normative_rules.text: csr:vstart[] is not modified by vector instructions that raise illegal-instruction exceptions.

normative_rules.name: vstart_sz_writable
normative_rules.text: The csr:vstart[] CSR is defined to have only enough writable bits to hold the largest element index (one less than the maximum VLMAX).

normative_rules.name: vstart_val_rsv
normative_rules.text: The use of csr:vstart[] values greater than the largest element index for the current csr:vtype[] setting is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vstart_vtype_dep
normative_rules.text: Implementations are permitted to raise illegal-instruction exceptions when attempting to execute a vector instruction with a value of csr:vstart[] that the implementation can never produce when executing that same instruction with the same csr:vtype[] setting.

normative_rules.name: vxrm_val_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: The vector fixed-point rounding-mode register holds a two-bit read-write rounding-mode field in the least-significant bits (csr:vxrm[][1:0]).  The upper bits, csr:vxrm[][XLEN-1:2], should be written as zeros.

normative_rules.name: vcsr_vxrm_op
normative_rules.text: The vector fixed-point rounding-mode is given a separate CSR address to allow independent access, but is also reflected as a field in csr:vcsr[].

normative_rules.name: vxrm_op
normative_rules.text: The fixed-point rounding algorithm is specified as follows. Suppose the pre-rounding result is v, and d bits of that result are to be rounded off. Then the rounded result is (v >> d) + r, where r depends on the rounding mode as specified in the following table.

normative_rules.name: vxsat_op_acc_sz
normative_rules.text: The csr:vxsat[] CSR has a single read-write least-significant bit (csr:vxsat[][0]) that indicates if a fixed-point instruction has had to saturate an output value to fit into a destination format. The remaining bits, csr:vxsat[][XLEN-1:1], should be written as zeros.

normative_rules.name: vcsr_vxsat_op
normative_rules.text: The csr:vxsat[] bit is mirrored in csr:vcsr[].

normative_rules.name: vcsr_vxrm_vxsat_acc
normative_rules.text: The csr:vxrm[] and csr:vxsat[] separate CSRs can also be accessed via fields in the XLEN-bit-wide vector control and status CSR, csr:vcsr[].

normative_rules.name: vector_reset_state
normative_rules.text:
The vector extension must have a consistent state at reset.  In
particular, csr:vtype[] and csr:vl[] must have values that can be read and
then restored with a single csr:vsetvl[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: vreg_lmul1_op
normative_rules.text: When LMUL=1, elements are simply packed in order from the least-significant to most-significant bits of the vector register.

normative_rules.name: vreg_flmul_op
normative_rules.text: When LMUL < 1, only the first LMUL*VLEN/SEW elements in the vector register are used.  The remaining space in the vector register is treated as part of the tail, and hence must obey the vta setting.

normative_rules.name: vreg_lmulge2_op
normative_rules.text: When vector registers are grouped, the elements of the vector register group are packed contiguously in element order beginning with the lowest-numbered vector register and moving to the next-highest-numbered vector register in the group once each vector register is filled.

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_vtype_indp
normative_rules.text: A vector mask occupies only one vector register regardless of SEW and LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_sz
normative_rules.text: Each element is allocated a single mask bit in a mask vector register. The mask bit for element i is located in bit i of the mask register, independent of SEW or LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vreg_scalar_lmul_indp
normative_rules.text:
Any vector register can be used to hold a scalar regardless
of the current LMUL setting.

normative_rules.name: eew_emul
normative_rules.text: Each vector operand has an effective element width (EEW) and an effective LMUL (EMUL) that is used to determine the size and location of all the elements within a vector register group.  By default, for most operands of most instructions, EEW=SEW and EMUL=LMUL.

normative_rules.name: eew_emul_sew_lmul_dep
normative_rules.text: EEW/EMUL = SEW/LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vnarrowing_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
Narrowing instructions have a source operand that has
EEW=2*SEW and EMUL=2*LMUL but with a destination where EEW=SEW and EMUL=LMUL.

normative_rules.name: emul_offgroup_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Using other than the lowest-numbered
vector register to specify a vector register group is a reserved
encoding.

normative_rules.name: vreg_source_eew_rsv
normative_rules.text: A vector register cannot be used to provide source operands with more than one EEW for a single instruction.  A mask register source is considered to have EEW=1 for this constraint.  An encoding that would result in the same vector register being read with two or more different EEWs, including when the vector register appears at different positions within two or more vector register groups, is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vreg_overlap_legal
normative_rules.text: A destination vector register group can overlap a source vector register group only if one of the following holds:

normative_rules.name: vreg_mask_overlap
normative_rules.text: For the purpose of determining register group overlap constraints, mask elements have EEW=1.

normative_rules.name: vreg_overlap_rsv
normative_rules.text: Any instruction encoding that violates the overlap constraints is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vreg_overlap_agn
normative_rules.text: When source and destination registers overlap and have different EEW, the instruction is mask- and tail-agnostic, regardless of the setting of the csr::[vta] and csr::[vma] bits in csr:vtype[].

normative_rules.name: emul_rsv
normative_rules.text: The largest vector register group used by an instruction can not be greater than 8 vector registers (i.e., EMUL≤8), and if a vector instruction would require greater than 8 vector registers in a group, the instruction encoding is reserved.  For example, a widening operation that produces a widened vector register group result when LMUL=8 is reserved as this would imply a result EMUL=16.

normative_rules.name: vreg_scalar_emul
normative_rules.text: Widened scalar values, e.g., input and output to a widening reduction operation, are held in the first element of a vector register and have EMUL=1. If an implementation supports EEW > VLEN, EEW-wide widened scalar values are held in a vector register group with EMUL = EEW/VLEN.

normative_rules.name: vmask_inactive_op
normative_rules.text:
Element operations
that are masked off (inactive) never generate exceptions.

normative_rules.name: vmask_agn_op
normative_rules.text:
The
destination vector register elements corresponding to masked-off
elements are handled with either a mask-undisturbed or mask-agnostic
policy depending on the setting of the csr::[vma] bit in csr:vtype[]

normative_rules.name: vreg_vmask
normative_rules.text: The mask value used to control execution of a masked vector instruction is always supplied by vector register v0.

normative_rules.name: vreg_vmask_rsv
normative_rules.text: The destination vector register group for a masked vector instruction cannot overlap the source mask register (v0), unless the destination vector register is being written with a mask value (e.g., compares) or the scalar result of a reduction.  These instruction encodings are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vmask_vm_enc
normative_rules.text: Where available, masking is encoded in a single-bit vm field in the  instruction (inst[25]).

normative_rules.name: vector_prestart_element
normative_rules.text: The prestart elements do not raise exceptions and do not update the destination vector register.

normative_rules.name: vector_active_element
normative_rules.text: The active elements can raise exceptions and update the destination vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vector_inactive_element
normative_rules.text: The inactive elements do not raise exceptions and do not update any destination vector register group unless masked agnostic is specified (csr:vtype[vma]=1), in which case inactive elements may be overwritten with 1s.

normative_rules.name: vector_tail_element
normative_rules.text: The tail elements do not raise exceptions, and do not update any destination vector register group unless tail agnostic is specified (csr:vtype[vta]=1), in which case tail elements may be overwritten with 1s, or with the result of the instruction in the case of mask-producing instructions except for mask loads.  When LMUL < 1, the tail includes the elements past VLMAX that are held in the same vector register.

normative_rules.name: vstart_vl_dep
normative_rules.text: When csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[], there are no body elements, and no elements are updated in any destination vector register group, including that no tail elements are updated with agnostic values.

normative_rules.name: vstart_vl_scalar_indp
normative_rules.text: Instructions that write an x register or f register do so even when csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[], including when csr:vl[]=0.

normative_rules.name: vset_op
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vsetvli[], insn:vsetivli[], and insn:vsetvl[] instructions set the csr:vtype[] and csr:vl[] CSRs based on
their arguments, and write the new value of csr:vl[] into rd.

normative_rules.name: vset_vstart
normative_rules.text: The configuration-setting instructions do not depend on csr:vstart[]; they reset csr:vstart[] to zero.

normative_rules.name: vtype_acc
normative_rules.text: The new csr:vtype[] value is encoded in the immediate fields of insn:vsetvli[] and insn:vsetivli[], and in the rs2 register for insn:vsetvl[].

normative_rules.name: vtype_vill_val
normative_rules.text:
If the csr:vtype[] value is not supported by the implementation, then
the csr::[vill] bit is set in csr:vtype[], the remaining bits in csr:vtype[] are
set to zero

normative_rules.name: vtype_vstart_op
normative_rules.text: the csr:vl[] register is also set to zero.

normative_rules.name: vtype_vill_val_vill
normative_rules.text: A csr:vtype[] value with csr::[vill] set is treated as an unsupported configuration.

normative_rules.name: vtype_vill_all_bits
normative_rules.text: Implementations must consider all bits of the csr:vtype[] value to determine if the configuration is supported.  An unsupported value in any location within the csr:vtype[] value must result in csr::[vill] being set.

normative_rules.name: vsetvl_op
normative_rules.text: When rs1 is not x0, the AVL is an unsigned integer held in the x register specified by rs1, and the new csr:vl[] value is also written to the x register specified by rd.

normative_rules.name: vsetvl_op_rs1_x0_rd_nx0
normative_rules.text: When rs1=x0 but rd≠x0, the maximum unsigned integer value (~0) is used as the AVL, and the resulting VLMAX is written to vl and also to the x register specified by rd.

normative_rules.name: vsetvl_op_rs1_x0_rd_x0
normative_rules.text: When rs1=x0 and rd=x0, the instructions operate as if the current vector length in csr:vl[] is used as the AVL, and the resulting value is written to csr:vl[], but not to a destination register.  This form can only be used when VLMAX and hence csr:vl[] is not actually changed by the new SEW/LMUL ratio.

normative_rules.name: vtype_vset_rsv
normative_rules.text: Use of the instructions with a new SEW/LMUL ratio that would result in a change of VLMAX is reserved. Use of the instructions is also reserved if csr::[vill] was 1 beforehand.

normative_rules.name: reserved_vill_set
normative_rules.text: Implementations may set csr::[vill] in either case.

normative_rules.name: vsetivli_op
normative_rules.text: For the insn:vsetivli[] instruction, the AVL is encoded as a 5-bit zero-extended immediate (0—​31) in the rs1 field.

normative_rules.name: vl_val_lead_in
normative_rules.text: The insn:vset*[] instructions first set VLMAX according to their csr:vtype[] argument, then set csr:vl[] obeying the following constraints:

normative_rules.name: vl_val_list
normative_rules.text:
csr:vl[] = AVL if AVL ≤ VLMAX
ceil(AVL / 2) ≤ vl ≤ VLMAX if AVL < (2 * VLMAX)
csr:vl[] = VLMAX if AVL ≥ (2 * VLMAX)
Deterministic on any given implementation for same input AVL and VLMAX values
These specific properties follow from the prior rules:

csr:vl[] = 0 if  AVL = 0
csr:vl[] > 0 if AVL > 0
csr:vl[] ≤ VLMAX
csr:vl[] ≤ AVL
a value read from csr:vl[] when used as the AVL argument to insn:vset*[] results in the same value in csr:vl[], provided the resultant VLMAX equals the value of VLMAX at the time that csr:vl[] was read

normative_rules.name: vector_load_store_semantics
normative_rules.text:
Vector loads and stores move values between vector registers and
memory.

normative_rules.name: vector_masked_memory_access
normative_rules.text:
Vector loads and stores can be masked, and they only access memory or raise
exceptions for active elements.

normative_rules.name: vector_masked_inactive_behavior
normative_rules.text:
Masked vector loads do not update inactive elements in the destination vector
register group, unless masked agnostic is specified (csr:vtype[vma]=1).

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_vstart
normative_rules.text: All vector loads and stores may generate and accept a non-zero csr:vstart[] value.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_strided_eew
normative_rules.text: Vector memory unit-stride and constant-stride operations directly encode EEW of the data to be transferred statically in the instruction to reduce the number of csr:vtype[] changes when accessing memory in a mixed-width routine.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_indexed_eew
normative_rules.text: Indexed operations use the explicit EEW encoding in the instruction to set the size of the indices used, and use SEW/LMUL to specify the data width.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_base_stride_regtype
normative_rules.text:
Vector load/store base
registers and strides are taken from the x registers.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_base
normative_rules.text: The base effective address for all vector accesses is given by the contents of the x register named in rs1.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_unit_stride_op
normative_rules.text: Vector unit-stride operations access elements stored contiguously in memory starting from the base effective address.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_constant_stride_op
normative_rules.text: Vector constant-stride operations access the first memory element at the base effective address, and then access subsequent elements at address increments given by the byte offset contained in the x register specified by rs2.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_indexed_op
normative_rules.text: Vector indexed operations add the contents of each element of the vector offset operand specified by vs2 to the base effective address to give the effective address of each element.  The data vector register group has EEW=SEW, EMUL=LMUL, while the offset vector register group has EEW encoded in the instruction and EMUL=(EEW/SEW)*LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_bytewise
normative_rules.text: The vector offset operand is treated as a vector of byte-address offsets.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_xlen_dep
normative_rules.text: If the vector offset elements are narrower than XLEN, they are zero-extended to XLEN before adding to the base effective address.  If the vector offset elements are wider than XLEN, the least-significant XLEN bits are used in the address calculation.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_eew_rsv
normative_rules.text: If the implementation does not support the EEW of the offset elements, the instruction is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_stride_ordered_op
normative_rules.text: Vector unit-stride and constant-stride memory accesses do not guarantee ordering between individual element accesses.  The vector indexed load and store memory operations have two forms, ordered and unordered.  The indexed-ordered variants preserve element ordering on memory accesses.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_stride_unordered_op
normative_rules.text: For unordered instructions (mop[1:0]!=11) there is no guarantee on element access order.  If the accesses are to a strongly ordered IO region, the element accesses can be initiated in any order.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_stride_unordered_precise
normative_rules.text: For implementations with precise vector traps, exceptions on indexed-unordered stores must also be precise.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_nf_op
normative_rules.text: The nf[2:0] field encodes the number of fields in each segment.  For regular vector loads and stores, nf=0, indicating that a single value is moved between a vector register group and memory at each element position.  Larger values in the nf field are used to access multiple contiguous fields within a segment as described below in .

normative_rules.name: vector_wholels_nf_op
normative_rules.text: The nf[2:0] field also encodes the number of whole vector registers to transfer for the whole vector register load/store instructions.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
Vector loads and stores have an EEW encoded directly in the
instruction.  The corresponding EMUL is calculated as EMUL =
(EEW/SEW)*LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_emul_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If the EMUL would be out of range (EMUL>8 or
EMUL<1/8), the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_emul_offgroup_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The vector register
groups must have legal register specifiers for the selected EMUL,
otherwise the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_indexed_eew_emul
normative_rules.text: Vector unit-stride and constant-stride use the EEW/EMUL encoded in the instruction for the data values, while vector indexed loads and stores use the EEW/EMUL encoded in the instruction for the index values and the SEW/LMUL encoded in csr:vtype[] for the data values.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_ins_req
normative_rules.text: Implementations must provide vector loads and stores with EEWs corresponding to all supported SEW settings.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_ins_rsv
normative_rules.text: Vector load/store encodings for unsupported EEW widths are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_mew_rsv
normative_rules.text: The mew bit (inst[28]) when set is expected to be used to encode expanded memory sizes of 128 bits and above, but these encodings are currently reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_unit_stride_mask
normative_rules.text: Additional unit-stride mask load and store instructions are provided to transfer mask values to/from memory.  These operate similarly to unmasked byte loads or stores (EEW=8), except that the effective vector length is evl = ceil(csr:vl[]/8) (i.e. EMUL=1), and the destination register is always written with a tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_neg_zero_stride
normative_rules.text: Negative and zero strides are supported.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_constant_stride_unordered
normative_rules.text: Element accesses within a constant-stride instruction are unordered with respect to each other.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_constant_stride_x0
normative_rules.text: When rs2=x0, then an implementation is allowed, but not required, to perform fewer memory operations than the number of active elements, and may perform different numbers of memory operations across different dynamic executions of the same static instruction.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_trigger
normative_rules.text:
The unit-stride fault-only-first load instructions are used to
vectorize loops with data-dependent exit conditions (while loops).
These instructions execute as a regular load except that they will
only take a trap caused by a synchronous exception on element 0.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_op
normative_rules.text: If element 0 raises an exception, csr:vl[] is not modified, and the trap is taken.  If an element > 0 raises an exception, the corresponding trap is not taken, and the vector length csr:vl[] is reduced to the index of the element that would have raised an exception.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_overwrite_past_trap
normative_rules.text:
Load instructions may overwrite active destination vector register
group elements past the element index at which the trap is reported.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_past_trap
normative_rules.text: Similarly, fault-only-first load instructions may update active destination elements past the element that causes trimming of the vector length (but not past the original vector length).  The values of these spurious updates do not have to correspond to the values in memory at the addressed memory locations.  Non-idempotent memory locations can only be accessed when it is known the corresponding element load operation will not be restarted due to a trap or vector-length trimming.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_no_exception
normative_rules.text: Even when an exception is not raised, implementations are permitted to process fewer than csr:vl[] elements and reduce csr:vl[] accordingly, but if csr:vstart[]=0 and csr:vl[]>0, then at least one element must be processed.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_interrupt_behavior
normative_rules.text: When the fault-only-first instruction takes a trap due to an interrupt, implementations should not reduce csr:vl[] and should instead set a csr:vstart[] value.

normative_rules.name: nfields
normative_rules.text: The three-bit nf field in the vector instruction encoding is an unsigned integer that contains one less than the number of fields per segment, NFIELDS.

normative_rules.name: emul_nfields_rsv
normative_rules.text: The EMUL setting must be such that EMUL * NFIELDS ≤ 8, otherwise the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: nfields_op
normative_rules.text: Each field will be held in successively numbered vector register groups.  When EMUL>1, each field will occupy a vector register group held in multiple successively numbered vector registers, and the vector register group for each field must follow the usual vector register alignment constraints (e.g., when EMUL=2 and NFIELDS=4, each field’s vector register group must start at an even vector register, but does not have to start at a multiple of 8 vector register number).

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_rsv
normative_rules.text: If the vector register numbers accessed by the segment load or store would increment past 31, then the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_op
normative_rules.text: The csr:vl[] register gives the number of segments to move, which is equal to the number of elements transferred to each vector register group.  Masking is also applied at the level of whole segments.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_unordered
normative_rules.text: For segment loads and stores, the individual memory accesses used to access fields within each segment are unordered with respect to each other even for ordered indexed segment loads and stores.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_vstart_dep
normative_rules.text: The csr:vstart[] value is in units of whole segments.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_partial_access
normative_rules.text:
If a trap occurs during
access to a segment, it is implementation-defined whether a subset
of the faulting segment's accesses are performed before the trap is taken.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_unit_stride_op
normative_rules.text: The vector unit-stride load and store segment instructions move packed contiguous segments into multiple destination vector register groups.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_unit_stride_vd_vs3
normative_rules.text: For loads, the vd register will hold the first field loaded from the segment.  For stores, the vs3 register is read to provide the first field to be stored to each segment.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_ff_unit_stride_op
normative_rules.text: For fault-only-first segment loads, if an exception is detected partway through accessing the zeroth segment, the trap is taken. If an exception is detected partway through accessing a subsequent segment, csr:vl[] is reduced to the index of that segment.

normative_rules.name: vector_ff_seg_partial_access
normative_rules.text: In both cases, it is implementation-defined whether a subset of the segment is loaded.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_ff_overload
normative_rules.text: These instructions may overwrite destination vector register group elements past the point at which a trap is reported or past the point at which vector length is trimmed.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_constant_stride_op
normative_rules.text: Vector constant-stride segment loads and stores move contiguous segments where each segment is separated by the byte-stride offset given in the rs2 argument.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_constant_stride_unordered
normative_rules.text: Accesses to the fields within each segment can occur in any order, including the case where the byte stride is such that segments overlap in memory.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_indexed_op
normative_rules.text: Vector indexed segment loads and stores move contiguous segments where each segment is located at an address given by adding the scalar base address in the rs1 field to byte offsets in vector register vs2.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_indexed_unordered
normative_rules.text: However, even for the ordered form, accesses to the fields within an individual segment are not ordered with respect to each other.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_indexed_eew_emul_op
normative_rules.text: The data vector register group has EEW=SEW, EMUL=LMUL, while the index vector register group has EEW encoded in the instruction with EMUL=(EEW/SEW)*LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_indexed_emul_nfields_val
normative_rules.text: The EMUL * NFIELDS ≤ 8 constraint applies to the data vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_indexed_vreg_rsv
normative_rules.text: For vector indexed segment loads, the destination vector register groups cannot overlap the source vector register group (specified by vs2), else the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_wholereg_eew
normative_rules.text: The load instructions have the element width encoded in the mew and width fields following the pattern of regular unit-stride loads. EEW is computed as EEW=min(VLEN*NFIELDS, EEW_encoded).

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_wholereg_op
normative_rules.text:
NFIELDS
indicates the number of vector registers to transfer, numbered
successively after the base.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_wholereg_nf_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Only NFIELDS values of 1, 2, 4, 8 are
supported, with other values reserved.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_wholereg_op_cont
normative_rules.text:
When multiple registers are
transferred, the lowest-numbered vector register is held in the
lowest-numbered memory addresses and successive vector register
numbers are placed contiguously in memory.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_seg_wholereg_evl
normative_rules.text: The instructions operate with an effective vector length, evl=NFIELDS*VLEN/EEW, regardless of current settings in csr:vtype[] and csr:vl[].  The usual property that no elements are written if csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[] does not apply to these instructions. Similarly, the property that the instructions are reserved if csr:vstart[] exceeds the largest element index for the current csr:vtype[] setting does not apply. Instead, the instructions are reserved if csr:vstart[] ≥ evl.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_wholereg_misaligned_exception
normative_rules.text: Implementations are allowed to raise a misaligned address exception on whole register loads and stores if the base address is not naturally aligned to the larger of the size of the encoded EEW in bytes (EEW/8) or the implementation’s smallest supported SEW size in bytes (SEWMIN/8).

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_misaligned_exception
normative_rules.text: If an element accessed by a vector memory instruction is not naturally aligned to the size of the element, either the element is transferred successfully or an address-misaligned exception is raised on that element.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_scalar_misaligned_independence
normative_rules.text: Support for misaligned vector memory accesses is independent of an implementation’s support for misaligned scalar memory accesses.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_scalar_misaligned_dependence
normative_rules.text: Vector misaligned memory accesses follow the same rules for atomicity as scalar misaligned memory accesses.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_program_order
normative_rules.text: Vector memory instructions appear to execute in program order on the local hart.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_rvwmo
normative_rules.text: Vector memory instructions follow RVWMO at the instruction level.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_rvtso
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ztso[] extension is implemented, vector memory instructions additionally follow RVTSO at the instruction level.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_indexed_ordered_ordered
normative_rules.text: Except for vector indexed-ordered loads and stores, element operations are unordered within the instruction.

normative_rules.name: vector_ls_indexed_ordered_rvwmo
normative_rules.text: Vector indexed-ordered loads and stores read and write elements from/to memory in element order respectively, obeying RVWMO at the element level.

normative_rules.name: vl_control_dependency
normative_rules.text: Instructions affected by the vector length register csr:vl[] have a control dependency on csr:vl[], rather than a data dependency.

normative_rules.name: vmask_control_dependency
normative_rules.text: Similarly, masked vector instructions have a control dependency on the source mask register, rather than a data dependency.

normative_rules.name: V_fp_frm
normative_rules.text: All vector floating-point operations use the dynamic rounding mode in the csr:frm[] register.

normative_rules.name: V_inv_frm_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Use of the frm field
when it contains an invalid rounding mode by any vector floating-point
instruction--even those that do not depend on the rounding mode--is
reserved, irrespective of the values of csr:vstart[] and csr:vl[].

normative_rules.name: vop-vv_vreg_vs2_vs1
normative_rules.text: Vector-vector operations take two vectors of operands from vector register groups specified by vs2 and vs1 respectively.

normative_rules.name: vop-vx_vop-vi_vreg_vs2
normative_rules.text: the vector register group operand is specified by vs2.

normative_rules.name: vop-vi_imm_5bit
normative_rules.text:
For integer operations, the scalar can be a 5-bit immediate, imm[4:0], encoded
in the rs1 field.  The value is sign-extended to SEW bits, unless otherwise specified.

normative_rules.name: vop-vx_xreg_rs1
normative_rules.text:
For integer operations, the scalar can be taken from the scalar x
register specified by rs1.

normative_rules.name: vop-vx_rs1_trunc_lsb_sewbits
normative_rules.text: If XLEN>SEW, the least-significant SEW bits of the x register are used, unless otherwise specified.

normative_rules.name: vop-vx_rs1_sext_sewbits
normative_rules.text:
If XLEN<SEW, the value from the x register is sign-extended to SEW
bits.

normative_rules.name: vfop_freg
normative_rules.text:
For floating-point operations, the scalar can be taken from a scalar
f register.

normative_rules.name: vfop_freg_nanbox_lsb_sewbits
normative_rules.text:
If FLEN > SEW, the value in the f registers is
checked for a valid NaN-boxed value, in which case the
least-significant SEW bits of the f register are used, else the
canonical NaN value is used.

normative_rules.name: V_fp_eew_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Vector instructions where any
floating-point vector operand's EEW is not a supported floating-point
type width (which includes when FLEN < SEW) are reserved.

normative_rules.name: V_masked
normative_rules.text:
Vector arithmetic instructions are masked under control of the vm
field.

normative_rules.name: vwop_vd_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
A few vector arithmetic instructions are defined to be widening
operations where the destination vector register group has EEW=2*SEW
and EMUL=2*LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vnop_vd_vs2_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
A few instructions are provided to convert double-width source vectors
into single-width destination vectors.  These instructions convert a
vector register group specified by vs2 with EEW/EMUL=2*SEW/2*LMUL to a vector register
group with the current SEW/LMUL setting.

normative_rules.name: vnop_vs1_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
Where there is a second
source vector register group (specified by vs1), this has the same
(narrower) width as the result (i.e., EEW=SEW).

normative_rules.name: vadd_vsub_op
normative_rules.text: Vector integer add and subtract are provided.

normative_rules.name: vrsub_op
normative_rules.text:
Reverse-subtract
instructions are also provided for the vector-scalar forms.

normative_rules.name: vwaddu_vwadd_vwsubu_vwsub_op
normative_rules.text:
The widening add/subtract instructions are provided in both signed and
unsigned variants, depending on whether the narrower source operands
are first sign- or zero-extended before forming the double-width sum.

normative_rules.name: vsext_vzext_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector integer extension instructions zero- or sign-extend a
source vector integer operand with EEW less than SEW to fill SEW-sized
elements in the destination.

normative_rules.name: vsext_vzext_vs_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
The EEW of the source is 1/2, 1/4, or
1/8 of SEW, while EMUL of the source is (EEW/SEW)*LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vsext_vzext_vd_eew_emul
normative_rules.text:
The
destination has EEW equal to SEW and EMUL equal to LMUL.

normative_rules.name: vsext_vzext_ill_eew_emul_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If the source EEW is not a supported width, or source EMUL would be
below the minimum legal LMUL, the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vmadc_vmsbc_vadc_vsbc_carry_v0
normative_rules.text:
The carry inputs and outputs are represented using the mask register
layout as described in <<sec-mask-register-layout>>.  Due to
encoding constraints, the carry input must come from the implicit v0
register,

normative_rules.name: vadc_vsbc_op
normative_rules.text:
insn:vadc[] and insn:vsbc[] add or subtract the source operands and the carry-in or
borrow-in, and write the result to vector register vd.

normative_rules.name: vadc_vsbc_masked_write_all_elem
normative_rules.text:
These instructions are encoded as masked instructions (vm=0), but they operate
on and write back all body elements.

normative_rules.name: vadc_vsbc_unmasked_rsv
normative_rules.text: Encodings corresponding to the unmasked versions (vm=1) are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vmadc_vmsbc_op_masked
normative_rules.text:
insn:vmadc[] and insn:vmsbc[] add or subtract the source operands, optionally
add the carry-in or subtract the borrow-in if masked (vm=0), and
write the resulting carry-out or borrow-out back to mask register vd.

normative_rules.name: vmadc_vmsbc_op_unmasked
normative_rules.text: If unmasked (vm=1), there is no carry-in or borrow-in.

normative_rules.name: vmadc_vmsbc_masked_write_all_elem
normative_rules.text:
These instructions
operate on and write back all body elements, even if masked.

normative_rules.name: vmadc_vmsbc_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
Because these
instructions produce a mask value, they always operate with a
tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmsbc_borrow_neg
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vmsbc[], the borrow is defined to be 1 iff the difference, prior to
truncation, is negative.

normative_rules.name: vadc_vsbc_vd_v0_rsv
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vadc[] and insn:vsbc[], the instruction encoding is reserved if the
destination vector register is v0.

normative_rules.name: vand_vor_vxor_op
normative_rules.text:
# Bitwise logical operations.
vand.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm   # Vector-vector
vand.vx vd, vs2, rs1, vm   # vector-scalar
vand.vi vd, vs2, imm, vm   # vector-immediate

vor.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm    # Vector-vector
vor.vx vd, vs2, rs1, vm    # vector-scalar
vor.vi vd, vs2, imm, vm    # vector-immediate

vxor.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm    # Vector-vector
vxor.vx vd, vs2, rs1, vm    # vector-scalar
vxor.vi vd, vs2, imm, vm    # vector-immediate

normative_rules.name: vsll_vsrl_vsra_op
normative_rules.text:
A full set of vector shift instructions are provided, including
logical shift left (insn:sll[]), and logical (zero-extending insn:srl[]) and
arithmetic (sign-extending insn:sra[]) shift right.  The data to be shifted
is in the vector register group specified by vs2 and the shift
amount value can come from a vector register group vs1, a scalar
integer register rs1, or a zero-extended 5-bit immediate.

normative_rules.name: vsll_vsrl_vsra_shamt
normative_rules.text:
Only the low
lg2(SEW) bits of the shift-amount value are used to control the shift
amount.

normative_rules.name: vnsrl_vnsra_op
normative_rules.text:
The narrowing right shifts extract a smaller field from a wider
operand and have both zero-extending (insn:srl[]) and sign-extending
(insn:sra[]) forms.  The shift amount can come from a vector register
group, or a scalar x register, or a zero-extended 5-bit immediate.

normative_rules.name: vnsrl_vnsra_shamt
normative_rules.text:
The low lg2(2*SEW) bits of the shift-amount value are
used (e.g., the low 6 bits for a SEW=64-bit to SEW=32-bit narrowing
operation).

normative_rules.name: vmseq_vmsne_vmsltu_vmslt_vmsleu_vmsle_vmsgtu_vmsgt_op
normative_rules.text:
The following integer compare instructions write 1 to the destination
mask register element if the comparison evaluates to true, and 0
otherwise.  The destination mask vector is always held in a single
vector register, with a layout of elements as described in
<<sec-mask-register-layout>>.

normative_rules.name: vmseq_vmsne_vmsltu_vmslt_vmsleu_vmsle_vmsgtu_vmsgt_vd_v0_legal
normative_rules.text:
The destination mask vector register
may be the same as the source vector mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: vmseq_vmsne_vmsltu_vmslt_vmsleu_vmsle_vmsgtu_vmsgt_maskundisturbed
normative_rules.text: Compares effectively AND in the mask under a mask-undisturbed policy if the destination register is v0,

normative_rules.name: vmseq_vmsne_vmsltu_vmslt_vmsleu_vmsle_vmsgtu_vmsgt_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
Compares write mask registers, and so always operate under a
tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vminu_vmin_vmaxu_vmax_op
normative_rules.text:
Signed and unsigned integer minimum and maximum instructions are
supported.

normative_rules.name: vmul_vmulh_vmulhu_vmulhsu_op
normative_rules.text:
The single-width multiply instructions perform a SEW-bit*SEW-bit
multiply to generate a 2*SEW-bit product, then return one half of the
product in the SEW-bit-wide destination.  The mul versions write
the low half of the product to the destination register, while the
mulh versions write the high half of the product to the
destination register.

normative_rules.name: vdivu_vdiv_vremu_vrem_op
normative_rules.text:
The divide and remainder instructions are equivalent to the RISC-V
standard scalar integer multiply/divides, with the same results for
extreme inputs.

normative_rules.name: vwmul_vwmulu_vwmulsu_op
normative_rules.text:
The widening integer multiply instructions return the full 2*SEW-bit
product from an SEW-bit*SEW-bit multiply.

normative_rules.name: vmacc_vnmsac_vmadd_vnmsub_op
normative_rules.text:
The integer multiply-add instructions are destructive and are provided
in two forms, one that overwrites the addend or minuend
(insn:vmacc[], insn:vnmsac[]) and one that overwrites the first multiplicand
(insn:vmadd[], insn:vnmsub[]).

normative_rules.name: vmacc_vnmsac_vmadd_vnmsub_op_lowhalf
normative_rules.text: The low half of the product is added or subtracted from the third operand.

normative_rules.name: vwmaccu_vwmacc_vwmaccsu_vwmaccus_op
normative_rules.text:
The widening integer multiply-add instructions add the full 2*SEW-bit
product from a SEW-bit*SEW-bit multiply to a 2*SEW-bit value and
produce a 2*SEW-bit result.

normative_rules.name: vmerge_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector integer merge instructions combine two source operands
based on a mask.

normative_rules.name: vmerge_all_elem
normative_rules.text:
Unlike regular arithmetic instructions, the
merge operates on all body elements (i.e., the set of elements from
csr:vstart[] up to the current vector length in csr:vl[]).

normative_rules.name: vmerge_op_mask
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vmerge[] instructions are encoded as masked instructions (vm=0).
The instructions combine two
sources as follows.  At elements where the mask value is zero, the
first operand is copied to the destination element, otherwise the
second operand is copied to the destination element.  The first
operand is always a vector register group specified by vs2.  The
second operand is a vector register group specified by vs1 or a
scalar x register specified by rs1 or a 5-bit sign-extended
immediate.

normative_rules.name: vmv_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector integer move instructions copy a source operand to a vector
register group.
The insn:vmv.v.v[] variant copies a vector register group, whereas the insn:vmv.v.x[] and
insn:vmv.v.i[] variants splat a scalar register or immediate to all active
elements of the destination vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vmv_vs2_nv0_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The first operand specifier (vs2) must contain v0, and any other vector
register number in vs2 is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vsaddu_vsadd_vssubu_vssub_op
normative_rules.text:
Saturating forms of integer add and subtract are provided, for both
signed and unsigned integers.

normative_rules.name: vsaddu_vsadd_vssubu_vssub_op_overflow_vxsat_op_vsaddsub
normative_rules.text:
If the result would overflow the
destination, the result is replaced with the closest representable
value, and the csr:vxsat[] bit is set.

normative_rules.name: vaaddu_vaadd_vasubu_vasub_op
normative_rules.text:
The averaging add and subtract instructions right shift the result by
one bit and round off the result according to the setting in csr:vxrm[].
Computation is performed in infinite precision before rounding and truncating.

normative_rules.name: vasub_vasubu_op_overflow
normative_rules.text: For insn:vasub[] and insn:vasubu[], overflow is ignored and the result wraps around.

normative_rules.name: vsmul_op
normative_rules.text:
The signed fractional multiply instruction produces a 2*SEW product of
the two SEW inputs, then shifts the result right by SEW-1 bits,
rounding these bits according to csr:vxrm[], then saturates the result to
fit into SEW bits.

normative_rules.name: vxsat_op_vsmul
normative_rules.text:
If the result causes saturation, the csr:vxsat[] bit
is set.

normative_rules.name: vssrl_vssra_op
normative_rules.text:
These instructions shift the input value right, and round off the
shifted out bits according to csr:vxrm[].  The scaling right shifts have
both zero-extending (insn:vssrl[]) and sign-extending (insn:vssra[]) forms.  The
data to be shifted is in the vector register group specified by vs2
and the shift amount value can come from a vector register group
vs1, a scalar integer register rs1, or a zero-extended 5-bit
immediate.

normative_rules.name: vssrl_vssra_shamt
normative_rules.text: Only the low lg2(SEW) bits of the shift-amount value are used to control the shift amount.

normative_rules.name: vnclipu_vnclip_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vnclip[] instructions are used to pack a fixed-point value into a
narrower destination.  The instructions support rounding, scaling, and
saturation into the final destination format.  The source data is in
the vector register group specified by vs2. The scaling shift amount
value can come from a vector register group vs1, a scalar integer
register rs1, or a zero-extended 5-bit immediate.

normative_rules.name: vnclipu_vnclip_shamt
normative_rules.text:
The low
lg2(2*SEW) bits of the vector or scalar shift-amount value (e.g., the
low 6 bits for a SEW=64-bit to SEW=32-bit narrowing operation) are
used to control the right shift amount, which provides the scaling.

normative_rules.name: vnclipu_vnclip_rounding
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vnclipu[] and insn:vnclip[], the rounding mode is specified in the
csr:vxrm[] CSR.  Rounding occurs around the least-significant bit of the
destination and before saturation.

normative_rules.name: vnclipu_overflow
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vnclipu[], the shifted rounded source value is treated as an
unsigned integer and saturates if the result would overflow the
destination viewed as an unsigned integer.

normative_rules.name: vnclip_overflow
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vnclip[], the shifted rounded source value is treated as a signed
integer and saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed
as a signed integer.

normative_rules.name: vxsat_op_vnclip_u
normative_rules.text:
If any destination element is saturated, the least-significant bit is set in the
csr:vxsat[] register.

normative_rules.name: V_fp_eew_ieee_nsupported_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If the EEW of a vector
floating-point operand does not correspond to a supported IEEE
floating-point type, the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vf_requires_vx
normative_rules.text:
Vector floating-point instructions require the presence of base scalar
floating-point extensions corresponding to the supported vector
floating-point element widths.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_off_V_fp_ill
normative_rules.text:
If the floating-point unit status field csr:mstatus[fs] is Off then any
attempt to execute a vector floating-point instruction will raise an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_dirty_V_fp
normative_rules.text:
Any vector floating-point instruction
that modifies any floating-point extension state (i.e., floating-point
CSRs or f registers) must set csr:mstatus[fs] to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_mstatus_fs_off_hypervisor_V_fp_ill
normative_rules.text:
If the hypervisor extension is implemented and V=1, the csr:vsstatus[fs] field is
additionally in effect for vector floating-point instructions.  If
csr:vsstatus[fs] or csr:mstatus[fs] is Off then any
attempt to execute a vector floating-point instruction will raise an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_mstatus_fs_dirty_hypervisor_V_fp
normative_rules.text:
Any vector floating-point instruction
that modifies any floating-point extension state (i.e., floating-point
CSRs or f registers) must set both csr:mstatus[fs] and csr:vsstatus[fs] to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: fflags_op_V_fp
normative_rules.text:
A vector floating-point exception at any active floating-point element
sets the standard FP exception flags in the csr:fflags[] register.  Inactive
elements do not set FP exception flags.

normative_rules.name: vfadd_vfsub_vfrsub_op
normative_rules.text:
# Floating-point add
vfadd.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm   # Vector-vector
vfadd.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm   # vector-scalar

# Floating-point subtract
vfsub.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm   # Vector-vector
vfsub.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm   # Vector-scalar vd[i] = vs2[i] - f[rs1]
vfrsub.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # Scalar-vector vd[i] = f[rs1] - vs2[i]

normative_rules.name: vfwadd_op
normative_rules.text:
# Widening FP add/subtract, 2*SEW = SEW +/- SEW
vfwadd.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm  # vector-vector
vfwadd.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # vector-scalar
vfwsub.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm  # vector-vector
vfwsub.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # vector-scalar

# Widening FP add/subtract, 2*SEW = 2*SEW +/- SEW
vfwadd.wv  vd, vs2, vs1, vm  # vector-vector
vfwadd.wf  vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # vector-scalar
vfwsub.wv  vd, vs2, vs1, vm  # vector-vector
vfwsub.wf  vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # vector-scalar

normative_rules.name: vfmul_vfdiv_vfrdiv_op
normative_rules.text:
# Floating-point multiply
vfmul.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm   # Vector-vector
vfmul.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm   # vector-scalar

# Floating-point divide
vfdiv.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm   # Vector-vector
vfdiv.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm   # vector-scalar

# Reverse floating-point divide vector = scalar / vector
vfrdiv.vf vd, vs2, rs1, vm  # scalar-vector, vd[i] = f[rs1]/vs2[i]

normative_rules.name: vfwmul_op
normative_rules.text:
# Widening floating-point multiply
vfwmul.vv    vd, vs2, vs1, vm # vector-vector
vfwmul.vf    vd, vs2, rs1, vm # vector-scalar

normative_rules.name: vfmacc_vfnmacc_vfmsac_vfnmsac_vfmadd_vfnmadd_vfmsub_vfnmsub_op
normative_rules.text:
All four varieties of fused multiply-add are provided, and in two
destructive forms that overwrite one of the operands, either the
addend or the first multiplicand.

normative_rules.name: vfwmacc_vfwnmacc_vfwmsac_vfwnmsac_op
normative_rules.text:
The widening floating-point fused multiply-add instructions all
overwrite the wide addend with the result.  The multiplier inputs are
all SEW wide, while the addend and destination is 2*SEW bits wide.

normative_rules.name: vfsqrt_op
normative_rules.text: The insn:vfsqrt.v[] instruction is a unary vector-vector instruction.

normative_rules.name: vfrsqrt7_op
normative_rules.text:
This is a unary vector-vector instruction that returns an estimate of
1/sqrt(x) accurate to 7 bits.

normative_rules.name: vfrsqrt7_op_unex
normative_rules.text:
For the non-exceptional cases, the low bit of the exponent and the six high
bits of significand (after the leading one) are concatenated and used to
address the following table.
The output of the table becomes the seven high bits of the result significand
(after the leading one); the remainder of the result significand is zero.
Subnormal inputs are normalized and the exponent adjusted appropriately before
the lookup.
The output exponent is chosen to make the result approximate the reciprocal of
the square root of the argument.

normative_rules.name: vfrsqrt7_op_precise
normative_rules.text:
More precisely, the result is computed as follows.
Let the normalized input exponent be equal to the input exponent if the input
is normal, or 0 minus the number of leading zeros in the significand
otherwise.
If the input is subnormal, the normalized input significand is given by
shifting the input significand left by 1 minus the normalized input exponent,
discarding the leading 1 bit.
The output exponent equals floor((3*B - 1 - the normalized input exponent) / 2),
where B is the exponent bias. The output sign equals the input sign.

normative_rules.name: vfrec7_op
normative_rules.text:
This is a unary vector-vector instruction that returns an estimate of
1/x accurate to 7 bits.

normative_rules.name: vfrec7_op_unex
normative_rules.text:
For the non-exceptional cases, the seven high bits of significand (after the
leading one) are used to address the following table.
The output of the table becomes the seven high bits of the result significand
(after the leading one); the remainder of the result significand is zero.
Subnormal inputs are normalized and the exponent adjusted appropriately before
the lookup.
The output exponent is chosen to make the result approximate the reciprocal of
the argument, and subnormal outputs are denormalized accordingly.

normative_rules.name: vfrec7_op_precise
normative_rules.text:
More precisely, the result is computed as follows.
Let the normalized input exponent be equal to the input exponent if the input
is normal, or 0 minus the number of leading zeros in the significand
otherwise.
The normalized output exponent equals (2*B - 1 - the normalized input exponent).
If the normalized output exponent is outside the range [-1, 2*B], the result
corresponds to one of the exceptional cases in the table above.

normative_rules.name: vfrec7_op_subnorm
normative_rules.text:
If the input is subnormal, the normalized input significand is given by
shifting the input significand left by 1 minus the normalized input exponent,
discarding the leading 1 bit.
Otherwise, the normalized input significand equals the input significand.
The following table gives the seven MSBs of the normalized output significand
as a function of the seven MSBs of the normalized input significand; the other
bits of the normalized output significand are zero.

normative_rules.name: vfrec7_op_output
normative_rules.text:
If the normalized output exponent is 0 or -1, the result is subnormal: the
output exponent is 0, and the output significand is given by concatenating
a 1 bit to the left of the normalized output significand, then shifting that
quantity right by 1 minus the normalized output exponent.
Otherwise, the output exponent equals the normalized output exponent, and the
output significand equals the normalized output significand.
The output sign equals the input sign.

normative_rules.name: vfmin_vfmax_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector floating-point insn:vfmin[] and insn:vfmax[] instructions have the
same behavior as the corresponding scalar floating-point instructions
in the ext:f[], ext:d[], and ext:q[] extensions: they perform the IEEE 754-2019 minimumNumber
or maximumNumber operation on active elements.

normative_rules.name: vfsgnj_vfsgnjn_vfsgnjx_op
normative_rules.text:
Vector versions of the scalar sign-injection instructions.  The result
takes all bits except the sign bit from the vector vs2 operands.

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmfne_vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_op
normative_rules.text:
These vector FP compare instructions compare two source operands and
write the comparison result to a mask register.

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmfne_vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_vd_single_vreg
normative_rules.text:
The destination mask
vector is always held in a single vector register, with a layout of
elements as described in <<sec-mask-register-layout>>.

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmfne_vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_vd_eq_v0
normative_rules.text:
The
destination mask vector register may be the same as the source vector
mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmfne_vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
Compares write mask registers, and so always
operate under a tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmfne_snan_invalid
normative_rules.text:
insn:vmfeq[] and insn:vmfne[] raise the invalid
operation exception only on signaling NaN inputs.

normative_rules.name: vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_sqnan_invalid
normative_rules.text:
insn:vmflt[], insn:vmfle[], insn:vmfgt[],
and insn:vmfge[] raise the invalid operation exception on both signaling and
quiet NaN inputs.

normative_rules.name: vmfne_vdval1_nan
normative_rules.text:
insn:vmfne[] writes 1 to the destination element when either
operand is NaN,

normative_rules.name: vmfeq_vmflt_vmfle_vmfgt_vmfge_vdval0_nan
normative_rules.text:
whereas the other compares write 0 when either operand
is NaN.

normative_rules.name: vfclass_op
normative_rules.text:
This is a unary vector-vector instruction that operates in the same
way as the scalar classify instruction.

normative_rules.name: vfclass_op_result
normative_rules.text:
The 10-bit mask produced by this instruction is placed in the
least-significant bits of the result elements.  The upper (SEW-10)
bits of the result are filled with zeros.

normative_rules.name: vfclass_sewge16
normative_rules.text:
The instruction is only
defined for SEW=16b and above, so the result will always fit in the
destination elements.

normative_rules.name: vfmerge_op
normative_rules.text: A vector-scalar floating-point merge instruction is provided,

normative_rules.name: vfmerge_all_elem
normative_rules.text:
operates on all body elements from csr:vstart[] up to the current vector
length in csr:vl[] regardless of mask value.

normative_rules.name: vfmerge_op_mask
normative_rules.text:
At elements where the mask value is zero, the first vector operand is
copied to the destination element, otherwise a scalar floating-point
register value is copied to the destination element.

normative_rules.name: vfmv_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector floating-point move instruction splats a floating-point
scalar operand to a vector register group.  The instruction copies a
scalar f register value to all active elements of a vector register
group.

normative_rules.name: vfmv_vs2_nv0_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The instruction must have the vs2 field set to v0, with all other
values for vs2 reserved.

normative_rules.name: vfcvt_op
normative_rules.text:
Conversion operations are provided to convert to and from
floating-point values and unsigned and signed integers, where both
source and destination are SEW wide.

normative_rules.name: vfcvt_op_exceptions
normative_rules.text:
The conversions follow the same rules on exceptional conditions as the
scalar conversion instructions.

normative_rules.name: vfcvt_op_frm
normative_rules.text:
The conversions use the dynamic rounding mode in csr:frm[], except for the rtz
variants, which round towards zero.

normative_rules.name: vfwcvt_op
normative_rules.text:
A set of conversion instructions is provided to convert between
narrower integer and floating-point datatypes to a type of twice the
width.

normative_rules.name: vfwcvt_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
These instructions have the same constraints on vector register overlap
as other widening instructions (see <<sec-widening>>).

normative_rules.name: vfncvt_op
normative_rules.text:
A set of conversion instructions is provided to convert wider integer
and floating-point datatypes to a type of half the width.

normative_rules.name: vfncvt_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
These instructions have the same constraints on vector register overlap
as other narrowing instructions (see <<sec-narrowing>>).

normative_rules.name: vreduction_scalar_def
normative_rules.text:
Vector reduction operations take a vector register group of elements
and a scalar held in element 0 of a vector register group, and perform a
reduction using some binary operator, to produce a scalar result in
element 0 of a vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_scalar_disregard_lmul
normative_rules.text:
The scalar input and output operands
are held in element 0 of a group with EMUL = ceil(EEW/VLEN), regardless of LMUL setting.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_vd_overlap_vs
normative_rules.text:
The destination vector register can overlap the source operands,
including the mask register.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_scalar_disregard_maskval
normative_rules.text:
Inactive elements from the source vector register group are excluded
from the reduction, but the scalar operand is always included
regardless of the mask values.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_tail_policy
vreduction_vl_0
normative_rules.text:
If csr:vl[]=0, no operation is performed and the destination register is
not updated.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_trap
normative_rules.text:
Traps on vector reduction instructions are always reported with a
csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vreduction_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
Vector reduction operations raise an
illegal-instruction exception if csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vredsum_vredmaxu_vredmax_vredminu_vredmin_vredand_vredor_vredxor_op
normative_rules.text:
All operands and results of single-width reduction instructions have
the same SEW width.

normative_rules.name: vredsum_vredmaxu_vredmax_vredminu_vredmin_vredand_vredor_vredxor_overflow
normative_rules.text: Overflows wrap around on arithmetic sums.

normative_rules.name: vwredsumu_op
normative_rules.text:
The unsigned insn:vwredsumu.vs[] instruction zero-extends the SEW-wide
vector elements before summing them, then adds the 2*SEW-width scalar
element, and stores the result in a 2*SEW-width scalar element.

normative_rules.name: vwredsum_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vwredsum.vs[] instruction sign-extends the SEW-wide vector
elements before summing them.

normative_rules.name: vwredsumu_vwredsum_op_overflow
normative_rules.text: For both insn:vwredsumu.vs[] and insn:vwredsum.vs[], overflows wrap around.

normative_rules.name: vfredosum_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfredosum[] instruction must sum the floating-point values in
element order, starting with the scalar in vs1[0]

normative_rules.name: vfredosum_op_exceptions
normative_rules.text:
where each addition operates identically to the scalar floating-point
instructions in terms of raising exception flags and generating or
propagating special values.

normative_rules.name: vfredosum_maskoff
normative_rules.text:
When the operation is masked (vm=0), the masked-off elements do not
affect the result or the exception flags.

normative_rules.name: vfredusum_op
normative_rules.text:
The implementation must produce a result equivalent to a reduction tree
composed of binary operator nodes, with the inputs being elements from
the source vector register group (vs2) and the source scalar value
(vs1[0]).  Each operator in the tree accepts two inputs and produces
one result.
Each operator first computes an exact sum as a RISC-V scalar floating-point
addition with infinite exponent range and precision, then converts this exact
sum to a floating-point format with range and precision each at least as great
as the element floating-point format indicated by SEW, rounding using the
currently active floating-point dynamic rounding mode and raising exception
flags as necessary.
A different floating-point range and precision may be chosen for the result of
each operator.
A node where one input is derived only from elements masked-off or beyond the
active vector length may either treat that input as the additive identity of the
appropriate EEW or simply copy the other input to its output.
The rounded result from the root node in the tree is converted (rounded again,
using the dynamic rounding mode) to the standard floating-point format
indicated by SEW.

normative_rules.name: vfredusum_additive_impl
normative_rules.text:
The additive identity is +0.0 when rounding down (towards -∞) or
-0.0 for all other rounding modes.

normative_rules.name: vfredusum_redtree
normative_rules.text:
The reduction tree structure must be deterministic for a given value
in csr:vtype[] and csr:vl[].

normative_rules.name: vfredmin_vfredmax_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfredmin[] and insn:vfredmax[] instructions reduce the scalar argument in
vs1[0] and active elements in vs2 using the IEEE 754-2019 minimumNumber and
maximumNumber operations, respectively.

normative_rules.name: vfwredosum_vfwredusum_op
normative_rules.text:
Widening forms of the sum reductions are provided that
read and write a double-width reduction result.

normative_rules.name: vfwredosum_vfwredusum_op_reduction
normative_rules.text:
The reduction of the SEW-width elements is performed as in the
single-width reduction case, with the elements in vs2 promoted
to 2*SEW bits before adding to the 2*SEW-bit accumulator.

normative_rules.name: vmask_maskreg_def
normative_rules.text:
Vector mask-register logical operations operate on mask registers.
Each element in a mask register is a single bit,

normative_rules.name: instrgrp_vmask_disregard_vlmul
normative_rules.text:
so these instructions
all operate on single vector registers regardless of the setting of
the csr::[vlmul] field in csr:vtype[].  They do not change the value of
csr::[vlmul].

normative_rules.name: vmask_vd_overlap_vs
normative_rules.text:
The destination vector register may be the same as either
source vector register.

normative_rules.name: vmask_vstart
normative_rules.text:
As with other vector instructions, the elements with indices less than
csr:vstart[] are unchanged, and csr:vstart[] is reset to zero after execution.

normative_rules.name: vmasklogical_unmasked
normative_rules.text: Vector mask logical instructions are always unmasked,

normative_rules.name: vmasklogical_masked_rsv
normative_rules.text:
so there are no
inactive elements, and the encodings with vm=0 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vmasklogical_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
Mask elements past csr:vl[], the tail elements, are
always updated with a tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmand_vmnand_vmandn_vmxor_vmor_vmnor_vmorn_vmxnor_op
normative_rules.text:
vmand.mm vd, vs2, vs1   # vd.mask[i] =   vs2.mask[i] &&  vs1.mask[i]
vmnand.mm vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] = !(vs2.mask[i] &&  vs1.mask[i])
vmandn.mm vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] =   vs2.mask[i] && !vs1.mask[i]
vmxor.mm  vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] =   vs2.mask[i] ^^  vs1.mask[i]
vmor.mm  vd, vs2, vs1   # vd.mask[i] =   vs2.mask[i] ||  vs1.mask[i]
vmnor.mm  vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] = !(vs2.mask[i] ||  vs1.mask[i])
vmorn.mm  vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] =   vs2.mask[i] || !vs1.mask[i]
vmxnor.mm vd, vs2, vs1  # vd.mask[i] = !(vs2.mask[i] ^^  vs1.mask[i])

normative_rules.name: vcpop_vs_single_vreg
normative_rules.text:
The source operand is a single vector register holding mask register
values as described in <<sec-mask-register-layout>>.

normative_rules.name: vcpop_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vcpop.m[] instruction counts the number of mask elements of the
active elements of the vector source mask register that have the value
1 and writes the result to a scalar x register.

normative_rules.name: vcpop_op_mask
normative_rules.text:
The operation can be performed under a mask, in which case only the
masked elements are counted.

normative_rules.name: vcpop_vl0
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vcpop.m[] instruction writes x[rd] even if csr:vl[]=0 (with the
value 0, since no mask elements are active).

normative_rules.name: vcpop_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:vcpop.m[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vcpop_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vcpop.m[] instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vfirst_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfirst[] instruction finds the lowest-numbered active element of
the source mask vector that has the value 1 and writes that element's
index to rd.  If no active element has the value 1, -1 is written
to rd.

normative_rules.name: vfirst_vl0
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfirst.m[] instruction writes x[rd] even if vl=0 (with the
value -1, since no mask elements are active).

normative_rules.name: vfirst_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:vfirst[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vfirst_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vfirst[] instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vmsbf_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vmsbf.m[] instruction takes a mask register as input and writes
results to a mask register.  The instruction writes a 1 to all active
mask elements before the first active source element that is a 1, then
writes a 0 to that element and all following active elements.  If
there is no set bit in the active elements of the source vector, then
all active elements in the destination are written with a 1.

normative_rules.name: vmsbf_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
The tail elements in the destination mask register are updated under a
tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmsbf_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:vmsbf.m[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vmsbf_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vmsbf.m[] instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vmsbf_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination register cannot overlap the source register
and, if masked, cannot overlap the mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: vmsif_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector mask set-including-first instruction is similar to
set-before-first, except it also includes the element with a set bit.

normative_rules.name: vmsif_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
The tail elements in the destination mask register are updated under a
tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmsif_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:vmsif.m[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vmsif_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vmsif.m[] instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vmsif_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination register cannot overlap the source register
and, if masked, cannot overlap the mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: vmsof_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector mask set-only-first instruction is similar to
set-before-first, except it only sets the first element with a bit
set, if any.

normative_rules.name: vmsof_tail_agnostic
normative_rules.text:
The tail elements in the destination mask register are updated under a
tail-agnostic policy.

normative_rules.name: vmsof_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:vmsof.m[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vmsof_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
The
insn:vmsof.m[] instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.

normative_rules.name: vmsof_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination register cannot overlap the source register
and, if masked, cannot overlap the mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: viota_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:viota.m[] instruction reads a source vector mask register and
writes to each element of the destination vector register group the
sum of all the bits of elements in the mask register
whose index is less than the element, e.g., a parallel prefix sum of
the mask values.

normative_rules.name: viota_op_masked
normative_rules.text:
This instruction can be masked, in which case only the enabled
elements contribute to the sum.

normative_rules.name: viota_op_zext
normative_rules.text:
The result value is zero-extended to fill the destination element if
SEW is wider than the result.

normative_rules.name: viota_op_overflow
normative_rules.text:
If the result value would overflow the
destination SEW, the least-significant SEW bits are retained.

normative_rules.name: viota_trap
normative_rules.text: Traps on insn:viota.m[] are always reported with a csr:vstart[] of 0,

normative_rules.name: viota_restart
normative_rules.text:
execution is always restarted from the beginning when resuming after a
trap handler.

normative_rules.name: viota_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
An illegal-instruction exception is raised if
csr:vstart[] is non-zero.
