normative_rules.name: viota_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination register group cannot overlap the source register
and, if masked, cannot overlap the mask register (v0).

normative_rules.name: vid_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vid.v[] instruction writes each element's index to the
destination vector register group, from 0 to csr:vl[]-1.

normative_rules.name: vid_op_mask
normative_rules.text:
The instruction can be masked.  Masking does not change the
index value written to active elements.

normative_rules.name: vid_vs2_nv0_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The vs2 field of the instruction must be set to v0, otherwise the
encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vid_op_zext
normative_rules.text:
The result value is zero-extended to fill the destination element if
SEW is wider than the result.

normative_rules.name: vid_op_overflow
normative_rules.text:
If the result value would overflow the
destination SEW, the least-significant SEW bits are retained.

normative_rules.name: vmv-x-s_vmv-s-x_ignorelmul
normative_rules.text: The instructions ignore LMUL; EMUL is computed as ceil(EEW/VLEN).

normative_rules.name: vmv-x-s_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vmv.x.s[] instruction copies a single SEW-wide element from index 0 of the
source vector register to a destination integer register.  If SEW > XLEN, the
least-significant XLEN bits are transferred and the upper SEW-XLEN bits are
ignored.  If SEW < XLEN, the value is sign-extended to XLEN bits.

normative_rules.name: vmv-s-x_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vmv.s.x[] instruction copies the scalar integer register to element 0 of
the destination vector register group with EMUL = ceil(EEW/VLEN).
If SEW < XLEN, the least-significant bits
are copied and the upper XLEN-SEW bits are ignored.  If SEW > XLEN, the value
is sign-extended to SEW bits.  The other elements in the destination vector
register ( 0 < index < VLEN/SEW) are treated as tail elements using the current tail agnostic/undisturbed policy.

normative_rules.name: vmv-s-x_vstart_ge_vl
normative_rules.text:
If csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[], no
operation is performed and the destination register is not updated.

normative_rules.name: vmv-s-x_vmv-x-s_masked_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The encodings corresponding to the masked versions (vm=0) of
insn:vmv.x.s[] and insn:vmv.s.x[] are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vslide_vstart_ge_vl
normative_rules.text:
For all of the insn:vslideup[], insn:vslidedown[], insn:vslide1up[], insn:vfslide1up[],
insn:vslide1down[], and insn:vfslide1down[] instructions, if csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[], the instruction performs no
operation and leaves the destination vector register unchanged.

normative_rules.name: vslide_mask
normative_rules.text:
The slide instructions may be masked, with mask element i
controlling whether destination element i is written.  The mask
undisturbed/agnostic policy is followed for inactive elements.

normative_rules.name: vslideup_op
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vslideup[], the value in csr:vl[] specifies the maximum number of destination
elements that are written.  The start index (OFFSET) for the
destination can be either specified using an unsigned integer in the
x register specified by rs1, or a 5-bit immediate, zero-extended to XLEN bits.
If XLEN > SEW, OFFSET is not truncated to SEW bits.
Destination elements OFFSET through csr:vl[]-1 are written if unmasked and
if OFFSET < csr:vl[].

normative_rules.name: vslideup_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination vector register group for insn:vslideup[] cannot overlap
the source vector register group, otherwise the instruction encoding
is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vslidedown_op
normative_rules.text:
For insn:vslidedown[], the value in csr:vl[] specifies the maximum number of
destination elements that are written.  The remaining elements past
csr:vl[] are handled according to the current tail policy
(<<sec-agnostic>>).

normative_rules.name: vslidedown_op_src
normative_rules.text:
The start index (OFFSET) for the source can be either specified
using an unsigned integer in the x register specified by rs1, or a
5-bit immediate, zero-extended to XLEN bits.
If XLEN > SEW, OFFSET is not truncated to SEW bits.

normative_rules.name: vslide1up-vx_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vslide1up[] instruction places the x register argument at
location 0 of the destination vector register group, provided that
element 0 is active, otherwise the destination element update follows the
current mask agnostic/undisturbed policy.  If XLEN < SEW, the value is
sign-extended to SEW bits.  If XLEN > SEW, the least-significant bits
are copied over and the high XLEN-SEW bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: vslide1up-vx_op_rem_elem
normative_rules.text:
The remaining active csr:vl[]-1 elements are copied over from index i in
the source vector register group to index i+1 in the destination
vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vslide1up-vx_op_vl
normative_rules.text:
The csr:vl[] register specifies the maximum number of destination vector
register elements updated with source values, and remaining elements
past csr:vl[] are handled according to the current tail policy
(<<sec-agnostic>>).

normative_rules.name: vslide1up-vx_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vslide1up[] instruction requires that the destination vector
register group does not overlap the source vector register group.
Otherwise, the instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vslide1down-vx_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vslide1down[] instruction copies the first csr:vl[]-1 active elements
values from index i+1 in the source vector register group to index
i in the destination vector register group.

normative_rules.name: vslide1down-vx_op_vl
normative_rules.text:
The csr:vl[] register specifies the maximum number of destination vector
register elements written with source values, and remaining elements
past csr:vl[] are handled according to the current tail policy
(<<sec-agnostic>>).

normative_rules.name: vslide1down-vx_op_details
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vslide1down[] instruction places the x register argument at
location csr:vl[]-1 in the destination vector register, provided that
element csr:vl[]-1 is active, otherwise the destination element update
follows the current mask agnostic/undisturbed policy.
If XLEN < SEW, the value is sign-extended to SEW bits.  If
XLEN > SEW, the least-significant bits are copied over and the high
SEW-XLEN bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_vs2_uint
normative_rules.text:
The index values in the second vector are
treated as unsigned integers.

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_vs_ignore_vl
normative_rules.text:
The source vector can be read at any
index < VLMAX regardless of csr:vl[].

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_vl
normative_rules.text:
The maximum number of elements to write to
the destination register is given by csr:vl[],

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_tail
normative_rules.text:
and the remaining elements
past csr:vl[] are handled according to the current tail policy
(<<sec-agnostic>>).

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_mask
normative_rules.text:
The operation can be masked, and the mask
undisturbed/agnostic policy is followed for inactive elements.

normative_rules.name: vrgather-vv_op_vrgatherei16-vv_op
normative_rules.text:
vrgather.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm     # vd[i] = (vs1[i] >= VLMAX) ? 0 : vs2[vs1[i]];
vrgatherei16.vv vd, vs2, vs1, vm # vd[i] = (vs1[i] >= VLMAX) ? 0 : vs2[vs1[i]];

normative_rules.name: vrgather-vv_sew_lmul
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vrgather.vv[] form uses SEW/LMUL for both the data and
indices.

normative_rules.name: vrgatherei16-vv_sew_lmul
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vrgatherei16.vv[] form uses SEW/LMUL for the data in
vs2 but EEW=16 and EMUL = (16/SEW)*LMUL for the indices in vs1.

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_id_ge_vlmax
normative_rules.text:
If an element index is out of range ( vs1[i] ≥ VLMAX )
then zero is returned for the element value.

normative_rules.name: vrgather-vx_vrgather-vi_op
normative_rules.text:
Vector-scalar and vector-immediate forms of the register gather are
also provided.  These read one element from the source vector at the
given index, and write this value to the active elements
of the destination vector register. The index value in the scalar
register and the immediate, zero-extended to XLEN bits, are treated as
unsigned integers.  If XLEN > SEW, the index value is not truncated
to SEW bits.

normative_rules.name: vrgather_vrgatherei16_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
For any insn:vrgather[] instruction, the destination vector register group
cannot overlap with the source vector register groups, otherwise the
instruction encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vcompress_op
normative_rules.text:
The vector mask register specified by vs1 indicates which of the
first csr:vl[] elements of vector register group vs2 should be extracted
and packed into contiguous elements at the beginning of vector
register vd. The remaining elements of vd are treated as tail
elements according to the current tail policy
(<<sec-agnostic>>).

normative_rules.name: vcompress_enc
normative_rules.text: insn:vcompress[] is encoded as an unmasked instruction (vm=1).

normative_rules.name: vcompress_masked_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The equivalent
masked instruction (vm=0) is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vcompress_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The destination vector register group cannot overlap the source vector
register group or the source mask register, otherwise the instruction
encoding is reserved.

normative_rules.name: vcompress_trap
normative_rules.text:
A trap on a insn:vcompress[] instruction is always reported with a
csr:vstart[] of 0.

normative_rules.name: vcompress_vstart_n0_ill
normative_rules.text:
Executing a insn:vcompress[] instruction with a non-zero
csr:vstart[] raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: vmv-nr-r_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vmv&#60;nr&#62;r.v[] instructions copy whole vector registers (i.e., all
VLEN bits) and can copy whole vector register groups.  The nr value
in the opcode is the number of individual vector registers, NREG, to
copy.  The instructions operate as if EMUL = NREG, EEW = min(VLEN*EMUL, SEW), and effective
length evl = EMUL * VLEN/EEW.

normative_rules.name: vmv-nr-r_enc
normative_rules.text:
The instruction is encoded as an OPIVI instruction.  The number of
vector registers to copy is encoded in the low three bits of the
imm field (imm[2:0]) using the same encoding as the nf[2:0] field for memory
instructions (Figure <<fig-nf>>), i.e., imm[2:0] = NREG-1.

normative_rules.name: vmv-nr-r_nreg_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The value of NREG must be 1, 2, 4, or 8, and values of imm[4:0]
other than 0, 1, 3, and 7 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vmv-nr-r_vreg_constr
normative_rules.text:
The source and destination vector register numbers must be aligned
appropriately for the vector register group size,

normative_rules.name: vmv-nr-r_unaligned_rsv
normative_rules.text:
encodings with
other vector register numbers are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vfmv-f-s_vfmv-s-f_ignorelmul
normative_rules.text: The instructions ignore LMUL; EMUL is computed as ceil(EEW/VLEN).

normative_rules.name: vfmv-f-s_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfmv.f.s[] instruction copies a single SEW-wide element from index
0 of the source vector register to a destination scalar floating-point
register.

normative_rules.name: vfmv-s-f_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfmv.s.f[] instruction copies the scalar floating-point register
to element 0 of the destination vector register.  The other elements
in the destination vector register (0 < index < VLEN/SEW) are treated
as tail elements using the current tail agnostic/undisturbed policy.

normative_rules.name: vfmv-s-f_vstart_ge_vl
normative_rules.text:
If csr:vstart[] ≥ csr:vl[], no operation is performed and the destination
register is not updated.

normative_rules.name: vfmv-s-f_masked_rsv
normative_rules.text:
The encodings corresponding to the masked versions (vm=0) of
insn:vfmv.f.s[] and insn:vfmv.s.f[] are reserved.

normative_rules.name: vslide1up-vf_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfslide1up[] instruction is defined analogously to insn:vslide1up[],
but sources its scalar argument from an f register.

normative_rules.name: vslide1down-vf_op
normative_rules.text:
The insn:vfslide1down[] instruction is defined analogously to insn:vslide1down[],
but sources its scalar argument from an f register.

normative_rules.name: epc_vstart_op_V_trap
normative_rules.text:
On a trap during a vector instruction (caused by either a synchronous
exception or an asynchronous interrupt), the existing csr:*epc[] CSR is
written with a pointer to the trapping vector instruction, while the
csr:vstart[] CSR contains the element index on which the trap was
taken.

normative_rules.name: vec_store_nonidempotent_no_update
normative_rules.text:
Non-idempotent memory regions must not have been updated for
indices equal to or greater than the element that caused a synchronous
trap during a vector store instruction.

normative_rules.name: egs_ge_vlmax_rsv
normative_rules.text: Vector instructions with EGS > VLMAX are reserved.

normative_rules.name: egs_vl_rsv
normative_rules.text:
When an operand is a vector of element groups, the
csr:vl[] setting must correspond to an integer multiple of the element group
size, with other values of csr:vl[] reserved.

normative_rules.name: egs_vl_avl
normative_rules.text:
When element group instructions are present, an additional constraint
is placed on the setting of csr:vl[] based on an AVL value
(augmenting <<constraints-on-setting-vl>>).
EGSMAX is the largest EGS supported by the
implementation.  When AVL > VLMAX, the value of csr:vl[] must be set to
either VLMAX or a positive integer multiple of EGSMAX.

normative_rules.name: egs_sew_eew
normative_rules.text:
The csr:vtype[] SEW can be used to indicate or calculate the effective
element size (EEW) of one or more operands of an element group
instruction.  Where the operand is an element group, SEW and EEW refer
to the number of bits in each individual element within a group not
the number of bits in the group as a whole.

normative_rules.name: egs_lmul_emul
normative_rules.text:
The csr:vtype[] LMUL setting can be used to indicate or calculate the
effective length multiplier (EMUL) for one or more operands.  Element
group instructions tend to exhibit a much wider range of relationships
between various operand EEW/EMUL values.  For example, an instruction
might take a vector of length N of 4-element groups with EEW=8b and
reduce each group to produce a vector length N of 1-element groups
with EEW=32b. In this case, the input and output EMUL values are equal
even though the EEW settings differ by a factor of 4.

normative_rules.name: egs_egw
normative_rules.text:
The element group width (EGW) is the number of bits in the
element group as a whole.
For example, the SHA-256 instructions in the ext:zvknha[] extension operate on an
EGW of 128, with EGS=4 and EEW=32.
It is possible to use LMUL to concatenate multiple vector registers together
to support larger EGW>VLEN.

normative_rules.name: Zve_xlen
normative_rules.text: ext:zve32x[] is compatible with all currently defined base ISAs.

normative_rules.name: Zve_precise_traps
normative_rules.text: The ext:zve32x[] extension has precise traps.

normative_rules.name: Zve_eew
normative_rules.text: ext:zve32x[] provides support for EEW of 8, 16, and 32.

normative_rules.name: Zve32x_Zve64x_nsupport_freg
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve32x[] supports all vector integer permutation instructions
(<<sec-vector-integer-permute>>).

normative_rules.name: Zve32x_dependent_Zicsr
normative_rules.text: The ext:zve32x[] extension depends on the ext:zicsr[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zve32f_Zve64f_dependent_F
normative_rules.text: The ext:zve32f[] extension depends on the ext:zve32x[] and ext:f[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zve32f_instr_perm
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve32f[] supports all vector floating-point permutation instructions
(<<sec-vector-float-permute>>) for floating-point operands with EEW=32.

normative_rules.name: Zve32f_Zve64x_dependent_Zve32x
normative_rules.text: ext:zve64x[] depends upon the ext:zve32x[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zve_nsupport_eew64_xlen32
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve64x[] supports all vector load and store instructions
(<<sec-vector-memory>>),
except EEW=64 for index values is not supported when XLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: Zve64_eew64_nsupport_vmulh
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve64x[] supports all vector integer instructions
(<<sec-vector-integer>>), except that
the insn:vmulh[] integer multiply
variants that return the high half of the product (insn:vmulh.vv[],
insn:vmulh.vx[], insn:vmulhu.vv[], insn:vmulhu.vx[], insn:vmulhsu.vv[],
insn:vmulhsu.vx[]) are not included for EEW=64.

normative_rules.name: Zve64_eew64_nsupport_vsmul
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve64x[] supports all vector fixed-point arithmetic
instructions (<<sec-vector-fixed-point>>), except that insn:vsmul.vv[] and
insn:vsmul.vx[] are not included for EEW=64.

normative_rules.name: Zve64f_dependent_Zve32f_Zve64x
normative_rules.text: ext:zve64f[] depends on the ext:zve64x[] and ext:zve32f[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zve64d_dependent_Zve64f
normative_rules.text: The ext:zve64d[] extension depends on the ext:zve64f[] and ext:d[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zve64d_instr_perm
normative_rules.text:
ext:zve64d[] supports all vector floating-point permutation instructions
(<<sec-vector-float-permute>>) for floating-point operands with EEW=32 or EEW=64.

normative_rules.name: misa_v_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:misa[v] bit is set for implementations providing csr:misa[] and
supporting V.

normative_rules.name: V_precise_traps
normative_rules.text: The V vector extension has precise traps.

normative_rules.name: V_dependent_Zvl128b_Zve64d
normative_rules.text: The V vector extension depends upon the Zvl128b and Zve64d extensions.

normative_rules.name: V_supported_eew
normative_rules.text: The V extension supports EEW of 8, 16, 32, and 64.

normative_rules.name: V_instr_config
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports the vector configuration instructions
(<<sec-vector-config>>).

normative_rules.name: V_instr_ls_eew64_nsupported_xlen32
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector load and store instructions
(<<sec-vector-memory>>), except the V extension does not
support EEW=64 for index values when XLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: V_instr_int
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector integer instructions
(<<sec-vector-integer>>).

normative_rules.name: V_instr_fixedpt
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector fixed-point arithmetic
instructions (<<sec-vector-fixed-point>>).

normative_rules.name: V_instr_red
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector integer single-width and
widening reduction operations (<<sec-vector-integer-reduce>>,
<<sec-vector-integer-reduce-widen>>).

normative_rules.name: V_instr_mask
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector mask instructions
(<<sec-vector-mask>>).

normative_rules.name: V_instr_perm
normative_rules.text:
The V extension supports all vector permutation instructions
(<<sec-vector-integer-permute>>, <<sec-vector-float-permute>>).

normative_rules.name: V_dependent_F_D
normative_rules.text:
The V extension depends upon the F and D
extensions, and implements all vector floating-point instructions
(<<sec-vector-float>>) for floating-point operands with EEW=32
or EEW=64 (including widening instructions and conversions between
FP32 and FP64).

normative_rules.name: V_fp_reductions
normative_rules.text:
Vector single-width floating-point reductions
(<<sec-vector-float-reduce>>) for EEW=32 and EEW=64 are supported as
well as widening reductions from FP32 to FP64.

normative_rules.name: Zvfhmin_dependent_Zve32f
normative_rules.text: The ext:zvfhmin[] extension depends on the extlink:zve32f[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zvfh_instr
normative_rules.text:
When the ext:zvfh[] extension is implemented, all instructions in
<<sec-vector-float>>, <<sec-vector-float-reduce>>,
<<sec-vector-float-reduce-widen>>, <<sec-vector-float-move>>,
<<sec-vfslide1up>>, and <<sec-vfslide1down>>
become defined when SEW=16.

normative_rules.name: Zvfh_eew16
normative_rules.text:
The EEW=16 floating-point operands of these instructions use the binary16
format.

normative_rules.name: Zvfh_instr_cvt
normative_rules.text:
Additionally, conversions between 8-bit integers and binary16 values are
provided.  The floating-point-to-integer narrowing conversions
(insn:vfncvt.x.f.w[], insn:vfncvt.xu.f.w[], insn:vfncvt.rtz.x.f.w[], and insn:vfncvt.rtz.xu.f.w[]) and integer-to-floating-point
widening conversions (insn:vfwcvt.f.x.v[] and insn:vfwcvt.f.xu.v[]) become defined when SEW=8.

normative_rules.name: Zvfh_dependent_Zve32f_Zfhmin
normative_rules.text: The ext:zvfh[] extension depends on the extlink:zve32f[] and extlink:zfhmin[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zvfbfmin_depends_Zve32f
normative_rules.text: This extension depends upon the ext:zve32f[] extension.

normative_rules.name: vfncvtbf16-f-f-w_enc
normative_rules.text: Encoding

normative_rules.name: vfncvtbf16-f-f-w_sew_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 16

normative_rules.name: vfncvtbf16-f-f-w_op
normative_rules.text: Narrowing convert from FP32 to BF16. Round according to the frm register.

normative_rules.name: vfwcvtbf16-f-f-v_enc
normative_rules.text: Encoding

normative_rules.name: vfwcvtbf16-f-f-v_sew_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 16

normative_rules.name: vfwcvtbf16-f-f-v_op
normative_rules.text: Widening convert from BF16 to FP32. The conversion is exact.

normative_rules.name: Zvfbfwma_depends
normative_rules.text: This extension depends upon the ext:zvfbfmin[] and ext:zfbfmin[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: vfwmaccbf16_sew_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 16

normative_rules.name: vfwmaccbf16_op
normative_rules.text: This instruction performs a widening fused multiply-accumulate operation, where each pair of BF16 values are multiplied and their unrounded product is added to the corresponding FP32 accumulate value. The sum is rounded according to the frm register.

normative_rules.name: vfwmaccbf16-vv
normative_rules.text: In the vector-vector version, the BF16 elements are read from vs1 and vs2 and FP32 accumulate value is read from vd. The FP32 result is written to the destination register vd.

normative_rules.name: vfwmaccbf16-vf
normative_rules.text: The vector-scalar version is similar, but instead of reading elements from vs1, a scalar BF16 value is read from the FPU register rs1.

normative_rules.name: Zvbb_dependent_Zve32x
normative_rules.text: ext:zvbb[] depends upon the ext:zve32x[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zvbb_eew
normative_rules.text: ext:zvbb[] provides support for EEW of 8, 16, and 32.

normative_rules.name: Zvbb_eew_Zve64x
normative_rules.text: If ext:zve64x[] is supported then ext:zvbb[] also adds support for EEW=64.

normative_rules.name: vandn_op
normative_rules.text: Each bit of Op1 is inverted and logically ANDed with the corresponding bits in vs2.

normative_rules.name: vandn-vx_rs1
normative_rules.text: In the vector-scalar version, Op1 is the sign-extended or truncated value in scalar register rs1.

normative_rules.name: vandn-vv_vs1
normative_rules.text: In the vector-vector version, Op1 is vs1.

normative_rules.name: vbrev-v_op
normative_rules.text: A bit reversal is performed on the bits of each element.

normative_rules.name: vbrev8-v_op
normative_rules.text: A bit reversal is performed on the bits of each byte.

normative_rules.name: vclz-v_op
normative_rules.text: A leading zero count is performed on each element.

normative_rules.name: vclz-v_op_zeroinput
normative_rules.text: The result for zero-valued inputs is the value SEW.

normative_rules.name: vcpop-v_op
normative_rules.text: A population count is performed on each element.

normative_rules.name: vctz-v_op
normative_rules.text: A trailing zero count is performed on each element.

normative_rules.name: vrev8-v_op
normative_rules.text: A byte reversal is performed on each element of vs2, effectively performing an endian swap.

normative_rules.name: vrol_op
normative_rules.text:
The elements in vs2 are rotated left by the rotate amount specified by either
the corresponding elements of vs1 (vector-vector), or integer register rs1
(vector-scalar).
Only the low log2(SEW) bits of the rotate-amount value are used, all other
bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: vror_op
normative_rules.text:
The elements in vs2 are rotated right by the rotate amount specified by either
the corresponding elements of vs1 (vector-vector), integer register rs1
(vector-scalar), or an immediate value (vector-immediate).
Only the low log2(SEW) bits of the rotate-amount value are used, all other
bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: vwsll_op
normative_rules.text:
The elements in vs2 are zero-extended to 2×SEW bits, then shifted left
by the shift amount specified by either
the corresponding elements of vs1 (vector-vector), integer register rs1
(vector-scalar), or an immediate value (vector-immediate).
Only the low log2(2×SEW) bits of the shift-amount value are used, all other
bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: Zvbc_dependent_Zve64x
normative_rules.text: ext:zvbc[] depends upon the ext:zve64x[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zvbc_sew64only
normative_rules.text: The instructions in ext:zvbc[] are only defined for SEW=64.

normative_rules.name: vclmul_sewn64_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 64

normative_rules.name: vclmul_op
normative_rules.text:
Each 64-bit element in the vs2 vector register is carry-less multiplied by
either each 64-bit element in vs1 (vector-vector), or the 64-bit value
from integer register rs1 (vector-scalar). The result is the least
significant 64 bits of the carry-less product.

normative_rules.name: vclmulh_sewn64_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 64

normative_rules.name: vclmulh_op
normative_rules.text:
Each 64-bit element in the vs2 vector register is carry-less multiplied by
either each 64-bit element in vs1 (vector-vector), or the 64-bit value
from integer register rs1 (vector-scalar). The result is the most
significant 64 bits of the carry-less product.

normative_rules.name: Zk_scalar_xreg_op
normative_rules.text:
All instructions described herein use the general-purpose x
registers, and obey the 2-read-1-write register access constraint.

normative_rules.name: Zkr_seed_addr
normative_rules.text: The entropy source extension defines the csr:seed[] CSR at address 0x015. This CSR provides up to 16 physical csr::[entropy] bits that can be used to seed cryptographic random bit generators.

normative_rules.name: seed_csr_unpriv
normative_rules.text: csr:seed[] is an unprivileged CSR located at address 0x015.

normative_rules.name: seed_ro_illegal
normative_rules.text:
Attempts to access the csr:seed[] CSR using a read-only CSR-access instruction
(insn:csrrs[]/insn:csrrc[] with rs1=x0 or insn:csrrsi[]/insn:csrrci[] with uimm=0) raise an
illegal-instruction exception; any other CSR-access instruction may be used
to access csr:seed[].

normative_rules.name: seed_write_ignore
normative_rules.text: The write value (in rs1 or uimm) must be ignored by implementations.

normative_rules.name: seed_exec_mode_control
normative_rules.text:
The csr:seed[] CSR is also access controlled by execution mode, and attempted
read or write access will raise an illegal-instruction exception outside M-mode
unless access is explicitly granted. See <<crypto_scalar_es_access>> for
more details.

normative_rules.name: seed_entropy_unique
normative_rules.text:
Each returned csr:seed[][15:0] = csr::[entropy] value represents unique randomness
when csr::[opst]=ES16 (seed[31:30] = 10), even if its numerical value is
the same as that of a previously polled csr::[entropy] value.

normative_rules.name: seed_entropy_zero_non_es16
normative_rules.text: When csr::[opst] is not ES16, csr::[entropy] must be set to 0.

normative_rules.name: seed_wipe_on_read
normative_rules.text:
For security reasons, the interface guarantees that secret
csr::[entropy] words are not made available multiple times. Hence polling (reading) must
also have the side effect of clearing (wipe-on-read) the csr::[entropy] contents and
changing the state to WAIT (unless there is csr::[entropy] immediately
available for ES16). Other states (BIST, WAIT, and DEAD)
may be unaffected by polling.

normative_rules.name: seed_bist_latch
normative_rules.text:
Such a BIST alarm must be latched until polled at least once to enable
software to record its occurrence.

normative_rules.name: seed_min_security_256
normative_rules.text:
Any implementation of the csr:seed[] CSR that limits the security
strength shall not reduce it to less than 256 bits.

normative_rules.name: seed_disable_if_weak
normative_rules.text:
If the security
level is under 256 bits, then the interface must not be available.

normative_rules.name: Zkt_optional_instr
normative_rules.text:
Vendors do not have to implement all of the list's instructions to be
ext:zkt[] compliant;

normative_rules.name: Zkt_impl_must_constant_latency
normative_rules.text: if they claim to have ext:zkt[] and implement any of the listed instructions, it must have data-independent latency.

normative_rules.name: zvk_dataindep_timing
normative_rules.text:
All instructions
shall be implemented with data-independent timing. That is, the latency of
the execution of these instructions shall not vary with different input values.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_eeweqsew
normative_rules.text: For all of the vector crypto instructions in this specification, EEW=SEW.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vl_vstart_egsconstr
normative_rules.text:
Since csr:vl[] and csr:vstart[] refer to elements, Vector Crypto instructions that use elements groups
(See <<crypto-vector-element-groups>>) require that these values are an integer multiple of the
Element Group Size (EGS).

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vl_vstart_rsv
normative_rules.text: Instructions that violate the csr:vl[] or csr:vstart[] requirements are reserved.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_lmul_egwconstr
normative_rules.text:
For element-group instructions, LMUL×VLEN must always be at least as large as EGW, otherwise an
illegal-instruction exception is raised, even if csr:vl[]=0.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_sew_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Some Vector Crypto instructions are only defined for a specific SEW. In such a case
all other SEW values are reserved.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vsins_vs2
normative_rules.text: In the case of the insn:*.vs[] instructions defined in this specification, vs2 holds a 128-bit scalar element group.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vsins_vdvs2overlap
normative_rules.text:
For implementations with VLEN ≥ 128, vs2 refers to a single register. Thus, the vd register group must not
overlap the vs2 register.
However, in implementations where VLEN < 128, vs2 refers to a register group comprised of the number
of registers needed to hold the 128-bit scalar element group. In this case, the vd register group must not
overlap this vs2 register group.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vsins_vd
normative_rules.text: they return vector results to vd, which is also a source vector operand.

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_vsins_vs2function
normative_rules.text:
These instructions enable a single key, specified as a scalar element group in vs2, to be
applied to each element group of register group vd.

normative_rules.name: Zvknhb_Zvkn_Zvknc_Zvkng_Zvksc_depZve64x
normative_rules.text: The extlink:zvknhb[], extlink:zvkn[], extlink:zvknc[], extlink:zvkng[], and extlink:zvksc[] depend on ext:zve64x[].

normative_rules.name: Zvkb_Zvkg_Zvkned_Zvknha_Zvksed_Zvksh_Zvks_Zvksc_Zvksg_Zvkt_depZve32x
normative_rules.text: All of the other Vector Crypto Extensions depend on ext:zve32x[].

normative_rules.name: Zvknhb_impZvknha
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknhb[] implies ext:zvknha[].

normative_rules.name: veccrypto_indepZkt
normative_rules.text:
It is important to note that the Vector Crypto instructions are independent of the
implementation of the ext:zkt[] extension and do not require that ext:zkt[] is implemented.

normative_rules.name: Zvkg_egw128b_elem32b
normative_rules.text: All of these instructions work on 128-bit element groups comprised of four 32-bit elements.

normative_rules.name: Zvkg_dataindeptiming
normative_rules.text: To help avoid side-channel timing attacks, these instructions shall be implemented with data-independent timing.

normative_rules.name: Zvkg_vl
normative_rules.text:
The number of element groups to be processed is csr:vl[]/EGS.
csr:vl[] must be set to the number of SEW=32 elements to be processed and
therefore must be a multiple of EGS=4.

normative_rules.name: Zvkg_vstart
normative_rules.text: Likewise, csr:vstart[] must be a multiple of EGS=4.

normative_rules.text: SHA-512: these instructions work on 256-bit element groups comprised of four 64-bit elements.

normative_rules.text: ext:zvknhb[] supports SHA-256 and SHA-512.

normative_rules.name: Zvknha_sha256
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknha[] supports only SHA-256.

normative_rules.text: To help avoid side-channel timing attacks, these instructions shall be implemented with data-independent timing.

normative_rules.name: Zvknha_Zvknhb_vl
normative_rules.text:
The number of element groups to be processed is csr:vl[]/EGS.
csr:vl[] must be set to the number of SEW elements to be processed and

normative_rules.name: Zvknha_Zvknhb_vstart

32-bit elements.

normative_rules.name: Zvksed_dataindeptiming
normative_rules.text: To help avoid side-channel timing attacks, these instructions shall be implemented with data-independent timing.

normative_rules.name: Zvksed_vl
normative_rules.text:
The number of element groups to be processed is csr:vl[]/EGS.
csr:vl[] must be set to the number of SEW=32 elements to be processed and

normative_rules.text:
All of these instructions work on 256-bit element groups comprised of
eight 32-bit elements.

normative_rules.name: Zvksh_dataindeptiming

csr:vl[] must be set to the number of SEW=32 elements to be processed and

normative_rules.name: Zvksh_vstart

normative_rules.name: Zvkt_req
normative_rules.text: The Zvkt extension requires all implemented instructions from the following list to be executed with data-independent execution latency as defined in the RISC-V Scalar Cryptography Extensions specification.

normative_rules.name: Zvkt_diel_def
normative_rules.text:
Data-independent execution latency (DIEL) applies to all data operands of an instruction, even those that are not a
part of the body or that are inactive. However, DIEL does not apply
to other values such as csr:vl[], csr:vtype[], and the mask (when used to control
execution of a masked vector instruction).

normative_rules.name: Zvkt_diel_constants_exempt
normative_rules.text:
Also, DIEL does not apply to constant values specified in the
instruction encoding such as the use of the zero register (x0), and, in the
case of immediate forms of an instruction, the values in the immediate
fields (i.e., imm and uimm).

normative_rules.name: Zvkt_diel_control_exempt
normative_rules.text:
In some cases--which are explicitly specified in the lists below--operands that are used as control rather than data
are exempt from DIEL.

normative_rules.name: vaesdf_final
normative_rules.text: A final-round AES block cipher decryption is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaesdf_ops
normative_rules.text: The InvShiftRows and InvSubBytes steps are applied to each round state element group from vd.

normative_rules.name: vaesdf_xor_form
normative_rules.text:
This is then XORed with the round key in either the corresponding element group in vs2 (vector-vector
form) or scalar element group in vs2 (vector-scalar form).

normative_rules.name: vaesdm_mid
normative_rules.text: A middle-round AES block cipher decryption is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaesdm_ops
normative_rules.text: The InvShiftRows and InvSubBytes steps are applied to each round state element group from vd.

normative_rules.name: vaesdm_xor_form
normative_rules.text:
This is then XORed with the round key in either the corresponding element group in vs2 (vector-vector
form) or the scalar element group in vs2 (vector-scalar form).

normative_rules.name: vaesdm_invmix
normative_rules.text: InvMixColumns step.

normative_rules.name: vaesef_final
normative_rules.text: A final-round encryption function of the AES block cipher is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaesef_ops
normative_rules.text: The SubBytes and ShiftRows steps are applied to each round state element group from vd.

normative_rules.name: vaesef_xor_form
normative_rules.text:
This is then XORed with the round key in either the corresponding element group in vs2 (vector-vector
form) or the scalar element group in vs2 (vector-scalar form).

normative_rules.name: vaesem_mid
normative_rules.text: A middle-round encryption function of the AES block cipher is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaesem_ops
normative_rules.text: The SubBytes, ShiftRows, and MixColumns steps are applied to each round state element group from vd.

normative_rules.name: vaesem_xor_form
normative_rules.text:
This is then XORed with the round key in either the corresponding element group in vs2 (vector-vector
form) or the scalar element group in vs2 (vector-scalar form).

normative_rules.name: vaeskf1_round
normative_rules.text: A single round of the forward AES-128 KeySchedule is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf1_wordgen
normative_rules.text:
The next round key is generated word by word from the
current round key element group in vs2 and the immediately previous word of the
round key.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf1_uimm_src
normative_rules.text:
ranges from 1 to 10, comes from uimm[3:0];
uimm[4] is ignored.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf1_uimm_map
normative_rules.text:
The out-of-range uimm[3:0] values of 0 and 11&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;15 are mapped to in-range
values by inverting uimm[3].

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_round
normative_rules.text: A single round of the forward AES-256 KeySchedule is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_wordgen
normative_rules.text:
The next round key is generated word by word from the
previous round key element group in vd and the immediately previous word of the
round key.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_rcon_lsw
normative_rules.text:
least significant word of the next round key is generated by
applying a function to the most significant word of the current round key and
then XORing the result with the round constant.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_rcon_func
normative_rules.text: The round number is used to select the round constant as well as the function.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_uimm_src
normative_rules.text:
ranges from 2 to 14, comes from uimm[3:0];
uimm[4] is ignored.

normative_rules.name: vaeskf2_uimm_map
normative_rules.text:
The out-of-range uimm[3:0] values of 0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;1 and 15 are mapped to in-range
values by inverting uimm[3].

normative_rules.name: vaesz_round0
normative_rules.text: A round-0 AES block cipher operation is performed.

normative_rules.name: vaesz-vs_only
normative_rules.text: There is only a insn:*.vs[] form of the instruction.

normative_rules.name: vaesz_vs2_rk
normative_rules.text:
vs2 holds a
scalar element group that is used
as the round key for all of the round state element groups.

normative_rules.name: vghsh-vv_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vghsh-vv_op
normative_rules.text:
This instruction treats all of the inputs and outputs as 128-bit polynomials and
performs operations over GF[2].
It produces the next partial hash (Y~i+1~) by adding the current partial
hash (Y~i~) to the cipher text block (X~i~) and then multiplying (over GF(2^128^))
this sum by the Hash Subkey (H).

normative_rules.name: vghsh-vv_op_gf
normative_rules.text:
The multiplication over GF(2^128^) is a carry-less multiply of two 128-bit polynomials
modulo GHASH's irreducible polynomial (x^128^ + x^7^ + x^2^ + x + 1).

normative_rules.name: vghsh-vv_op_coeff
normative_rules.text:
The NIST specification (see extlink:zvkg[]) orders the coefficients from left to right x~0~x~1~x~2~...x~127~
for a polynomial x~0~ + x~1~u +x~2~ u^2^ + ... + x~127~u^127^. This can be viewed as a collection of
byte elements in memory with the byte containing the lowest coefficients (i.e., 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
residing at the lowest memory address. Since the bits in the bytes are reversed,
this instruction internally performs bit swaps within bytes to put the bits in the standard ordering
(e.g., 7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0).

normative_rules.name: vghsh-vv_exeindepdata
normative_rules.text:
This instruction must always be implemented such that its execution latency does not depend
on the data being operated upon.

normative_rules.name: vgmul-vv_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vgmul-vv_op
normative_rules.text:
This instruction treats all of the inputs and outputs as 128-bit polynomials and
performs operations over GF[2].
It produces the product over GF(2^128^) of the two 128-bit inputs.

normative_rules.name: vgmul-vv_op_gf
normative_rules.text:
The multiplication over GF(2^128^) is a carry-less multiply of two 128-bit polynomials
modulo GHASH's irreducible polynomial (x^128^ + x^7^ + x^2^ + x + 1).

normative_rules.name: vgmul-vv_op_coeff
normative_rules.text:
The NIST specification (see extlink:zvkg[]) orders the coefficients from left to right x~0~x~1~x~2~...x~127~
for a polynomial x~0~ + x~1~u +x~2~ u^2^ + ... + x~127~u^127^. This can be viewed as a collection of
byte elements in memory with the byte containing the lowest coefficients (i.e., 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7)
residing at the lowest memory address. Since the bits in the bytes are reversed,
This instruction internally performs bit swaps within bytes to put the bits in the standard ordering
(e.g., 7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0).

normative_rules.name: vgmul-vv_exeindepdata
normative_rules.text:
This instruction must always be implemented such that its execution latency does not depend
on the data being operated upon.

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_Zvknha_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknha[]: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_Zvknhb_sewn32or64_rsv
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknhb[]: SEW is any value other than 32 or 64

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_vdoverlapvs1vs2_rsv
normative_rules.text: The vd register group overlaps with either vs1 or vs2

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_op_sew32
normative_rules.text: SEW=32: 2 rounds of SHA-256 compression are performed (ext:zvknha[] and ext:zvknhb[])

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_op_sew64
normative_rules.text: SEW=64: 2 rounds of SHA-512 compression are performed (ext:zvknhb[])

normative_rules.name: vsha2chl-vv_op
normative_rules.text:
Two words of vs1 are processed with
the 8 words of current state held in vd and vs2 to perform two
rounds of hash computation producing four words of the
next state.

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_Zvknha_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknha[]: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_Zvknhb_sewn32or64_rsv
normative_rules.text: ext:zvknhb[]: SEW is any value other than 32 or 64

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_vdoverlapvs1vs2_rsv
normative_rules.text: The vd register group overlaps with either vs1 or vs2

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_op_sew32
normative_rules.text: SEW=32: Four rounds of SHA-256 message schedule expansion are performed (ext:zvknha[] and ext:zvknhb[])

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_op_sew64
normative_rules.text: SEW=64: Four rounds of SHA-512 message schedule expansion are performed (ext:zvknhb[])

normative_rules.name: vsha2ms-vv_op
normative_rules.text:
Eleven of the last 16 SEW-sized message-schedule words from vd (oldest), vs2,
and vs1 (most recent) are processed to produce the
next 4 message-schedule words.

normative_rules.name: vsm3c-vi_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsm3c-vi_vdoverlapvs2_rsv
normative_rules.text: The vd register group overlaps with the vs2 register group

normative_rules.name: vsm3c-vi_op
normative_rules.text: Two rounds of SM3 compression are performed.

normative_rules.name: vsm3c-vi_op_sm3
normative_rules.text:
The current state of eight 32-bit words is read in as an element group from vd. Eight 32-bit
message words are read in as an element group from vs2, although only four of them are used.
All of the 32-bit input words are byte-swapped from big endian to little endian.
These inputs are processed somewhat differently based on the round group (as specified in uimm),
and the next state is generated as an element group of eight 32-bit words.
The next state of eight 32-bit words are generated,
swapped from little endian to big endian, and are returned in
an eight-element group.

normative_rules.name: vsm3c-vi_op_rnd
normative_rules.text:
The round number is provided by the 5-bit uimm unsigned immediate. Legal values are 0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;31
and indicate which group of two rounds are being performed. For example, if uimm=1,
then rounds 2 and 3 are being performed.

normative_rules.name: vsm3me-vv_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsm3me-vv_vdoverlapvs2_rsv
normative_rules.text: The vd register group overlaps with the vs2 register group.

normative_rules.name: vsm3me-vv_op
normative_rules.text: Eight rounds of SM3 message expansion are performed.

normative_rules.name: vsm3me-vv_op_sm3
normative_rules.text:
The sixteen most recent 32-bit message words are read in as two
eight-element groups from vs1 and vs2. Each of these words is
swapped from big endian to little endian.
The next eight 32-bit message words are generated,
swapped from little endian to big endian, and are returned in
an eight-element group.

normative_rules.name: vsm4k-vi_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsm4k-vi_op
normative_rules.text: Four rounds of the SM4 Key Expansion are performed.

normative_rules.name: vsm4k-vi_op_sm4k
normative_rules.text:
Four round keys are read in as a 4-element group from vs2. Each of the next four round keys are generated
by iteratively XORing the last three round keys with a constant that is indexed by the Round Group Number,
performing a byte-wise substitution, and then performing XORs between rotated versions of this value
and the corresponding current round key.

normative_rules.name: vsm4k-vi_op_rnd
normative_rules.text:
The Round group number comes from uimm[2:0]; the bits in uimm[4:3] are ignored.
Round group numbers range from 0 to 7 and indicate which
group of four round keys are being generated. Round Keys range from 0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;31.
For example, if uimm=1, then round keys 4, 5, 6, and 7 are being generated.

normative_rules.name: vsm4r_sewn32_rsv
normative_rules.text: SEW is any value other than 32

normative_rules.name: vsm4r-vs_vdoverlapvs2_rsv
normative_rules.text: Only for the insn:*.vs[] form: the vd register group overlaps the vs2 register

normative_rules.name: vsm4r_op
normative_rules.text: Four rounds of SM4 Encryption/Decryption are performed.

normative_rules.name: vsm4r_op_sm4encdec
normative_rules.text:
The four words of current state are read as a 4-element group from vd
and the round keys are read from either the corresponding 4-element group
in vs2 (vector-vector form) or the scalar element group in vs2
(vector-scalar form).
The next four words of state are generated
by iteratively XORing the last three words of the state with
the corresponding round key, performing
a byte-wise substitution, and then performing XORs between rotated
versions of this value and the corresponding current state.
