normative_rules.name: always_priv_level
normative_rules.text:
At any time, a RISC-V hardware thread (hart) is running at some
privilege level encoded as a mode in one or more CSRs (control and
status registers).

normative_rules.name: priv_levels_txt
normative_rules.text: Three RISC-V privilege levels are currently defined

normative_rules.name: priv_levels_tbl
normative_rules.text:
Level|Encoding|Name|Abbreviation
===
0|00|User/Application|U¶1|01|Supervisor|S¶2|10|Reserved| ¶3|11|Machine|M
===

normative_rules.name: non_priv_exc
normative_rules.text:
attempts to perform operations not
permitted by the current privilege mode will cause an exception to be
raised.

normative_rules.name: m_level_high_priv_only_mandatory
normative_rules.text:
The machine level has the highest privileges and
is the only mandatory privilege level for a RISC-V hardware platform.

normative_rules.name: priv_combs_txt
normative_rules.text: Implementations might provide anywhere from 1 to 3 privilege modes

normative_rules.name: priv_combs_tbl
normative_rules.text:
Number of levels|Supported Modes|Intended Usage
===
1|M|Simple embedded systems¶2|M, U|Secure embedded systems¶3|M, S, U|Systems running Unix-like operating systems
===

normative_rules.name: m_mode_mandatory
normative_rules.text: All hardware implementations must provide M-mode

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_higher_priv
normative_rules.text:
although CSRs and instructions are associated with one privilege
level, they are also accessible at all higher privilege levels.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_no_read_side_effects
normative_rules.text:
Standard CSRs do not have side effects on reads but may have side
effects on writes.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_rw
normative_rules.text: The top two bits (csr[11:10]) indicate whether the register is read/write (00,01, or 10) or read-only (11).

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_access
normative_rules.text: The next two bits (csr[9:8]) encode the lowest privilege level that can access the CSR, with the pattern 10 representing hypervisor CSRs.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_illegal_mode
normative_rules.text:
Attempts to access a CSR address without sufficient privilege
raise illegal-instruction exceptions or, as described in
<<sec:hcauses>>, virtual-instruction exceptions.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_illegal_acc
normative_rules.text: Attempts to write a read-only CSR address raise illegal-instruction exceptions.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_write_ro
normative_rules.text:
A read/write register might also contain some bits that are
read-only, in which case writes to the read-only bits are ignored.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_nonexistent_rsv
normative_rules.text: Instructions that access a non-existent CSR address are reserved.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_debug_range
normative_rules.text:
Machine-mode standard read-write CSRs 0x7A0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;0x7BF are reserved for
use by the debug system. Of these CSRs, 0x7A0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;0x7AF are accessible
to machine mode, whereas

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_debug_illegal
normative_rules.text:
0x7B0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;0x7BF are only visible to debug mode.
Implementations must raise illegal-instruction exceptions on
machine-mode access to the latter set of registers.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_wpri_roz
normative_rules.text:
For forward compatibility, implementations that do not
furnish these fields must make them read-only zero. These fields are
labeled WPRI in the register descriptions.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_wlrl
normative_rules.text:
Software
should not write anything other than legal values to such a field, and
should not assume a read will return a legal value unless the last write
was of a legal value, or the register has not been written since another
operation (e.g., reset) set the register to a legal value. These fields
are labeled WLRL in the register descriptions.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_wlrl_exception
normative_rules.text:
Implementations are permitted but not required to raise an
illegal-instruction exception if an instruction attempts to write a
non-supported value to a WLRL field.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_wlrl_deterministic
normative_rules.text:
Implementations can return arbitrary
bit patterns on the read of a WLRL field when the last write was of an
illegal value, but the value returned should deterministically depend on
the illegal written value and the value of the field prior to the write.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_warl_def
normative_rules.text:
Some read/write CSR fields are only defined for a subset of bit
encodings, but allow any value to be written while guaranteeing to
return a legal value whenever read.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_warl
normative_rules.text:
Implementations will not raise an exception on writes of unsupported
values to a WARL field.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_warl_deterministic
normative_rules.text:
Implementations can return any legal value on the
read of a WARL field when the last write was of an illegal value, but the
legal value returned should deterministically depend on the illegal
written value and the architectural state of the hart.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_field_modulation
normative_rules.text:
If a write to one CSR changes the set of legal values allowed for a
field of a second CSR, then unless specified otherwise, the second CSR's
field immediately gets an UNSPECIFIED value from among its new legal values. This
is true even if the field's value before the write remains legal after
the write; the value of the field may be changed in consequence of the
write to the controlling CSR.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_field_modulation_no_side_effects
normative_rules.text:
A change to the value of a CSR for this reason is not a write to the
affected CSR and thus does not trigger any side effects specified for
that CSR.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_implicit_read
normative_rules.text:
Unless otherwise specified, the value returned by an implicit read of a
CSR is the same value that would have been returned by an explicit read
of the CSR, using a CSR-access instruction in a sufficient privilege
mode.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_width_modulation
normative_rules.text: If the width of a CSR is changed (for example, by changing SXLEN or UXLEN, as described in ), the values of the writable fields and bits of the new-width CSR are, unless specified otherwise, determined from the previous-width CSR as though by this algorithm:

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_width_modulation_no_side_effects
normative_rules.text:
Changing the width of a CSR is not a read or write of the CSR and thus
does not trigger any side effects.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_wide_csr_access
normative_rules.text:
If a standard CSR is wider than XLEN bits, then an explicit read
of the CSR returns the register's least-significant XLEN bits,
and an explicit write to the CSR modifies only the register's
least-significant XLEN bits, leaving the upper bits unchanged.

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_high_half_alias
normative_rules.text:
The high-half CSR aliases bits 63:32 of its namesake
64-bit CSR, thus providing a way for RV32 software
to read and modify the otherwise-unreachable qty:32[bits].

normative_rules.name: Zicsr_high_half_rv64_rsv
normative_rules.text:
Standard high-half CSRs are accessible only when
the base RISC-V instruction set is RV32 (XLEN=32).
For RV64 (when XLEN=64), the addresses of all standard high-half CSRs
are reserved, so an attempt to access a high-half CSR
typically raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: m_highest_priv_mode
normative_rules.text:
machine-mode (M-mode), which is the highest privilege mode in a RISC-V
hart.

normative_rules.name: m_mode_first_at_reset
normative_rules.text:
M-mode is used for low-level access to a hardware platform and
is the first mode entered at reset.

normative_rules.name: m_access_all_lower_priv_csrs
normative_rules.text: M-mode code can access all CSRs at lower privilege levels.

normative_rules.name: misa_acc
normative_rules.text: The csr:misa[] CSR is a WARL read-write register

normative_rules.name: misa_always_rd
normative_rules.text: This register must be readable in any implementation

normative_rules.name: misa_csr_implemented
normative_rules.text: a value of zero can be returned to indicate this feature has not been implemented

normative_rules.name: misa_mxl_op_isa
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[mxl] (Machine XLEN) field encodes the native base integer ISA width as
shown in <<norm:misa_mxl_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: misa_mxl_acc
normative_rules.text: The csr::[mxl] field is read-only.

normative_rules.name: misa_mxl_op_nz
normative_rules.text:
If csr:misa[] is nonzero, the
csr::[mxl] field indicates the effective XLEN in M-mode, a constant termed MXLEN.

normative_rules.name: xlen_le_mxlen
normative_rules.text:
XLEN is never greater than MXLEN, but XLEN might be smaller than MXLEN in
less-privileged modes.

normative_rules.name: misa_mxl_enc
normative_rules.text:
MXL|XLEN
===
1|32¶2|64¶3|Reserved
===

normative_rules.name: misa_sz
normative_rules.text: The csr:misa[] CSR is MXLEN bits wide.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_enc_txt
normative_rules.text:
The Extensions field encodes the presence of the standard extensions,
with a single bit per letter of the alphabet (bit 0 encodes presence of
extension ext:a[], bit 1 encodes presence of extension ext:b[], through to
bit 25 which encodes ext:z[]).

normative_rules.name: misa_i_op
normative_rules.text: The csr::[i] bit will be set for the RV32I and RV64I base ISAs

normative_rules.name: misa_e_op
normative_rules.text: the csr::[e] bit will be set for RV32E and RV64E.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_warl_op
normative_rules.text:
The Extensions field is a WARL field that can contain writable bits where the
implementation allows the supported ISA to be modified.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_reset_maximal
normative_rules.text:
At reset, the Extensions field shall contain the maximal set of supported extensions,
and csr::[i] shall be selected over csr::[e] if both are available.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_disabling
normative_rules.text: When a standard extension is disabled by clearing its bit in csr:misa[], the instructions and CSRs defined or modified by the extension revert to their defined or reserved behaviors as if the extension is not implemented.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_rsv_ret_0
normative_rules.text: All bits that are reserved for future use must return zero when read.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_enc_tbl
normative_rules.text:
Bit|Character|Description
===
0|csr::[a]|Atomic extension¶1|csr::[b]|B extension¶2|csr::[c]|Compressed extension¶3|csr::[d]|Double-precision floating-point extension¶4|csr::[e]|RV32E/64E base ISA¶5|csr::[f]|Single-precision floating-point extension¶6|csr::[g]|Reserved¶7|csr::[h]|Hypervisor extension¶8|csr::[i]|RV32I/64I base ISA¶9|csr::[j]|Reserved¶10|csr::[k]|Reserved¶11|csr::[l]|Reserved¶12|csr::[m]|Integer Multiply/Divide extension¶13|csr::[n]|Tentatively reserved for User-Level Interrupts extension¶14|csr::[o]|Reserved¶15|csr::[p]|Tentatively reserved for Packed-SIMD extension¶16|csr::[q]|Quad-precision floating-point extension¶17|csr::[r]|Reserved¶18|csr::[s]|Supervisor mode implemented¶19|csr::[t]|Reserved¶20|csr::[u]|User mode implemented¶21|csr::[v]|Vector extension¶22|csr::[w]|Reserved¶23|csr::[x]|Non-standard extensions implemented¶24|csr::[y]|Reserved¶25|csr::[z]|Reserved
===

normative_rules.name: misa_x_op
normative_rules.text: The csr::[x] bit will be set if there are any non-standard extensions.

normative_rules.name: misa_B_op
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[b] bit is 1, the implementation supports the instructions provided by the
ext:zba[], ext:zbb[], and ext:zbs[] extensions.

normative_rules.name: misa_m_op
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[m] bit is 1, the implementation supports all multiply and
division instructions defined by the ext:m[] extension.

normative_rules.name: Zmmul_misa_m
normative_rules.text:
if the ext:zmmul[] extension is supported then
the multiply instructions it specifies are supported irrespective
of the value of the csr::[m] bit.

normative_rules.name: misa_s_op
normative_rules.text: When the csr::[s] bit is 1, the implementation supports supervisor mode.

normative_rules.name: misa_u_op
normative_rules.text: When the csr::[u] bit is 1, the implementation supports user mode.

normative_rules.name: misa_e_acc
normative_rules.text: The csr::[e] bit is read-only.

normative_rules.name: misa_e_not_i
normative_rules.text:
Unless csr:misa[] is all read-only zero, the
csr::[e] bit always reads as the complement of the csr::[i] bit.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_dependencies
normative_rules.text:
If an ISA feature x depends on an ISA feature y, then attempting to
enable feature x but disable feature y results in both features
being disabled.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_collective_warl
normative_rules.text:
An implementation may impose additional constraints on the collective
setting of two or more csr:misa[] fields, in which case they function
collectively as a single WARL field. An attempt to write an unsupported combination causes those bits to be set to some supported combination.

normative_rules.name: misa_inc_ialign
normative_rules.text:
Writing csr:misa[] may increase IALIGN, e.g., by disabling the
ext:c[] extension. If an instruction that would write csr:misa[] increases IALIGN,
and the subsequent instruction's address is not IALIGN-bit aligned, the
write to csr:misa[] is suppressed, leaving csr:misa[] unchanged.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_reenable_unspec
normative_rules.text:
When software enables an extension that was previously disabled, then
all state uniquely associated with that extension is UNSPECIFIED, unless otherwise specified by that extension.

normative_rules.name: mvendorid_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mvendorid[] CSR is a 32-bit read-only register providing the JEDEC
manufacturer ID of the provider of the core.

normative_rules.name: mvendorid_always_rd
normative_rules.text:
This register must be readable in any implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to
indicate the field is not implemented or that this is a non-commercial implementation.

normative_rules.name: mvendorid_enc
normative_rules.text:
JEDEC manufacturer IDs are ordinarily encoded as a sequence of one-byte
continuation codes 0x7f, terminated by a one-byte ID not equal to
0x7f, with an odd parity bit in the most-significant bit of each byte.
mvendorid encodes the number of one-byte continuation codes in the
Bank field, and encodes the final byte in the Offset field, discarding
the parity bit.

normative_rules.name: marchid_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:marchid[] CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register encoding the base
microarchitecture of the hart.

normative_rules.name: marchid_always_rd
normative_rules.text:
This register must be readable in any
implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate the field is not implemented.

normative_rules.name: mimpid_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mimpid[] CSR provides a unique encoding of the version of the
processor implementation.

normative_rules.name: mimpid_always_rd
normative_rules.text:
This register must be readable in any
implementation, but a value of 0 can be returned to indicate that the field is not implemented.

normative_rules.name: mhartid_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mhartid[] CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register containing the
integer ID of the hardware thread running the code.

normative_rules.name: mhartid_always_rd
normative_rules.text: This register must be readable in any implementation.

normative_rules.name: mhartid_one_is_zero
normative_rules.text: one hart must have a hart ID of zero.

normative_rules.name: mhartid_unique
normative_rules.text: Hart IDs must be unique within the execution environment.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mstatus[] register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as
shown in <<mstatusreg-rv32>> for RV32 and <<mstatusreg>> for RV64. csr:mstatus[] must be implemented.

normative_rules.name: mstatush_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: For RV32 only, csr:mstatush[] is a 32-bit read/write register formatted as shown in <<mstatushreg>>.

normative_rules.name: mstatush_enc
normative_rules.text: Bits 30:4 of csr:mstatush[] generally contain the same fields found in bits 62:36 of csr:mstatus[] for RV64. Fields csr::[sd], csr::[sxl], and csr::[uxl] do not exist in mstatush.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_sie_exist
normative_rules.text:
Global interrupt-enable bits, csr::[mie] and csr::[sie], are provided for M-mode and
S-mode respectively.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_sie_op
normative_rules.text:
When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts are globally
enabled when xIE=1 and globally disabled when xIE=0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xie_intr_en_dis
normative_rules.text:
Interrupts for lower-privilege modes, w<x,
are always globally disabled regardless of the setting of any global wIE bit for the
lower-privilege mode.  Interrupts for higher-privilege modes, y>x,
are always globally enabled regardless of the
setting of the global yIE bit for the higher-privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sie_spie_rdonly0
mstatus_xpie_xpp_op
normative_rules.text:
each privilege mode x that can respond to
interrupts has a two-level stack of interrupt-enable bits and privilege modes.
xPIE holds the value of the interrupt-enable bit active prior
to the trap, and xPP holds the previous privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xpp_enc
normative_rules.text: The xPP fields can only hold privilege modes up to x

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mpp_sz
normative_rules.text: csr::[mpp] is two bits wide

normative_rules.name: mstatus_spp_sz
normative_rules.text: csr::[spp] is one bit wide.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xpie_xie_xpp_trap_op
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is taken from privilege mode y
into privilege mode x, xPIE is set to the value of xIE; xIE is
set to 0; and xPP is set to y.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xret_op
normative_rules.text:
When executing an xRET instruction, supposing
xPP holds the value y, xIE is set to xPIE; the privilege mode is
changed to y; xPIE is set to 1; and xPP is set to the
least-privileged supported mode (U if U-mode is implemented, else M). If
y≠M, xRET also sets csr::[mprv]=0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xpp_warl
normative_rules.text: xPP fields are WARL fields that can hold only privilege mode x and any implemented privilege mode lower than x.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xpp_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If privilege mode x is not implemented, then xPP must be read-only 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mdt_sz_warl
normative_rules.text: The M-mode-disable-trap (csr::[mdt]) bit is a WARL field introduced by the ext:smdbltrp[] extension.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mdt_rst
normative_rules.text: Upon reset, the csr::[mdt] field is set to 1.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_clr_by_mdt
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[mdt] bit is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write,
the csr::[mie] (Machine Interrupt Enable) bit is cleared to 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_clr_by_mdt_rv64
normative_rules.text: For RV64, this clearing occurs regardless of the value written, if any, to the csr::[mie] bit by the same write.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_set_mdt_0
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[mie] bit can only be set to 1 by an
explicit CSR write if the csr::[mdt] bit is already 0

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_set_mdt_0_rv64
normative_rules.text: or, for RV64, is being set to 0 by the same write

normative_rules.name: trap_exp
normative_rules.text: When a trap is to be taken into M-mode, if the csr::[mdt] bit is currently 0, it is then set to 1, and the trap is delivered as expected.

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_mdt_1
normative_rules.text: However, if csr::[mdt] is already set to 1, then this is an unexpected trap.

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_rnmi
normative_rules.text:
When the ext:smrnmi[] extension
is implemented, a trap caused by an RNMI is not considered an unexpected trap
irrespective of the state of the csr::[mdt] bit.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mdt_not_set_rnmi
normative_rules.text: A trap caused by an RNMI does not set the csr::[mdt] bit.

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_mnstatus_nmie_0
normative_rules.text:
a trap that occurs when executing in M-mode with
csr:mnstatus[nmie] set to 0 is an unexpected trap.

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_hndl_lead_in
normative_rules.text: In the event of a unexpected trap, the handling is as follows:

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_hndl_rnmi
normative_rules.text:
When the Smrnmi extension is implemented and csr:mnstatus[nmie] is 1, the hart
traps to the RNMI interrupt trap handler. To deliver this trap, the csr:mnepc[] and
csr:mncause[] registers are written with the values that the unexpected trap would have
written to the csr:mepc[] and csr:mcause[] registers respectively. The privilege
mode information fields in the csr:mnstatus[] register are written to indicate
M-mode and its csr::[nmie] field is set to 0.

normative_rules.name: trap_unexp_hndl_no_rnmi
normative_rules.text:
When the ext:smrnmi[] extension is not implemented, or if the ext:smrnmi[] extension is
implemented and csr:mnstatus[nmie] is 0, the hart enters a critical-error state
without updating any architectural state, including the pc. This state
involves ceasing execution, disabling all interrupts (including NMIs), and
asserting a critical-error signal to the platform.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mdt_clr_mret_sret
normative_rules.text: The csr::[mdt] bit is set to 0.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_clr_mret_sret
normative_rules.text: If the Ssdbltrp extension is also implemented, and the new privilege mode is U, VS, or VU, then csr:sstatus[sdt] is also set to 0.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sdt_clr_mret_sret
normative_rules.text: Additionally, if it is VU, then csr:vsstatus[sdt] is also set to 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mdt_clr_mnret
normative_rules.text: When the ext:smdbltrp[] extension is implemented, the insn:mnret[] instruction, provided by the ext:smrnmi[] extension, sets the csr::[mdt] bit to 0 if the new privilege mode is not M.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_clr_mnret
normative_rules.text: If the ext:ssdbltrp[] extension is also implemented, and the new privilege mode is U, VS, or VU, then csr:sstatus[sdt] is also set to 0.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sdt_clr_mnret
normative_rules.text: Additionally, if it is VU, then csr:vsstatus[sdt] is also set to 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sxl_uxl_warl_op
normative_rules.text:
For RV64 harts, the csr::[sxl] and csr::[uxl] fields are WARL fields that control the
value of XLEN for S-mode and U-mode, respectively.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sxl_uxl_enc
normative_rules.text: The encoding of these fields is the same as the csr::[mxl] field of csr:misa[], shown in <<norm:misa_mxl_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: sxlen_uxlen
normative_rules.text: The effective XLEN in S-mode and U-mode are termed SXLEN and UXLEN, respectively.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sxl_uxl_sxlen_uxlen_mxlen32
normative_rules.text: When MXLEN=32, the csr::[sxl] and csr::[uxl] fields do not exist, and SXLEN=32 and UXLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sxl_acc_mxlen64
normative_rules.text:
When MXLEN=64, if S-mode is not supported, then csr::[sxl] is read-only zero.
Otherwise, it is a WARL field that encodes the current value of SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sxl_rdonly_mxlen64
normative_rules.text:
an implementation may make csr::[sxl] be a read-only field whose
value always ensures that SXLEN=MXLEN.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_uxl_acc_mxlen64
normative_rules.text:
When MXLEN=64, if U-mode is not supported, then csr::[uxl] is read-only zero.
Otherwise, it is a WARL field that encodes the current value of UXLEN.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_uxl_rdonly_mxlen64
normative_rules.text:
an implementation may make csr::[uxl] be a read-only field whose
value always ensures that UXLEN=MXLEN or UXLEN=SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_uxl_legal_vals_smode
normative_rules.text: If S-mode is implemented, the set of legal values that the csr::[uxl] field may assume excludes those that would cause UXLEN to be greater than SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: xlen_reduction_op
normative_rules.text: Whenever XLEN in any mode is set to a value less than the widest supported XLEN, all operations must ignore source operand register bits above the configured XLEN, and must sign-extend results to fill the entire widest supported XLEN in the destination register. Similarly, pc bits above XLEN are ignored, and when the pc is written, it is sign-extended to fill the widest supported XLEN.

normative_rules.name: xlen_reduction_hint_op
normative_rules.text: Some HINT instructions are encoded as integer computational instructions that overwrite their destination register with its current value, e.g., insn:c.addi[x8,0]. When such a HINT is executed with XLEN < MXLEN and bits MXLEN..XLEN of the destination register not all equal to bit XLEN-1, it is implementation-defined whether bits MXLEN..XLEN of the destination register are unchanged or are overwritten with copies of bit XLEN-1.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_ldst_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[mprv]=0, explicit memory accesses
behave as normal, using the translation and
protection mechanisms of the current privilege mode. When csr::[mprv]=1, load
and store memory addresses are translated and protected, and endianness
is applied, as though the current privilege mode were set to csr::[mpp].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_inst_xlat_op
normative_rules.text:
Instruction address-translation and protection are unaffected by the
setting of csr::[mprv].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_rdonly0_no_umode
normative_rules.text: csr::[mprv] is read-only 0 if U-mode is not supported; otherwise, it must be writable.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_clr_mret_sret_less_priv
normative_rules.text:
An insn:mret[] or insn:sret[] instruction that changes the privilege mode to a mode
less privileged than M also sets csr::[mprv]=0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mxr_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[mxr]=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1 in <<sv32pte>>) will succeed.
When csr::[mxr]=1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or
X=1) will succeed.
csr::[mxr] only affects loads whose effective privilege mode is less than M.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mxr_rdonly0_no_smode
normative_rules.text: csr::[mxr] is read-only 0 if S-mode is not supported or if csr:satp[mode] is read-only 0; otherwise, it must be writable.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sum_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[sum]=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode
(U=1 in <<sv32pte>>) will fault. When csr::[sum]=1, these accesses are permitted.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sum_op_no_vm
normative_rules.text: csr::[sum] has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sum_op_mprv_mpp
normative_rules.text:
while csr::[sum] is ordinarily ignored when not
executing in S-mode, it is in effect when csr::[mprv]=1 and csr::[mpp]=S.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sum_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: csr::[sum] is read-only 0 if S-mode is not supported or if csr:satp[mode] is read-only 0; otherwise, it must be writable.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mxr_sum_op_acc_fault
normative_rules.text: The csr::[mxr] and csr::[sum] mechanisms only affect the interpretation of permissions encoded in page-table entries. In particular, they have no impact on whether access-fault exceptions are raised due to PMAs or PMP.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mstatush_xbe_warl
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[mbe], csr::[sbe], and csr::[ube] bits in csr:mstatus[] and csr:mstatush[] are WARL fields that
control the endianness of memory accesses other than instruction fetches.
Each may be read/write or read-only.

normative_rules.name: endianness_inst_fetch_little
normative_rules.text: Instruction fetches are always little-endian.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mbe_op
normative_rules.text: csr::[mbe] controls whether non-instruction-fetch memory accesses made from M-mode (assuming csr:mstatus[mprv]=0) are little-endian (csr::[mbe]=0) or big-endian (csr::[mbe]=1).

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sbe_op
normative_rules.text: If S-mode is not supported, csr::[sbe] is read-only 0. Otherwise, csr::[sbe] controls whether explicit load and store memory accesses made from S-mode are little-endian (csr::[sbe]=0) or big-endian (csr::[sbe]=1).

normative_rules.name: mstatus_ube_op
normative_rules.text: If U-mode is not supported, csr::[ube] is read-only 0. Otherwise, UBE controls whether explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode are little-endian (csr::[ube]=0) or big-endian (csr::[ube]=1).

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sbe_implicit
normative_rules.text:
For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory management data
structures, such as page tables, endianness is always controlled by csr::[sbe].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sbe_change_fence
normative_rules.text:
Since changing csr::[sbe] alters the implementation’s interpretation of these
data structures, if any such data structures remain in use across a
change to csr::[sbe], M-mode software must follow such a change to csr::[sbe] by
executing an insn:sfence.vma[] instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sbe_rocopy
normative_rules.text:
If S-mode is supported, an implementation may make csr::[sbe] be a read-only
copy of csr::[mbe].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_ube_rocopy
normative_rules.text:
If U-mode is supported, an implementation may make csr::[ube] be a
read-only copy of either csr::[mbe] or csr::[sbe].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tvm_warl
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[tvm] (Trap Virtual Memory) bit is a WARL field that supports intercepting
supervisor virtual-memory management operations.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tvm_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[tvm]=1, attempts to
read or write the csr:satp[] CSR or execute an insn:sfence.vma[] or insn:sinval.vma[]
instruction while executing in S-mode will raise an illegal-instruction
exception. When csr::[tvm]=0, these operations are permitted in S-mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tvm_acc
mstatus_tw_warl
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[tw] (Timeout Wait) bit is a WARL field that supports intercepting the
insn:wfi[] instruction (see <<wfi>>).

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tw_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[tw]=0, the insn:wfi[] instruction may execute in modes less privileged than M when not prevented for
some other reason. When csr::[tw]=1, then if insn:wfi[] is executed in any
less-privileged mode, and it does not complete within an
implementation-specific, bounded time limit, the insn:wfi[] instruction causes
an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tw_always_illegal
normative_rules.text:
An implementation may have insn:wfi[] always
raise an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M when
csr::[tw]=1, even if there are pending globally-disabled interrupts when the
instruction is executed.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tw_acc
normative_rules.text:
csr::[tw] is read-only 0 when there are no modes less privileged than M;
otherwise, it must be writable.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tw_umode_op
normative_rules.text:
When S-mode is implemented, then executing insn:wfi[] in U-mode causes an
illegal-instruction exception, regardless of the value of the csr::[tw] bit, unless the
instruction completes within an implementation-specific, bounded time limit.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tsr_warl
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[tsr] (Trap insn:sret[]) bit is a WARL field that supports intercepting the
supervisor exception return instruction, insn:sret[].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tsr_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[tsr]=1, attempts to
execute insn:sret[] while executing in S-mode will raise an illegal-instruction
exception. When csr::[tsr]=0, this operation is permitted in S-mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tsr_acc
normative_rules.text:
csr::[tsr] is read-only 0 when S-mode is not supported;
otherwise, it must be writable.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_warl
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[fs][1:0] and csr::[vs][1:0] WARL fields
and the csr::[xs][1:0] read-only field are used
to reduce the cost of context save and restore by setting and tracking
the current state of the floating-point unit and any other user-mode
extensions respectively.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[fs] field encodes the status of the
floating-point unit state, including the floating-point registers
f0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;f31 and the CSRs csr:fcsr[], csr:frm[], and csr:fflags[].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[vs] field encodes the status of the
vector extension state, including the vector
registers v0&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;v31 and the CSRs csr:vcsr[], csr:vxrm[], csr:vxsat[], csr:vstart[],
csr:vl[], csr:vtype[], and csr:vlenb[].

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xs_encodes_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[xs] field encodes the status of
additional user-mode extensions and associated state.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_enc
normative_rules.text:
Status|FS and VS Meaning|XS Meaning
===
0|Off|All off¶1|Initial|None dirty or clean, some on¶2|Clean|None dirty, some clean¶3|Dirty|Some dirty
===

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_acc1
normative_rules.text: If the ext:f[] extension is implemented, the csr::[fs] field shall not be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_acc2
normative_rules.text: If neither the ext:f[] extension nor S-mode is implemented, then csr::[fs] is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_rdonly0_s_no_F
normative_rules.text:
If S-mode is implemented but the ext:f[] extension is not,
csr::[fs] may optionally be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_acc1
normative_rules.text: If the v registers are implemented, the csr::[vs] field shall not be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_acc2
normative_rules.text:
If neither the v registers nor S-mode is implemented, then csr::[vs] is
read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_rdonly0_s_no_V
normative_rules.text:
If S-mode is implemented but the v registers are not,
csr::[vs] may optionally be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xs_acc
normative_rules.text:
In harts without additional user extensions requiring new state, the
csr::[xs] field is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xs_equiv
normative_rules.text:
Every additional extension with state
provides a CSR field that encodes the equivalent of the csr::[xs] states.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_xs_summary_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[xs] field represents a summary of all extensions' status as shown in
<<norm:mstatus_fs_vs_xs_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_acc
normative_rules.text: The csr::[sd] bit is a read-only bit

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_summary_op
normative_rules.text:
summarizes whether either the csr::[fs], csr::[vs],
or csr::[xs] fields signal the presence of some dirty state that will require
saving extended user context to memory.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If csr::[fs], csr::[vs], and csr::[xs] are all read-only zero, then csr::[sd] is also always zero.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_off_op
normative_rules.text:
When an extension's status is set to Off, any instruction that attempts
to read or write the corresponding state will cause an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_initial_op
normative_rules.text:
When the status is Initial, the corresponding
state should have an initial constant value.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_clean_op
normative_rules.text:
When the status is Clean,
the corresponding state is potentially different from the initial value,
but matches the last value stored on a context swap.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_dirty_op
normative_rules.text:
When the status is Dirty,
the corresponding state has potentially been modified since the last context save.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_vs_xs_update_indep_priv
normative_rules.text:
The status fields are
also updated during execution of instructions, regardless of privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_wr
normative_rules.text:
Changing the setting of csr::[fs] has no effect on the contents of the
floating-point register state. In particular, setting csr::[fs]=Off does not
destroy the state, nor does setting csr::[fs]=Initial clear the contents.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_wr
normative_rules.text:
the setting of VS has no effect on the contents of the vector
register state.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_imprecise
normative_rules.text:
Implementations may choose to track the dirtiness of the floating-point
register state imprecisely by reporting the state to be dirty even when
it has not been modified.
On some implementations, some instructions
that do not mutate the floating-point state may cause the state to
transition from Initial or Clean to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_no_dirty_track
normative_rules.text:
dirtiness might not be tracked at all, in which case the valid FS states
are Off and Dirty, and an attempt to set csr::[fs] to Initial or Clean causes
it to be set to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_fs_no_change_dirty
normative_rules.text:
If an instruction explicitly or implicitly writes a floating-point
register or the csr:fcsr[] but does not alter its contents, and csr::[fs]=Initial
or csr::[fs]=Clean, it is implementation-defined whether FS transitions to
Dirty.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_imprecise
normative_rules.text:
Implementations may choose to track the dirtiness of the vector register
state in an analogous imprecise fashion, including possibly setting
csr::[vs] to Dirty when software attempts to set csr::[vs]=Initial or csr::[vs]=Clean.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_vs_no_change_dirty
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[vs]=Initial or csr::[vs]=Clean, it is implementation-defined whether an
instruction that writes a vector register or vector CSR but does not
alter its contents causes csr::[vs] to transition to Dirty.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_sd_formula
normative_rules.text:
The csr::[sd] bit is read-only and is set when either the csr::[fs], csr::[vs], or csr::[xs] bits
encode a Dirty state (i.e., csr::[sd]=(csr::[fs]==0b11 OR csr::[xs]==0b11 OR csr::[vs]==0b11)).

normative_rules.name: mstatus_spelp_mpelp_op
normative_rules.text:
The ext:zicfilp[] extension adds the csr::[spelp] and csr::[mpelp] fields that hold the previous
csr::[elp], and are updated as specified in <<ZICFILP_FORWARD_TRAPS>>.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_spelp_mpelp_enc_lead_in
normative_rules.text: The x`PELP` fields are encoded as follows:

normative_rules.name: mstatus_spelp_mpelp_enc_list
normative_rules.text:
0 - NO_LP_EXPECTED - no landing pad instruction expected.
1 - LP_EXPECTED - a landing pad instruction is expected.

normative_rules.name: mtvec_sz_warl_acc
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mtvec[] register is an MXLEN-bit WARL read/write register that holds
trap vector configuration, consisting of a vector base address (csr::[base])
and a vector mode (csr::[mode]).

normative_rules.name: mtvec_mandatory
normative_rules.text: The csr:mtvec[] register must always be implemented

normative_rules.name: mtvec_rdonly
normative_rules.text: can contain a read-only value.

normative_rules.name: mtvec_base_align_4b
normative_rules.text:
The value in the csr::[base] field must
always be aligned on a 4-byte boundary

normative_rules.name: mtvec_base_align_func_mode
normative_rules.text:
the csr::[mode] setting may impose
additional alignment constraints on the value in the csr::[base] field.

normative_rules.name: mtvec_mode_enc
normative_rules.text:
Value|Name|Description
===
0|Direct|All traps set pc to csr::[base].¶1|Vectored|Asynchronous interrupts set pc to csr::[base]+4×cause.¶≥2| — |Reserved
===

normative_rules.name: mtvec_mode_direct_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[mode]=Direct, all traps into
machine mode cause the pc to be set to the address in the csr::[base] field.

normative_rules.name: mtvec_mode_vectored_op
normative_rules.text:
When csr::[mode]=Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into machine mode cause
the pc to be set to the address in the csr::[base] field, whereas interrupts
cause the pc to be set to the address in the csr::[base] field plus four
times the interrupt cause number.

normative_rules.name: trap_def_m_mode
normative_rules.text:
By default, all traps at any privilege level are handled in machine
mode

normative_rules.name: medeleg_mideleg_per_bit_rw
normative_rules.text:
implementations can provide individual read/write bits within
csr:medeleg[] and csr:mideleg[] to indicate that certain exceptions and interrupts should
be processed directly by a lower privilege level.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: The machine exception delegation register (csr:medeleg[]) is a 64-bit read/write register.

normative_rules.name: mideleg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The machine interrupt delegation (csr:mideleg[]) register is an MXLEN-bit
read/write register.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_mideleg_mandatory_s_mode
normative_rules.text:
In harts with S-mode, the medeleg and mideleg registers must
exist

normative_rules.name: medeleg_mideleg_delegate_op
normative_rules.text:
setting a bit in csr:medeleg[] or csr:mideleg[] will delegate the
corresponding trap, when occurring in S-mode or U-mode, to the S-mode
trap handler.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_mideleg_omit_wo_s_mode
normative_rules.text: In harts without S-mode, the csr:medeleg[] and csr:mideleg[] registers should not exist.

normative_rules.name: trap_del_s_mode_op
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is delegated to S-mode,
the csr:scause[] register is written
with the trap cause; the csr:sepc[] register is written with the virtual
address of the instruction that took the trap; the csr:stval[] register is
written with an exception-specific datum; the csr::[spp] field of csr:mstatus[] is
written with the active privilege mode at the time of the trap; the
csr::[spie] field of csr:mstatus[] is written with the value of the csr::[sie] field at the
time of the trap; and the csr::[sie] field of csr:mstatus[] is cleared.

normative_rules.name: trap_del_s_mode_no_m_mode
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mcause[], csr:mepc[], and csr:mtval[] registers and the csr::[mpp] and csr::[mpie] fields of
csr:mstatus[] are not written.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_mideleg_warl
normative_rules.text:
An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps, with the
supported delegatable bits found by writing one to every bit location,
then reading back the value in csr:medeleg[] or csr:mideleg[] to see which bit
positions hold a one.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_no_rd1
normative_rules.text: An implementation shall not have any bits of csr:medeleg[] be read-only one

normative_rules.name: mideleg_no_rd1
normative_rules.text:
an implementation shall not fix as read-only one
any bits of csr:mideleg[] corresponding to machine-level interrupts

normative_rules.name: mideleg_rd1_lower_level
normative_rules.text: may do so for lower-level interrupts

normative_rules.name: trap_never_trans_lower
normative_rules.text:
Traps never transition from a more-privileged mode to a less-privileged mode.
For example, if M-mode has delegated illegal-instruction
exceptions to S-mode, and M-mode software later executes an illegal
instruction, the trap is taken in M-mode, rather than being delegated to S-mode.

normative_rules.name: trap_horiz
normative_rules.text:
traps may be taken horizontally. Using the same
example, if M-mode has delegated illegal-instruction exceptions to
S-mode, and S-mode software later executes an illegal instruction, the
trap is taken in S-mode.

normative_rules.name: trap_del_intr_priv_lvl
normative_rules.text:
Delegated interrupts result in the interrupt being masked at the
delegator privilege level. For example, if the supervisor timer
interrupt (STI) is delegated to S-mode by setting csr:mideleg[][5], STIs
will not be taken when executing in M-mode. By contrast, if csr:mideleg[][5]
is clear, STIs can be taken in any mode and regardless of current mode
will transfer control to M-mode.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_enc_txt
normative_rules.text:
csr:medeleg[] has a bit position allocated for every synchronous exception
shown in <<norm:mcause_exccode_enc_img>>, with the index of the
bit position equal to the value returned in the csr:mcause[] register

normative_rules.name: medelegh_sz_acc_enc_xlen32
normative_rules.text:
When XLEN=32, csr:medelegh[] is a 32-bit read/write register
that aliases bits 63:32 of csr:medeleg[].

normative_rules.name: medelegh_omit_xlen64
normative_rules.text: The csr:medelegh[] register does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: mideleg_enc_txt
normative_rules.text:
csr:mideleg[] holds trap delegation bits for individual interrupts, with the
layout of bits matching those in the csr:mip[] register

normative_rules.name: medeleg_when_rd0
normative_rules.text:
For exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes, the
corresponding csr:medeleg[] bits should be read-only zero. In particular,
csr:medeleg[][11] is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: medeleg_16_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: The csr:medeleg[][16] is read-only zero as double trap is not delegatable.

normative_rules.name: mip_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mip[] register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register containing
information on pending interrupts

normative_rules.name: mie_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
csr:mie[] is the corresponding
MXLEN-bit read/write register containing interrupt enable bits.

normative_rules.name: mip_mie_enc_txt
normative_rules.text:
Interrupt cause number i (as reported in CSR csr:mcause[],
<<mcause>>) corresponds with bit i in both csr:mip[] and csr:mie[].
Bits 15:0 are allocated to standard interrupt causes only, while
bits 16 and above are designated for platform use.

normative_rules.name: intr_mip_mie_op
normative_rules.text:
An interrupt i will trap to M-mode (causing the privilege mode to
change to M-mode) if all of the following are true: (a) either the
current privilege mode is M and the csr::[mie] bit in the csr:mstatus[] register is
set, or the current privilege mode has less privilege than M-mode;
(b) bit i is set in both csr:mip[] and csr:mie[]; and (c) if register
csr:mideleg[] exists, bit i is not set in csr:mideleg[].

normative_rules.name: intr_mip_mie_bounded_time
normative_rules.text:
These conditions for an interrupt trap to occur must be evaluated in a
bounded amount of time from when an interrupt becomes, or ceases to be,
pending in csr:mip[],

normative_rules.name: intr_mip_mie_xret_csrwr
normative_rules.text:
be evaluated immediately following the
execution of an xRET instruction or an explicit write to a CSR on
which these interrupt trap conditions expressly depend (including csr:mip[],
csr:mie[], csr:mstatus[], and csr:mideleg[]).

normative_rules.name: intr_m_mode_highest_pri
normative_rules.text: Interrupts to M-mode take priority over any interrupts to lower privilege modes.

normative_rules.name: mip_mandatory
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mip[] register must always be implemented,
but can contain read-only zeros in any position, indicating that interrupt
can never become pending.

normative_rules.name: mip_bits_wr_or_rdonly
normative_rules.text: Each individual bit in register csr:mip[] may be writable or may be read-only.

normative_rules.name: mip_bits_wr_op
normative_rules.text:
When bit i in csr:mip[] is writable, a pending interrupt i
can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit.

normative_rules.name: mip_bits_rdonly_op
normative_rules.text:
If interrupt i can become pending but bit i in csr:mip[] is read-only, the implementation must
provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt.

normative_rules.name: mie_mandatory
normative_rules.text: The csr:mie[] register must always be implemented.

normative_rules.name: mie_bits_wr
normative_rules.text: A bit in csr:mie[] must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending.

normative_rules.name: mie_bits_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: Bits of csr:mie[] that are not writable must be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mip_mie_std_enc_txt
normative_rules.text:
The standard portions (bits 15:0) of the csr:mip[] and csr:mie[] registers are
formatted as shown in <<norm:mip_std_enc_img>> and <<norm:mie_std_enc_img>> respectively.

normative_rules.name: mip_meip_mie_meie_op
normative_rules.text:
Bits csr:mip[meip] and csr:mie[meie] are the interrupt-pending and
interrupt-enable bits for machine-level external interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_meip_rdonly
normative_rules.text:
csr::[meip] is read-only in csr:mip[], and is set and cleared by a platform-specific
interrupt controller.

normative_rules.name: mip_mtip_mie_mtie_op
normative_rules.text:
Bits csr:mip[mtip] and csr:mie[mtie] are the interrupt-pending and
interrupt-enable bits for machine timer interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_mtip_rdonly
normative_rules.text:
csr::[mtip] is read-only in the csr:mip[] register, and is cleared by writing to
the memory-mapped machine-mode timer compare register.

normative_rules.name: mip_msip_mie_msie_op
normative_rules.text:
Bits csr:mip[msip] and csr:mie[msie] are the interrupt-pending and
interrupt-enable bits for machine-level software interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_msip_rdonly
normative_rules.text:
csr::[msip] is read-only in csr:mip[], and is written by accesses to memory-mapped control
registers, which are used to provide machine-level interprocessor interrupts.

normative_rules.name: msip_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: A hart's memory-mapped csr:msip[] register is a 32-bit read/write register

normative_rules.name: msip_enc
normative_rules.text: bits 31&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;1 read as zero and bit 0 contains the csr::[msip] bit.

normative_rules.name: msip_update_max_time
normative_rules.text:
When the memory-mapped csr:msip[] register changes, it is guaranteed to be
reflected in csr:mip[msip] eventually, but not necessarily immediately.

normative_rules.name: mip_msip_mie_msie_maybe_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
If a system has only one hart, or
if a platform standard supports the delivery of machine-level
interprocessor interrupts through external interrupts (MEI) instead,
then csr:mip[msip] and csr:mie[msie] may both be read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: std_mach_intr_impl
normative_rules.text:
Each standard machine interrupt type (MEI, MTI, MSI) might not be implemented,
in which case the corresponding interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable
bits are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: mip_sxip_mie_sxie_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
If supervisor mode is not implemented, bits csr::[seip], csr::[stip], and csr::[ssip] of
csr:mip[] and csr::[seie], csr::[stie], and csr::[ssie] of csr:mie[] are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: mip_seip_mie_seie_op
normative_rules.text:
If supervisor mode is implemented, bits csr:mip[seip] and csr:mie[seie] are
the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level external interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_seip_acc
normative_rules.text: csr::[seip] is writable in csr:mip[]

normative_rules.name: intr_sei_op
normative_rules.text:
Supervisor-level external interrupts are made pending based on the logical-OR of the
software-writable csr::[seip] bit and the signal from the external interrupt controller.

normative_rules.name: mip_seip_rdcsr
normative_rules.text:
When csr:mip[] is read with a CSR instruction, the value of the
csr::[seip] bit returned in the rd destination register is the logical-OR of
the software-writable bit and the interrupt signal from the interrupt
controller

normative_rules.name: mip_seip_wrcsr
normative_rules.text:
the signal from the interrupt controller is not used to
calculate the value written to csr::[seip]. Only the software-writable csr::[seip] bit
participates in the read-modify-write sequence of a insn:csrrs[] or insn:csrrc[] instruction.

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_mie_stie_op
normative_rules.text:
If supervisor mode is implemented, its csr:mip[stip] and csr:mie[stie] are
the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level timer interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_no_stimecmp_acc
normative_rules.text:
If the csr:stimecmp[] register is not implemented, csr::[stip] is writable in
csr:mip[]

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_no_stimecmp_mmode_write
normative_rules.text:
may be written by M-mode software to deliver timer interrupts to
S-mode.

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_stimecmp_acc
normative_rules.text:
If the csr:stimecmp[] (supervisor-mode timer compare) register is
implemented, csr::[stip] is read-only in csr:mip[]

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_reflects_stimecmp
normative_rules.text:
reflects the supervisor-level timer
interrupt signal resulting from csr:stimecmp[].

normative_rules.name: mip_stip_stimecmp_clr
normative_rules.text:
This timer interrupt signal is
cleared by writing csr:stimecmp[] with a value greater than the current time value.

normative_rules.name: mip_ssip_mie_ssie_op
normative_rules.text:
If supervisor mode is implemented, bits csr:mip[ssip] and csr:mie[ssie] are
the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level software interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_ssip_acc
normative_rules.text: csr::[ssip] is writable in csr:mip[]

normative_rules.name: mip_ssip_intr_ctrl
normative_rules.text:
may also be set to 1
by a platform-specific interrupt controller.

normative_rules.name: mip_lcofip_mie_lcofie_op
normative_rules.text:
If the ext:sscofpmf[] extension is implemented, bits csr:mip[lcofip] and
csr:mie[lcofie] are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for local-counter-overflow interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mip_lcofip_acc
normative_rules.text: csr::[lcofip] is read-write in csr:mip[]

normative_rules.name: mip_lcofip_reflects_overflow
normative_rules.text:
reflects the occurrence of a local
counter-overflow overflow interrupt request resulting from any of the mhpmeventn.OF bits being set.

normative_rules.name: mip_lcofip_mie_lcofie_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
If the ext:sscofpmf[] extension is not implemented, csr:mip[lcofip] and csr:mie[lcofie] are
read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: intr_m_mode_pri
normative_rules.text:
Multiple simultaneous interrupts destined for M-mode are handled in the
following decreasing priority order: MEI, MSI, MTI, SEI, SSI, STI, LCOFI.

normative_rules.name: mcycle_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mcycle[] CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor
core on which the hart is running.

normative_rules.name: minstret_op
normative_rules.text: The csr:minstret[] CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired.

normative_rules.name: mcycle_minstret_sz
normative_rules.text: The csr:mcycle[] and csr:minstret[] registers have 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 harts.

normative_rules.name: mcycle_minstret_rst
normative_rules.text:
The counter registers have an arbitrary value after the hart is reset,
and can be written with a given value.

normative_rules.name: mcycle_minstret_wr
normative_rules.text: Any CSR write takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.

normative_rules.name: mcycle_shared
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mcycle[] CSR may be
shared between harts on the same core, in which case writes to
csr:mcycle[] will be visible to those harts.

normative_rules.name: mhpmcounter_num
normative_rules.text:
The hardware performance monitor includes 29 additional 64-bit event
counters, csr:mhpmcounter3[]&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;csr:mhpmcounter31[].

normative_rules.name: mhpmevent_sz_warl_op
normative_rules.text:
The event selector CSRs,
csr:mhpmevent3[]&#8205;&#8211;&#8205;csr:mhpmevent31[], are 64-bit WARL registers that control which
event causes the corresponding counter to increment.

normative_rules.name: mhpmevent_enc
normative_rules.text:
The meaning of these events is defined by the platform,
but event 0 is defined to mean no event.

normative_rules.name: mhpmcounter_mandatory
normative_rules.text: All counters should be implemented

normative_rules.name: mhpmcounter_mhpmevent_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: a legal implementation is to make both the counter and its corresponding event selector be read-only 0.

normative_rules.name: mhpmcounter_warl
normative_rules.text: The mhpmcounters are WARL registers

normative_rules.name: mhpmcounter_sz
normative_rules.text: support up to 64 bits of precision on RV32 and RV64.

normative_rules.name: mcycleh_minstreth_mhpmh_op
normative_rules.text:
reads of the csr:mcycleh[], csr:minstreth[], mhpmcounternh, and mhpmeventnh
CSRs return bits 63-32 of the corresponding register, and writes change only bits 63-32.

normative_rules.name: mhpmeventh_presence
normative_rules.text: The mhpmeventnh CSRs are provided only if the ext:sscofpmf[] extension is implemented.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_sz
normative_rules.text: The counter-enable csr:mcounteren[] register is a 32-bit register

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_op
normative_rules.text:
controls the availability of the hardware performance-monitoring
counters to the next-lower privileged mode.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_inc_inaccessible
normative_rules.text:
The settings in this register only control accessibility. The act of
reading or writing this register does not affect the underlying
counters, which continue to increment even when not accessible.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_clr_ill_inst_exc
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[cy], csr::[tm], csr::[ir], or HPMn bit in the csr:mcounteren[] register is
clear, attempts to read the csr:cycle[], csr:time[], csr:instret[], or
hpmcountern register while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_set_nxt_priv
normative_rules.text:
When one of these bits is set, access to
the corresponding register is permitted in the next implemented
privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_tm_clr
normative_rules.text:
when the csr::[tm] bit in the csr:mcounteren[] register is clear, attempts to
access the csr:stimecmp[] or csr:vstimecmp[] register while executing in a mode less
privileged than M will cause an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_tm_set
normative_rules.text:
When this bit is set, access to the csr:stimecmp[] or csr:vstimecmp[] register is permitted in S-mode
if implemented, and access to the csr:vstimecmp[] register (via csr:stimecmp[]) is
permitted in VS-mode if implemented and not otherwise prevented by the csr::[tm] bit in
csr:hcounteren[].

normative_rules.name: cycle_instret_hpmcounter_op_rdonly
normative_rules.text: The csr:cycle[], csr:instret[], and hpmcountern CSRs are read-only shadows of csr:mcycle[], csr:minstret[], and mhpmcountern, respectively.

normative_rules.name: time_op_rdonly
normative_rules.text: The csr:time[] CSR is a read-only shadow of the memory-mapped csr:mtime[] register.

normative_rules.name: cycleh_instreth_hpmcounternh_op_rdonly
normative_rules.text:
when XLEN=32, the csr:cycleh[], csr:instreth[] and hpmcounternh CSRs
are read-only shadows of csr:mcycleh[], csr:minstreth[] and mhpmcounternh, respectively.

normative_rules.name: timeh_op_rdonly
normative_rules.text:
When XLEN=32, the csr:timeh[] CSR is a read-only shadow of the
upper 32 bits of the memory-mapped csr:mtime[] register

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_flds_mandatory_warl
normative_rules.text:
In harts with U-mode, the csr:mcounteren[] must be
implemented, but all fields are WARL

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_flds_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
may be read-only zero, indicating reads to the
corresponding counter will cause an illegal-instruction exception when
executing in a less-privileged mode.

normative_rules.name: mcounteren_presence
normative_rules.text: In harts without U-mode, the csr:mcounteren[] register should not exist.

normative_rules.name: mcountinhibit_sz_warl
normative_rules.text:
The counter-inhibit register csr:mcountinhibit[] is a 32-bit
WARL register that controls which of the hardware performance-monitoring counters increment.

normative_rules.name: mcountinhibit_only_inc
normative_rules.text:
The settings in this register only control whether the
counters increment; their accessibility is not affected by the setting
of this register.

normative_rules.name: mcountinhibit_clear_op
normative_rules.text:
When the csr::[cy], csr::[ir], or HPMn bit in the csr:mcountinhibit[] register is clear,
the csr:mcycle[], csr:minstret[], or mhpmcountern register increments as usual.
When the csr::[cy], csr::[ir], or HPMn bit is set, the corresponding counter does
not increment.

normative_rules.name: mcountinhibit_cy_shared
normative_rules.text:
The csr:mcycle[] CSR may be shared between harts on the same core,
in which case the csr:mcountinhibit[cy] field is also shared between those harts,
and so writes to csr:mcountinhibit[cy] will be visible to those harts.

normative_rules.name: mcountinhibit_not_impl
normative_rules.text:
If the csr:mcountinhibit[] register is not implemented, the implementation
behaves as though the register were set to zero.

normative_rules.name: mscratch_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The mscratch register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register dedicated
for use by machine mode.  The mscratch register must be implemented.

normative_rules.name: mepc_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: mepc is an MXLEN-bit read/write register

normative_rules.name: mepc_align
normative_rules.text: The low bit of mepc (mepc[0]) is always zero. On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, the two low bits (mepc[1:0]) are always zero.

normative_rules.name: mepc_bit1_dyn_ialign_op
normative_rules.text:
If an implementation allows IALIGN to be either 16 or 32 (by changing
CSR misa, for example), then, whenever IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] is
masked on reads so that it appears to be 0. This masking occurs also for
the implicit read by the MRET instruction. Though masked, mepc[1]
remains writable when IALIGN=32.

normative_rules.name: mepc_warl
normative_rules.text:
mepc is a WARL register that must be implemented and
must be able to hold all valid virtual
addresses. It need not be capable of holding all possible invalid addresses.

normative_rules.name: mepc_inv_addr_conv
normative_rules.text:
Prior to writing mepc, implementations may convert an
invalid address into some other invalid address that mepc is capable of holding.

normative_rules.name: mepc_op
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is taken into M-mode, mepc is written with the virtual
address of the instruction that was interrupted or that encountered the
exception. Otherwise, mepc is never written by the implementation,
though it may be explicitly written by software.

normative_rules.name: mcause_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: The mcause register is an MXLEN-bit read-write register

normative_rules.name: mcause_mandatory
normative_rules.text: The mcause register must be implemented.

normative_rules.name: mcause_op
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is taken into
M-mode, mcause is written with a code indicating the event that
caused the trap. Otherwise, mcause is never written by the
implementation, though it may be explicitly written by software.

normative_rules.name: mcause_intr_op
normative_rules.text:
The Interrupt bit in the mcause register is set if the trap was
caused by an interrupt.

normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_op
normative_rules.text:
The Exception Code field contains a code identifying
the last exception or interrupt.

normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_wlrl
normative_rules.text: The Exception Code is a WLRL field, so is only guaranteed to hold supported exception codes.

normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_ld_ldrsv
normative_rules.text: Note that load and load-reserved instructions generate load exceptions

normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_st_sc_amo
normative_rules.text:
store, store-conditional, and AMO instructions generate
store/AMO exceptions.

normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_priority_order
normative_rules.text:
If an instruction may raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the
decreasing priority order of <<norm:exc_priority>> indicates which
exception is taken and reported in mcause.

normative_rules.name: custom_exc_priority
normative_rules.text: The priority of any custom synchronous exceptions is implementation-defined.
