normative_rules.name: mcause_exccode_priority_misaligned
normative_rules.text:
Load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions may have either higher or
lower priority than load/store/AMO page-fault and access-fault exceptions.

normative_rules.name: mtval_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The mtval register is an MXLEN-bit read-write register formatted as
shown in <<norm:mtval_enc_img>>

normative_rules.name: mtval_op
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is taken into M-mode,
mtval is either set to zero or written with exception-specific
information to assist software in handling the trap. Otherwise, mtval
is never written by the implementation, though it may be explicitly
written by software.

normative_rules.name: mtval_per_exc_behavior
normative_rules.text:
The hardware platform will specify which exceptions
must set mtval informatively, which may unconditionally set it to
zero, and which may exhibit either behavior, depending on the underlying event
that caused the exception.

normative_rules.name: mtval_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
The mtval register must always be implemented. If the
hardware platform specifies that no exceptions set mtval
to a nonzero value, then mtval is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mtval_vaddr_wr_faulting_addr
normative_rules.text:
If mtval is written with a nonzero value when a breakpoint,
address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception
occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then mtval will contain the
faulting virtual address.

normative_rules.name: mtval_ebreak_op
normative_rules.text:
On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, mtval
is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.

normative_rules.name: mtval_vaddr_not_paddr
normative_rules.text:
When page-based virtual memory is enabled, mtval is written with the
faulting virtual address, even for physical-memory access-fault exceptions.

normative_rules.name: mtval_vaddr_wr_misaligned_addr
normative_rules.text:
If mtval is written with a nonzero value when a misaligned load or
store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then mtval will
contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.

normative_rules.name: mtval_varlen_wr
normative_rules.text:
If mtval is written with a nonzero value when an instruction
access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with
variable-length instructions, then mtval will contain the virtual
address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault

normative_rules.name: mepc_varlen_wr
normative_rules.text: mepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.

normative_rules.name: mtval_instr_bits_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
The mtval register can optionally also be used to return the faulting
instruction bits on an illegal-instruction exception

normative_rules.name: mtval_instr_bits_list
normative_rules.text:
the actual faulting instruction
the first ILEN bits of the faulting instruction
the first MXLEN bits of the faulting instruction

normative_rules.name: mtval_ill_instr_exc_in_low_bits
normative_rules.text:
On an illegal-instruction exception, the instruction
bits are zero-extended and loaded into csr:mtval[].

normative_rules.name: mtval_swchk_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
On a trap caused by a software-check exception, the mtval register holds
the cause for the exception. The following encodings are defined:

normative_rules.name: mtval_swchk_list
normative_rules.text:
0 - No information provided.
2 - Landing Pad Fault. Defined by the Zicfilp extension ().
3 - Shadow Stack Fault. Defined by the Zicfiss extension ().

normative_rules.name: mtval_other_traps_zero
normative_rules.text: For other traps, mtval is set to zero

normative_rules.name: mtval_warl
normative_rules.text: If mtval is not read-only zero, it is a WARL register

normative_rules.name: mtval_vaddr_and_0_sz
normative_rules.text: must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value zero.

normative_rules.name: mtval_inv_addr_conv
normative_rules.text:
Prior to writing mtval, implementations may convert an invalid address
into some other invalid address that mtval is capable of holding.

normative_rules.name: mtval_instr_bits_sz
normative_rules.text:
If the feature to return the faulting instruction bits is implemented,
mtval must also be able to hold all values less than 2^N^, where
N is the smaller of MXLEN and ILEN.

normative_rules.name: mconfigptr_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: The mconfigptr register is an MXLEN-bit read-only CSR formatted as shown in <<norm:mconfigptr_enc_img>>

normative_rules.name: mconfigptr_op
normative_rules.text: holds the physical address of a configuration data structure.

normative_rules.name: mconfigptr_align
normative_rules.text:
The pointer alignment in bits must be no smaller than MXLEN: i.e., if MXLEN is
8×n, then mconfigptr[log~2~n-1:0] must be zero.

normative_rules.name: mconfigptr_mandatory
normative_rules.text: The mconfigptr register must be implemented

normative_rules.name: mconfigptr_val
normative_rules.text:
it may be zero to indicate the
configuration data structure does not exist or that an alternative
mechanism must be used to locate it.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The menvcfg CSR is a 64-bit read/write register, formatted
as shown in <<norm:menvcfg_enc_img>>

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_op
normative_rules.text:
controls certain characteristics of the execution environment
for modes less privileged than M.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_fiom_fence_op
normative_rules.text:
If bit FIOM (Fence of I/O implies Memory) is set to one in menvcfg,
FENCE instructions executed in modes less privileged than M are modified
so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O implies also the
requirement to order main memory accesses. <<norm:menvcfg_fiom_fence_presuc_op>>
details the modified interpretation of FENCE instruction bits PI, PO,
SI, and SO for modes less privileged than M when FIOM=1.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_fiom_atomic_op
normative_rules.text:
for modes less privileged than M when FIOM=1, if an atomic
instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O has its aq
and/or rl bit set, then that instruction is ordered as though it
accesses both device I/O and memory.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_fiom_rdonly0_ok
normative_rules.text:
If S-mode is not supported, or if satp.MODE is read-only zero (always
Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_fiom_fence_presuc_op
normative_rules.text:
Instruction bit|Meaning when set
===
PI
PO|Predecessor device input and memory reads (PR implied)
Predecessor device output and memory writes (PW implied)¶SI
SO|Successor device input and memory reads (SR implied)
Successor device output and memory writes (SW implied)
===

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pbmte_op
normative_rules.text:
The PBMTE bit controls whether the Svpbmt extension is available for use
in S-mode and G-stage address translation (i.e., for page tables pointed
to by satp or hgatp). When PBMTE=1, Svpbmt is available for S-mode
and G-stage address translation. When PBMTE=0, the implementation
behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pbmte_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If Svpbmt is not implemented, PBMTE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pbmte_henvcfg_pbmte_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
for implementations with the hypervisor extension,
henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pbmte_fence
normative_rules.text:
After changing menvcfg.PBMTE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with
rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches
with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' PBMT fields.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_adue_op
normative_rules.text:
If the Svadu extension is implemented, the ADUE bit controls whether hardware
updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled for S-mode and G-stage address translations.
When ADUE=1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode
address translation, and the implementation behaves as though the Svade
extension were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
When the hypervisor extension is implemented, if ADUE=1, hardware updating of
PTE A/D bits is enabled during G-stage address translation, and the
implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were not implemented for
G-stage address translation.
When ADUE=0, the implementation behaves as though Svade were implemented for
S-mode and G-stage address translation.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_adue_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If Svadu is not implemented, ADUE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_adue_henvcfg_adue_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
for implementations with the hypervisor extension,
henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_adue_fence
normative_rules.text:
After changing menvcfg.ADUE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with
rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches
with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' A/D bits.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cde_op
normative_rules.text:
If the Smcdeleg extension is implemented, the CDE (Counter Delegation Enable) bit
controls whether Zicntr and Zihpm counters can be delegated to S-mode. When CDE=1, the Smcdeleg extension is
enabled, see <<smcdeleg>>. When CDE=0, the Smcdeleg and Ssccfg extensions appear to be not implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cde_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If Smcdeleg is not implemented, CDE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_stce_exists
normative_rules.text: The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to menvcfg CSR.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_stce_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: When the Sstc extension is not implemented, STCE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_stce_enable_op
normative_rules.text: The STCE bit enables stimecmp for S-mode when set to one.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_stce_zero_op
normative_rules.text:
When this extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, an attempt
to access stimecmp or vstimecmp in a mode other than M-mode raises an
illegal-instruction exception, STCE in henvcfg is read-only zero, and STIP
in mip and sip reverts to its defined behavior as if this extension is not
implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_stce_zero_vstip
normative_rules.text:
Further, if the H extension is implemented, then hip.VSTIP also
reverts its defined behavior as if this extension is not implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbze_op
normative_rules.text:
The Zicboz extension adds the CBZE (Cache Block Zero instruction enable) field
to menvcfg. When the CBZE field is set to 1, it enables execution of the
cache block zero instruction, CBO.ZERO, in modes less privileged than M.
Otherwise, the instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less
privileged than M.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbze_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: When the Zicboz extension is not implemented, CBZE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbcfe_op
normative_rules.text:
The Zicbom extension adds the CBCFE (Cache Block Clean and Flush instruction
Enable) field to menvcfg. When the CBCFE field is set to 1, it enables
execution of the cache block clean instruction (CBO.CLEAN) and the cache block
flush instruction (CBO.FLUSH) in modes less privileged than M. Otherwise, these
instructions raise an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbcfe_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBCFE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbie_warl_op
normative_rules.text:
The Zicbom extension adds the CBIE (Cache Block Invalidate instruction Enable)
WARL field to menvcfg to control execution of the cache block invalidate
instruction (CBO.INVAL) in modes less privileged than M. When CBIE is set to
0b00, the instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less
privileged than M.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbie_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBIE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbie_cbo-inval_op_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
When CBIE is set to 0b01
or 0b11, and when enabled for execution in modes less privileged than M, it
behaves as follows:

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_cbie_cbo-inval_op_list
normative_rules.text:
0b01 — The instruction is executed and performs a flush operation, even if configured by a mode less privileged than M to perform an invalidate operation.
0b11 — The instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation, unless configured by a mode less privileged than M to perform a flush operation.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pmm_op
normative_rules.text:
If the Smnpm extension is implemented, the PMM field enables or disables
pointer masking (see <<Zpm>>) for the next-lower privilege mode (S-/HS-mode if
S-mode is implemented, or U-mode otherwise), according to the values in
<<norm:menvcfg_pmm_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pmm_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
If Smnpm is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero.
The PMM field is read-only zero for RV32.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_pmm_enc
normative_rules.text:
Value|Description
===
00|Pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN = 0)¶01|Reserved¶10|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 57 (PMLEN = 7 on RV64)¶11|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 48 (PMLEN = 16 on RV64)
===

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_lpe_op_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
The Zicfilp extension adds the LPE field in menvcfg. When the LPE field is
set to 1 and S-mode is implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in S-mode.
If LPE field is set to 1 and S-mode is not implemented, the Zicfilp extension
is enabled in U-mode. When the LPE field is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not
enabled in S-mode, and the following rules apply to S-mode. If the LPE field
is 0 and S-mode is not implemented, then the same rules apply to U-mode.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_lpe_op_list
normative_rules.text:
The hart does not update the ELP state; it remains as NO_LP_EXPECTED.
The LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_sse_op_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
The Zicfiss extension adds the SSE field to menvcfg.
When the SSE field is set to 1 the Zicfiss extension is activated in S-mode. When SSE field is 0,
the following rules apply to privilege modes that are less than M:

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_sse_op_list
normative_rules.text:
32-bit Zicfiss instructions will revert to their behavior as defined by Zimop.
16-bit Zicfiss instructions will revert to their behavior as defined by Zcmop.
The pte.xwr=0b010 encoding in VS/S-stage page tables becomes reserved.
SSAMOSWAP.W/D raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_sse_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When menvcfg.SSE is 0, the henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE fields are
read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_dte_op
normative_rules.text:
The Ssdbltrp extension adds the double-trap-enable (DTE) field in menvcfg.
When menvcfg.DTE is zero, the implementation behaves as though Ssdbltrp is not
implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_dte_sdt_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When Ssdbltrp is not implemented sstatus.SDT, vsstatus.SDT, and
henvcfg.DTE bits are read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfgh_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
When XLEN=32, menvcfgh is a 32-bit read/write register
that aliases bits 63:32 of menvcfg.
The menvcfgh register does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_mandatory_u_mode
normative_rules.text:
In harts with U-mode, menvcfg must be
implemented, but all WARL fields may be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfgh_mandatory_s_mode_rv32
normative_rules.text: For harts with S-mode and XLEN=32, menvcfgh must be similarly implemented.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_menvcfgh_no_u_mode
normative_rules.text:
If U-mode is not supported, then registers menvcfg and menvcfgh do
not exist.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
mseccfg is a 64-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in <<norm:mseccfg_enc_img>>,
that controls security features.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_presence
normative_rules.text: It exists if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented. Otherwise, it is reserved.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sseed_useed_presence
normative_rules.text: The Zkr extension adds the SSEED and USEED fields to the mseccfg CSR to control access to the seed CSR from modes less privileged than M.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_useed_u_mode_op
normative_rules.text:
When USEED is 0, access to the seed CSR in U-mode raises an
illegal-instruction exception. When USEED is 1, read-write access to the
seed CSR from U-mode is allowed; all other types of accesses raise an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_useed_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If Zkr or U-mode is not implemented, USEED is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sseed_sorhs_mode_op
normative_rules.text:
When SSEED is 0, access to the seed CSR from S-/HS-mode raises an
illegal-instruction exception. When SSEED is 1, read-write access to the
seed CSR from S-/HS-mode is allowed; all other types of accesses raise an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sseed_rdonly0
normative_rules.text: If Zkr or S-mode is not implemented, SSEED is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sseed_vsorvu_mode_op
normative_rules.text:
When the H extension is also implemented,
access to the seed CSR from an
HS-qualified instruction leads to a virtual-instruction exception in VS and
VU modes; all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_sseed_useed_op_tbl
normative_rules.text:
Mode|SSEED|USEED|Description
===
M|-|-|The seed CSR is always available in machine
                              mode as normal (with a CSR read-write
                              instruction.) Attempted read without a write
                              raises an illegal-instruction exception
                              regardless of mode and access control bits.¶U|-|0|Any seed CSR access raises an
                              illegal-instruction exception.¶U|-|1|The seed CSR is accessible as normal. No
                              exception is raised for read-write.¶S/HS|0|-|Any seed CSR access raises an
                              illegal-instruction exception.¶S/HS|1|-|The seed CSR is accessible as normal. No
                              exception is raised for read-write.¶VS/VU|0|-|Any seed CSR access raises an
                              illegal-instruction exception.¶VS/VU|1|-|A read-write seed access raises a
                              virtual-instruction exception, while other access
                              conditions raise an illegal-instruction exception.
===

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_rlb_mmwp_mml_presence
normative_rules.text: The Smepmp extension adds the RLB, MMWP, and the MML fields in mseccfg.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_rlb_op_warl
normative_rules.text: mseccfg.RLB (Rule Locking Bypass) is a WARL field that provides a mechanism to temporarily modify Locked PMP rules. When mseccfg.RLB is 1, locked PMP rules may be removed or modified. When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg.L is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mmwp_op_warl
normative_rules.text: The mseccfg.MMWP (Machine-Mode Allowlist Policy) is a WARL field. This field changes the default PMP policy for Machine mode when accessing memory regions that don’t have a matching PMP rule. This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset. When set it changes the default PMP policy for M-mode when accessing memory regions that don’t have a matching PMP rule, to denied instead of ignored.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_warl
normative_rules.text: The mseccfg.MML (Machine Mode Lockdown) is a WARL field.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_sticky
normative_rules.text:
This is a sticky bit, meaning that once set it cannot be unset
until a PMP reset.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_set
normative_rules.text: When mseccfg.MML is set the system's behavior changes in the following way:

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_pmpcfg_l_op
normative_rules.text:
The meaning of pmpcfg.L changes:
Instead of marking a rule as locked and
enforced in all modes, it now marks a rule as M-mode-only when set and
S/U-mode-only when unset. The formerly reserved encoding of pmpcfg.RW=01,
and the encoding pmpcfg.LRWX=1111, now encode a Shared-Region.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_m_rule_op
normative_rules.text:
An M-mode-only rule is enforced on accesses whose effective privilege
mode is Machine and denied to accesses whose effective privilege mode is Supervisor
or User. It also remains locked so that any further modifications to its
associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset,
unless mseccfg.RLB is set.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_soru_rule_op
normative_rules.text:
An S/U-mode-only rule is enforced on accesses whose effective privilege
mode is Supervisor or User and denied to accesses whose effective privilege
mode is Machine.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_shared_rule_op
normative_rules.text:
A Shared-Region rule is enforced on all modes, with restrictions depending
on the pmpcfg.L and pmpcfg.X bits:

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_shared_l0_op
normative_rules.text:
A Shared-Region rule where pmpcfg.L is not set can be used for sharing
data between M-mode and S/U-mode, so is not executable. M-mode has
read/write access to that region, and S/U-mode has read access if pmpcfg.X
is not set, or read/write access if pmpcfg.X is set.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_shared_l1_op
normative_rules.text:
A Shared-Region rule where pmpcfg.L is set can be used for sharing code
between M-mode and S/U-mode, so is not writable. Both M-mode and S/U-mode
have execute access on the region, and M-mode also has read access if
pmpcfg.X is set. The rule remains locked so that any further
modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are
ignored until a PMP reset, unless mseccfg.RLB is set.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_shared_lrwx_1111_op
normative_rules.text:
The encoding pmpcfg.LRWX=1111 can be used for sharing data between M-mode
and S/U mode, where both modes only have read-only access to the region. The
rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated
configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset, unless
mseccfg.RLB is set.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_x_restrict
normative_rules.text:
Adding a rule with executable privileges that either is M-mode-only or a
locked Shared-Region is not possible and such pmpcfg writes are
ignored, leaving pmpcfg unchanged. This restriction can be temporarily
lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_exec_code
normative_rules.text:
Executing code with Machine mode privileges is only possible from memory
regions with a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule
with executable privileges. Executing code from a region without a matching
rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.

normative_rules.name: pmp_rw01_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If mseccfg.MML is not set, the combination of pmpcfg.RW=01 remains
reserved for future standard use.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_pmm_presence_op
normative_rules.text:
If the Smmpm extension is implemented,
the PMM field enables or disables pointer masking (see <<Zpm>>) for M-mode
according to the values in <<norm:mseccfg_pmm_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_pmm_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
If Smmpm is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero.
The PMM field is read-only zero for RV32.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_pmm_enc
normative_rules.text:
Value|Description
===
00|Pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN = 0)¶01|Reserved¶10|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 57 (PMLEN = 7 on RV64)¶11|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 48 (PMLEN = 16 on RV64)
===

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mlpe_presence
normative_rules.text: The Zicfilp extension adds the MLPE field in mseccfg.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mlpe_set_op
normative_rules.text: When MLPE field is 1, Zicfilp extension is enabled in M-mode.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mlpe_clr_op_lead_in
normative_rules.text:
When the MLPE field is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled
in M-mode and the following rules apply to M-mode.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mlpe_clr_op_list
normative_rules.text:
The hart does not update the ELP state; it remains as NO_LP_EXPECTED.
The LPAD instruction operates as a no-op.

normative_rules.name: mseccfgh_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
When XLEN=32 only, mseccfgh is a 32-bit read/write register that
aliases bits 63:32 of mseccfg.

normative_rules.name: mseccfgh_presence
normative_rules.text:
Register mseccfgh exists when XLEN=32 and mseccfg is implemented;
it does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: mtime_acc
normative_rules.text:
Platforms provide a real-time counter, exposed as a memory-mapped
machine-mode read-write register, mtime.

normative_rules.name: mtime_op
normative_rules.text: mtime must increment at constant frequency

normative_rules.name: mtime_tick_period
normative_rules.text:
the platform must provide a mechanism for
determining the period of an mtime tick.

normative_rules.name: mtime_wrap
normative_rules.text: The mtime register will wrap around if the count overflows.

normative_rules.name: mtime_sz
normative_rules.text: The mtime register has a 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems.

normative_rules.name: mtimecmp_sz
normative_rules.text:
Platforms provide a 64-bit memory-mapped machine-mode timer
compare register (mtimecmp).

normative_rules.name: mtime_intr_pending
normative_rules.text:
A machine timer interrupt becomes pending
whenever mtime contains a value greater than or equal to mtimecmp,
treating the values as unsigned integers.
The interrupt remains posted until mtimecmp becomes greater than mtime

normative_rules.name: mtime_intr_taken
normative_rules.text:
The interrupt will only be taken if interrupts are
enabled and the MTIE bit is set in the mie register.

normative_rules.name: mtime_intr_mtip_visibility
normative_rules.text:
If the result of the comparison between mtime and mtimecmp
changes, it is guaranteed to be reflected in MTIP eventually, but not necessarily immediately.

normative_rules.name: mtimecmp_rv32_wr
normative_rules.text:
In RV32, memory-mapped writes to mtimecmp modify only one 32-bit part
of the register.

normative_rules.name: mtime_mtimecmp_rv64_wr
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, naturally aligned 64-bit memory accesses to the mtime and
mtimecmp registers are additionally supported and are atomic.

normative_rules.name: time_timeh_visibility_mtime
normative_rules.text:
When mtime changes, it is guaranteed to be reflected in time
and timeh eventually, but not necessarily immediately.

normative_rules.name: ecall_priv_mode_op
normative_rules.text: The ECALL instruction is used to make a request to the supporting execution environment. When executed in U-mode, S-mode, or M-mode, it generates an environment-call-from-U-mode exception, environment-call-from-S-mode exception, or environment-call-from-M-mode exception, respectively, and performs no other operation.

normative_rules.name: ebreak_debugger_transfer_op
normative_rules.text: The EBREAK instruction is used by debuggers to cause control to be transferred back to a debugging environment. Unless overridden by an external debug environment, EBREAK raises a breakpoint exception and performs no other operation.

normative_rules.name: ecall_ebreak_epc_value
normative_rules.text:
ECALL and EBREAK cause the receiving privilege mode’s epc register to
be set to the address of the ECALL or EBREAK instruction itself, not
the address of the following instruction.

normative_rules.name: ecall_ebreak_no_minstret_inc
normative_rules.text:
As ECALL and EBREAK cause
synchronous exceptions, they are not considered to retire, and should
not increment the minstret CSR.

normative_rules.name: mret_presence
normative_rules.text: MRET is always provided.

normative_rules.name: sret_presence
normative_rules.text:
SRET must be provided if supervisor mode is supported, and
should raise an illegal-instruction exception otherwise.

normative_rules.name: sret_ill_inst_exc_rst
normative_rules.text:
SRET should also raise an illegal-instruction exception when TSR=1
in mstatus, as described in <<virt-control>>.

normative_rules.name: xret_in_higher_mode
normative_rules.text:
An xRET instruction can be executed in privilege mode x or higher,
where executing a lower-privilege xRET instruction will pop the relevant lower-privilege
interrupt enable and privilege mode stack.

normative_rules.name: xret_in_lower_mode
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to execute an xRET
instruction in a mode less privileged than x will raise an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: xret_op
normative_rules.text:
In addition to manipulating the privilege stack as described in <<privstack>>,
xRET sets the pc to the value stored in the xepc register.

normative_rules.name: xret_clr_lr_resv
normative_rules.text:
If the Zalrsc extension is supported, the xRET instruction is allowed to
clear any outstanding LR address reservation but is not required to.

normative_rules.name: wfi_op
normative_rules.text:
The Wait for Interrupt instruction (WFI) informs the
implementation that the current hart can be stalled until an interrupt
might need servicing.

normative_rules.name: wfi_all_privileged_modes
normative_rules.text: WFI is available in all privileged modes

normative_rules.name: wfi_opt_u_mode
normative_rules.text: optionally available to U-mode.

normative_rules.name: wfi_ill_exc
normative_rules.text:
This instruction may raise an illegal-instruction exception when TW=1 in mstatus, as
described in <<virt-control>>.

normative_rules.name: wfi_mepc_val
normative_rules.text:
If an enabled interrupt is present or later becomes present while the
hart is stalled, the interrupt trap will be taken on the following
instruction, i.e., execution resumes in the trap handler and mepc = pc + 4.

normative_rules.name: wfi_resume_reason
normative_rules.text:
Implementations are permitted to resume execution for any reason, even if an
enabled interrupt has not become pending.
Hence, a legal implementation is to simply implement the WFI instruction as a NOP.

normative_rules.name: wfi_intr_dis
normative_rules.text: The WFI instruction can also be executed when interrupts are disabled.

normative_rules.name: wfi_unaffected_conditions
normative_rules.text:
The operation of WFI must be unaffected by the global interrupt bits in
mstatus (MIE and SIE) and the delegation register mideleg (i.e.,
the hart must resume if a locally enabled interrupt becomes pending,
even if it has been delegated to a less-privileged mode), but should
honor the individual interrupt enables (e.g, MTIE) (i.e.,
implementations should avoid resuming the hart if the interrupt is
pending but not locally enabled).

normative_rules.name: wfi_resume_any_priv
normative_rules.text:
WFI is also required to resume
execution for locally enabled interrupts pending at any privilege level,
regardless of the global interrupt enable at each privilege level.

normative_rules.name: wfi_no_intr_pc
normative_rules.text:
If the event that causes the hart to resume execution
does not cause an interrupt to be taken, execution will resume at pc + 4

normative_rules.name: m_mode_priv_at_reset
normative_rules.text: Upon reset, a hart’s privilege mode is set to M.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mie_mprv_rst
normative_rules.text: The mstatus fields MIE and MPRV are reset to 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mstatush_mbe_rst
normative_rules.text: If little-endian memory accesses are supported, the mstatus/mstatush field MBE is reset to 0.

normative_rules.name: misa_extensions_reset_ref
normative_rules.text:
The misa register is reset to enable the maximal set of supported
extensions, as described in <<misa>>.

normative_rules.name: ld_rsv_rst
normative_rules.text:
For implementations with the Zalrsc standard extension, there is no valid
load reservation.

normative_rules.name: pc_rst
normative_rules.text: The pc is set to an implementation-defined reset vector.

normative_rules.name: mcause_rst1_val
normative_rules.text: The mcause register is set to a value indicating the cause of the reset.

normative_rules.name: pmp_a_l_rst
normative_rules.text:
Writable PMP registers’ A and L fields are set to 0, unless
the platform mandates a different reset value for some PMP registers’ A
and L fields.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_vsatp_mode_rst
normative_rules.text:
If the hypervisor extension is implemented, the
hgatp.MODE and vsatp.MODE fields are reset to 0.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_nmie_rst
normative_rules.text: If the Smrnmi extension is implemented, the mnstatus.NMIE field is reset to 0.

normative_rules.name: warl_rst
normative_rules.text: No WARL field contains an illegal value.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mlpe_rst
normative_rules.text: If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, the mseccfg.MLPE field is reset to 0.

normative_rules.name: rst_other_state_unspec
normative_rules.text: All other hart state is UNSPECIFIED.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_mml_mmwp_rlb_rst
normative_rules.text:
The MML, MMWP, and RLB fields of the mseccfg register
are set to 0, unless the platform mandates a different reset value.

normative_rules.name: mcause_rst2_val
normative_rules.text:
The mcause values after reset have implementation-specific
interpretation

normative_rules.name: mcause_rst_zero
normative_rules.text:
the value 0 should be returned on implementations
that do not distinguish different reset conditions. Implementations that
distinguish different reset conditions should only use 0 to indicate the
most complete reset.

normative_rules.name: mseccfg_useed_sseed_rst
normative_rules.text:
The USEED and SSEED fields of the mseccfg CSR
must have defined reset values. The system must not allow them to be in an undefined state
after reset.

normative_rules.name: nmi_op
normative_rules.text:
cause an immediate jump to an implementation-defined NMI
vector running in M-mode regardless of the state of a hart’s interrupt
enable bits. The mepc register is written with the virtual address of
the instruction that was interrupted,

normative_rules.name: nmi_mcause_source
normative_rules.text:
mcause is set to a value
indicating the source of the NMI.

normative_rules.name: nmi_mcause_impl_def
normative_rules.text: The values written to mcause on an NMI are implementation-defined.

normative_rules.name: nmi_mcause_restrictions
normative_rules.text:
The high Interrupt bit of mcause should be set to indicate
that this was an interrupt. An Exception Code of 0 is reserved to mean unknown
cause and implementations that do not distinguish sources of NMIs via
the mcause register should return 0 in the Exception Code.

normative_rules.name: nmi_no_rst
normative_rules.text: NMIs do not reset processor state

normative_rules.name: pma_indep_exec_context
normative_rules.text:
PMAs do not vary by execution
context.

normative_rules.name: pma_chk_paddr
normative_rules.text:
PMAs are checked for any access to physical memory, including accesses
that have undergone virtual to physical memory translation.

normative_rules.name: pma_precise_recom
normative_rules.text:
Precisely trapped PMA violations manifest as instruction, load, or store
access-fault exceptions, distinct from virtual-memory page-fault exceptions.

normative_rules.name: pma_imprecise_ok
normative_rules.text:
Precise PMA traps might not always be possible, for example,
when probing a legacy bus architecture that uses access failures as part
of the discovery mechanism. In this case, error responses from
peripheral devices will be reported as imprecise bus-error interrupts.

normative_rules.name: pma_mm_vs_io_def
normative_rules.text: The most important characterization of a given memory address range is whether it holds regular main memory or I/O devices. Regular main memory is required to have a number of properties, specified below, whereas I/O devices can have a much broader range of attributes. Memory regions that do not fit into regular main memory, for example, device scratchpad RAMs, are categorized as I/O regions.

normative_rules.name: pma_mm_rw
normative_rules.text:
Main memory regions always support read and write of all access widths
required by the attached devices

normative_rules.name: pma_mm_ifetch
normative_rules.text: can specify whether instruction fetch is supported.

normative_rules.name: pma_io_rwx_per_sz
normative_rules.text:
I/O regions can specify which combinations of read, write, or execute
accesses to which data widths are supported.

normative_rules.name: pma_vm_hw_tbl_acc
normative_rules.text:
For systems with page-based virtual memory, I/O and memory regions can
specify which combinations of hardware page-table reads and hardware
page-table writes are supported.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_levels
normative_rules.text:
Within AMOs, there are four levels of support: AMONone, AMOSwap,
AMOLogical, and AMOArithmetic. AMONone indicates that no AMO
operations are supported. AMOSwap indicates that only amoswap
instructions are supported in this address range. AMOLogical indicates
that swap instructions plus all the logical AMOs (amoand, amoor,
amoxor) are supported. AMOArithmetic indicates that all RISC-V AMOs defined by
the A extension are supported.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_sz_support
normative_rules.text:
For each level of support, naturally aligned AMOs of a given width
are supported if the underlying memory region supports reads and writes of that width.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_far_subset_proc
normative_rules.text: Main memory and I/O regions may only support a subset or none of the processor-supported atomic operations.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_Zacas_levels1
normative_rules.text:
The Zacas extension defines three additional levels of support: AMOCASW,
AMOCASD, and AMOCASQ.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_Zacas_levels2
normative_rules.text:
AMOCASW indicates that in addition to instructions indicated by AMOArithmetic-level support, the AMOCAS.W instruction is supported. AMOCASD indicates that
in addition to instructions indicated by AMOCASW-level support, the AMOCAS.D
instruction is supported. AMOCASQ indicates that in addition to instructions
indicated by AMOCASD-level support, the AMOCAS.Q instruction is supported.

normative_rules.name: pma_amo_Zabha_req
normative_rules.text:
The AMOs specified by the Zabha extension require the same level of support as
the corresponding instructions in the Zaamo standard extension or the Zacas extension.

normative_rules.name: Ziccamoa_pma_amo_req
normative_rules.text:
The ext:ziccamoa[] extension requires
AMOArithmetic-level support to main memory regions with both the coherence and
cacheability PMAs.

normative_rules.name: Ziccamoc_pma_amo_req
normative_rules.text:
The ext:ziccamoc[] extension requires AMOCASQ-level
support to main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs.

normative_rules.name: pma_rsrv_levels
normative_rules.text:
For LR/SC, there are three levels of support indicating combinations
of the reservability and eventuality properties: RsrvNone,
RsrvNonEventual, and RsrvEventual. RsrvNone indicates that no LR/SC
operations are supported (the location is non-reservable).
RsrvNonEventual indicates that the operations are supported (the
location is reservable), but without the eventual success guarantee
described in the unprivileged ISA specification. RsrvEventual indicates
that the operations are supported and provide the eventual success guarantee.

normative_rules.name: Ziccrse_pma_rsrv_req
normative_rules.text:
The ext:ziccrse[] extension requires RsrvEventual
support to main memory regions with both the coherence and cacheability PMAs.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_def
normative_rules.text: The misaligned atomicity granule PMA provides constrained support for misaligned AMOs. This PMA, if present, specifies the size of a misaligned atomicity granule, a naturally aligned power-of-two number of bytes. Specific supported values for this PMA are represented by MAGNN, e.g., MAG16 indicates the misaligned atomicity granule is at least 16 bytes.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_insts
normative_rules.text:
The misaligned atomicity granule PMA applies only to
AMOs defined in the ext:zaamo[], ext:zabha[], and ext:zacas[] extensions;
loads and stores
defined in the base ISAs; loads and stores of no more than XLEN bits
defined in the ext:f[], ext:d[], and ext:q[] extensions; the load-acquire and
store-release instructions defined in the ext:zalasr[] extension; and compressed
encodings of the foregoing loads and stores.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_op_within
normative_rules.text:
if all accessed bytes lie within the same
misaligned atomicity granule, the instruction will not raise an exception for
reasons of address alignment, and the instruction will give rise to only one
memory operation for the purposes of RVWMO--i.e., it will execute atomically.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_op_amo
normative_rules.text:
If a misaligned AMO accesses a region that does not specify a misaligned
atomicity granule PMA, or if not all accessed bytes lie within the same
misaligned atomicity granule, then an exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_op_ldst
normative_rules.text:
For regular loads and stores that access such a region or for which not all
accessed bytes lie within the same atomicity granule, then either an exception
is raised, or the access proceeds but is not guaranteed to be atomic.

normative_rules.name: pma_mag_exc
normative_rules.text:
Implementations may raise access-fault exceptions instead of
address-misaligned exceptions for some misaligned accesses, indicating the
instruction should not be emulated by a trap handler.

normative_rules.name: Zama16b_pma_mag_req
normative_rules.text:
The Zama16b extension requires MAG16 support to main
memory regions.

normative_rules.name: pma_mo_io_chan_def
normative_rules.text:
Each strongly ordered I/O region specifies a numbered ordering channel,
which is a mechanism by which ordering guarantees can be provided
between different I/O regions.

normative_rules.name: pma_mo_io_chan_0
normative_rules.text:
Channel 0 is used to indicate
point-to-point strong ordering only, where only accesses by the hart to
the single associated I/O region are strongly ordered.

normative_rules.name: pma_mo_io_chan_1
normative_rules.text: Channel 1 is used to provide global strong ordering across all I/O regions. Any accesses by a hart to any I/O region associated with channel 1 can only be observed to have occurred in program order by all other harts and I/O devices, including relative to accesses made by that hart to relaxed I/O regions or strongly ordered I/O regions with different channel numbers. In other words, any access to a region in channel 1 is equivalent to executing a fence io,io instruction before and after the instruction.

normative_rules.name: pma_mo_io_chan_other
normative_rules.text: Other larger channel numbers provide program ordering to accesses by that hart across any regions with the same channel number

normative_rules.name: pma_mo_dyn
normative_rules.text: Systems might support dynamic configuration of ordering properties on each memory region.

normative_rules.name: pma_non_cacheable
normative_rules.text:
If a PMA indicates non-cacheability, then accesses to that region must
be satisfied by the memory itself, not by any caches.

normative_rules.name: pma_idp_mm
normative_rules.text: Main memory regions are assumed to be idempotent.

normative_rules.name: pma_idp_no_spec
normative_rules.text:
If accesses are
non-idempotent, i.e., there is potentially a side effect on any read or
write access, then speculative or redundant accesses must be avoided.

normative_rules.name: pma_idp_implicit_ok
normative_rules.text:
For non-idempotent regions, implicit reads and writes must not be
performed early or speculatively, with the following exceptions. When a
non-speculative implicit read is performed, an implementation is
permitted to additionally read any of the bytes within a naturally
aligned power-of-2 region containing the address of the non-speculative
implicit read. Furthermore, when a non-speculative instruction fetch is
performed, an implementation is permitted to additionally read any of
the bytes within the next naturally aligned power-of-2 region of the
same size (with the address of the region taken modulo 2^XLEN^).

normative_rules.name: pma_idp_implicit_sz
normative_rules.text:
The size of these naturally aligned power-of-2 regions is
implementation-defined, but, for systems with page-based virtual memory,
must not exceed the smallest supported page size.

normative_rules.name: pmp_granularity
normative_rules.text:
The granularity of PMP access control settings are platform-specific,
but the standard PMP encoding supports regions as small as four bytes.

normative_rules.name: pmp_mmode_only_regions
normative_rules.text:
Certain regions’ privileges can be hardwired—for example, some regions
might only ever be visible in machine mode but in no lower-privilege
layers.

normative_rules.name: pmp_check_priv_modes
normative_rules.text:
PMP checks are applied to all accesses whose effective privilege mode is
S or U, including instruction fetches and data accesses in S and U mode,
and data accesses in M-mode when the MPRV bit in mstatus is set and
the MPP field in mstatus contains S or U.

normative_rules.name: pmp_check_pagetable_access
normative_rules.text:
PMP checks are also applied
to page-table accesses for virtual-address translation, for which the
effective privilege mode is S.

normative_rules.name: pmp_mmode_locking
normative_rules.text:
Optionally, PMP checks may additionally
apply to M-mode accesses, in which case the PMP registers themselves are
locked, so that even M-mode software cannot change them until the hart
is reset.

normative_rules.name: pmp_violation_precise_trap
normative_rules.text: PMP violations are always trapped precisely at the processor.

normative_rules.name: pmp_entry_structure
normative_rules.text:
PMP entries are described by an 8-bit configuration register and one
MXLEN-bit address register. Some PMP settings additionally use the
address register associated with the preceding PMP entry.

normative_rules.name: pmp_entry_count
normative_rules.text:
Up to 64 PMP
entries are supported. Implementations may implement zero, 16, or 64 PMP
entries; the lowest-numbered PMP entries must be implemented first.

normative_rules.name: pmp_csrs_warl_access
normative_rules.text:
All
PMP CSR fields are WARL and may be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: pmp_csr_mode
normative_rules.text:
PMP CSRs are only
accessible to M-mode.

normative_rules.name: pmp_cfg_rv32_layout
normative_rules.text:
For RV32, sixteen CSRs, pmpcfg0–pmpcfg15, hold
the configurations pmp0cfg–pmp63cfg for the 64 PMP entries, as shown
in <<pmpcfg-rv32>>.

normative_rules.name: pmp_cfg_rv64_layout
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, eight
even-numbered CSRs, pmpcfg0, pmpcfg2, …, pmpcfg14, hold the
configurations for the 64 PMP entries, as shown in
<<pmpcfg-rv64>>.

normative_rules.name: pmp_cfg_rv64_illegal
normative_rules.text:
For RV64, the odd-numbered
configuration registers, pmpcfg1, pmpcfg3, …, pmpcfg15, are
illegal.

normative_rules.name: pmp_addr_registers
normative_rules.text: The PMP address registers are CSRs named pmpaddr0-pmpaddr63.

normative_rules.name: pmp_addr_encoding
normative_rules.text:
Each
PMP address register encodes bits 33-2 of a 34-bit physical address for
RV32, as shown in <<pmpaddr-rv32>>. For RV64,
each PMP address register encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical
address, as shown in <<pmpaddr-rv64>>.

normative_rules.name: pmp_addr_warl
normative_rules.text:
Not all
physical address bits may be implemented, and so the pmpaddr registers
are WARL.

normative_rules.name: pmp_cfg_permissions
normative_rules.text:
<<pmpcfg>> shows the layout of a PMP configuration
register. The R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry
permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively. When one
of these bits is clear, the corresponding access type is denied.

normative_rules.name: pmp_rwx_warl
normative_rules.text:
The R,
W, and X fields form a collective WARL field for which the combinations with R=0 and W=1 are reserved.

normative_rules.name: pmp_exec_fault
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to fetch an instruction from a PMP region that does not have
execute permissions raises an instruction access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: pmp_load_fault
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to execute a load or load-reserved instruction that accesses
a physical address within a PMP region without read permissions raises a
load access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: pmp_store_fault
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to execute a store,
store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses a physical address
within a PMP region without write permissions raises a store
access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: pmp_cbm_fault
normative_rules.text:
The permissions required for a cache-block management instruction to access
a PMP region are defined in <<cmo>>; when such access is not permitted, the instruction raises a
store access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: pmp_a_field_encoding
normative_rules.text:
The A field in a PMP entry's configuration register encodes the
address-matching mode of the associated PMP address register. The
encoding of this field is shown in <<pmpcfg-a>>.

normative_rules.name: pmp_a_field_off
normative_rules.text: When A=0, this PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.

normative_rules.name: pmp_a_field_napot_na4
pmp_napot_encoding_low_bits
normative_rules.text:
NAPOT ranges make use of the low-order bits of the associated address
register to encode the size of the range, as shown in
<<pmpcfg-napot>>.

normative_rules.name: pmp_a_field_tor
normative_rules.text:
If TOR is selected, the associated address register forms the top of the
address range, and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom
of the address range. If PMP entry i's A field is set to
TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr~i-1~≤y<pmpaddr~i~ (irrespective of the value of pmpcfg~i-1~). If PMP entry 0's A field is set to TOR, zero is used for the lower bound, and so it matches
any address y<pmpaddr~0~.

normative_rules.name: pmp_region_granularity_g
normative_rules.text:
Although the PMP mechanism supports regions as small as four bytes,
platforms may specify coarser PMP regions. In general, the PMP grain is
2^G+2^ bytes and must be the same across all PMP regions.

normative_rules.name: pmp_na4_select_restriction
normative_rules.text: When G ≥ 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable.

normative_rules.name: pmp_napot_addr_read_mask
normative_rules.text:
When
G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg~i~.A[1] is set,
i.e. the mode is NAPOT, then bits pmpaddr~i~[G-2:0]
read as all ones.

normative_rules.name: pmp_tor_off_addr_read_mask
normative_rules.text:
When G ≥ 1 and
pmpcfg~i~.A[1] is clear, i.e. the mode is OFF or TOR,
then bits pmpaddr~i~[G-1:0] read as all zeros. Bits
pmpaddr~i~[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.

normative_rules.name: pmp_addr_retention_on_mode_change
normative_rules.text:
Although changing pmpcfg~i~.A[1] affects the value
read from pmpaddr~i~, it does not affect the
underlying value stored in that register—in particular,
pmpaddr~i~[G-1] retains its original value when
pmpcfg~i~.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then
back to NAPOT.

normative_rules.name: pmp_l_bit_function
normative_rules.text:
The L bit indicates that the PMP entry is locked, i.e., writes to the
configuration register and associated address registers are ignored.

normative_rules.name: pmp_locked_until_reset
normative_rules.text: Locked PMP entries remain locked until the hart is reset.

normative_rules.name: pmp_l_bit_write_protection
normative_rules.text:
If PMP entry
i is locked, writes to pmpicfg and pmpaddri are ignored. Additionally, if PMP
entry i is locked and pmpicfg.A is set
to TOR, writes to pmpaddri-1 are ignored.

normative_rules.name: pmp_l_bit_m_mode_enforcement
normative_rules.text:
In addition to locking the PMP entry, the L bit indicates whether the
R/W/X permissions are additionally enforced on M-mode accesses.
When the L bit is
set, these permissions are enforced for all privilege modes. When the L
bit is clear, any M-mode access matching the PMP entry will succeed; the
R/W/X permissions apply only to S and U modes.

normative_rules.name: pmp_misaligned_access_behavior
normative_rules.text:
On some implementations, misaligned loads, stores, and instruction
fetches may be decomposed into multiple memory operations, some of which may
succeed before an access-fault exception occurs, as described in the RVWMO
specification. PMP checking is performed on each memory operation independently.

normative_rules.name: pmp_entry_priority
normative_rules.text:
PMP entries are statically prioritized. The lowest-numbered PMP entry
that matches any byte of a memory operation determines whether that operation
succeeds or fails.

normative_rules.name: pmp_full_match_required
normative_rules.text:
The matching PMP entry must match all bytes of a memory
operation, or the operation fails, irrespective of the L, R, W, and X bits.

normative_rules.name: pmp_rwx_check
normative_rules.text:
If a PMP entry matches all bytes of a memory operation, then the L, R, W, and X
bits determine whether the operation succeeds or fails. If the L bit is
clear and the privilege mode of the access is M, the operation succeeds.
Otherwise, if the L bit is set or the privilege mode of the access is S
or U, then the operation succeeds only if the R, W, or X bit corresponding
to the access type is set.

normative_rules.name: pmp_no_entry_match
normative_rules.text:
If no PMP entry matches an M-mode memory operation, the operation succeeds.
If no PMP entry matches an S-mode or U-mode memory operation, the operation
fails if at least one PMP entry is implemented and succeeds otherwise.

normative_rules.name: pmp_access_fault_exception
normative_rules.text:
Failed memory operations generate an instruction, load, or store access-fault
exception.

normative_rules.name: pmp_with_paging
normative_rules.text:
When paging is enabled,
instructions that access virtual memory may result in multiple
physical-memory accesses, including implicit references to the page
tables. The PMP checks apply to all of these accesses.

normative_rules.name: pmp_speculative_translations
normative_rules.text:
Implementations with virtual memory are permitted to perform address
translations speculatively and earlier than required by an explicit
memory access, and are permitted to cache them in address translation
cache structures—including possibly caching the identity mappings from
effective address to physical address used in Bare translation modes and
M-mode. The PMP settings for the resulting physical address may be
checked (and possibly cached) at any point between the address
translation and the explicit memory access.

normative_rules.name: pmp_sfence_required
normative_rules.text:
when the PMP settings
are modified, M-mode software must synchronize the PMP settings with the
virtual memory system and any PMP or address-translation caches. This is
accomplished by executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and
rs2=x0, after the PMP CSRs are written.

normative_rules.name: sstatus
normative_rules.text: The sstatus register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in  when SXLEN=32 and  when SXLEN=64. The sstatus register keeps track of the processor’s current operating state.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_spp
normative_rules.text: The SPP bit indicates the privilege level at which a hart was executing before entering supervisor mode. When a trap is taken, SPP is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, or 1 otherwise. When an SRET instruction (see ) is executed to return from the trap handler, the privilege level is set to user mode if the SPP bit is 0, or supervisor mode if the SPP bit is 1; SPP is then set to 0.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sie
normative_rules.text: The SIE bit enables or disables all interrupts in supervisor mode. When SIE is clear, interrupts are not taken while in supervisor mode. When the hart is running in user-mode, the value in SIE is ignored, and supervisor-level interrupts are enabled. The supervisor can disable individual interrupt sources using the sie CSR.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_spie
normative_rules.text: The SPIE bit indicates whether supervisor interrupts were enabled prior to trapping into supervisor mode. When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to SIE, and SIE is set to 0. When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to SPIE, then SPIE is set to 1.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_subset_mstatus
normative_rules.text: The sstatus register is a subset of the mstatus register.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_uxl
normative_rules.text: The UXL field controls the value of XLEN for U-mode, termed UXLEN, which may differ from the value of XLEN for S-mode, termed SXLEN. The encoding of UXL is the same as that of the MXL field of misa, shown in .

normative_rules.name: sstatus_uxl_sz
normative_rules.text: When SXLEN=32, the UXL field does not exist, and UXLEN=32. When SXLEN=64, it is a WARL field that encodes the current value of UXLEN. In particular, an implementation may make UXL be a read-only field whose value always ensures that UXLEN=SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_uxl_behavior
normative_rules.text: If UXLEN≠SXLEN, instructions executed in the narrower mode must ignore source register operand bits above the configured XLEN, and must sign-extend results to fill the widest supported XLEN in the destination register.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_uxl_addr_modulo
normative_rules.text:
If UXLEN < SXLEN, user-mode instruction-fetch addresses
and load and store effective addresses are taken modulo
2^UXLEN^.

normative_rules.name: hint_sxlen
normative_rules.text: Some HINT instructions are encoded as integer computational instructions that overwrite their destination register with its current value, e.g., c.addi x8, 0. When such a HINT is executed with XLEN < SXLEN and bits SXLEN..XLEN of the destination register not all equal to bit XLEN-1, it is implementation-defined whether bits SXLEN..XLEN of the destination register are unchanged or are overwritten with copies of bit XLEN-1.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_mxr
normative_rules.text: The MXR (Make eXecutable Readable) bit modifies the privilege with which loads access virtual memory. When MXR=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1 in ) will succeed. When MXR=1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed. MXR has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sum
normative_rules.text: The SUM (permit Supervisor User Memory access) bit modifies the privilege with which S-mode loads and stores access virtual memory. When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1 in ) will fault. When SUM=1, these accesses are permitted. SUM has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect, nor when executing in U-mode. Note that S-mode can never execute instructions from user pages, regardless of the state of SUM.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sum_satp_mode
normative_rules.text: SUM is read-only 0 if satp.MODE is read-only 0.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_ube
normative_rules.text: The UBE bit is a WARL field that controls the endianness of explicit memory accesses made from U-mode, which may differ from the endianness of memory accesses in S-mode. An implementation may make UBE be a read-only field that always specifies the same endianness as for S-mode.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_ube_endianness_op
normative_rules.text:
UBE controls whether explicit load and store memory accesses made from
U-mode are little-endian (UBE=0) or big-endian (UBE=1).

normative_rules.name: sstatus_ube_implicit
normative_rules.text: UBE has no effect on instruction fetches, which are implicit memory accesses that are always little-endian.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_ube_implicit_smode
normative_rules.text:
For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory management data
structures, such as page tables, S-mode endianness always applies and
UBE is ignored.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_spelp
normative_rules.text: Access to the SPELP field, added by Zicfilp, accesses the homonymous fields of mstatus when V=0, and the homonymous fields of vsstatus when V=1.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt
normative_rules.text: The S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) bit is a WARL field introduced by the Ssdbltrp extension to address double trap (See ) at privilege modes lower than M.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_sstatus_sie_overwrite
normative_rules.text: When the SDT bit is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write, the SIE (Supervisor Interrupt Enable) bit is cleared to 0. This clearing occurs regardless of the value written, if any, to the SIE bit by the same write. The SIE bit can only be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write if the SDT bit is being set to 0 by the same write or is already 0.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_trap
normative_rules.text:
When a trap is to be taken into S-mode, if the SDT bit is currently 0,
it is then set to 1, and the trap is delivered as expected.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_unexpected_trap
normative_rules.text:
However, if SDT is
already set to 1, then this is an unexpected trap.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_double_trap
normative_rules.text:
In the event of an
unexpected trap, a double-trap exception trap is delivered into M-mode.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_double_trap_regs
normative_rules.text:
To
deliver this trap, the hart writes registers, except mcause and mtval2, with
the same information that the unexpected trap would have written if it was
taken into M-mode.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_double_trap_mtval2
normative_rules.text:
The mtval2 register is then set to what would be otherwise
written into the mcause register by the unexpected trap.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_double_trap_mcause
normative_rules.text:
The mcause
register is set to 16, the double-trap exception code.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_sret
normative_rules.text: An SRET instruction sets the SDT bit to 0.

normative_rules.name: stvec
normative_rules.text: The stvec register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that holds trap vector configuration, consisting of a vector base address (BASE) and a vector mode (MODE).

normative_rules.name: stvec_op
normative_rules.text: The BASE field in stvec is a WARL field that can hold any valid virtual or physical address, subject to the following alignment constraints: the address must be 4-byte aligned, and MODE settings other than Direct might impose additional alignment constraints on the value in the BASE field.

normative_rules.name: stvec_sz_base
normative_rules.text: Note that the CSR contains only bits XLEN-1 through 2 of the address BASE. When used as an address, the lower two bits are filled with zeroes to obtain an XLEN-bit address that is always aligned on a 4-byte boundary.

normative_rules.name: stvec_mode_enc
normative_rules.text:
Value|Name|Description
===
0
1
≥2|Direct
Vectored|All exceptions set pc to BASE.
Asynchronous interrupts set pc to BASE+4×cause.
Reserved
===

normative_rules.name: sip_sie
normative_rules.text: The sip register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register containing information on pending interrupts, while sie is the corresponding SXLEN-bit read/write register containing interrupt enable bits. Interrupt cause number i (as reported in CSR scause, ) corresponds with bit i in both sip and sie. Bits 15:0 are allocated to standard interrupt causes only, while bits 16 and above are designated for platform use.

normative_rules.name: sie_sip_supervisor_strap
normative_rules.text: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode if both of the following are true: (a) either the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode; and (b) bit i is set in both sip and sie.

normative_rules.name: sie_sip_strap_time_constraint
normative_rules.text: These conditions for an interrupt trap to occur must be evaluated in a bounded amount of time from when an interrupt becomes, or ceases to be, pending in sip, and must also be evaluated immediately following the execution of an SRET instruction or an explicit write to a CSR on which these interrupt trap conditions expressly depend (including sip, sie and sstatus).

normative_rules.name: s_interrupt_priority
normative_rules.text: Interrupts to S-mode take priority over any interrupts to lower privilege modes.

normative_rules.name: sip_acc
normative_rules.text:
Each individual bit in register sip may be writable or may be
read-only.

normative_rules.name: sip_op
normative_rules.text:
When bit i in sip is writable, a pending interrupt i
can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit. If interrupt i can become
pending but bit i in sip is read-only, the implementation must
provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt (which
may involve a call to the execution environment).

normative_rules.name: sie_acc
normative_rules.text:
A bit in sie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever
become pending. Bits of sie that are not writable are read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: sip_sie_bits_sz
normative_rules.text: The standard portions (bits 15:0) of registers sip and sie are formatted as shown in Figures  and  respectively.

normative_rules.name: sip_seip_sie_seie
normative_rules.text: Bits sip.SEIP and sie.SEIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level external interrupts. If implemented, SEIP is read-only in sip, and is set and cleared by the execution environment, typically through a platform-specific interrupt controller.

normative_rules.name: sip_stip_sie_stie
normative_rules.text: Bits sip.STIP and sie.STIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level timer interrupts. If implemented, STIP is read-only in sip. When the Sstc extension is not implemented, STIP is set and cleared by the execution environment. When the Sstc extension is implemented, STIP reflects the timer interrupt signal resulting from stimecmp. The sip.STIP bit, in response to timer interrupts generated by stimecmp, is set by writing stimecmp with a value that is less than or equal to time, and is cleared by writing stimecmp with a value greater than time.

normative_rules.name: sip_ssip_sie_ssie
normative_rules.text: Bits sip.SSIP and sie.SSIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for supervisor-level software interrupts. If implemented, SSIP is writable in sip and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.

normative_rules.name: sip_sie_Sscofpmf
normative_rules.text: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, bits sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for local-counter-overflow interrupts. LCOFIP is read-write in sip and reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow overflow interrupt request resulting from any of the mhpmeventn.OF bits being set. If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: std_super_intr_impl
normative_rules.text:
Each standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) might not be implemented,
in which case the corresponding interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable
bits are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: sip_sie_warl
normative_rules.text: All bits in sip and sie are WARL fields.

normative_rules.name: sip_sie_priority_bit_order
normative_rules.text: Multiple simultaneous interrupts destined for supervisor mode are handled in the following decreasing priority order: SEI, SSI, STI, LCOFI.

normative_rules.name: supervisor_timer_scheduling
normative_rules.text: The implementation must provide a facility for scheduling timer interrupts in terms of the real-time counter, time.

normative_rules.name: scounteren
normative_rules.text: The counter-enable (scounteren) CSR is a 32-bit register that controls the availability of the hardware performance monitoring counters to U-mode.

normative_rules.name: scounteren_op
normative_rules.text: When the CY, TM, IR, or HPMn bit in the scounteren register is clear, attempts to read the cycle, time, instret, or hpmcountern register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception. When one of these bits is set, access to the corresponding register is permitted.

normative_rules.name: scounteren_acc
normative_rules.text: scounteren must be implemented. However, any of the bits may be read-only zero, indicating reads to the corresponding counter will cause an exception when executing in U-mode. Hence, they are effectively WARL fields.

normative_rules.name: sscratch
normative_rules.text:
The sscratch CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register, dedicated
for use by the supervisor.

normative_rules.name: sepc
normative_rules.text: sepc is an SXLEN-bit read/write CSR formatted as shown in . The low bit of sepc (sepc[0]) is always zero. On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, the two low bits (sepc[1:0]) are always zero.

normative_rules.name: sepc_op_mask_ialign32
normative_rules.text: If an implementation allows IALIGN to be either 16 or 32 (by changing CSR misa, for example), then, whenever IALIGN=32, bit sepc[1] is masked on reads so that it appears to be 0. This masking occurs also for the implicit read by the SRET instruction. Though masked, sepc[1] remains writable when IALIGN=32.

normative_rules.name: sepc_acc_invalid_addr
normative_rules.text: sepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses. It need not be capable of holding all possible invalid addresses. Prior to writing sepc, implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that sepc is capable of holding.

normative_rules.name: sepc_op_trap_write
normative_rules.text: When a trap is taken into S-mode, sepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that encountered the exception. Otherwise, sepc is never written by the implementation, though it may be explicitly written by software.

normative_rules.name: scause
normative_rules.text: The scause CSR is an SXLEN-bit read-write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into S-mode, scause is written with a code indicating the event that caused the trap. Otherwise, scause is never written by the implementation, though it may be explicitly written by software.

normative_rules.name: scause_exception_code_acc
normative_rules.text:
The
Exception Code is a WLRL field.

normative_rules.name: scause_exception_code_sz
normative_rules.text:
It is required to hold the values 0–31
(i.e., bits 4–0 must be implemented), but otherwise it is only
guaranteed to hold supported exception codes.

normative_rules.name: scause_interrupt
normative_rules.text: The Interrupt bit in the scause register is set if the trap was caused by an interrupt. The Exception Code field contains a code identifying the last exception or interrupt.  lists the possible exception codes for the current supervisor ISAs. The Exception Code is a WLRL field. It is required to hold the values 0–31 (i.e., bits 4–0 must be implemented), but otherwise it is only guaranteed to hold supported exception codes.

normative_rules.name: stval
normative_rules.text: The stval CSR is an SXLEN-bit read-write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into S-mode, stval is written with exception-specific information to assist software in handling the trap. Otherwise, stval is never written by the implementation, though it may be explicitly written by software. The hardware platform will specify which exceptions must set stval informatively, which may unconditionally set it to zero, and which may exhibit either behavior, depending on the underlying event that caused the exception.

normative_rules.name: stval_op_faulting_addr
normative_rules.text: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then stval will contain the faulting virtual address.

normative_rules.name: stval_op_breakpoint
normative_rules.text: On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, stval is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.

normative_rules.name: stval_op_load_store_fault
normative_rules.text: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a misaligned load or store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.

normative_rules.name: stval_faulting_address_variable_instr
normative_rules.text: If stval is written with a nonzero value when an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with variable-length instructions, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault, while sepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.

normative_rules.name: stval_op_illegal_instr
normative_rules.text: The stval register can optionally also be used to return the faulting instruction bits on an illegal-instruction exception (sepc points to the faulting instruction in memory). If stval is written with a nonzero value when an illegal-instruction exception occurs, then stval will contain the shortest of:

normative_rules.name: stval_op_illegal_instr_format
normative_rules.text: On an illegal-instruction exception, the instruction bits are zero-extended and loaded into csr:stval[].

normative_rules.name: stval_exception_info
normative_rules.text: On a trap caused by a software-check exception, the stval register holds the cause for the exception. The following encodings are defined:

normative_rules.name: stval_op_other_traps
normative_rules.text: For other traps, stval is set to zero, but a future standard may redefine stval’s setting for other traps.

normative_rules.name: stval_acc
normative_rules.text:
stval is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual
addresses and the value 0. It need not be capable of holding all
possible invalid addresses.

normative_rules.name: stval_inv_addr_conv
normative_rules.text:
Prior to writing stval, implementations
may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that
stval is capable of holding.

normative_rules.name: stval_instr_bits_sz
normative_rules.text:
If the feature to return the faulting
instruction bits is implemented, stval must also be able to hold all
values less than 2^N^, where N is the smaller
of SXLEN and ILEN.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg
normative_rules.text: The senvcfg CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in , that controls certain characteristics of the U-mode execution environment.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_fiom
normative_rules.text: If bit FIOM (Fence of I/O implies Memory) is set to one in senvcfg, FENCE instructions executed in U-mode are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O implies also the requirement to order main memory accesses.  details the modified interpretation of FENCE instruction bits PI, PO, SI, and SO in U-mode when FIOM=1.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_fiom_op_atomic
normative_rules.text: Similarly, for U-mode when FIOM=1, if an atomic instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O has its aq and/or rl bit set, then that instruction is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_fiom_acc
normative_rules.text: If satp.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_fiom_fence_presuc_op
normative_rules.text:
Instruction bit|Meaning when set
===
PI
PO|Predecessor device input and memory reads (PR implied)
Predecessor device output and memory writes (PW implied)¶SI
SO|Successor device input and memory reads (SR implied)
Successor device output and memory writes (SW implied)
===

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbze
normative_rules.text:
The Zicboz extension adds the CBZE (Cache Block Zero instruction enable) field
to senvcfg.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbze_op
normative_rules.text:
The CBZE field controls execution of the cache block zero
instruction (CBO.ZERO) in U-mode.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbze_umode_op
normative_rules.text:
Execution of CBO.ZERO in U-mode is enabled
only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and CBZE is
set to 1; otherwise, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbze_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When the Zicboz
extension is not implemented, CBZE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbcfe
normative_rules.text:
The Zicbom extension adds the CBCFE (Cache Block Clean and Flush instruction
Enable) field to senvcfg to control execution of the CBO.CLEAN and
CBO.FLUSH instructions in U-mode.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbcfe_umode_op
normative_rules.text:
Execution of these instructions in U-mode is
enabled only if execution of these instructions is enabled for use in S-mode and
CBCFE is set to 1; otherwise, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbcfe_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When
the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBCFE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbie
normative_rules.text:
The Zicbom extension adds the CBIE (Cache Block Invalidate instruction Enable)
WARL field to senvcfg to control execution of the CBO.INVAL instruction in
U-mode.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbie_rsv
normative_rules.text: The encoding 0b10 is reserved.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbie_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When the Zicbom extension is not
implemented, CBIE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_cbie_umode_op
normative_rules.text:
Execution of CBO.INVAL in U-mode is
enabled only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and
CBIE is set to 0b01 or 0b11; otherwise, an illegal-instruction exception is
raised.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_s_mode_enabled_op
normative_rules.text:
If CBO.INVAL is enabled in S-mode to perform a flush operation, then when the
instruction is enabled in U-mode it performs a flush operation, even if CBIE
is set to 0b11. Otherwise, the instruction behaves as follows, depending on the
CBIE encoding:

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_s_mode_flush_enc
normative_rules.text: 0b01 -- The instruction is executed and performs a flush operation.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_s_mode_inval_enc
normative_rules.text: 0b11 -- The instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_pmm_ssnpm
