normative_rules.text: If the Ssnpm extension is implemented, the PMM field enables or disables pointer masking (see ) for the next-lower privilege mode (U/VU), according to the values in . If Ssnpm is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero. The PMM field is read-only zero for RV32.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_pmm_immediate
normative_rules.text: Changing senvcfg.PMM takes effect immediately, without the need to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction.

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_pmm_enc
normative_rules.text:
Value|Description
===
00|Pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN = 0)¶01|Reserved¶10|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 57 (PMLEN = 7 on RV64)¶11|Pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN - 48 (PMLEN = 16 on RV64)
===

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_lpe_Zicfilp
normative_rules.text: The Zicfilp extension adds the LPE field in senvcfg. When the LPE field is set to 1, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in VU/U-mode. When the LPE field is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in VU/U-mode and the following rules apply to VU/U-mode:

normative_rules.name: senvcfg_sse_Zicfiss
normative_rules.text: The Zicfiss extension adds the SSE field in senvcfg. When the SSE field is set to 1, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VU/U-mode. When the SSE field is 0, the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VU/U-mode, and the following rules apply:

normative_rules.name: satp
normative_rules.text: The satp CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in  for SXLEN=32 and  for SXLEN=64, which controls supervisor-mode address translation and protection. This register holds the physical page number (PPN) of the root page table, i.e., its supervisor physical address divided by 4 KiB; an address space identifier (ASID), which facilitates address-translation fences on a per-address-space basis; and the MODE field, which selects the current address-translation scheme. Further details on the access to this register are described in .

normative_rules.name: satp_mode
normative_rules.text:
<<norm:satp_mode_enc>> shows the encodings of the MODE field when
SXLEN=32 and SXLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_bare_op
normative_rules.text:
When MODE=Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are
equal to supervisor physical addresses, and there is no additional
memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme described
in <<pmp>>.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_bare_zero_fields
normative_rules.text:
To select MODE=Bare, software must write
zero to the remaining fields of satp (bits 30–0 when SXLEN=32, or bits
59–0 when SXLEN=64).

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_bare_nonzero_unspec
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to select MODE=Bare with a nonzero
pattern in the remaining fields has an UNSPECIFIED effect on the value that the
remaining fields assume and an UNSPECIFIED effect on address translation and
protection behavior.

normative_rules.name: satp_bare_rsv_custom
normative_rules.text:
When SXLEN=32, the satp encodings corresponding to MODE=Bare and
ASID[8:7]=3 are designated for custom use, whereas the encodings
corresponding to MODE=Bare and ASID[8:7]≠3 are reserved
for future standard use. When SXLEN=64, all satp encodings
corresponding to MODE=Bare are reserved for future standard use.

normative_rules.name: svbare_satp_mode_bare
normative_rules.text:
If an implementation supports the Svbare extension, then the satp
register's MODE field must be capable of holding the value Bare.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_sxlen32
normative_rules.text: When SXLEN=32, the only other valid setting for MODE is Sv32, a paged virtual-memory scheme described in .

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_sxlen64
normative_rules.text: When SXLEN=64, three paged virtual-memory schemes are defined: Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57, described in , , and , respectively. One additional scheme, Sv64, will be defined in a later version of this specification. The remaining MODE settings are reserved for future use and may define different interpretations of the other fields in satp.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_op_unsupported
normative_rules.text: Implementations are not required to support all MODE settings, and if satp is written with an unsupported MODE, the entire write has no effect; no fields in satp are modified.

normative_rules.name: asidlen
normative_rules.text: The number of ASID bits is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero.

normative_rules.name: asid_lsb_first
normative_rules.text:
The
least-significant bits of ASID are implemented first: that is, if
ASIDLEN > 0, ASID[ASIDLEN-1:0] is writable.

normative_rules.name: asidmax
normative_rules.text:
The maximal
value of ASIDLEN, termed ASIDMAX, is 9 for Sv32 or 16 for Sv39, Sv48,
and Sv57.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_enc
normative_rules.text:
SXLEN=32
===
Value|Name|Description¶0|Bare|No translation or protection.¶1|Sv32|Page-based 32-bit virtual addressing (see ).¶SXLEN=64¶Value|Name|Description¶0|Bare|No translation or protection.¶1-7|-|Reserved for standard use¶8|Sv39|Page-based 39-bit virtual addressing (see ).¶9|Sv48|Page-based 48-bit virtual addressing (see ).¶10|Sv57|Page-based 57-bit virtual addressing (see ).¶11|Sv64|Reserved for page-based 64-bit virtual addressing.¶12-13|-|Reserved for standard use¶14-15|-|Designated for custom use
===

normative_rules.name: satp_op_active
normative_rules.text: The satp CSR is considered active when the effective privilege mode is S-mode or U-mode. Executions of the address-translation algorithm may only begin using a given value of satp when satp is active.

normative_rules.name: satp_op_sfence_vma
normative_rules.text:
Note that writing satp does not imply any ordering constraints between
page-table updates and subsequent address translations, nor does it
imply any invalidation of address-translation caches.

normative_rules.name: stimecmp_stimecmph_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The stimecmp CSR is a 64-bit register and
has 64-bit precision on all RV32 and RV64 systems.
In RV32 only, accesses to the stimecmp CSR access the low 32 bits,
while accesses to the stimecmph CSR access the high 32 bits of stimecmp.

normative_rules.name: mip_sip_stip_op
normative_rules.text: A supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending, as reflected in the STIP bit in the mip and sip registers whenever time contains a value greater than or equal to stimecmp, treating the values as unsigned integers. If the result of this comparison changes, it is guaranteed to be reflected in STIP eventually, but not necessarily immediately. The interrupt remains posted until stimecmp becomes greater than time, typically as a result of writing stimecmp. The interrupt will be taken based on the standard interrupt enable and delegation rules.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_op
normative_rules.text:
The supervisor memory-management fence instruction SFENCE.VMA is used to
synchronize updates to in-memory memory-management data structures with
current execution. Instruction execution causes implicit reads and
writes to these data structures; however, these implicit references are
ordinarily not ordered with respect to explicit loads and stores.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_ordering
normative_rules.text:
Executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction guarantees that any previous stores
already visible to the current RISC-V hart are ordered before certain
implicit references by subsequent instructions in that hart to the
memory-management data structures. The specific set of operations
ordered by SFENCE.VMA is determined by rs1 and rs2, as described
below.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_invalidation
normative_rules.text:
SFENCE.VMA is also used to invalidate entries in the
address-translation cache associated with a hart (see <<sv32algorithm>>).

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_local_only
normative_rules.text:
SFENCE.VMA orders only the local hart’s implicit references to the
memory-management data structures.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_all_asid_va
normative_rules.text:
If rs1=x0 and rs2=x0, the fence orders all reads and writes
made to any level of the page tables, for all address spaces. The fence
also invalidates all address-translation cache entries, for all address
spaces.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_asid_only
normative_rules.text:
If rs1=x0 and rs2≠x0, the fence orders all
reads and writes made to any level of the page tables, but only for the
address space identified by integer register rs2. Accesses to global
mappings (see <<translation>>) are not ordered. The
fence also invalidates all address-translation cache entries matching
the address space identified by integer register rs2, except for
entries containing global mappings.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_va_all_asid
normative_rules.text:
If rs1≠x0 and rs2=x0, the fence orders only
reads and writes made to leaf page table entries corresponding to the
virtual address in rs1, for all address spaces. The fence also
invalidates all address-translation cache entries that contain leaf page
table entries corresponding to the virtual address in rs1, for all
address spaces.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_va_asid
normative_rules.text:
If rs1≠x0 and rs2≠x0, the
fence orders only reads and writes made to leaf page table entries
corresponding to the virtual address in rs1, for the address space
identified by integer register rs2. Accesses to global mappings are
not ordered. The fence also invalidates all address-translation cache
entries that contain leaf page table entries corresponding to the
virtual address in rs1 and that match the address space identified by
integer register rs2, except for entries containing global mappings.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_invalid_va
normative_rules.text: If the value held in rs1 is not a valid virtual address, then the SFENCE.VMA instruction has no effect. No exception is raised in this case.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_rs2_bits
normative_rules.text: When rs2≠x0, bits SXLEN-1:ASIDMAX of the value held in rs2 are reserved for future standard use. Until their use is defined by a standard extension, they should be zeroed by software and ignored by current implementations. Furthermore, if ASIDLEN<ASIDMAX, the implementation shall ignore bits ASIDMAX-1:ASIDLEN of the value held in rs2.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_ordering_semantics
normative_rules.text: An implicit read of the memory-management data structures may return any translation for an address that was valid at any time since the most recent SFENCE.VMA that subsumes that address. The ordering implied by SFENCE.VMA does not place implicit reads and writes to the memory-management data structures into the global memory order in a way that interacts cleanly with the standard RVWMO ordering rules. In particular, even though an SFENCE.VMA orders prior explicit accesses before subsequent implicit accesses, and those implicit accesses are ordered before their associated explicit accesses, SFENCE.VMA does not necessarily place prior explicit accesses before subsequent explicit accesses in the global memory order. These implicit loads also need not otherwise obey normal program order semantics with respect to prior loads or stores to the same address.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_implicit_access
normative_rules.text: Implementations must only perform implicit reads of the translation data structures pointed to by the current contents of the satp register or a subsequent valid (V=1) translation data structure entry, and must only raise exceptions for implicit accesses that are generated as a result of instruction execution, not those that are performed speculatively.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_sum_mxr_effect
normative_rules.text:
Changes to the sstatus fields SUM and MXR take effect immediately,
without the need to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_mode_effect
normative_rules.text:
Changing
satp.MODE from Bare to other modes and vice versa also takes effect
immediately, without the need to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_asid_effect
normative_rules.text: Likewise, changes to satp.ASID take effect immediately.

normative_rules.name: asid_hart_private
normative_rules.text: If a hart employs an address-translation cache, that cache must appear to be private to that hart. In particular, the meaning of an ASID is local to a hart; software may choose to use the same ASID to refer to different address spaces on different harts.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_roz_sfence_illegal
normative_rules.text: For implementations that make satp.MODE read-only zero (always Bare), attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction might raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: satp_ppn_Sv32_sz
normative_rules.text: 22-bit physical page number (PPN)

normative_rules.name: fetch_page_fault_no_x
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to fetch an instruction from a page that does not have
execute permissions raises a fetch page-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: load_page_fault_no_r
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to execute a load or load-reserved
instruction whose effective address lies
within a page without read permissions raises a load page-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: store_page_fault_no_w
normative_rules.text:
Attempting to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero
instruction whose effective address lies within a page without write
permissions raises a store page-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: cbm_page_fault
normative_rules.text:
The permissions required for a cache-block management instruction are
defined in <<cmo>>; when address translation does not permit any access, the instruction raises a
store page-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: pte_u_op
normative_rules.text:
The U bit indicates whether the page is accessible to user mode. U-mode
software may only access the page when U=1. If the SUM bit in the
sstatus register is set, supervisor mode software may also access
pages with U=1.

normative_rules.name: pte_u_no_s_exec
normative_rules.text:
Irrespective of SUM, the supervisor may not execute
code on pages with U=1.

normative_rules.name: pte_g_op
normative_rules.text:
The G bit designates a global mapping. Global mappings are those that
exist in all address spaces. For non-leaf PTEs, the global setting
implies that all mappings in the subsequent levels of the page table are
global.

normative_rules.name: pte_rsw_ignored
normative_rules.text:
The RSW field is reserved for use by supervisor software; the
implementation shall ignore this field.

normative_rules.name: pte_a_def
normative_rules.text:
Each leaf PTE contains an accessed (A) and dirty (D) bit. The A bit
indicates the virtual page has been read, written, or fetched from since
the last time the A bit was cleared.

normative_rules.name: pte_d_def
normative_rules.text:
The D bit indicates the virtual
page has been written since the last time the D bit was cleared.

normative_rules.name: Svade_access_ad_bit_clear
normative_rules.text:
The Svade extension: when a virtual page is accessed and the A bit is
clear, or is written and the D bit is clear, a page-fault exception is
raised.

normative_rules.name: pte_ad_scheme_uniform
normative_rules.text:
All harts in a system must employ the same PTE-update scheme as each
other.

normative_rules.name: lr_sc_rsrv_set_page
normative_rules.text: For implementations with both page-based virtual memory and the ext:a[] standard extension, the LR/SC reservation set must lie completely within a single base physical page (i.e., a naturally aligned 4 KiB physical-memory region).

normative_rules.name: Sv39_sxlen_va_sz
normative_rules.text:
This section describes a simple paged virtual-memory system for
SXLEN=64, which supports 39-bit virtual address spaces.

normative_rules.name: Sv39_va_signext
normative_rules.text:
must have bits 63–39 all equal to bit 38, or else
a page-fault exception will occur

normative_rules.name: Sv39_vpn_sz
normative_rules.text: 27-bit VPN

normative_rules.name: satp_ppn_Sv39_sz
normative_rules.text: 44-bit PPN

normative_rules.name: Sv39_levels
normative_rules.text: three-level page table

normative_rules.name: Sv39_page_offset_sz
normative_rules.text: 12-bit page offset is untranslated

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pte_count_sz
normative_rules.text:
Sv39 page tables contain 2^9^ page table entries
(PTEs), eight bytes each.

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pt_sz
normative_rules.text: exactly the size of a page

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pt_align
normative_rules.text: must always be aligned to a page boundary

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pte_Svnapot_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If Svnapot is not implemented, bit 63 remains
reserved and must be zeroed by software for forward compatibility, or
else a page-fault exception is raised

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pte_Svpbmt_rsv
normative_rules.text:
If Svpbmt is not implemented, bits 62-61 remain
reserved and must be zeroed by software for forward compatibility, or
else a page-fault exception is raised

normative_rules.name: Sv39_pte_future_rsv
normative_rules.text:
must be zeroed by software for forward
compatibility. If any of these bits are set, a page-fault exception is
raised

normative_rules.name: Sv39_leaf_any_level
normative_rules.text: Any level of PTE may be a leaf PTE

normative_rules.name: Sv39_page_sizes
normative_rules.text: 2 MiB megapages and 1 GiB gigapages

normative_rules.name: Sv39_superpage_align
normative_rules.text:
must be virtually and physically
aligned to a boundary equal to its size

normative_rules.name: Sv39_superpage_align_fault
normative_rules.text:
A page-fault exception is raised if
the physical address is insufficiently aligned

normative_rules.name: Sv39_ptesize
normative_rules.text: PTESIZE equals 8

normative_rules.name: Sv48_sxlen
normative_rules.text: SXLEN=64

normative_rules.name: Sv48_va_sz
normative_rules.text: 48-bit virtual address spaces

normative_rules.name: Sv48_requires_Sv39
normative_rules.text:
Implementations that support Sv48 must also
support Sv39

normative_rules.name: Sv48_va_signext
normative_rules.text:
must have bits 63–48 all equal to bit 47, or else
a page-fault exception will occur

normative_rules.name: Sv48_vpn_sz
normative_rules.text: 36-bit VPN

normative_rules.name: satp_ppn_Sv48_sz
normative_rules.text: 44-bit PPN

normative_rules.name: Sv48_levels
normative_rules.text: four-level page table

normative_rules.name: Sv48_page_offset_sz
normative_rules.text: 12-bit page offset is untranslated

normative_rules.name: Sv48_leaf_any_level
normative_rules.text: Any level of PTE may be a leaf PTE

normative_rules.name: Sv48_page_sizes
normative_rules.text:
2 MiB megapages, 1 GiB gigapages, and
512 GiB terapages

normative_rules.name: Sv48_superpage_align
normative_rules.text:
must be virtually and physically aligned to
a boundary equal to its size

normative_rules.name: Sv48_superpage_align_fault
normative_rules.text:
A page-fault exception is raised if
the physical address is insufficiently aligned

normative_rules.name: Sv48_ptesize
normative_rules.text: PTESIZE equals 8

normative_rules.name: Sv57_sxlen_va_sz
normative_rules.text:
This section describes a simple paged virtual-memory system designed for
RV64 systems, which supports
57-bit virtual address spaces.

normative_rules.name: Sv57_requires_Sv48
normative_rules.text:
Implementations that support Sv57 must also
support Sv48

normative_rules.name: Sv57_va_signext
normative_rules.text:
must have bits 63–57 all equal to bit 56, or else
a page-fault exception will occur

normative_rules.name: Sv57_vpn_sz
normative_rules.text: 45-bit VPN

normative_rules.name: satp_ppn_Sv57_sz
normative_rules.text: 44-bit PPN

normative_rules.name: Sv57_levels
normative_rules.text: five-level page table

normative_rules.name: Sv57_page_offset_sz
normative_rules.text: 12-bit page offset is untranslated

normative_rules.name: Sv57_leaf_any_level
normative_rules.text: Any level of PTE may be a leaf PTE

normative_rules.name: Sv57_page_sizes
normative_rules.text:
2 MiB megapages, 1 GiB gigapages, 512 GiB
terapages, and 256 TiB petapages

normative_rules.name: Sv57_superpage_align
normative_rules.text:
must be virtually and physically aligned to
a boundary equal to its size

normative_rules.name: Sv57_superpage_align_fault
normative_rules.text:
A page-fault exception is raised if
the physical address is insufficiently aligned

normative_rules.name: Sv57_ptesize
normative_rules.text: PTESIZE equals 8

normative_rules.name: H_requires_i
normative_rules.text:
The hypervisor extension depends on an ext:i[] base integer ISA with 32
x registers (RV32I or RV64I), not RV32E or RV64E, which have only 16 x
registers.

normative_rules.name: H_mtval_nrz
normative_rules.text: CSR mtval must not be read-only zero

normative_rules.name: H_vm_supported
normative_rules.text:
standard
page-based address translation must be supported, either Sv32 for RV32,
or a minimum of Sv39 for RV64

normative_rules.name: misa_H_op
normative_rules.text: The hypervisor extension is enabled by setting bit 7 in the misa CSR

normative_rules.name: H_csrs_hs_not_vs
normative_rules.text:
Additional CSRs are provided to HS-mode, but not to VS-mode,
to manage two-stage address translation and to control the behavior of a
VS-mode guest: hstatus, hedeleg, hideleg, hvip, hip, hie,
hgeip, hgeie, henvcfg, henvcfgh, hcounteren, htimedelta,
htimedeltah, htval, htinst, and hgatp.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_sub
normative_rules.text:
When V=1, the VS CSRs substitute for the corresponding supervisor CSRs,
taking over all functions of the usual supervisor CSRs except as
specified otherwise. Instructions that normally read or modify a
supervisor CSR shall instead access the corresponding VS CSR.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_acc_vs
normative_rules.text:
When V=1,
an attempt to read or write a VS CSR directly by its own separate CSR
address causes a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_acc_u
normative_rules.text:
Attempts from U-mode
cause an illegal-instruction exception as usual.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_acc_m_hs
normative_rules.text:
The VS CSRs can be
accessed as themselves only from M-mode or HS-mode.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_v1
normative_rules.text:
While V=1, the normal HS-level supervisor CSRs that are replaced by VS
CSRs retain their values but do not affect the behavior of the machine
unless specifically documented to do so.

normative_rules.name: H_vscsrs_v0
normative_rules.text:
when V=0, the VS
CSRs do not ordinarily affect the behavior of the machine other than
being readable and writable by CSR instructions.

normative_rules.name: H_scsrs_nomatch
normative_rules.text:
Some standard supervisor CSRs (senvcfg, scounteren, and scontext,
possibly others) have no matching VS CSR. These supervisor CSRs continue
to have their usual function and accessibility even when V=1, except
with VS-mode and VU-mode substituting for HS-mode and U-mode.

normative_rules.name: hsxlen
normative_rules.text:
we use the term HSXLEN to refer to the effective XLEN
when executing in HS-mode

normative_rules.name: vsxlen
normative_rules.text:
VSXLEN to refer to the effective XLEN
when executing in VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The hstatus register is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in  when HSXLEN=32 and  when HSXLEN=64. The hstatus register provides facilities analogous to the mstatus register for tracking and controlling the exception behavior of a VS-mode guest.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsxl_op
normative_rules.text:
The VSXL field controls the effective XLEN for VS-mode (known as
VSXLEN), which may differ from the XLEN for HS-mode (HSXLEN).

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsxl_32
normative_rules.text:
When
HSXLEN=32, the VSXL field does not exist, and VSXLEN=32.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsxl_64
normative_rules.text:
When HSXLEN=64,
VSXL is a WARL field that is encoded the same as the MXL field of misa,
shown in <<norm:misa_mxl_enc>>.

normative_rules.name: vsxl_ro
normative_rules.text:
In particular, an
implementation may make VSXL be a read-only field whose value always
ensures that VSXLEN=HSXLEN.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsxl_change
normative_rules.text: If HSXLEN is changed from 32 to a wider width, and if field VSXL is not restricted to a single value, it gets the value corresponding to the widest supported width not wider than the new HSXLEN.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vtsr_op
normative_rules.text:
When VTSR=1, an attempt in VS-mode to execute SRET raises a
virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vtw_op
normative_rules.text:
When VTW=1 (and assuming mstatus.TW=0),
an attempt in VS-mode to execute WFI raises a virtual-instruction
exception if the WFI does not complete within an
implementation-specific, bounded time limit.

normative_rules.name: vtw_virtinstr
normative_rules.text:
An implementation may have
WFI always raise a virtual-instruction exception in VS-mode when VTW=1
(and mstatus.TW=0), even if there are pending globally-disabled
interrupts when the instruction is executed.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vtvm_op
normative_rules.text:
When VTVM=1, an attempt in
VS-mode to execute SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA or to access CSR satp
raises a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vgein_op
normative_rules.text:
The VGEIN (Virtual Guest External Interrupt Number) field selects a
guest external interrupt source for VS-level external interrupts.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vgein_wlrl
normative_rules.text:
VGEIN
is a WLRL field that must be able to hold values between zero and the
maximum guest external interrupt number (known as GEILEN), inclusive.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vgein_zero
normative_rules.text:
When VGEIN=0, no guest external interrupt source is selected for
VS-level external interrupts.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vgein_acc
normative_rules.text:
GEILEN may be zero, in which case VGEIN
may be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hu_op
normative_rules.text: Field HU (Hypervisor in U-mode) controls whether the virtual-machine load/store instructions, HLV, HLVX, and HSV, can be used also in U-mode. When HU=1, these instructions can be executed in U-mode the same as in HS-mode. When HU=0, all hypervisor instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hupmm_u_mode
normative_rules.text:
When Ssnpm extension is implemented, the HUPMM field enables or disables
pointer masking (see <<Zpm>>) for HLV.* and HSV.* instructions in U-mode,
according to the values in <<henvcfg-pmm-values>>, when their explicit memory
access is performed as though in VU-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hupmm_vu_mode
normative_rules.text:
In HS- and M-modes, pointer masking
for these instructions is enabled or disabled by senvcfg.PMM, when their
explicit memory access is performed as though in VU-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hupmm_vs_mode
normative_rules.text:
Setting henvcfg.PMM
enables or disables pointer masking for HLV.* and HSV.* when their
explicit memory access is performed as though in VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hupmm_not_ssnpm_access
normative_rules.text:
When the Ssnpm
extension is not implemented, the HUPMM field is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_hupmm_rv32_access
normative_rules.text:
The HUPMM
field is read-only zero for RV32.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_spv_op
normative_rules.text:
The SPV bit (Supervisor Previous Virtualization mode) is written by the
implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode. Just as the SPP
bit in sstatus is set to the (nominal) privilege mode at the time of
the trap, the SPV bit in hstatus is set to the value of the
virtualization mode V at the time of the trap.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_spv_sret
normative_rules.text:
When an SRET instruction
is executed when V=0, V is set to SPV.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_spvp_op
normative_rules.text:
When V=1 and a trap is taken into HS-mode, bit SPVP (Supervisor Previous
Virtual Privilege) is set to the nominal privilege mode at the time of
the trap, the same as sstatus.SPP. But if V=0 before a trap, SPVP is
left unchanged on trap entry.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_spvp_virtls_op
normative_rules.text:
SPVP controls the effective privilege of
explicit memory accesses made by the virtual-machine load/store
instructions, HLV, HLVX, and HSV.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_gva_op
normative_rules.text: Field GVA (Guest Virtual Address) is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode. For any trap (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault) that writes a guest virtual address to stval, GVA is set to 1. For any other trap into HS-mode, GVA is set to 0.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsbe_warl
normative_rules.text:
The VSBE bit is a WARL field that controls the endianness of explicit memory
accesses made from VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsbe_op
normative_rules.text:
If VSBE=0, explicit load and store memory
accesses made from VS-mode are little-endian, and if VSBE=1, they are
big-endian.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsbe_implicit
normative_rules.text:
VSBE also controls the endianness of all implicit accesses
to VS-level memory management data structures, such as page tables.

normative_rules.name: hstatus_vsbe_acc
normative_rules.text:
An
implementation may make VSBE a read-only field that always specifies the
same endianness as HS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hedeleg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
Register hedeleg is a 64-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in
<<norm:hedeleg_img>>.

normative_rules.name: hideleg_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
Register hideleg is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in
<<norm:hideleg_img>>.

normative_rules.name: hedeleg_op
normative_rules.text:
A synchronous trap that has been delegated to HS-mode (using medeleg)
is further delegated to VS-mode if V=1 before the trap and the
corresponding hedeleg bit is set.

normative_rules.name: hedeleg_acc
normative_rules.text:
Each bit of hedeleg shall be
either writable or read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: hedeleg_bits_required
normative_rules.text:
Many bits of hedeleg are required
specifically to be writable or zero, as enumerated in
<<hedeleg-bits>>.

normative_rules.name: hedeleg_bit0_ialign32
normative_rules.text:
Bit 0, corresponding to
instruction address-misaligned exceptions, must be writable if
IALIGN=32.

normative_rules.name: hedelegh_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: When XLEN=32, hedelegh is a 32-bit read/write register that aliases bits 63:32 of hedeleg. Register hedelegh does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: hideleg_op
normative_rules.text:
An interrupt that has been delegated to HS-mode (using mideleg) is
further delegated to VS-mode if the corresponding hideleg bit is set.

normative_rules.name: hideleg_acc
normative_rules.text:
Among bits 15:0 of hideleg, bits 10, 6, and 2 (corresponding to the
standard VS-level interrupts) are writable, and bits 12, 9, 5, and 1
(corresponding to the standard S-level interrupts) are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: hideleg_trans
normative_rules.text:
When a virtual supervisor external interrupt (code 10) is delegated to
VS-mode, it is automatically translated by the machine into a supervisor
external interrupt (code 9) for VS-mode, including the value written to
vscause on an interrupt trap. Likewise, a virtual supervisor timer
interrupt (6) is translated into a supervisor timer interrupt (5) for
VS-mode, and a virtual supervisor software interrupt (2) is translated
into a supervisor software interrupt (1) for VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hvip_sz_op
normative_rules.text: Register hvip is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register that a hypervisor can write to indicate virtual interrupts intended for VS-mode. Bits of hvip that are not writable are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: hvip_acc
normative_rules.text: The standard portion (bits 15:0) of hvip is formatted as shown in . Bits VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP of hvip are writable. Setting VSEIP=1 in hvip asserts a VS-level external interrupt; setting VSTIP asserts a VS-level timer interrupt; and setting VSSIP asserts a VS-level software interrupt.

normative_rules.name: hip_hie_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
Registers hip and hie are HSXLEN-bit read/write registers that
supplement HS-level’s sip and sie respectively.

normative_rules.name: hip_op
normative_rules.text:
The hip register
indicates pending VS-level and hypervisor-specific interrupts

normative_rules.name: hie_op
normative_rules.text: hie contains enable bits for the same interrupts

normative_rules.name: sie_hip_hie_mutex
normative_rules.text: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit shall be read-only zero in both hip and hie. Hence, the nonzero bits in sie and hie are always mutually exclusive, and likewise for sip and hip.

normative_rules.name: hideleg_hs
normative_rules.text: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode whenever all of the following are true: (a) either the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (b) bit i is set in both sip and sie, or in both hip and hie; and (c) bit i is not set in hideleg.

normative_rules.name: hip_acc
normative_rules.text: If bit i of sie is read-only zero, the same bit in register hip may be writable or may be read-only. When bit i in hip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit. If interrupt i can become pending in hip but bit i in hip is read-only, then either the interrupt can be cleared by clearing bit i of hvip, or the implementation must provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt (which may involve a call to the execution environment).

normative_rules.name: hie_acc
normative_rules.text: A bit in hie shall be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending in hip. Bits of hie that are not writable shall be read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: hip_sgeip_sgeie_acc_op
normative_rules.text: Bits hip.SGEIP and hie.SGEIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for guest external interrupts at supervisor level (HS-level). SGEIP is read-only in hip, and is 1 if and only if the bitwise logical-AND of CSRs hgeip and hgeie is nonzero in any bit. (See .)

normative_rules.name: hip_vseip_vseie_op
normative_rules.text: Bits hip.VSEIP and hie.VSEIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for VS-level external interrupts. VSEIP is read-only in hip, and is the logical-OR of these interrupt sources:

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_vstie_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
Bits csr:hip[vstip] and csr:hie[vstie] are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable
bits for VS-level timer interrupts.

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_acc
normative_rules.text:
csr::[vstip] is read-only in csr:hip[], and is the
logical-OR of csr:hvip[vstip] and, when the ext:sstc[] extension is implemented, the
timer interrupt signal resulting from csr:vstimecmp[].

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_vstimecmp_op
normative_rules.text:
The csr:hip[vstip] bit, in
response to timer interrupts generated by csr:vstimecmp[], is set by writing
csr:vstimecmp[] with a value that is less than or equal to the sum of csr:time[] and
csr:htimedelta[], truncated to qty:64[bits]; it is cleared by writing csr:vstimecmp[] with a
greater value.

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_defined_v0
normative_rules.text: The csr:hip[vstip] bit remains defined while V=0 as well as V=1.

normative_rules.name: hip_vssip_vssie_op
normative_rules.text: Bits hip.VSSIP and hie.VSSIE are the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for VS-level software interrupts. VSSIP in hip is an alias (writable) of the same bit in hvip.

normative_rules.name: hsint_priority
normative_rules.text: Multiple simultaneous interrupts destined for HS-mode are handled in the following decreasing priority order: SEI, SSI, STI, SGEI, VSEI, VSSI, VSTI, LCOFI.

normative_rules.name: hgeip_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The hgeip register is an HSXLEN-bit read-only register, formatted as
shown in <<hgeipreg>>, that indicates pending guest
external interrupts for this hart.

normative_rules.name: hgeie_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The hgeie register is an HSXLEN-bit
read/write register, formatted as shown in
<<norm:hgeie_img>>, that contains enable bits for the
guest external interrupts at this hart.

normative_rules.name: hgeip_hgeie_fields
normative_rules.text:
Guest external interrupt number
i corresponds with bit i in both hgeip and hgeie.

normative_rules.name: hgeip_bit_op
normative_rules.text:
Each bit of hgeip summarizes all pending interrupts
directed to one virtual hart, as collected and reported by an interrupt
controller.

normative_rules.name: geilen
normative_rules.text: The number of bits implemented in hgeip and hgeie for guest external interrupts is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero. This number is known as GEILEN. The least-significant bits are implemented first, apart from bit 0. Hence, if GEILEN is nonzero, bits GEILEN:1 shall be writable in hgeie, and all other bit positions shall be read-only zeros in both hgeip and hgeie.

normative_rules.name: hgeie_op
normative_rules.text: Register hgeie selects the subset of guest external interrupts that cause a supervisor-level (HS-level) guest external interrupt. The enable bits in hgeie do not affect the VS-level external interrupt signal selected from hgeip by hstatus.VGEIN.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The henvcfg CSR is a 64-bit read/write register, formatted as shown in , that controls certain characteristics of the execution environment when virtualization mode V=1.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_fiom_op
normative_rules.text: If bit FIOM (Fence of I/O implies Memory) is set to one in henvcfg, FENCE instructions executed when V=1 are modified so the requirement to order accesses to device I/O implies also the requirement to order main memory accesses.  details the modified interpretation of FENCE instruction bits PI, PO, SI, and SO when FIOM=1 and V=1.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_fiom_order
normative_rules.text: Similarly, when FIOM=1 and V=1, if an atomic instruction that accesses a region ordered as device I/O has its aq and/or rl bit set, then that instruction is ordered as though it accesses both device I/O and memory.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_pbmte_op
normative_rules.text: The PBMTE bit controls whether the Svpbmt extension is available for use in VS-stage address translation. When PBMTE=1, Svpbmt is available for VS-stage address translation. When PBMTE=0, the implementation behaves as though Svpbmt were not implemented for VS-stage address translation. If Svpbmt is not implemented, PBMTE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_adue_op
normative_rules.text: If the Svadu extension is implemented, the ADUE bit controls whether hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled for VS-stage address translation. When ADUE=1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during VS-stage address translation, and the implementation behaves as though the Svade extension were not implemented for VS-mode address translation. When ADUE=0, the implementation behaves as though Svade were implemented for VS-stage address translation. If Svadu is not implemented, ADUE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_stce
normative_rules.text: The Sstc extension adds the STCE (STimecmp Enable) bit to henvcfg CSR.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_stce_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
When
the Sstc extension is not implemented, STCE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_stce_op
normative_rules.text:
The STCE bit
enables vstimecmp for VS-mode when set to one.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_stce_zero_op
normative_rules.text:
When STCE bit in henvcfg is
zero, an attempt to access stimecmp (really vstimecmp) when V=1 raises a
virtual-instruction exception, and VSTIP in hip reverts to its defined behavior
as if this extension is not implemented.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_cbze
normative_rules.text: The Zicboz extension adds the CBZE (Cache Block Zero instruction enable) field to henvcfg. The CBZE field applies to execution of the cache block zero instruction (CBO.ZERO) in privilege modes VS and VU, and only when the instruction is HS-qualified. If the instruction is not HS-qualified, it raises an illegal-instruction exception. If the instruction is HS-qualified and the CBZE field is set to 1, the instruction is enabled for execution; otherwise, if the CBZE field is set to 0, it raises a virtual-instruction exception. When the Zicboz extension is not implemented, CBZE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_cbcfe
normative_rules.text: The Zicbom extension adds the CBCFE (Cache Block Clean and Flush instruction Enable) field to henvcfg. When V=1, if the CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH instructions are not HS-qualified, they raise an illegal-instruction exception. If the instructions are HS-qualified and the CBCFE field is set to 1, the instructions are enabled for execution; otherwise, if the CBCFE field is set to 0, they raise a virtual-instruction exception. When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBCFE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_cbie
normative_rules.text: The Zicbom extension adds the CBIE (Cache Block Invalidate instruction Enable) WARL field to henvcfg. The CBIE field controls execution of the cache block invalidate instruction (CBO.INVAL) in privilege modes VS and VU. The encoding 0b10 is reserved. When the Zicbom extension is not implemented, CBIE is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_h_mode_veq1_op
normative_rules.text: When V=1, if the CBO.INVAL instruction is not HS-qualified, it raises an illegal-instruction exception. If the instruction is HS-qualified and the CBIE field is set to 0b01 or 0b11, the instruction is enabled for execution; otherwise, it raises a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_h_mode_enabled_op
normative_rules.text:
If CBO.INVAL is enabled in HS-mode to perform a flush operation, then when the
instruction is enabled in VS- or VU-mode it performs a flush operation, even if
CBIE is set to 0b11. Otherwise, when the instruction is enabled for
execution, its behavior depends on the CBIE encoding, as follows:

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_h_mode_flush_enc
normative_rules.text:
0b01 -- The instruction is executed and performs a flush operation, even if
configured by VS-mode to perform an invalidate operation.

normative_rules.name: cbo-inval_h_mode_inval_enc
normative_rules.text:
0b11 -- The instruction is executed and performs an invalidate operation,
unless configured by VS-mode to perform a flush operation.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_pmm_op
normative_rules.text: If the Ssnpm extension is implemented, the PMM field enables or disables pointer masking (see ) for VS-mode, according to the values in . When the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field is read-only zero. The PMM field is read-only zero for RV32.

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_lpe_op
normative_rules.text: The Zicfilp extension adds the LPE field in henvcfg. When the LPE field is set to 1, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in VS-mode. When the LPE field is 0, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in VS-mode and the following rules apply to VS-mode:

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_sse_op
normative_rules.text: The Zicfiss extension adds the SSE field in henvcfg. If the SSE field is set to 1, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VS-mode. When the SSE field is 0, the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VS-mode, and the following rules apply when V=1:

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_dte_op
normative_rules.text: The Ssdbltrp extension adds the double-trap-enable (DTE) field in henvcfg. When henvcfg.DTE is zero, the implementation behaves as though Ssdbltrp is not implemented for VS-mode and the vsstatus.SDT bit is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: henvcfgh_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: When XLEN=32, henvcfgh is a 32-bit read/write register that aliases bits 63:32 of henvcfg. Register henvcfgh does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_sz
normative_rules.text: The counter-enable register hcounteren is a 32-bit register that controls the availability of the hardware performance monitoring counters to the guest virtual machine.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_op
normative_rules.text:
When the CY, TM, IR, or HPMn bit in the hcounteren register is
clear, attempts to read the cycle, time, instret, or
hpmcounter n register while V=1 will cause a virtual-instruction
exception if the same bit in mcounteren is 1.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_set_op
normative_rules.text:
When one of these bits
is set, access to the corresponding register is permitted when V=1,
unless prevented for some other reason.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_scounteren_vu_op
normative_rules.text:
In VU-mode, a counter is not
readable unless the applicable bits are set in both hcounteren and
scounteren.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_acc
normative_rules.text: In addition, when the TM bit in the hcounteren register is clear, attempts to access the vstimecmp register (via stimecmp) while executing in VS-mode will cause a virtual-instruction exception if the same bit in mcounteren is set. When this bit and the same bit in mcounteren are both set, access to the vstimecmp register (if implemented) is permitted in VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: hcounteren_warl
normative_rules.text: hcounteren must be implemented. However, any of the bits may be read-only zero, indicating reads to the corresponding counter will cause an exception when V=1. Hence, they are effectively WARL fields.

normative_rules.name: htimedelta_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The htimedelta CSR is a 64-bit read/write register
that contains the delta
between the value of the time CSR and the value returned in VS-mode or
VU-mode. That is, reading the time CSR in VS or VU mode returns the
sum of the contents of htimedelta and the actual value of time.

normative_rules.name: htimedeltah_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: When XLEN=32, htimedeltah is a 32-bit read/write register that aliases bits 63:32 of htimedelta. Register htimedeltah does not exist when XLEN=64.

normative_rules.name: time_htimedelta_req
normative_rules.text: If the time CSR is implemented, htimedelta (and htimedeltah for XLEN=32) must be implemented.

normative_rules.name: htval_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The htval register is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into HS-mode, htval is written with additional exception-specific information, alongside stval, to assist software in handling the trap.

normative_rules.name: htval_trapval
normative_rules.text: When a guest-page-fault trap is taken into HS-mode, csr:htval[] is written with either zero or the guest physical address that faulted, shifted right by qty:2[bits]. For other traps, csr:htval[] is set to zero, but a future standard or extension may redefine csr:htval[]'s setting for other traps.

normative_rules.name: htval_val
normative_rules.text: htval is a WARL register that must be able to hold zero and may be capable of holding only an arbitrary subset of other 2-bit-shifted guest physical addresses, if any.

normative_rules.name: htinst_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The htinst register is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into HS-mode, htinst is written with a value that, if nonzero, provides information about the instruction that trapped, to assist software in handling the trap. The values that may be written to htinst on a trap are documented in .

normative_rules.name: htinst_val
normative_rules.text: htinst is a WARL register that need only be able to hold the values that the implementation may automatically write to it on a trap.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The hgatp register is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register, formatted as
shown in <<rv32hgatp>> for HSXLEN=32 and
<<rv64hgatp>> for HSXLEN=64, which controls
G-stage address translation and protection, the second stage of
two-stage translation for guest virtual addresses (see
<<two-stage-translation>>).

normative_rules.name: hgatp_tvm_illegal
normative_rules.text:
When mstatus.TVM=1, attempts to read or write hgatp while
executing in HS-mode will raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_bare
normative_rules.text:
<<hgatp-mode>> shows the encodings of the MODE field when
HSXLEN=32 and HSXLEN=64. When MODE=Bare, guest physical addresses are
equal to supervisor physical addresses, and there is no further memory
protection for a guest virtual machine beyond the physical memory
protection scheme described in <<pmp>>. In this
case, software must write zero to the remaining fields in hgatp.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_Sv
normative_rules.text: When HSXLEN=32, the only other valid setting for MODE is Sv32x4, which is a modification of the usual Sv32 paged virtual-memory scheme, extended to support 34-bit guest physical addresses. When HSXLEN=64, modes Sv39x4, Sv48x4, and Sv57x4 are defined as modifications of the Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57 paged virtual-memory schemes. All of these paged virtual-memory schemes are described in .

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_warl
normative_rules.text: A write to hgatp with an unsupported MODE value is not ignored as it is for satp. Instead, the fields of hgatp are WARL in the normal way, when so indicated.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_root_pt_sz_align
normative_rules.text:
As explained in <<guest-addr-translation>>, for the
paged virtual-memory schemes (Sv32x4, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, and Sv57x4), the
root page table is 16 KiB and must be aligned to a 16-KiB boundary.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_ppn_op
normative_rules.text:
In
these modes, the lowest two bits of the physical page number (PPN) in
hgatp always read as zeros.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_ppn_acc
normative_rules.text:
An implementation that supports only the
defined paged virtual-memory schemes and/or Bare may make PPN[1:0]
read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_vmid
normative_rules.text: The number of VMID bits is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_vmid_lsbs
normative_rules.text:
The
least-significant bits of VMID are implemented first: that is, if
VMIDLEN > 0, VMID[VMIDLEN-1:0] is writable. The maximal
value of VMIDLEN, termed VMIDMAX, is 7 for Sv32x4 or 14 for Sv39x4,
Sv48x4, and Sv57x4.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_op_hfence_gvma
normative_rules.text:
Note that writing hgatp does not imply any ordering constraints
between page-table updates and subsequent G-stage address translations.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vsstatus register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register sstatus, formatted as shown in  when VSXLEN=32 and  when VSXLEN=64. When V=1, vsstatus substitutes for the usual sstatus, so instructions that normally read or modify sstatus actually access vsstatus instead.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_uxl_op
normative_rules.text: The UXL field controls the effective XLEN for VU-mode, which may differ from the XLEN for VS-mode (VSXLEN). When VSXLEN=32, the UXL field does not exist, and VU-mode XLEN=32. When VSXLEN=64, UXL is a WARL field that is encoded the same as the MXL field of misa, shown in . In particular, an implementation may make UXL be a read-only copy of field VSXL of hstatus, forcing VU-mode XLEN=VSXLEN.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_uxl_change
normative_rules.text: If VSXLEN is changed from 32 to a wider width, and if field UXL is not restricted to a single value, it gets the value corresponding to the widest supported width not wider than the new VSXLEN.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_fs_op
normative_rules.text: When V=1, both vsstatus.FS and the HS-level sstatus.FS are in effect. Attempts to execute a floating-point instruction when either field is 0 (Off) raise an illegal-instruction exception. Modifying the floating-point state when V=1 causes both fields to be set to 3 (Dirty).

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_vs_op
normative_rules.text: Similarly, when V=1, both vsstatus.VS and the HS-level sstatus.VS are in effect. Attempts to execute a vector instruction when either field is 0 (Off) raise an illegal-instruction exception. Modifying the vector state when V=1 causes both fields to be set to 3 (Dirty).

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sd_xs_op
normative_rules.text: Read-only fields SD and XS summarize the extension context status as it is visible to VS-mode only. For example, the value of the HS-level sstatus.FS does not affect vsstatus.SD.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_ube
normative_rules.text: An implementation may make field UBE be a read-only copy of hstatus.VSBE.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_v0
normative_rules.text: When V=0, vsstatus does not directly affect the behavior of the machine, unless a virtual-machine load/store (HLV, HLVX, or HSV) or the MPRV feature in the mstatus register is used to execute a load or store as though V=1.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_spelp_op
normative_rules.text: The Zicfilp extension adds the SPELP field that holds the previous ELP, and is updated as specified in . The SPELP field is encoded as follows:

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sdt_op
normative_rules.text: The Ssdbltrp adds an S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) field extension to address double trap (See ) in VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: vsip_vsie_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vsip and vsie registers are VSXLEN-bit read/write registers that are VS-mode’s versions of supervisor CSRs sip and sie, formatted as shown in  and  respectively. When V=1, vsip and vsie substitute for the usual sip and sie, so instructions that normally read or modify sip/sie actually access vsip/vsie instead. However, interrupts directed to HS-level continue to be indicated in the HS-level sip register, not in vsip, when V=1.

normative_rules.name: vsip_vsie_lcofi
normative_rules.text: Extension Shlcofideleg supports delegating LCOFI interrupts to VS-mode. If the Shlcofideleg extension is implemented, hideleg bit 13 is writable; otherwise, it is read-only zero. When bit 13 of hideleg is zero, vsip.LCOFIP and vsie.LCOFIE are read-only zeros. Else, vsip.LCOFIP and vsie.LCOFIE are aliases of sip.LCOFIP and sie.LCOFIE.

normative_rules.name: vsip_vsie_sei
normative_rules.text: When bit 10 of hideleg is zero, vsip.SEIP and vsie.SEIE are read-only zeros. Else, vsip.SEIP and vsie.SEIE are aliases of hip.VSEIP and hie.VSEIE.

normative_rules.name: vsip_vsie_sti
normative_rules.text: When bit 6 of hideleg is zero, vsip.STIP and vsie.STIE are read-only zeros. Else, vsip.STIP and vsie.STIE are aliases of hip.VSTIP and hie.VSTIE.

normative_rules.name: vsip_vsie_ssi
normative_rules.text: When bit 2 of hideleg is zero, vsip.SSIP and vsie.SSIE are read-only zeros. Else, vsip.SSIP and vsie.SSIE are aliases of hip.VSSIP and hie.VSSIE.

normative_rules.name: vstvec_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vstvec register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register stvec, formatted as shown in . When V=1, vstvec substitutes for the usual stvec, so instructions that normally read or modify stvec actually access vstvec instead. When V=0, vstvec does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.

normative_rules.name: vsscratch_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vsscratch register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register sscratch, formatted as shown in . When V=1, vsscratch substitutes for the usual sscratch, so instructions that normally read or modify sscratch actually access vsscratch instead. The contents of vsscratch never directly affect the behavior of the machine.

normative_rules.name: vsepc_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vsepc register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register sepc, formatted as shown in . When V=1, vsepc substitutes for the usual sepc, so instructions that normally read or modify sepc actually access vsepc instead. When V=0, vsepc does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.

normative_rules.name: vsepc_warl
normative_rules.text: vsepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold the same set of values that sepc can hold, with VSXLEN substituting for SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: vscause_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vscause register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register scause, formatted as shown in . When V=1, vscause substitutes for the usual scause, so instructions that normally read or modify scause actually access vscause instead. When V=0, vscause does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.

normative_rules.name: vscause_wlrl
normative_rules.text: vscause is a WLRL register that must be able to hold the same set of values that scause can hold, with VSXLEN substituting for SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: vstval_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vstval register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register stval, formatted as shown in . When V=1, vstval substitutes for the usual stval, so instructions that normally read or modify stval actually access vstval instead. When V=0, vstval does not directly affect the behavior of the machine.

normative_rules.name: vstval_warl
normative_rules.text: vstval is a WARL register that must be able to hold the same set of values that stval can hold, with VSXLEN substituting for SXLEN.

normative_rules.name: vsatp_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The vsatp register is a VSXLEN-bit read/write register that is VS-mode’s version of supervisor register satp, formatted as shown in  for VSXLEN=32 and  for VSXLEN=64. When V=1, vsatp substitutes for the usual satp, so instructions that normally read or modify satp actually access vsatp instead. vsatp controls VS-stage address translation, the first stage of two-stage translation for guest virtual addresses (see ).

normative_rules.name: vs_stage_speculative_a_bit
normative_rules.text:
when vsatp is active, VS-stage
page-table entries’ A bits must not be set as a result of speculative
execution, unless the effective privilege mode is VS or VU.

normative_rules.name: vsatp_mode_unsupported_v0
normative_rules.text:
When V=0, a write to vsatp with an unsupported MODE value is either
ignored as it is for satp, or the fields of vsatp are treated as WARL in
the normal way.

normative_rules.name: vsatp_mode_unsupported_v1
normative_rules.text:
However, when V=1, a write to satp with an unsupported
MODE value is ignored and no write to vsatp is effected.

normative_rules.name: vsatp_asidlen
normative_rules.text:
The ASID field in the vsatp register has the same number of implemented bits
as that of the satp register, i.e., it is ASIDLEN bits wide.

normative_rules.name: vsatp_v0
normative_rules.text: When V=0, vsatp does not directly affect the behavior of the machine, unless a virtual-machine load/store (HLV, HLVX, or HSV) or the MPRV feature in the mstatus register is used to execute a load or store as though V=1.

normative_rules.name: vstimecmp_sz
normative_rules.text:
The csr:vstimecmp[] CSR is a 64-bit register and has 64-bit precision on all RV32
and RV64 systems.

normative_rules.name: vstimecmp_acc
normative_rules.text:
In RV32 only, accesses to the csr:vstimecmp[] CSR access the low
qty:32[bits], while accesses to the csr:vstimecmph[] CSR access the high qty:32[bits] of
csr:vstimecmp[].

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_op
normative_rules.text:
A virtual supervisor timer interrupt becomes pending, as reflected in the
csr::[vstip] bit in the csr:hip[] register, whenever (csr:time[] + csr:htimedelta[]), truncated
to qty:64[bits], contains a value greater than or equal to csr:vstimecmp[], treating
the values as unsigned integers.

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_clear
normative_rules.text:
If the result of this comparison changes, it is guaranteed to be reflected in
csr::[vstip] eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
The interrupt remains posted until csr:vstimecmp[] becomes greater than (csr:time[] + csr:htimedelta[]),
typically as a result of writing csr:vstimecmp[].

normative_rules.name: hip_vstip_enable
normative_rules.text:
The interrupt will be taken based on the standard interrupt enable and
delegation rules while V=1.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_mode
normative_rules.text:
The hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions are valid
only in M-mode or HS-mode, or in U-mode when hstatus.HU=1.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_priv
normative_rules.text:
Each
instruction performs an explicit memory access with an effective privilege mode
of VS or VU. The effective privilege mode of the explicit memory access is VU
when hstatus.SPVP=0, and VS when hstatus.SPVP=1.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_trans
normative_rules.text:
As usual for VS-mode and
VU-mode, two-stage address translation is applied, and
the HS-level sstatus.SUM is ignored.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_sstatus_mxr
normative_rules.text:
HS-level sstatus.MXR makes
execute-only pages readable by explicit loads for both stages of address translation
(VS-stage and G-stage)

normative_rules.name: hlsv_vsstatus_mxr
normative_rules.text:
vsstatus.MXR affects only the first
translation stage (VS-stage).

normative_rules.name: hlsv_op
normative_rules.text: For every RV32I or RV64I load instruction, LB, LBU, LH, LHU, LW, LWU, and LD, there is a corresponding virtual-machine load instruction: HLV.B, HLV.BU, HLV.H, HLV.HU, HLV.W, HLV.WU, and HLV.D. For every RV32I or RV64I store instruction, SB, SH, SW, and SD, there is a corresponding virtual-machine store instruction: HSV.B, HSV.H, HSV.W, and HSV.D. Instructions HLV.WU, HLV.D, and HSV.D are not valid for RV32, of course.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_u_op
normative_rules.text: Instructions HLVX.HU and HLVX.WU are the same as HLV.HU and HLV.WU, except that execute permission takes the place of read permission during address translation. That is, the memory being read must be executable in both stages of address translation, but read permission is not required. For the supervisor physical address that results from address translation, the supervisor physical memory attributes must grant both execute and read permissions. (The supervisor physical memory attributes are the machine’s physical memory attributes as modified by physical memory protection, , for supervisor level.)

normative_rules.name: hlvx-wu_valid32
normative_rules.text: HLVX.WU is valid for RV32, even though LWU and HLV.WU are not.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_virtinst
normative_rules.text:
Attempts to execute a virtual-machine load/store instruction (HLV, HLVX,
or HSV) when V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hlsv_illegalinst
normative_rules.text:
Attempts to execute one of these same instructions from U-mode when hstatus.HU=0 cause an
illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_hfence-gvma_op
normative_rules.text: The hypervisor memory-management fence instructions, HFENCE.VVMA and HFENCE.GVMA, perform a function similar to SFENCE.VMA (), except applying to the VS-level memory-management data structures controlled by CSR vsatp (HFENCE.VVMA) or the guest-physical memory-management data structures controlled by CSR hgatp (HFENCE.GVMA). Instruction SFENCE.VMA applies only to the memory-management data structures controlled by the current satp (either the HS-level satp when V=0 or vsatp when V=1).

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_mode
normative_rules.text: HFENCE.VVMA is valid only in M-mode or HS-mode. Its effect is much the same as temporarily entering VS-mode and executing SFENCE.VMA. Executing an HFENCE.VVMA guarantees that any previous stores already visible to the current hart are ordered before all implicit reads by that hart done for VS-stage address translation for instructions that

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_limits
normative_rules.text: Implicit reads need not be ordered when hgatp.VMID is different than at the time HFENCE.VVMA executed. If operand rs1≠x0, it specifies a single guest virtual address, and if operand rs2≠x0, it specifies a single guest address-space identifier (ASID).

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_asid
normative_rules.text: When rs2≠x0, bits XLEN-1:ASIDMAX of the value held in rs2 are reserved for future standard use. Until their use is defined by a standard extension, they should be zeroed by software and ignored by current implementations. Furthermore, if ASIDLEN < ASIDMAX, the implementation shall ignore bits ASIDMAX-1:ASIDLEN of the value held in rs2.

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_tvm
normative_rules.text: Neither mstatus.TVM nor hstatus.VTVM causes HFENCE.VVMA to trap.

normative_rules.name: hfence-gvma_op
normative_rules.text: insn:hfence.gvma[] is valid only in HS-mode when csr:mstatus[tvm]=0, or in M-mode (irrespective of csr:mstatus[tvm]). Executing an insn:hfence.gvma[] instruction guarantees that any previous stores already visible to the current hart are ordered before all implicit reads by that hart done for G-stage address translation for instructions that follow the insn:hfence.gvma[]. If operand rs1≠x0, it specifies a single guest physical address, shifted right by qty:2[bits], and if operand rs2≠x0, it specifies a single virtual machine identifier (VMID).

normative_rules.name: hfence-gvma_vmid
normative_rules.text: When rs2≠x0, bits XLEN-1:VMIDMAX of the value held in rs2 are reserved for future standard use. Until their use is defined by a standard extension, they should be zeroed by software and ignored by current implementations. Furthermore, if VMIDLEN < VMIDMAX, the implementation shall ignore bits VMIDMAX-1:VMIDLEN of the value held in rs2.

normative_rules.name: hfence-gvma_mode
normative_rules.text: If hgatp.MODE is changed for a given VMID, an HFENCE.GVMA with rs1=x0 (and rs2 set to either x0 or the VMID) must be executed to order subsequent guest translations with the MODE change—even if the old MODE or new MODE is Bare.

normative_rules.name: hfence-vvma_hfence-gvma_exceptions
normative_rules.text: Attempts to execute HFENCE.VVMA or HFENCE.GVMA when V=1 cause a virtual-instruction exception, while attempts to do the same in U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception. Attempting to execute HFENCE.GVMA in HS-mode when mstatus.TVM=1 also causes an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mpv_op
normative_rules.text: The MPV bit (Machine Previous Virtualization Mode) is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into M-mode. Just as the MPP field is set to the (nominal) privilege mode at the time of the trap, the MPV bit is set to the value of the virtualization mode V at the time of the trap. When an MRET instruction is executed, the virtualization mode V is set to MPV, unless MPP=3, in which case V remains 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_gva_op
normative_rules.text: Field GVA (Guest Virtual Address) is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into M-mode. For any trap (breakpoint, address misaligned, access fault, page fault, or guest-page fault) that writes a guest virtual address to mtval, GVA is set to 1. For any other trap into M-mode, GVA is set to 0.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_modes
normative_rules.text: The TSR and TVM fields of mstatus affect execution only in HS-mode, not in VS-mode. The TW field affects execution in all modes except M-mode.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_tvm_hs
normative_rules.text: Setting TVM=1 prevents HS-mode from accessing hgatp or executing HFENCE.GVMA or HINVAL.GVMA, but has no effect on accesses to vsatp or instructions HFENCE.VVMA or HINVAL.VVMA.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_hypervisor
normative_rules.text: The hypervisor extension changes the behavior of the Modify Privilege field, MPRV, of mstatus. When MPRV=0, translation and protection behave as normal. When MPRV=1, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected, and endianness is applied, as though the current virtualization mode were set to MPV and the current nominal privilege mode were set to MPP.  enumerates the cases.

normative_rules.name: mstatus_mprv_hlsv
normative_rules.text: MPRV does not affect the virtual-machine load/store instructions, HLV, HLVX, and HSV. The explicit loads and stores of these instructions always act as though V=1 and the nominal privilege mode were hstatus.SPVP, overriding MPRV.

normative_rules.name: mideleg_acc_H
normative_rules.text: When the hypervisor extension is implemented, bits 10, 6, and 2 of mideleg (corresponding to the standard VS-level interrupts) are each read-only one. Furthermore, if any guest external interrupts are implemented (GEILEN is nonzero), bit 12 of mideleg (corresponding to supervisor-level guest external interrupts) is also read-only one. VS-level interrupts and guest external interrupts are always delegated past M-mode to HS-mode.

normative_rules.name: mideleg_hroz
normative_rules.text: For bits of mideleg that are zero, the corresponding bits in hideleg, hip, and hie are read-only zeros.

normative_rules.name: mip_mie_vs
normative_rules.text: The hypervisor extension gives registers mip and mie additional active bits for the hypervisor-added interrupts.  and  show the standard portions (bits 15:0) of registers mip and mie when the hypervisor extension is implemented.

normative_rules.name: mip_mie_alias
normative_rules.text: Bits SGEIP, VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP in mip are aliases for the same bits in hypervisor CSR hip, while SGEIE, VSEIE, VSTIE, and VSSIE in mie are aliases for the same bits in hie.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The mtval2 register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into M-mode, mtval2 is written with additional exception-specific information, alongside mtval, to assist software in handling the trap.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_trapval
normative_rules.text: When a guest-page-fault trap is taken into M-mode, csr:mtval2[] is written with either zero or the guest physical address that faulted, shifted right by qty:2[bits]. For other traps, csr:mtval2[] is set to zero, but a future standard or extension may redefine csr:mtval2[]'s setting for other traps.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_trapval_vstrans
normative_rules.text: If a guest-page fault is due to an implicit memory access during first-stage (VS-stage) address translation, a guest physical address written to mtval2 is that of the implicit memory access that faulted. Additional information is provided in CSR mtinst to disambiguate such situations.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_trapval_other
normative_rules.text: Otherwise, for misaligned loads and stores that cause guest-page faults, a nonzero guest physical address in mtval2 corresponds to the faulting portion of the access as indicated by the virtual address in mtval. For instruction guest-page faults on systems with variable-length instructions, a nonzero mtval2 corresponds to the faulting portion of the instruction as indicated by the virtual address in mtval.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_val
normative_rules.text: mtval2 is a WARL register that must be able to hold zero and may be capable of holding only an arbitrary subset of other 2-bit-shifted guest physical addresses, if any.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_Ssdbltrp
normative_rules.text: The Ssdbltrp extension (See ) requires the implementation of the mtval2 CSR.

normative_rules.name: mtinst_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The mtinst register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register formatted as shown in . When a trap is taken into M-mode, mtinst is written with a value that, if nonzero, provides information about the instruction that trapped, to assist software in handling the trap. The values that may be written to mtinst on a trap are documented in .

normative_rules.name: mtinst_val
normative_rules.text: mtinst is a WARL register that need only be able to hold the values that the implementation may automatically write to it on a trap.

normative_rules.name: H_vm_twostage
normative_rules.text:
Whenever the current virtualization mode V is 1, two-stage address
translation and protection is in effect. For any virtual memory access,
the original virtual address is converted in the first stage by VS-level
address translation, as controlled by the vsatp register, into a
guest physical address. The guest physical address is then converted
in the second stage by guest physical address translation, as controlled
by the hgatp register, into a supervisor physical address. The two
stages are known also as VS-stage and G-stage translation.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_mxr_vm
normative_rules.text:
The vsstatus field MXR, which makes execute-only pages readable by explicit loads, only
overrides VS-stage page protection. Setting MXR at VS-level does not
override guest-physical page protections.

normative_rules.name: sstatus_mxr_vm
normative_rules.text:
Setting MXR at HS-level,
however, overrides both VS-stage and G-stage execute-only permissions.

normative_rules.name: H_vm_gstagetrans
normative_rules.text: When V=1, memory accesses that would normally bypass address translation are subject to G-stage address translation alone. This includes memory accesses made in support of VS-stage address translation, such as reads and writes of VS-level page tables.

normative_rules.name: H_pmp
normative_rules.text: Machine-level physical memory protection applies to supervisor physical addresses and is in effect regardless of virtualization mode.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_bare_trans
normative_rules.text: When the address translation scheme selected by the MODE field of hgatp is Bare, guest physical addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses without modification, and no memory protection applies in the trivial translation of guest physical addresses to supervisor physical addresses.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_x4
normative_rules.text: When csr:hgatp[mode] specifies a translation scheme of Sv32x4, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, or Sv57x4, G-stage address translation is a variation on the usual page-based virtual address translation scheme of Sv32, Sv39, Sv48, or Sv57, respectively. In each case, the size of the incoming address is widened by qty:2[bits] (to 34, 41, 50, or qty:59[bits]). To accommodate the two extra bits, the root page table (only) is expanded by a factor of 4 to be qty:16[KiB] instead of the usual qty:4[KiB]. Matching its larger size, the root page table also must be aligned to a qty:16[KiB] boundary instead of the usual qty:4[KiB] page boundary. Except as noted, all other aspects of Sv32, Sv39, Sv48, or Sv57 are adopted unchanged for G-stage translation. Non-root page tables and all page table entries (PTEs) have the same formats as documented in , , , and .

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_sv32x4
normative_rules.text: For Sv32x4, an incoming guest physical address is partitioned into a virtual page number (VPN) and page offset as shown in . This partitioning is identical to that for an Sv32 virtual address as depicted in , except with two more bits at the high end in VPN[1]. (Note that the fields of a partitioned guest physical address also correspond one-for-one with the structure that Sv32 assigns to a physical address, depicted in .)

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_sv39x4
normative_rules.text: For Sv39x4, an incoming guest physical address is partitioned as shown in . This partitioning is identical to that for an Sv39 virtual address as depicted in , except with 2 more bits at the high end in VPN[2]. Address bits 63:41 must all be zeros, or else a guest-page-fault exception occurs.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_sv48x4
normative_rules.text: For Sv48x4, an incoming guest physical address is partitioned as shown in . This partitioning is identical to that for an Sv48 virtual address as depicted in , except with 2 more bits at the high end in VPN[3]. Address bits 63:50 must all be zeros, or else a guest-page-fault exception occurs.

normative_rules.name: hgatp_mode_Sv57x4
normative_rules.text: For Sv57x4, an incoming guest physical address is partitioned as shown in . This partitioning is identical to that for an Sv57 virtual address as depicted in , except with 2 more bits at the high end in VPN[4]. Address bits 63:59 must all be zeros, or else a guest-page-fault exception occurs.

normative_rules.name: H_vm_gpatrans
normative_rules.text: The conversion of an Sv32x4, Sv39x4, Sv48x4, or Sv57x4 guest physical address is accomplished with the same algorithm used for Sv32, Sv39, Sv48, or Sv57, as presented in , except that:

normative_rules.name: H_vm_gpapriv
normative_rules.text: For G-stage address translation, all memory accesses (including those made to access data structures for VS-stage address translation) are considered to be user-level accesses, as though executed in U-mode. Access type permissions—readable, writable, or executable—are checked during G-stage translation the same as for VS-stage translation. For a memory access made to support VS-stage address translation (such as to read/write a VS-level page table), permissions and the need to set A and/or D bits at the G-stage level are checked as though for an implicit load or store, not for the original access type. However, any exception is always reported for the original access type (instruction, load, or store/AMO).

normative_rules.name: H_vm_gpa_g
normative_rules.text: The G bit in all G-stage PTEs is currently not used. Until its use is defined by a standard extension, it should be cleared by software for forward compatibility, and must be ignored by hardware.

normative_rules.name: H_guest_page_fault
normative_rules.text: Guest-page-fault traps may be delegated from M-mode to HS-mode under the control of CSR csr:medeleg[], but cannot be delegated to other privilege modes. On a guest-page fault, CSR csr:mtval[] or csr:stval[] is written with the faulting guest virtual address as usual, and csr:mtval2[] or csr:htval[] is written either with zero or with the faulting guest physical address, shifted right by qty:2[bits]. CSR csr:mtinst[] or csr:htinst[] may also be written with information about the faulting instruction or other reason for the access, as explained in .

normative_rules.name: H_straddle
normative_rules.text: When an instruction fetch or a misaligned memory access straddles a page boundary, two different address translations are involved. When a guest-page fault occurs in such a circumstance, the faulting virtual address written to mtval/stval is the same as would be required for a regular page fault. Thus, the faulting virtual address may be a page-boundary address that is higher than the instruction’s original virtual address, if the byte at that page boundary is among the accessed bytes.

normative_rules.name: mtval2_htval_virtaddr
normative_rules.text: When a guest-page fault is not due to an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation, a nonzero guest physical address written to mtval2/htval shall correspond to the exact virtual address written to mtval/stval.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_v0
normative_rules.text: The behavior of the SFENCE.VMA instruction is affected by the current virtualization mode V. When V=0, the virtual-address argument is an HS-level virtual address, and the ASID argument is an HS-level ASID. The instruction orders stores only to HS-level address-translation structures with subsequent HS-level address translations.

normative_rules.name: sfence_vma_v1
