normative_rules.name: mcyclecfg_sz
normative_rules.text: csr:mcyclecfg[] and csr:minstretcfg[] are 64-bit registers

normative_rules.name: mcyclecfg_op
normative_rules.text: configure privilege mode filtering for the csr:cycle[] and csr:instret[] counters, respectively.

normative_rules.name: rv32_high_access
normative_rules.text: In RV32 only, accesses to the csr:mcyclecfg[] and csr:minstretcfg[] CSRs access the low 32 bits, while accesses to the csr:mcyclecfgh[] and csr:minstretcfgh[] CSRs access the high 32 bits of csr:mcyclecfg[] and csr:minstretcfg[], respectively.

normative_rules.name: all_xinh_zero
normative_rules.text: When all xINH bits are zero, event counting is enabled in all modes.

normative_rules.name: unimplemented_mode_bits
normative_rules.text: For each bit in 61:58, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: csr_supervisor_access
normative_rules.text: The content of these registers may be accessible from Supervisor level if the Smcdeleg/Ssccfg extensions are implemented.

normative_rules.name: counter_inhibited_behavior
normative_rules.text: The fundamental behavior of csr:cycle[] and csr:instret[] is modified in that counting does not occur while executing in an inhibited privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: cycle_counting
normative_rules.text: The csr:cycle[] counter will simply count CPU cycles while the CPU is in a non-inhibited privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: instret_non_inhibited
normative_rules.text: instructions that retire in a non-inhibited mode increment csr:instret[], and instructions that retire in an inhibited mode do not.

normative_rules.name: instret_exception
normative_rules.text: The former are not considered to retire, and hence do not increment csr:instret[].

normative_rules.name: instret_xret
normative_rules.text: The latter do retire, and should increment csr:instret[] only if the originating privilege mode is not inhibited.

normative_rules.name: Smrnmi_csrs
normative_rules.text:
The extension adds four new CSRs (mnepc, mncause,
mnstatus, and mnscratch) to hold the interrupted state

normative_rules.name: mnret_exist
normative_rules.text:
one new
instruction, MNRET, to resume from the RNMI handler.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_priority
normative_rules.text:
These interrupts
have higher priority than any other interrupt or exception on the hart

normative_rules.name: rnmi_not_disabled
normative_rules.text:
cannot be disabled by software. Specifically, they are not disabled
by clearing the mstatus.MIE register.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_trap_addr
normative_rules.text: The RNMI interrupt trap handler address is implementation-defined.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_exc_trap_addr
normative_rules.text:
RNMI also has an associated exception trap handler address, which is
implementation defined.

normative_rules.name: mnscratch_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The mnscratch CSR holds an MXLEN-bit read-write register which enables
the RNMI trap handler to save and restore the context that was
interrupted.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text:
The mnepc CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-write register which on entry to
the RNMI trap handler holds the PC of the instruction that took the
interrupt.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_bit0
normative_rules.text: The low bit of mnepc (mnepc[0]) is always zero.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_ialign32
normative_rules.text:
On implementations
that support only IALIGN=32, the two low bits (mnepc[1:0]) are always
zero.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_ialign_mask
normative_rules.text:
If an implementation allows IALIGN to be either 16 or 32 (by changing
CSR misa, for example), then, whenever IALIGN=32, bit mnepc[1] is
masked on reads so that it appears to be 0.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_bit1_writable
normative_rules.text:
Though masked, mnepc[1]
remains writable when IALIGN=32.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_warl
normative_rules.text:
mnepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual
addresses.

normative_rules.name: mnepc_invalid_convert
normative_rules.text:
Prior to writing mnepc, implementations may convert an
invalid address into some other invalid address that mnepc is capable
of holding.

normative_rules.name: mncause_op
normative_rules.text: The mncause CSR holds the reason for the RNMI.

normative_rules.name: mncause_interrupt
normative_rules.text: If the reason is an interrupt, bit MXLEN-1 is set to 1,

normative_rules.name: mncause_interrupt_code
normative_rules.text:
the RNMI
cause is encoded in the least-significant bits.

normative_rules.name: mncause_interrupt_zero
normative_rules.text:
If the reason is an interrupt and RNMI causes are not supported, bit MXLEN-1 is
set to 1, and zero is written to the least-significant bits.

normative_rules.name: mncause_doubletrap
normative_rules.text:
If the reason is an exception within M-mode that results in a double trap as
specified in the Smdbltrp extension, bit MXLEN-1 is set to 0 and the
least-significant bits are set to the cause code corresponding to the
exception that precipitated the double trap.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_mnpp_op
normative_rules.text:
The mnstatus CSR holds a two-bit field, MNPP, which on entry to the
RNMI trap handler holds the privilege mode of the interrupted context,
encoded in the same manner as mstatus.MPP.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_mnpv_op
normative_rules.text:
If the H extension is also
implemented, mnstatus also holds a one-bit
field, MNPV, which on entry to the RNMI trap handler holds the virtualization
mode of the interrupted context, encoded in the same manner as
mstatus.MPV.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_mnpelp_op
normative_rules.text:
If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, mnstatus also holds the MNPELP
field, which on entry to the RNMI trap handler holds the previous ELP state.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_mnpelp_update
normative_rules.text: When an RNMI trap is taken, MNPELP is set to ELP and ELP is set to 0.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_nmie_enable
normative_rules.text:
When NMIE=1, non-maskable interrupts
are enabled.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_nmie_disable
normative_rules.text: When NMIE=0, all interrupts are disabled.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_mprv_clear
normative_rules.text:
When NMIE=0, the hart behaves as though mstatus.MPRV were clear,
regardless of the current setting of mstatus.MPRV.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_nmie_reset
normative_rules.text: Upon reset, NMIE contains the value 0.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_nmie_set_clear
normative_rules.text: Software can set NMIE to 1, but attempts to clear NMIE have no effect.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_wfi
normative_rules.text:
For the purposes of the WFI instruction, NMIE is a global
interrupt enable, meaning that the setting of NMIE does not affect which
interrupts are locally enabled.
Furthermore, RNMIs are always considered to be locally enabled; hence, WFI is
required to resume execution if an RNMI becomes pending when NMIE=0,
or to take the interrupt if an RNMI becomes pending when NMIE=1.

normative_rules.name: mnstatus_reserved
normative_rules.text:
The other bits in mnstatus are reserved; software should write zeros
and hardware implementations should return zeros.

normative_rules.name: mnret_mode
normative_rules.text: MNRET is an M-mode-only instruction

normative_rules.name: mnret_restore
normative_rules.text:
This instruction also
sets mnstatus.NMIE.

normative_rules.name: mnret_mprv
normative_rules.text: If MNRET changes the privilege mode to a mode less privileged than M, it also sets mstatus.MPRV to 0.

normative_rules.name: mnret_Zicfilp
normative_rules.text:
If the Zicfilp extension is implemented, then if the new privileged mode
is y, MNRET sets ELP to the logical AND of yLPE (see <<FCFIACT>>) and mnstatus.MNPELP.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_entry
normative_rules.text:
When an RNMI interrupt is detected, the interrupted PC is written to the
mnepc CSR,

normative_rules.name: rnmi_entry_cause
normative_rules.text: the type of RNMI to the mncause CSR,

normative_rules.name: rnmi_entry_priv
normative_rules.text:
the privilege
mode of the interrupted context to the mnstatus CSR.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_entry_nmie_clear
normative_rules.text:
The
mnstatus.NMIE bit is cleared, masking all interrupts.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_enter_mmode
normative_rules.text:
The hart then enters machine-mode and jumps to the RNMI trap handler
address.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_resume
normative_rules.text:
The RNMI handler can resume original execution using the new MNRET
instruction, which restores the PC from mnepc, the privilege mode from
mnstatus, and also sets mnstatus.NMIE, which re-enables interrupts.

normative_rules.name: rnmi_exception_nmie0
normative_rules.text: When the Smdbltrp extension is not implemented, if the hart encounters an exception while executing in M-mode with the mnstatus.NMIE bit clear, the actions taken are the same as if the exception had occurred while mnstatus.NMIE were set, except that the program counter is set to the RNMI exception trap handler address.

normative_rules.name: Smcdeleg_Ssccfg_tandem
normative_rules.text: For a RISC-V hardware platform, Smcdeleg and Ssccfg must always be implemented in tandem.

normative_rules.name: Smcdeleg_cde_en
normative_rules.text: When the Smcdeleg/Ssccfg extensions are enabled (menvcfg.CDE=1), it further allows M-mode to delegate select counters to S-mode.

normative_rules.name: Smcdeleg_delegated_access
normative_rules.text:
The siselect (and vsiselect) index range 0x40-0x5F is reserved for
delegated counter access. When a counter i is delegated
(mcounteren[i]=1 and menvcfg.CDE=1) and siselect is
0x40+i, sireg* aliases counter i.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_sireg_cde0
normative_rules.text: attempts to access any sireg* when menvcfg.CDE = 0;

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_sireg3_6
normative_rules.text: attempts to access sireg3 or sireg6;

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_sireg4_5_xlen64
normative_rules.text: attempts to access sireg4 or sireg5 when XLEN = 64;

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_sireg_not_delegated
normative_rules.text:
attempts to access sireg* when siselect = 0x41, or when the counter
selected by siselect is not delegated to S-mode (the corresponding bit
in mcounteren = 0).

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_missing_extension_illegal
normative_rules.text: If any extension upon which the underlying state depends is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access the given state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_hyp_vs_or_vu_access_vsireg_illegal
normative_rules.text: If the hypervisor (H) extension is also implemented, then as specified by extensions Smcsrind/Sscsrind, a virtual-instruction exception is raised for attempts from VS-mode or VU-mode to directly access vsiselect or vsireg*, or attempts from VU-mode to access siselect or sireg*. Furthermore, while vsiselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F:

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_hyp_m_s_vsireg_illegal
normative_rules.text: An attempt to access any vsireg* from M or S mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_hyp_vs_access_sireg_conditional
normative_rules.text: An attempt from VS-mode to access any sireg* (really vsireg*) raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 0, or a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg.CDE = 1.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_scountinhibit_exists
normative_rules.text: Smcdeleg/Ssccfg defines a new scountinhibit register, a masked alias of mcountinhibit.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_scountinhibit_delegated_rw
normative_rules.text: For counters delegated to S-mode, the associated mcountinhibit bits can be accessed via scountinhibit

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_scountinhibit_nondelegated_ro
normative_rules.text: For counters not delegated to S-mode, the associated bits in scountinhibit are read-only zero.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_scountinhibit_cde0
normative_rules.text: When menvcfg.CDE=0, attempts to access scountinhibit raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_illegal_scountinhibit_vs_vu
normative_rules.text:
When Supervisor Counter Delegation
is enabled, attempts to access scountinhibit from VS-mode or VU-mode
raise a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_virtual_scountovf_vs_vu
normative_rules.text: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, when menvcfg.CDE=1, attempts to read scountovf from VS-mode or VU-mode raise a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_lcofi_mvip_mvien
normative_rules.text: For implementations that support Smcdeleg, Sscofpmf, and Smaia, the local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) bit (bit 13) in each of CSRs mvip and mvien is implemented and writable.

normative_rules.name: Ssccfg_lcofi_hvip_hvien
normative_rules.text: For implementations that support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Smaia/Ssaia, and the H extension, the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in each of hvip and hvien is implemented and writable.

normative_rules.name: Smdbltrp_with_Smrnmi_op
normative_rules.text:
When the Smrnmi extension (<<rnmi>>) is implemented, it enables
invocation of the RNMI handler on a double trap in M-mode to handle the
critical error.

normative_rules.name: ctr_depth
normative_rules.text: The number of records that can be held in the buffer depends upon both the implementation (the maximum supported depth) and the CTR configuration (the software selected depth).

normative_rules.name: Smctr_scope
normative_rules.text: The machine-level extension, Smctr, encompasses all newly added Control Status Registers (CSRs), instructions, and behavior modifications for a hart across all privilege levels.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_transfer_steps
normative_rules.text: The corresponding supervisor-level extension, Ssctr, is essentially identical to Smctr, except that it excludes machine-level CSRs and behaviors not intended to be directly accessible at the supervisor level.

normative_rules.name: Smctr_Ssctr_depend
normative_rules.text: Smctr and Ssctr depend on both the implementation of S-mode and the Sscsrind extension.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_mctrctl_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The mctrctl register is a 64-bit read/write register that enables and configures the CTR capability.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_mode_op
normative_rules.text: Enable transfer recording in the selected privileged mode(s).

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_rasemu_op
normative_rules.text: Enables RAS (Return Address Stack) Emulation Mode.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_mte_op
normative_rules.text: Enables recording of traps to M-mode when M=0.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_ste_op
normative_rules.text: Enables recording of traps to S-mode when S=0.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_bpfrz_op
normative_rules.text: Set sctrstatus.FROZEN on a breakpoint exception that traps to M-mode or S-mode.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_lcofifrz_op
normative_rules.text: Set sctrstatus.FROZEN on local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) that traps to M-mode or S-mode.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_excinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of exceptions.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_intrinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of interrupts.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_tretinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of trap returns.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_ntbren_op
normative_rules.text: Enable recording of not-taken branches.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_tkbrinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of taken branches.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_indcallinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of indirect calls.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_dircallinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of direct calls.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_indjmpinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of indirect jumps (without linkage).

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_dirjmpinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of direct jumps (without linkage).

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_corswapinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of co-routine swaps.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_retinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of function returns.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_indljmpinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of other indirect jumps (with linkage).

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_dirljmpinh_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit recording of other direct jumps (with linkage).

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_custom_op
normative_rules.text: WARL bits designated for custom use.

normative_rules.name: mctrctl_impl
normative_rules.text: All fields are optional except for M, S, U, and BPFRZ.  All unimplemented fields are read-only 0, while all implemented fields are writable.  If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, LCOFIFRZ must be writable.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_sctrctl_op
normative_rules.text: The sctrctl register provides supervisor mode access to a subset of mctrctl.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_sctrctl_acc
normative_rules.text: Bits 2 and 9 in sctrctl are read-only 0. As a result, the M and MTE fields in mctrctl are not accessible through sctrctl.  All other mctrctl fields are accessible through sctrctl.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_vsctrctl_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: If the H extension is implemented, the vsctrctl register is a 64-bit read/write register that is VS-mode's version of supervisor register sctrctl.  When V=1, vsctrctl substitutes for the usual sctrctl, so instructions that normally read or modify sctrctl actually access vsctrctl instead.

normative_rules.name: vsctrctl_s_op
normative_rules.text: Enable transfer recording in VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: vsctrctl_u_op
normative_rules.text: Enable transfer recording in VU-mode.

normative_rules.name: vsctrctl_ste_op
normative_rules.text: Enables recording of traps to VS-mode when S=0.

normative_rules.name: vsctrctl_bpfrz_op
normative_rules.text: Set sctrstatus.FROZEN on a breakpoint exception that traps to VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: vsctrctl_lcofifrz_op
normative_rules.text: Set sctrstatus.FROZEN on local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) that traps to VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: sctrdepth
normative_rules.text: The 32-bit sctrdepth register specifies the depth of the CTR buffer.

normative_rules.name: sctrdepth_depth_warl
normative_rules.text: WARL field that selects the depth of the CTR buffer.

normative_rules.name: sctrdepth_depth_entries_op
normative_rules.text: The depth of the CTR buffer dictates the number of entries to which the hardware records transfers. For a depth of N, the hardware records transfers to entries 0..N-1. All <<_entry_registers, Entry Registers>> read as '0' and are read-only when the selected entry is in the range N to 255.  When the depth is increased, the newly accessible entries contain unspecified but legal values.

normative_rules.name: sctrdepth_depth
normative_rules.text: It is implementation-specific which DEPTH value(s) are supported.

normative_rules.name: sctrdepth_mode
normative_rules.text: Attempts to access sctrdepth from VS-mode or VU-mode raise a virtual-instruction exception, unless CTR state enable access restrictions apply.

normative_rules.name: sctrstatus
normative_rules.text: The 32-bit sctrstatus register grants access to CTR status information and is updated by the hardware whenever CTR is active.  CTR is active when the current privilege mode is enabled for recording and CTR is not frozen.

normative_rules.name: sctrstatus_wrptr
normative_rules.text: WARL field that indicates the physical CTR buffer entry to be written next.  It is incremented after new transfers are recorded (see <<Behavior>>), though there are exceptions when xctrctl.RASEMU=1, see <<RAS (Return Address Stack) Emulation Mode>>.  For a given CTR depth (where depth = 2^(DEPTH+4)^), WRPTR wraps to 0 on an increment when the value matches depth-1, and to depth-1 on a decrement when the value is 0.  Bits above those needed to represent depth-1 (e.g., bits 7:4 for a depth of 16) are read-only 0. On depth changes, WRPTR holds an unspecified but legal value.

normative_rules.name: sctrstatus_frozen_op
normative_rules.text: Inhibit transfer recording.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_sctrstatus_acc
normative_rules.text:
Undefined bits in sctrstatus are WPRI. Status fields may be added by future extensions,
and software should ignore but preserve any fields that it does not recognize.  Undefined  bits must be implemented as read-only 0, unless a custom extension is implemented and enabled

normative_rules.name: siselect_acc_op
normative_rules.text: The siselect index range 0x200 through 0x2FF is reserved for CTR logical entries 0 through 255. When siselect holds a value in this range, sireg provides access to ctrsource, sireg2 provides access to ctrtarget, and sireg3 provides access to ctrdata.  sireg4, sireg5, and sireg6 are read-only 0.

normative_rules.name: vsiselect_op
normative_rules.text: When vsiselect holds a value in 0x200..0x2FF, the vsireg* registers provide access to the same CTR entry register state as the analogous sireg* registers.  There is not a separate set of entry registers for V=1.

normative_rules.name: ctrsource_op
normative_rules.text: The ctrsource register contains the source program counter, which is the pc of the recorded control transfer instruction, or the epc of the recorded trap.

normative_rules.name: ctrsource_ctrtarget_ctrdata_vbit
normative_rules.text: The valid (V) bit is set by the hardware when a transfer is recorded in the selected CTR buffer entry, and implies that data in ctrsource, ctrtarget, and ctrdata is valid for this entry.

normative_rules.name: Ssctr_ctrsource_sz_acc_op
normative_rules.text: ctrsource is an MXLEN-bit WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual or physical addresses that can serve as a pc. It need not be able to hold any invalid addresses; implementations may convert an invalid address into a valid address that the register is capable of holding.  When XLEN < MXLEN, both explicit writes (by software) and implicit writes (for recorded transfers) will be zero-extended.

normative_rules.name: ctrtarget_op
normative_rules.text:
The ctrtarget register contains the target (destination) program counter
of the recorded transfer.

normative_rules.name: ctrtarget_pc_next_br
normative_rules.text: For a not-taken branch, ctrtarget holds the PC of the next sequential instruction following the branch.

normative_rules.name: ctrtarget_misp
normative_rules.text:
The optional MISP bit is set by the hardware
when the recorded transfer is an instruction whose target or
taken/not-taken direction was mispredicted by the branch predictor. MISP
is read-only 0 when not implemented.

normative_rules.name: ctrtarget_sz_acc
normative_rules.text: ctrtarget is an MXLEN-bit WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual or physical addresses that can serve as a pc. It need not be able to hold any invalid addresses; implementations may convert an invalid address into a valid address that the register is capable of holding.  When XLEN < MXLEN, both explicit writes (by software) and implicit writes (by recorded transfers) will be zero-extended.

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_sz_acc
normative_rules.text:
The ctrdata register contains metadata for the recorded transfer. This
register must be implemented, though all fields within it are optional.
Unimplemented fields are read-only 0.  ctrdata is a 64-bit register.

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_type
normative_rules.text: Identifies the type of the control flow transfer recorded in the entry, using the encodings listed in xref:transfer-type-defs[xrefstyle=short].  Implementations that do not support this field will report 0.

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_ccv
normative_rules.text: Cycle Count Valid.

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_cc
normative_rules.text:
Cycle Count, composed of the Cycle Count Exponent (CCE, in
CC[15:12]) and Cycle Count Mantissa (CCM, in CC[11:0]).

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_undef
normative_rules.text: Undefined bits in ctrdata are WPRI. Undefined bits must be implemented as read-only 0, unless a <<_custom_extensions, custom extension>> is implemented and enabled.

normative_rules.name: sctrclr_zero_entries_op
normative_rules.text: Zeroes all  CTR <<_entry_registers, Entry Registers>>, for all DEPTH values

normative_rules.name: sctrclr_zero_cycle_counter_op
normative_rules.text: Zeroes the CTR cycle counter and CCV

normative_rules.name: sctrclr_acc
normative_rules.text: Any read of ctrsource, ctrtarget, or ctrdata that follows SCTRCLR, such that it precedes the next qualified control transfer, will return the value 0.  Further, the first recorded transfer following SCTRCLR will have ctrdata.CCV=0.

normative_rules.name: sctrclr_exceptions
normative_rules.text: SCTRCLR raises an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode, and a virtual-instruction exception in VU-mode, unless CTR state enable access restrictions apply.

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr1
normative_rules.text: When mstateen0.CTR=1, accesses to CTR register state behave as described in <<CSRs>> and <<Entry Registers>> above, while SCTRCLR behaves as described in <<Supervisor CTR Clear Instruction>>.

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr0
normative_rules.text: When mstateen0.CTR=0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, the following operations raise an illegal-instruction exception:

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr0_except_csr_access
normative_rules.text: Attempts to access sctrctl, vsctrctl, sctrdepth, or sctrstatus

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr0_except_indirect_access
normative_rules.text: Attempts to access sireg* when siselect is in 0x200..0x2FF, or vsireg* when vsiselect is in 0x200..0x2FF

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr0_except_sctrclr
normative_rules.text: Execution of the SCTRCLR instruction

normative_rules.name: mstateen_ctr0_qualified_transfer
normative_rules.text: When mstateen0.CTR=0, qualified control transfers executed in privilege modes less privileged than M-mode will continue to implicitly update entry registers and sctrstatus.

normative_rules.name: hstateen_ctr
normative_rules.text: If the H extension is implemented and mstateen0.CTR=1, the hstateen0.CTR bit controls access to supervisor CTR state when V=1.  This state includes sctrctl (really vsctrctl), sctrstatus, and sireg* (really vsireg*) when siselect (really vsiselect) is in 0x200..0x2FF.  hstateen0.CTR is read-only 0 when mstateen0.CTR=0.

normative_rules.name: hstateen_vs
normative_rules.text: When mstateen0.CTR=1 and hstateen0.CTR=1, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state behave as described in <<CSRs>> and <<Entry Registers>> above, while SCTRCLR behaves as described in <<Supervisor CTR Clear Instruction>>.  When mstateen0.CTR=1 and hstateen0.CTR=0, both VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state and VS-mode execution of SCTRCLR raise a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: hstateen0_ctr0_v1_op
normative_rules.text: When hstateen0.CTR=0, qualified control transfers executed while V=1 will continue to implicitly update entry registers and sctrstatus.

normative_rules.name: ctr_behavior
normative_rules.text: CTR records qualified control transfers.  Control transfers are qualified if they meet the following criteria:

normative_rules.name: ctr_behavior_criteria_priv_mode
normative_rules.text: The current privilege mode is enabled

normative_rules.name: ctr_behavior_criteria_transfer_type
normative_rules.text: The transfer type is not inhibited

normative_rules.name: ctr_behavior_criteria_not_frozen
normative_rules.text: sctrstatus.FROZEN is not set

normative_rules.name: ctr_behavior_criteria_retires
normative_rules.text: The transfer completes/retires

normative_rules.name: ctr_stack
normative_rules.text: Such qualified transfers update the <<_entry_registers, Entry Registers>> at logical entry 0.  As a result, older entries are pushed down the stack; the record previously in logical entry 0 moves to logical entry 1, the record in logical entry 1 moves to logical entry 2, and so on.  If the CTR buffer is full, the oldest recorded entry (previously at entry depth-1) is lost.

normative_rules.name: ctr_validbit
normative_rules.text: Recorded transfers will set the ctrsource.V bit to 1, and will update all implemented record fields.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_enabled
normative_rules.text: Traps between enabled privilege modes are recorded as normal.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_disabled_src
normative_rules.text: Traps from a disabled privilege mode to an enabled privilege mode are partially recorded, such that the ctrsource.PC is 0.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_disabled_tgt
normative_rules.text: Traps from an enabled mode to a disabled mode, known as external traps, are not recorded by default.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_enabled
normative_rules.text: Trap returns between enabled privilege modes are recorded as normal.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_to_disabled
normative_rules.text: Trap returns from an enabled mode back to a disabled mode are partially recorded, such that ctrtarget.PC is 0.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_from_disabled
normative_rules.text: Trap returns from a disabled mode to an enabled mode are not recorded.

normative_rules.name: debug_recording_inhibited
normative_rules.text: Recording in Debug Mode is always inhibited. Transfers into and out of Debug Mode are never recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_ee
normative_rules.text: Recorded

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_ed
normative_rules.text: External trap.  Not recorded by default,

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_de
normative_rules.text: Recorded, ctrsource.PC is 0.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trap_dd
normative_rules.text: Not recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_ee
normative_rules.text: Recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_ed
normative_rules.text: Recorded, ctrtarget.PC is 0.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_de
normative_rules.text: Not recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_trapret_dd
normative_rules.text: Not recorded.

normative_rules.name: exttrap_def
normative_rules.text: External traps are traps from a privilege mode enabled for CTR recording to a privilege mode that is not enabled for CTR recording.  The xctrctl.xTE bits allow M-mode, S-mode, and VS-mode to be enabled for CTR recording separately. When the xctrctl.xTE bits are clear, external traps are not recorded.

normative_rules.name: exttrap_requirements
normative_rules.text: External trap recording depends not only on the target mode, but on any intervening modes, which are modes that are more privileged than the source mode but less privileged than the target mode.  Not only must the external trap enable bit for the target mode be set, but the external trap enable bit(s) for any intervening modes must also be set.

normative_rules.name: exttrap_us
normative_rules.text: sctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_um
normative_rules.text: mctrctl.MTE, sctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_Sm
normative_rules.text: mctrctl.MTE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_vuvs
normative_rules.text: vsctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_vuhs
normative_rules.text: sctrctl.STE, vsctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_vum
normative_rules.text: mctrctl.MTE, sctrctl.STE, vsctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_vshs
normative_rules.text: sctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_vsm
normative_rules.text: mctrctl.MTE, sctrctl.STE

normative_rules.name: exttrap_ctrtarget0
normative_rules.text: In records for external traps, the ctrtarget.PC is 0.

normative_rules.name: exttrap_implreq
normative_rules.text: If external trap recording is implemented, mctrctl.MTE and sctrctl.STE must be implemented, while vsctrctl.STE must be implemented if the H extension is implemented.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttf_default
normative_rules.text: Default CTR behavior, when all transfer type filter bits (xctrctl[47:32]) are unimplemented or 0, is to record all control transfers within enabled privileged modes. By setting transfer type filter bits, software can opt out of recording select transfer types, or opt into recording non-default operations.  All transfer type filter bits are optional.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype0
normative_rules.text: Not used by CTR

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype1
normative_rules.text: Exception

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype2
normative_rules.text: Interrupt

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype3
normative_rules.text: Trap return

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype4
normative_rules.text: Not-taken branch

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype5
normative_rules.text: Taken branch

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype8
normative_rules.text: Indirect call

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype9
normative_rules.text: Direct call

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype10
normative_rules.text: Indirect jump (without linkage)

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype11
normative_rules.text: Direct jump (without linkage)

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype12
normative_rules.text: Co-routine swap

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype13
normative_rules.text: Function return

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype14
normative_rules.text: Other indirect jump (with linkage)

normative_rules.name: ctr_ttype15
normative_rules.text: Other direct jump (with linkage)

normative_rules.name: ctr_various_jump_enc
normative_rules.text: Encodings 8 through 15 refer to various encodings of jump instructions.  The types are distinguished as described below.

normative_rules.name: ctrdata_cc_supported
normative_rules.text: The ctrdata register may optionally include a count of CPU cycles elapsed since the prior CTR record.  The elapsed cycle count value is represented by the CC field, which has a 12-bit mantissa component (Cycle Count Mantissa, or CCM) and a 4-bit exponent component (Cycle Count Exponent, or CCE).

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_inc
normative_rules.text: The elapsed cycle counter (CtrCycleCounter) increments at the same rate as the mcycle counter.  Only cycles while CTR is active are counted, where active implies that the current privilege mode is enabled for recording and CTR is not frozen.  If the CtrCycleCounter value is less than 4096, the CC field is encoded with CCE holding 0 and CCM holding CtrCycleCounter bits 11:0.  Otherwise, CCE holds the index of the most significant one bit in the CtrCycleCounter value, minus 11, and CCM holds CtrCycleCounter bits CCE+10:CCE-1.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_reset
normative_rules.text: The CtrCycleCounter is reset on writes to xctrctl, and on execution of SCTRCLR, to ensure that any accumulated cycle counts do not persist across a context switch.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_impl
normative_rules.text:
An implementation that supports cycle counting must implement CCV and all
CCM bits, but may implement 0..4 exponent bits in CCE.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_cce_rdonly0
normative_rules.text:
Unimplemented CCE
bits are read-only 0.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_sat
normative_rules.text: The CC value saturates when all implemented bits in CCM and CCE are 1.

normative_rules.name: ctr_ccounter_ccv
normative_rules.text: The CC value is valid only when the Cycle Count Valid (CCV) bit is set.  If CCV=0, the CC value might not hold the correct count of elapsed active cycles since the last recorded transfer.  The next record will have CCV=0 after a write to xctrctl, or execution of SCTRCLR, since CtrCycleCounter is reset.  CCV should additionally be cleared after any other implementation-specific scenarios where active cycles might not be counted in CtrCycleCounter.

normative_rules.name: ctrctl_rasemu_op
normative_rules.text: When the optional xctrctl.RASEMU bit is implemented and set to 1, transfer recording behavior is altered to emulate the behavior of a return-address stack (RAS).

normative_rules.name: sctrstatus_frozen_inhibit
normative_rules.text: When sctrstatus.FROZEN=1, transfer recording is inhibited.

normative_rules.name: sctrstatus_frozen_set
normative_rules.text:
When sctrctl.LCOFIFRZ=1 and a local-counter-overflow interrupt
(LCOFI) traps (as a result of an HPM counter overflow) to M-mode or to S-mode, sctrstatus.FROZEN is set by hardware. This inhibits CTR recording until software clears FROZEN. The LCOFI trap itself is not recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_freeze_bp
normative_rules.text: Similarly, on a breakpoint exception that traps to M-mode or S-mode with sctrctl.BPFRZ=1, FROZEN is set by hardware. The breakpoint exception itself is not recorded.

normative_rules.name: ctr_freeze_vs
normative_rules.text: If the H extension is implemented, freeze behavior for LCOFIs and breakpoint exceptions that trap to VS-mode is determined by the LCOFIFRZ and BPFRZ values, respectively, in vsctrctl.  This includes virtual LCOFIs pended by a hypervisor.

normative_rules.name: ctr_custom_bits
normative_rules.text: Any custom CTR extension must be associated with a non-zero value within the designated custom bits in xctrctl.  When the custom bits hold a non-zero value that enables a custom extension, the extension may alter standard CTR behavior, and may define new custom status fields within sctrstatus or the CTR <<_entry_registers, Entry Registers>>.  All custom status fields, and standard status fields whose behavior is altered by the custom extension, must revert to standard behavior when the custom bits hold zero.  This includes read-only 0 behavior for any bits undefined by any implemented standard extensions.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_forward_traps
normative_rules.text:
A trap may need to be delivered to the same or to a higher privilege mode upon
completion of insn:jalr[]/insn:c.jalr[]/insn:c.jr[], but before the instruction at the target
of indirect call/jump was decoded

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_forward_trap_async_interrupt
normative_rules.text: Asynchronous interrupts.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_forward_trap_async_exception
normative_rules.text:
Synchronous exceptions with priority higher than that of a software-check
exception with xtval set to landing pad fault (code=2) (See
<<norm:exc_priority>> of Privileged Specification).

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_exception_priority
normative_rules.text: The software-check exception caused by ext:zicfilp[] has higher priority than an illegal-instruction exception but lower priority than instruction access-fault.

normative_rules.name: lpad_sw_exception
normative_rules.text: The software-check exception due to the instruction not being an insn:lpad[] instruction when ELP is LP_EXPECTED or a software-check exception caused by the insn:lpad[] instruction itself leads to a trap being delivered to the same or to a higher privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: cfi_mstatus_mpelp_op
normative_rules.text:
To store the previous ELP state on trap delivery to M-mode, an
csr::[mpelp] bit is provided in the csr:mstatus[] CSR.

normative_rules.name: cfi_mstatus_spelp_op
normative_rules.text:
To store the previous ELP state on trap
delivery to S/HS-mode, an csr::[spelp] bit is provided in the csr:mstatus[] CSR.

normative_rules.name: cfi_sstatus_spelp_op
normative_rules.text:
The
csr::[spelp] bit in mstatus can be accessed through the csr:sstatus[] CSR.

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_spelp_exists
normative_rules.text:
To store
the previous ELP state on traps to VS-mode, a csr::[spelp] bit is defined in the
csr:vsstatus[] (VS-modes version of csr:sstatus[]).

normative_rules.name: dcsr_pelp_op
normative_rules.text:
To store the previous ELP state on
transition to Debug Mode, a csr::[pelp] bit is defined in the csr:dcsr[] register.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_pelp_trap
normative_rules.text: When a trap is taken into privilege mode x, the csr::[xpelp] is set to ELP and ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_pelp_trap_return
normative_rules.text: An insn:mret[] or insn:sret[] instruction is used to return from a trap in M-mode or S-mode, respectively.  When executing an insn:xret[] instruction, if the new privilege mode is y, then ELP is set to the value of csr::[xpelp] if yLPE (see ) is 1; otherwise, it is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED; csr::[xpelp] is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfilp_pelp_debug_mode
normative_rules.text: Upon entry into Debug Mode, the csr::[pelp] bit in csr:dcsr[] is updated with the ELP at the privilege level the hart was previously in, and the ELP is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED. When a hart resumes from Debug Mode, if the new privilege mode is y, then ELP is set to the value of csr::[pelp] if yLPE (see ) is 1; otherwise, it is set to NO_LP_EXPECTED.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_ssp_csr
normative_rules.text: Attempts to access the csr:ssp[] CSR may result in either an illegal-instruction exception or a virtual-instruction exception, contingent upon the state of the csr:envcfg[sse] fields. The conditions are specified as follows:

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_m_menvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
If the privilege mode is less than M and csr:menvcfg[sse] is 0, an
illegal-instruction exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_u_senvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
Otherwise, if in U-mode and csr:senvcfg[sse] is 0, an illegal-instruction
exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_vs_henvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
Otherwise, if in VS-mode and csr:henvcfg[sse] is 0, a virtual-instruction
exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_vu_senvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
Otherwise, if in VU-mode and csr:senvcfg[sse] is 0,
a virtual-instruction exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_sse_access
normative_rules.text: Otherwise, the access is allowed.

normative_rules.name: Zicfiss_smode_xsse
normative_rules.text: When S-mode is not implemented, then xSSE is 0.

normative_rules.name: ss_page_enc
normative_rules.text:
The
encoding R=0, W=1, and X=0, is defined to represent an SS page.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_menvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
When
csr:menvcfg[sse]=0, this encoding remains reserved.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_henvcfg_sse
normative_rules.text:
Similarly, when V=1 and
csr:henvcfg[sse]=0, this encoding remains reserved at VS and VU levels.

normative_rules.name: satp_mode_bare
normative_rules.text:
If csr:satp[mode] (or csr:vsatp[mode] when V=1) is set to Bare and the effective
privilege mode is less than M, shadow stack instructions raise a store/AMO access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ssamoswap
normative_rules.text:
When the effective privilege mode is M, memory access
by an insn:ssamoswap.w[] or insn:ssamoswap.d[] instruction results in a store/AMO access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_page_access_fault
normative_rules.text:
Memory mapped as an SS page cannot be written to by instructions other than
insn:ssamoswap.w[], insn:ssamoswap.d[], insn:sspush[], and insn:c.sspush[]. Attempts will raise a store/AMO
access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_cache_block_access_fault
normative_rules.text:
Access to a SS page using cache-block operation
(insn:cbo.*[]) instructions is not permitted. Such accesses will raise a store/AMO
access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_implicit_access_fault
normative_rules.text:
Implicit accesses, including instruction fetches to an
SS page, are not permitted. Such accesses will raise an access-fault exception
appropriate to the access type.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_load
normative_rules.text:
However, the shadow stack is readable by all
instructions that only load from memory.

normative_rules.name: ss_fault_exception_code
normative_rules.text:
If a shadow stack (SS) instruction raises an access-fault, page-fault, or
guest-page-fault exception that is supposed to indicate the original instruction
type (load or store/AMO), then the reported exception cause is respectively a
store/AMO access fault (code 7), a store/AMO page fault (code 15), or a
store/AMO guest-page fault (code 23).

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_page_illegal_access
normative_rules.text:
Should a shadow stack instruction access a page that is
not designated as a shadow stack page and is not marked as read-only
(pte.xwr=0b001), a store/AMO access-fault exception will be invoked.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_read_only_page
normative_rules.text:
Conversely,
if the page being accessed by a shadow stack instruction is a read-only page, a
store/AMO page-fault exception will be triggered.

normative_rules.name: ssp_xlen_aligned
normative_rules.text: If the virtual address in csr:ssp[] is not XLEN aligned, then the insn:sspush[], insn:c.sspush[], insn:sspopchk[] and insn:c.sspopchk[] instructions cause a store/AMO access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: ssmp_ss_idempotent_memory
normative_rules.text:
If the memory referenced by
insn:sspush[], insn:c.sspush[], insn:sspopchk[], insn:c.sspopchk[], insn:ssamoswap.w[] and insn:ssamoswap.d[] instructions is not
idempotent, then the instructions cause a store/AMO access-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: active_g_stage_pte
normative_rules.text:
When G-stage page tables are active, the shadow stack instructions that access memory
require the G-stage page table to have read-write permission for the accessed
memory; else a store/AMO guest-page-fault exception is raised.

normative_rules.name: pm_ignore_upper_bits
normative_rules.text: RISC-V Pointer Masking (PM) is a feature that, when enabled, causes the CPU to ignore the upper bits of the effective address

normative_rules.name: pm_ignore_va
normative_rules.text: The ignore transformation differs depending on whether it applies to a virtual or physical address. For virtual addresses, it replaces the upper PMLEN bits with the sign extension of the PMLEN+1st bit.

normative_rules.name: pm_ignore_pa
normative_rules.text: When applied to a physical address, including guest-physical addresses (i.e., all cases except when the active satp register's MODE field != Bare), the ignore transformation replaces the upper PMLEN bits with 0. This includes both the case of running in M-mode and running in other privilege modes with Bare address translation mode.

normative_rules.name: pm_apply_explicit
normative_rules.text: When pointer masking is enabled, the ignore transformation will be applied to every explicit memory access (e.g., loads/stores, atomics operations, and floating point loads/stores).

normative_rules.name: pm_not_apply_implicit
normative_rules.text: The transformation does not apply to implicit accesses such as page-table walks or instruction fetches.

normative_rules.name: pm_deterministic_effect
normative_rules.text: Pointer masking with the same value of PMLEN always has the same effect for the same type of address (virtual or physical).

normative_rules.name: pmlen_supported_values
normative_rules.text: The current standard only supports PMLEN=XLEN-48 (i.e., PMLEN=16 in RV64) and PMLEN=XLEN-57 (i.e., PMLEN=7 in RV64).

normative_rules.name: pmlen_future_reserved
normative_rules.text: A setting has been reserved to potentially support other values of PMLEN in future standards.

normative_rules.name: pm_per_mode_control
normative_rules.text: Pointer masking is controlled separately for different privilege modes.

normative_rules.name: pm_auto_apply_active_mode
normative_rules.text: Different privilege modes may have different pointer masking settings active simultaneously and the hardware will automatically apply the pointer masking settings of the currently active privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: pm_config_next_higher
normative_rules.text: A privilege mode's pointer masking setting is configured by bits in configuration registers of the next-higher privilege mode.

normative_rules.name: pm_mode_only_dependency
normative_rules.text: the pointer masking setting that is applied only depends on the active privilege mode, not on the address that is being masked.

normative_rules.name: pm_explicit_accesses
normative_rules.text: Unless otherwise specified, pointer masking applies to all explicit memory accesses.

normative_rules.name: pm_mprv_spvp
normative_rules.text: MPRV and SPVP affect pointer masking as well, causing the pointer masking settings of the effective privilege mode to be applied.

normative_rules.name: pm_mxr_exception
normative_rules.text: When MXR is in effect at the effective privilege mode where explicit memory access is performed, pointer masking does not apply.

normative_rules.name: pm_cpu_only
normative_rules.text: Pointer masking only applies to accesses generated by instructions on the CPU (including CPU extensions such as an FPU). E.g., it does not apply to accesses generated by page-table walks, the IOMMU, or devices.

normative_rules.name: pm_misaligned_equivalence
normative_rules.text: Misaligned accesses are supported, subject to the same limitations as in the absence of pointer masking. The behavior is identical to applying the pointer masking transformation to every constituent aligned memory access.

normative_rules.name: pm_no_csr_sw
normative_rules.text: No pointer masking operations are applied when software reads/writes to CSRs, including those meant to hold addresses.

normative_rules.name: pm_warl_unaffected
normative_rules.text: The implemented WARL width of CSRs is unaffected by pointer masking

normative_rules.name: pm_csr_hw_apply
normative_rules.text: pointer masking, when applicable, is applied for hardware writes to a CSR (e.g., when the hardware writes the transformed address to stval when taking an exception).

normative_rules.name: pm_debug_trigger
normative_rules.text: Pointer masking is also applied, when applicable, to the memory access address when matching address triggers in debug.

normative_rules.name: pm_no_trap_vector_mask
normative_rules.text: on trap delivery (e.g., due to an exception or interrupt), pointer masking will not be applied to the address of the trap handler.

normative_rules.name: ssnpm_definition
normative_rules.text: A supervisor-level extension that provides pointer masking for the next lower privilege mode (U-mode), and for VS- and VU-modes if the H extension is present.

normative_rules.name: smnpm_definition
normative_rules.text: A machine-level extension that provides pointer masking for the next lower privilege mode (S/HS if S-mode is implemented, or U-mode otherwise).

normative_rules.name: smmpm_definition
normative_rules.text: A machine-level extension that provides pointer masking for M-mode.

normative_rules.name: pm_rv64_only
normative_rules.text: Pointer masking only applies to RV64.

normative_rules.name: pm_rv32_illegal
normative_rules.text: In RV32, trying to enable pointer masking will result in an illegal WARL write and not update the pointer masking configuration bits

normative_rules.name: pm_uxl_clear
normative_rules.text: Setting UXL/SXL to 1 will clear the corresponding pointer masking configuration bits.

normative_rules.name: pmlen_mode_depend
normative_rules.text: the supported values of PMLEN may depend on the effective privilege mode. The current standard only defines PMLEN=XLEN-48 and PMLEN=XLEN-57,

normative_rules.name: pmlen_illegal_warl
normative_rules.text: Trying to enable pointer masking in an unsupported scenario represents an illegal write to the corresponding pointer masking enable bit and follows WARL semantics.

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_pte_n
normative_rules.text:
In Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57, when a PTE has
N=1, the PTE represents a translation that is part
of a range of contiguous virtual-to-physical translations with the same
values for PTE bits 5–0.

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_range_napot
normative_rules.text:
Such ranges must be of a naturally aligned
power-of-2 (NAPOT) granularity larger than the base page size

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_depends_Sv39
normative_rules.text:
The Svnapot extension depends on the Sv39
extension

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_valid_encoding_ppn_subst
normative_rules.text:
If the encoding in pte is
valid according to <<norm:Svnapot_enc_tbl>>, then
instead of returning the original value of pte,
implicit reads of a NAPOT PTE
return a copy of pte in which pte.ppn[i][pte.napot_bits-1:0]
is replaced by vpn[i][pte.napot_bits-1:0].

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_reserved_encoding_fault
normative_rules.text:
reserved according to
<<norm:Svnapot_enc_tbl>>, then a page-fault exception must be raised

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_cache_entries
normative_rules.text:
Implicit reads of NAPOT page table entries
may create address-translation cache entries mapping
a + j×PTESIZE to a copy of pte in which
pte.ppn[i][pte.napot_bits-1:0] is replaced by
vpn[i][pte.napot_bits-1:0], for any or all j such that
j >> napot_bits = vpn[i] >> napot_bits, all for the
address space identified in satp as loaded by step 1

normative_rules.name: Svnapot_hyp_gstage
normative_rules.text:
Svnapot is also supported in G-stage
translation

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_pte_bits
normative_rules.text:
In Sv39, Sv48, and Sv57, bits 62-61 of a leaf page table entry indicate
the use of page-based memory types that override the PMA(s) for the
associated memory pages.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_depends_Sv39
normative_rules.text: The Svpbmt extension depends on the Sv39 extension

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_impl_may_override_pmas
normative_rules.text:
Implementations may override additional PMAs not explicitly listed in
<<norm:Svpbmt_enc_tbl>>.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_nonleaf_pte_pbmt_must_be_zero
normative_rules.text:
Until their use is defined by a standard extension, they must be cleared
by software for forward compatibility, or else a page-fault exception is
raised.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_leaf_pte_pbmt_reserved_3_fault
normative_rules.text:
Until this value is defined by a standard extension, using
this reserved value in a leaf PTE raises a page-fault exception.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_obeys_mem_ordering
normative_rules.text:
memory accesses to such pages obey the memory ordering rules of the
final effective attribute,

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_io_pma_nc_pbmt_obey_rvwmo
normative_rules.text:
If the underlying physical memory attribute for a page is I/O, and the
page has PBMT=NC, then
accesses to that page obey RVWMO.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_io_pma_nc_pbmt_treated_as_io_and_memory
normative_rules.text:
accesses to such pages are considered to be both I/O and main memory
accesses for the purposes of FENCE, .aq, and .rl.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_memory_pma_io_pbmt_strong_io_ordering
normative_rules.text:
accesses to that page obey strong channel
0 I/O ordering rules.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_memory_pma_io_pbmt_treated_as_io_and_memory
normative_rules.text:
accesses to
such pages are considered to be both I/O and main memory accesses for
the purposes of FENCE, .aq, and .rl.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_aliasing_attribute
normative_rules.text:
When Svpbmt is used with non-zero PBMT encodings, it is possible for
multiple virtual aliases of the same physical page to exist
simultaneously with different memory attributes. It is also possible for
a U-mode or S-mode mapping through a PTE with Svpbmt enabled to observe
different memory attributes for a given region of physical memory than a
concurrent access to the same page performed by M-mode or when
MODE=Bare. In such cases,
the behaviors dictated by the attributes
(including coherence, which is otherwise unaffected) may be violated.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_noncacheable_aliasing_no_coherence_loss
normative_rules.text:
Accessing the same location using different attributes that are both
non-cacheable (e.g., NC and IO)
does not cause loss of coherence,

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_noncacheable_aliasing_may_weaken_ordering
normative_rules.text:
might result in weaker memory ordering than the stricter attribute
ordinarily guarantees.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_noncacheable_aliasing_fence_prevents_ordering_loss
normative_rules.text:
fence iorw, iorw instruction
between such accesses suffices to prevent loss of memory ordering.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_cacheable_aliasing_may_cause_coherence_loss
normative_rules.text:
may
cause loss of coherence.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_cacheable_aliasing_fence_flush_fence_required
normative_rules.text: prevents both loss of coherence and loss of memory ordering:

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_hgatp_stage_override_rule
normative_rules.text:
if hgatp.MODE is not equal to zero, non-zero G-stage PTE PBMT bits
override the attributes in the PMA to produce an intermediate set of
attributes.

normative_rules.name: Svpbmt_vsatp_stage_override_rule
normative_rules.text:
if vsatp.MODE is not equal to zero, non-zero VS-stage PTE PBMT
bits override the intermediate attributes to produce the final set of
attributes used by accesses to the page in question.

normative_rules.name: Svadu_hw_update_a_d_bits
normative_rules.text: If the Svadu extension is implemented, the menvcfg.ADUE field is writable.

normative_rules.name: Svadu_hypervisor_adue_writable
normative_rules.text:
If the hypervisor extension is additionally implemented, the henvcfg.ADUE
field is also writable.

normative_rules.name: Svadu_disabled_hw_update_falls_back_to_Svade
normative_rules.text:
When hardware updating of A/D bits is disabled, the Svade extension,
which mandates exceptions when A/D bits need be set, instead takes effect.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sinval_vma_invalidates_same_as_sfence_vma
normative_rules.text:
However, unlike SFENCE.VMA, SINVAL.VMA
instructions are only ordered with respect to SFENCE.VMA,
SFENCE.W.INVAL, and SFENCE.INVAL.IR instructions as defined below.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sfence_w_inval_orders_before_sinval_vma
normative_rules.text:
The SFENCE.INVAL.IR
instruction guarantees that any previous SINVAL.VMA instructions executed
by the current hart are ordered before subsequent implicit references by
that hart to the memory-management data structures.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sequence_rs1_rs2
normative_rules.text:
the values of rs1 and rs2 for the SFENCE.VMA are the same as those
used in the SINVAL.VMA,

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sequence_reads_writes_before
normative_rules.text:
reads and writes prior to the SFENCE.W.INVAL are considered to be
those prior to the SFENCE.VMA,

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sequence_reads_writes_after
normative_rules.text:
reads and writes following the SFENCE.INVAL.IR are considered to be
those subsequent to the SFENCE.VMA.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_hinval_vvma_gvma
normative_rules.text:
These have the same semantics as SINVAL.VMA, except that they combine with
SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR to replace HFENCE.VVMA and
HFENCE.GVMA, respectively, instead of SFENCE.VMA.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_hinval_gvma_uses_vmid
normative_rules.text: HINVAL.GVMA uses VMIDs instead of ASIDs.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_illegal_instruction_u_mode
normative_rules.text:
In particular, an attempt to execute any of
these instructions in U-mode always raises an illegal-instruction
exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_illegal_instruction_tvm
normative_rules.text:
An attempt to execute SINVAL.VMA or HINVAL.GVMA in S-mode or HS-mode when
mstatus.TVM=1 also raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_virtual_instruction_vu_vs
normative_rules.text:
An attempt to execute HINVAL.VVMA or HINVAL.GVMA in VS-mode or VU-mode, or to
execute SINVAL.VMA in VU-mode, raises a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_virtual_instruction_vtvms
normative_rules.text:
When hstatus.VTVM=1, an attempt to execute SINVAL.VMA in VS-mode also raises
a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sfence_w_inval_inval_u_mode
normative_rules.text: raises an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sfence_w_inval_inval_vu_mode
normative_rules.text: Doing so in VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Svinval_sfence_w_inval_inval_s_vs_mode
normative_rules.text:
SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR are unaffected by the mstatus.TVM and
hstatus.VTVM fields and hence are always permitted in S-mode and VS-mode.

normative_rules.name: Svvptc_explicit_stores_update_valid_bit
normative_rules.text:
When the Svvptc extension is implemented, explicit stores by a hart that update
the Valid bit of leaf and/or non-leaf PTEs from 0 to 1 and are visible to a hart
will eventually become visible within a bounded timeframe to subsequent implicit
accesses by that hart to such PTEs.

normative_rules.name: Svrsw60t59b_reserved_bits_60_59
normative_rules.text:
If the Svrsw60t59b extension is implemented, then bits 60-59 of the page table
entries (PTEs) are reserved for use by supervisor software and are ignored by
the implementation.

normative_rules.name: Svrsw60t59b_H_g_stage_reserved_bits
normative_rules.text:
If the Hypervisor (H) extension is also implemented, then bits 60-59 of the
G-stage PTEs are reserved for use by supervisor software and are ignored by
the implementation.

normative_rules.name: Svrsw60t59b_depends_on_Sv39
normative_rules.text: The Svrsw60t59b extension depends on Sv39.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_srmcfg_introduced
normative_rules.text:
To facilitate this, the QoS Identifiers extension (Ssqosid) introduces the
srmcfg register, which configures a hart with two identifiers: a Resource
Control ID (RCID) and a Monitoring Counter ID (MCID). These identifiers
accompany each request issued by the hart to shared resource controllers.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_srmcfg_register_size
normative_rules.text:
The srmcfg register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register used to configure a
Resource Control ID (RCID) and a Monitoring Counter ID (MCID). Both RCID
and MCID are WARL fields.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_rcid_mcid_accompany_requests
normative_rules.text:
The RCID and MCID accompany each request made by the hart to shared resource
controllers. The RCID is used to determine the resource allocations (e.g.,
cache occupancy limits, memory bandwidth limits, etc.) to enforce. The MCID
is used to identify a counter to monitor resource usage.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_srmcfg_csr_applies_to_all_modes
normative_rules.text:
The RCID and MCID configured in the srmcfg CSR apply to all privilege
modes of software execution on that hart by default, but this behavior may be
overridden by future extensions.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_Smstateen_srmcfg_requires_mstateen0
normative_rules.text:
If extension Smstateen is implemented together with Ssqosid, then Ssqosid also
requires the SRMCFG bit in mstateen0 to be implemented.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_srmcfg_access_illegal_instruction
normative_rules.text:
If mstateen0.SRMCFG is 0, attempts to access srmcfg in privilege modes
less privileged than M-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssqosid_srmcfg_access_virtual_instruction
normative_rules.text:
If mstateen0.SRMCFG is 1 or if extension Smstateen is not implemented,
attempts to access srmcfg when V=1 raise a virtual-instruction exception.

normative_rules.name: Ssu64xl_uxl_sstatus
normative_rules.text: If the Ssu64xl extension is implemented, then sstatus.UXL must be capable of holding the value 2 (i.e., UXLEN=64 must be supported).

normative_rules.name: Ssccptr_memory_pte_reads
normative_rules.text: If the Ssccptr extension is implemented, then main memory regions with both the cacheability and coherence PMAs must support hardware page-table reads.

normative_rules.name: Sstvecd_stvec_mode_direct
normative_rules.text: If the Sstvecd extension is implemented, then stvec.MODE must be capable of holding the value 0 (Direct).

normative_rules.name: Sstvecd_stvec_base_aligned_address
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, when stvec.MODE=Direct, stvec.BASE must be capable of holding any valid four-byte-aligned address.

normative_rules.name: Sstvala_stval_faulting_vaddr
normative_rules.text: If the Sstvala extension is implemented, then stval must be written with the faulting virtual address for load, store, and instruction page-fault, access-fault, and misaligned exceptions, and for breakpoint exceptions that are defined to write an address to stval, other than those caused by execution of the EBREAK or C.EBREAK instructions.

normative_rules.name: Sstvala_stval_faulting_instruction
normative_rules.text: For virtual-instruction and illegal-instruction exceptions, stval must be written with the faulting instruction.

normative_rules.name: Sscounterenw_hpmcounter_scounteren
normative_rules.text: If the Sscounterenw extension is implemented, then for any hpmcounter that is not read-only zero, the corresponding bit in scounteren must be writable.

normative_rules.name: Ssstrict_no_nonconforming_extensions
normative_rules.text: If the Ssstrict extension is implemented, then no non-conforming extensions are present.

normative_rules.name: Ssstrict_unimplemented_opcodes_csr_exception
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, attempts to execute unimplemented opcodes or access unimplemented CSRs in the standard or reserved encoding spaces raises an illegal instruction exception that results in a contained trap to the supervisor-mode trap handler.

normative_rules.name: stimecmp_exist
normative_rules.text:
This extension adds the S-level stimecmp
CSR (<<stimecmp>>)

normative_rules.name: vstimecmp_exist
normative_rules.text: and the VS-level vstimecmp CSR (<<vstimecmp>>).

normative_rules.name: stce_bit_exist
normative_rules.text:
This extension adds the STCE bit to the menvcfg
(<<sec:menvcfg>>) and henvcfg
(<<sec:henvcfg>>) CSRs.

normative_rules.name: mhpmevent_inh_op
normative_rules.text: Each of the five xINH bits, when set, inhibit counting of events while in privilege mode x. All-zeroes for these bits results in counting of events in all modes.

normative_rules.name: mhpmevent_of_op
normative_rules.text:
The OF bit is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows, and remains set
until written by software.

normative_rules.name: hpmcounter_overflow
normative_rules.text:
Since hpmcounter values are unsigned values,
overflow is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.

normative_rules.name: count_overflow_interrupt
normative_rules.text: If an hpmcounter overflows while the associated OF bit is zero, then a count overflow interrupt request is generated. If the OF bit is one, then no interrupt request is generated. Consequently the OF bit also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.

normative_rules.name: count_overflow_trigger
normative_rules.text: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcountern or mhpmeventn registers, only from hardware increments of counter registers.

normative_rules.name: mhpmevent_of_bit_set
normative_rules.text:
Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by an hpmcounter sets the
associated OF bit.

normative_rules.name: lcofip_op
normative_rules.text:
When an OF bit is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets
the LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers.

normative_rules.name: scountovf_op
normative_rules.text: This extension adds the scountovf CSR, a 32-bit read-only register that contains shadow copies of the OF bits in the 29 mhpmevent CSRs (mhpmevent3 - mhpmevent31) - where scountovf bit X corresponds to `mhpmevent`X.

normative_rules.name: scountovf_smode_read_access_control
normative_rules.text:
Read access to bit X is subject to the same  mcounteren (or mcounteren and
hcounteren) CSRs that mediate access to the hpmcounter CSRs by S-mode (or
VS-mode).

normative_rules.name: scountovf_mmode_read_access
normative_rules.text: In M-mode, scountovf bit X is always readable.

normative_rules.name: scountovf_smode_read_access
normative_rules.text:
In S/HS-mode, scountovf bit X is readable when mcounteren bit
X is set, and otherwise reads as zero.

normative_rules.name: scountovf_vsmode_read_access
normative_rules.text:
Similarly, in VS mode, scountovf bit
X is readable when mcounteren bit X and hcounteren bit X are both set,
and otherwise reads as zero.

normative_rules.name: menvcfg_dte
normative_rules.text: The Ssdbltrp extension adds the menvcfg.DTE (See <<sec:menvcfg>>)

normative_rules.name: sstatus_sdt_exists
normative_rules.text:
and the
sstatus.SDT fields (See <<sstatus>>).

normative_rules.name: henvcfg_dte
normative_rules.text:
If the hypervisor extension is
additionally implemented, then the extension adds the henvcfg.DTE (See
<<sec:henvcfg>>)

normative_rules.name: vsstatus_sdt
normative_rules.text: and the vsstatus.SDT fields (See <<vsstatus>>).

normative_rules.name: Shvstvecd_vstvec_mode_direct
normative_rules.text: If the Shvstvecd extension is implemented, then vstvec.MODE must be capable of holding the value 0 (Direct).

normative_rules.name: Shvstvecd_vstvec_base_aligned_address
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, when vstvec.MODE=Direct, vstvec.BASE must be capable of holding any valid four-byte-aligned address.

normative_rules.name: Shcounterenw_hpmcounter_hcounteren
normative_rules.text: If the Shcounterenw extension is implemented, then for any hpmcounter that is not read-only zero, the corresponding bit in hcounteren must be writable.

normative_rules.name: Shvstvala_vstval_written
normative_rules.text: If the Shvstvala extension is implemented, vstval must be written in all cases described in  for stval.

normative_rules.name: Shtvala_htval_faulting_gpa
normative_rules.text: If the Shtvala extension is implemented, htval must be written with the faulting guest physical address in all circumstances permitted by the ISA.

normative_rules.name: Shvsatpa_satp_vsatp_modes
normative_rules.text: If the Shvsatpa extension is implemented, all translation modes supported in satp must be supported in vsatp.

normative_rules.name: Shgatpa_satp_hgatp_mode_support
normative_rules.text: If the Shgatpa extension is implemented, then for each supported virtual memory scheme SvNN supported in satp, the corresponding hgatp SvNNx4 mode must be supported.

normative_rules.name: Shgatpa_hgatp_bare_mode
normative_rules.text: Furthermore, the hgatp mode Bare must also be supported.
